It is you who think so much about your souls and are so afraid of losing your life, that you dare not draw near to the Life of life, lest it should consume you.
Our God, we will trust thee. Shall we not find thee equal to our faith? One day, we shall laugh ourselves to scorn that we looked for so little from thee; for thy giving will not be limited by our hoping.
O thou of little faith! “in everything,”﻿—I am quoting your own Bible; nay, more, I am quoting a divine soul that knew his master Christ, and in his strength opposed apostles, not to say christians, to their faces, because they could not believe more than a little in God; could believe only for themselves and not for their fellows; could believe for the few of the chosen nation, for whom they had God’s ancient *word*, but could not believe for the multitude of the nations, for the millions of hearts that God had made to search after him and find him;﻿—“In everything,” says St. Paul, “In everything, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God.” For this “everything,” nothing is too small. That it should trouble us is enough. There is some principle involved in it worth the notice even of God himself, for did he not make us so that the thing does trouble us? And surely for this “everything,” nothing can be too great. When the Son of man cometh and findeth too much faith on the earth﻿—may God in his mercy slay us. Meantime, we will hope and trust.
Do you count it a great faith to believe what God has said? It seems to me, I repeat, a little faith, and, if alone, worthy of reproach. To believe what he has not said is faith indeed, and blessed. For that comes of believing in **Him**. Can you not believe in God himself? Or, confess﻿—do you not find it so hard to believe what he has said, that even that is almost more than you can do? If I ask you why, will not the true answer be﻿—“Because we are not quite sure that he did say it”? If you believed in God you would find it easy to believe the word. You would not even need to inquire whether he had *said* it: you would know that he meant it.
Let us then dare something. Let us not always be unbelieving children.

Let us keep in mind that the Lord, not forbidding those who insist on seeing before they will believe, blesses those who have not seen and yet have believed﻿—those who trust in him more than that﻿—who believe without the sight of the eyes, without the hearing of the ears. They are blessed to whom a wonder is not a fable, to whom a mystery is not a mockery, to whom a glory is not an unreality﻿—who are content to ask, “Is it like Him?” It is a dull-hearted, unchildlike people that will be always putting God in mind of his promises. Those promises are good to reveal what God is; if they think them good as binding God, let them have it so for the hardness of their hearts. They prefer the Word to the Spirit: it is theirs.
Even such will leave us﻿—some of them will, if not all﻿—to the “uncovenanted mercies of God.” We desire no less; we hope for no better. Those are the mercies beyond our height, beyond our depth, beyond our reach. We know in whom we have believed, and we look for that which it hath not entered into the heart of man to conceive. Shall God’s thoughts be surpassed by man’s thoughts? God’s giving by man’s asking? God’s creation by man’s imagination? No. Let us climb to the height of our Alpine desires; let us leave them behind us and ascend the spear-pointed Himmalays of our aspirations; still shall we find the depth of God’s sapphire above us; still shall we find the heavens higher than the earth, and his thoughts and his ways higher than our thoughts and our ways.
Ah Lord! be thou in all our being; as not in the Sundays of our time alone, so not in the chambers of our hearts alone. We dare not think that thou canst not, carest not; that some things are not for thy beholding, some questions not to be asked of thee. For are we not all thine﻿—utterly thine? That which a man speaks not to his fellow, we speak to thee. Our very passions we hold up to thee, and say, “Behold, Lord! Think about us; for thus thou hast made us.” We would not escape from our history by fleeing into the wilderness, by hiding our heads in the sands of forgetfulness, or the repentance that comes of pain, or the lethargy of hopelessness. We take it, as our very life, in our hand, and flee with it unto thee. Triumphant is the answer which thou holdest for every doubt. It may be we could not understand it yet, even if thou didst speak it “with most miraculous organ.”

===Chinese===

让我们记住：主虽不禁止那些非看见不肯信的人，却赐福给那些没有看见就信的人——那些信他过于此的人——那些不用眼见、不用耳闻就信的人。那些人有福了——对他们，神迹不是寓言，奥秘不是嘲弄，荣耀不是虚幻——他们只满足于问：“这像他吗？”一个总是把神的应许挂在嘴边提醒神的民，是心里迟钝、没有孩子气的民。那些应许本为显明神是怎样的一位；他们若以为应许的好处在于捆住神，那就随他们硬着心这样对待吧。他们宁要字句不要圣灵：那是他们的份。
就连这样的人也会撇下我们——他们中有些人会，若非全部——去谈“神约外之怜悯”。我们所求的不下于此；我们所望的也不高于此。那些怜悯高过我们的高处，深过我们的深处，远过我们的所及。我们知道我们信的是谁，我们等候那眼睛未曾看见、人心也未曾想到的。神的思想岂能被人的思想超过？神的赐予岂能被人的祈求超过？神的创造岂能被人的想象超过？不能。让我们登上我们阿尔卑斯般愿望的高峰；让我们把它们留在身后，攀上我们志向那矛尖般直刺的喜马拉雅；我们仍要发现神蓝宝石般的深渊在我们之上；仍要发现天怎样高过地，他的思想和道路也怎样高过我们的思想和道路。
啊，主啊！愿你充满我们的一切存有；正如不只在你时间的主日里，也不只在我们心的内室里。我们不敢想你不能、也不顾；不敢想有些事不在你的眼目之内，有些问题不可向你提出。因为我们岂不全是你的——全然是你的？那人不向同伴说的话，我们向你诉说。我们连自己的激情也向你举起，说：“看哪，主！眷念我们，因为你是这样造了我们。”我们不愿逃避自己的历史——不逃入旷野，不把头藏进遗忘的沙土、痛苦的悔改或无望的麻木里。我们把它当作我们的生命握在手中，带着它逃奔到你那里。你为每一个疑问存留的回答是得胜的。也许，即使你用“最神奇的琴音”说出它，我们此刻还不能明白。

===Original===

But thou shalt at least find faith in the earth, O Lord, if thou comest to look for it now﻿—the faith of ignorant but hoping children, who know that they do not know, and believe that thou knowest.
And for our brothers and sisters, who cleave to what they call thy word, thinking to please thee so, they are in thy holy safe hands, who hast taught us that *whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him*; though *unto him that blasphemes against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven*.

===Chinese===

但你至少要在地上寻见信心，主啊，若你现在就来寻找——那是无知却存着盼望之孩子们的信心，他们知道自己不知道，并信你知道。
至于我们那些紧抓住他们所谓你之道不放、以为这样才能讨你喜悦的弟兄姊妹——他们在你圣洁稳妥的手中；你曾教导我们：*凡说话干犯人子的，还可得赦免*；惟独*亵渎圣灵的，总不得赦免*。

### It Shall Not Be Forgiven / 总不得赦免
===Original===

> And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven.

Whatever belonging to the region of thought and feeling is uttered in words, is of necessity uttered imperfectly. For thought and feeling are infinite, and human speech, although far-reaching in scope, and marvellous in delicacy, can embody them after all but approximately and suggestively. Spirit and Truth are like the Lady Una and the Red Cross Knight; Speech like the dwarf that lags behind with the lady’s “bag of needments.”
Our Lord had no design of constructing a system of truth in intellectual forms. The truth of the moment in its relation to him, The Truth, was what he spoke. He spoke out of a region of realities which he knew could only be suggested﻿—not represented﻿—in the forms of intellect and speech. With vivid flashes of life and truth his words invade our darkness, rousing us with sharp stings of light to will our awaking, to arise from the dead and cry for the light which he can give, not in the lightning of words only, but in indwelling presence and power.
How, then, must the truth fare with those who, having neither glow nor insight, will build intellectual systems upon the words of our Lord, or of his disciples? A little child would better understand Plato than they St. Paul. The meaning in those great hearts who knew our Lord is too great to enter theirs. The sense they find in the words must be a sense small enough to pass through their narrow doors. And if mere words, without the interpreting sympathy, may mean, as they may, almost anything the receiver will or can attribute to them, how shall the man, bent at best on the salvation of his own soul, understand, for instance, the meaning of that apostle who was ready to encounter banishment itself from the presence of Christ, that the beloved brethren of his nation might enter in? To men who are not simple, simple words are the most inexplicable of riddles.
If we are bound to search after what our Lord means﻿—and he speaks that we may understand﻿—we are at least equally bound to refuse any interpretation which seems to us unlike him, unworthy of him. He himself says, “Why do ye not of your own selves judge what is right?”

===Chinese===

> 凡说话干犯人子（Son of man）的，还可得赦免；惟独亵渎圣灵的，总不得赦免。

凡属于思想与情感之领域、又借言语说出的东西，都必然说得并不完全。因为思想与情感是无限的，而人的言语尽管范围宽广、精妙绝伦，终究只能近似地、提示性地把它们体现出来。灵与真理，好比乌娜小姐与红十字骑士；言语则像那落在后面、替小姐提着“针线袋”的侏儒。
我们主并没有设计一套以智性形式构筑的真理体系。他所说的，是那当下的真理在与他的关系中的本相——他本是那真理。他从一个实在之境说话；他知道那实在之境只能被提示——不能被再现——在智性与言语的形式之中。他的话以生命与真理的鲜活闪光侵入我们的黑暗，以尖锐的光之刺激励我们，叫我们定意醒来，从死里兴起，呼求那光——他能赐下的光，不只在言语的闪电之中，更在内住的同在与大能之中。
那么，真理在那些既无热忱又无洞察力、却要在我们主或他门徒的话语上建造智性体系的人手中，会遭到怎样的对待呢？一个小孩子还更容易理解柏拉图（Plato），他们却更难理解圣保罗。那些认识我们主的伟大心灵里的意义，太过宏大，进不了他们的心。他们在那些话语中找到的意义，必是小得足以穿过他们狭窄之门的意义。而若单是字句、没有解释性的共鸣，就可能——正如它们可能的那样——几乎意味着领受者愿意或能够归给它们的任何东西；那么，一个至多只顾自己灵魂得救的人，怎能理解那位使徒的心意呢——那位为使自己民族的蒙爱弟兄得以进入，宁愿自己被逐出基督面前？对不单纯的人，单纯的话是最难解的谜。
我们既必须寻求我们主的意思——他说话正是为叫我们明白——我们至少同样必须拒绝任何在我们看去不像他、不配他的解释。他自己说：“你们自己审量，什么是合理的，何尝不行呢？”

===Original===

In thus refusing, it may happen that, from ignorance or misunderstanding, we refuse the verbal form of its true interpretation, but we cannot thus refuse the spirit and the truth of it, for those we could not have seen without being in the condition to recognize them as the mind of Christ. Some misapprehension, I say, some obliquity, or some slavish adherence to old prejudices, may thus cause us to refuse the true interpretation, but we are none the less bound to refuse and wait for more light. To accept that as the will of our Lord which to us is inconsistent with what we have learned to worship in him already, is to introduce discord into that harmony whose end is to unite our hearts, and make them whole.
“Is it for us,” says the objector who, by some sleight of will, believes in the word apart from the meaning for which it stands, “to judge of the character of our Lord?” I answer, “This very thing he requires of us.” He requires of us that we should do him no injustice. He would come and dwell with us, if we would but open our chambers to receive him. How shall we receive him if, avoiding judgment, we hold this or that daub of authority or tradition hanging upon our walls to be the real likeness of our Lord? Is it not possible at least that, judging unrighteous judgment by such while we flatter ourselves that we are refusing to judge, we may close our doors against the Master himself as an impostor, not finding him like the picture that hangs in our oratory. And if we do not judge﻿—humbly and lovingly﻿—who is to judge for us? Better to refuse even the truth for a time, than, by accepting into our intellectual creed that which our heart cannot receive, not seeing its real form, to introduce hesitation into our prayers, a jar into our praises, and a misery into our love. If it be the truth, we shall one day see it another thing than it appears now, and love it because we see it lovely; for all truth is lovely. “Not to the unregenerate mind.” But at least, I answer, to the mind which can love that Man, Christ Jesus; and that part of us which loves him let us follow, and in its judgements let us trust; hoping, beyond all things else, for its growth and enlightenment by the Lord, who is that Spirit.

===Chinese===

在这拒绝中，可能因无知或误解，我们拒绝了真解释的字句形式；但我们不能因此拒绝其中的灵与真理，因为若非已处于能认出它们是基督之心意的心境，我们根本看不见它们。我说，某种误解、某种偏斜、或某种对旧偏见的奴性依附，可能使我们拒绝那真解释；但我们仍然必须拒绝，并等候更多的光。把我们看去与我们已经学着敬拜的他不相称的东西，当作我们主的旨意来接受，就是把不和谐引入那本要以我们的心为归依、使之完整为目标的和谐之中。
“难道由我们，”那个凭某种意志诡计、撇开话语所指的意义而信字句的反对者说，“来判断我们主的品格吗？”我回答：“这正是他要求于我们的。”他要求于我们的是对他不行不义。他愿意来与我们同住，只要我们肯敞开我们的内室迎接他。我们若避免判断，却把挂在墙上这幅或那幅权威或传统的涂抹当作我们主的真实像貌，怎能接待他呢？我们自以为拒绝判断、却凭这类图像行了不义的判断，岂不至少有可能把主人本人当作骗子关在门外，因为他不像挂在我们小礼拜堂里的那幅画吗？而我们若不判断——谦卑而慈爱地判断——谁来替我们判断呢？宁可暂时拒绝连那真理，也好过把我们心里不能领受的东西——看不见其真实形态的东西——收进我们智性的信条，从而给我们的祷告（prayer）引入犹豫，给我们的赞美引入刺耳的杂音，给我们的爱引入痛苦。它若是真理，有一日我们必看见它现在的表象之外的另一副面目，并因见它可爱而爱它；因为一切真理都是可爱的。“对未重生的心并不如此。”但至少，我回答，对那能爱那个人——基督耶稣——的心是如此；让我们跟随我们里面爱他的那一部分，并信靠它的判断；胜过一切地盼望它得着主的造就与光照——主就是那灵。

===Original===

Better, I say again, to refuse the right *form*, than, by accepting it in misapprehension of what it really is, to refuse the spirit, the truth that dwells therein. Which of these, I pray, is liker to the sin against the Holy Ghost? To mistake the meaning of the Son of man may well fill a man with sadness. But to care so little for him as to receive as his what the noblest part of our nature rejects as low and poor, or selfish and wrong, that surely is more like the sin against the Holy Ghost that can never be forgiven; for it is a sin against the truth itself, not the embodiment of it in him.
Words for their full meaning depend upon their source, the person who speaks them. An utterance may even seem commonplace, till you are told that thus spoke one whom you know to be always thinking, always feeling, always acting. Recognizing the mind whence the words proceed, you know the scale by which they are to be understood. So the words of God cannot mean just the same as the words of man. “Can we not, then, understand them?” Yes, we can understand them﻿—we can understand them *more* than the words of men. Whatever a good word means, as used by a good man, it means just infinitely more as used by God. And the feeling or thought expressed by that word takes higher and higher forms in us as we become capable of understanding him﻿—that is, as we become like him.
I am far less anxious to show what the sin against the Holy Ghost means, than to show what the nonforgiveness means; though I think we may arrive at some understanding of both. I cannot admit for a moment that there is anything in the Bible too mysterious to be looked into; for the Bible is a *revelation*, an unveiling. True, into many things uttered there I can see only a little way. But that little way is the way of life; for the depth of their mystery is God. And even setting aside the duty of the matter, and seeking for justification as if the duty were doubtful, it is reason enough for inquiring into such passages as this before me, that they are often torture to human minds, chiefly those of holy women and children. I knew a child who believed she had committed the sin against the Holy Ghost, because she had, in her toilette, made an improper use of a pin. Dare not to rebuke me for adducing the diseased fancy of a child in a weighty matter of theology. “Despise not one of these little ones.”

===Chinese===

我再说一遍：宁可拒绝正确的*形式*，也好过因误解其真义而接受了它，却拒绝了住在其中的灵、其中的真理。请问，这两者哪一个更像干犯圣灵的罪呢？误解人子的意思，尽可使人满心忧伤。但对他如此轻慢，以致把我们天性中最高贵的部分所拒绝为卑劣贫乏、或自私错谬的东西，当作他的来领受——那 surely 更像那永不得赦免的干犯圣灵的罪；因为那是抵挡真理本身的罪，不是他在人里面道成肉身（the Incarnation）之体现的罪。
话语的完整意义，系于其源头，即说话的那个人。一句话甚至可能显得平平无奇，直到你被告知：说这话的，是你知道的那位永远在思想、永远在感受、永远在行动的人。认出了话语所出的心，你就知道了衡量它们的尺度。所以神的话不可能恰好意味着与人话相同的东西。“那么我们就不能明白它们吗？”能，我们能明白——我们能比明白人的话*更*明白它们。一句好话在好人嘴里意味着什么，在神嘴里就意味着无限更多。而那话所表达的情感或思想，随着我们变得能够明白他——就是说，随着我们变得像他——就在我们里面取得越来越高的形态。
我远不那么急于表明干犯圣灵的罪是什么意思，而是急于表明“不得赦免”是什么意思；尽管我想两者我们都能达到某种理解。我不能承认圣经里有什么事过于神秘、不可探究；因为圣经是*启示*，是揭幕。不错，其中所说许多事，我只能看进去一点点。但那一点点乃是生命之路；因为它们奥秘的深处就是神。即使撇开这事的本分不谈、仿佛本分可疑似的去寻求辩护理由，探究我面前这类经文的理由也已足够：它们常常成为人心的折磨，主要是圣洁的妇女和儿童的心。我认识一个小女孩，她以为自己犯了干犯圣灵的罪，因为她梳妆时不当使用了一枚别针。不要因我在神学的重大问题上援引一个孩子的病态幻想而责备我。“不可轻看这小子里的一个。”

===Original===

Would the theologians were as near the truth in such matters as the children. *Diseased fancy!* The child knew, *and was conscious that she knew*, that she was doing wrong because she had been forbidden. *There was rational ground for her fear.* How would Jesus have received the confession of the darling? *He* would not have told her she was silly, and “never to mind.” Child as she was, might he not have said to her, “I do not condemn thee: go and sin no more”?
To reach the first position necessary for the final attainment of our end, I will inquire what the divine forgiveness means. And in order to arrive at this naturally, I will begin by asking what the human forgiveness means; for, if there be any meaning in the Incarnation, it is through the Human that we must climb up to the Divine.
I do not know that it is of much use to go back to the Greek or the English word for any primary idea of the act﻿—the one meaning “a sending away,” the other, “a giving away.” It will be enough if we look at the feelings associated with the exercise of what is called “forgiveness.”
A man will say: “*I* forgive, but I cannot forget. Let the fellow never come in my sight again.” To what does such a forgiveness reach? To the remission or sending away of the penalties which the wronged believes he can claim from the wrongdoer.
*But there is no sending away of the wrong itself from between them.*
Again, a man will say: “He has done a very mean action, but he has the worst of it himself in that he is capable of doing so. I despise him too much to desire revenge. I will take no notice of it. I forgive him. I don’t care.”
Here, again, there is no sending away of the wrong from between them﻿—no “remission” of the sin.
A third will say: “I suppose I must forgive him; for if I do not forgive him, God will not forgive me.”
This man is a *little* nearer the truth, inasmuch as a ground of sympathy, though only that of common sin, is recognized as between the offender and himself.
One more will say: “He has wronged me grievously. It is a dreadful thing to me, and more dreadful still to him, that he should have done it. He has hurt me, but he has nearly killed himself. He shall have no more injury from it that I can save him. I cannot feel the same towards him yet; but I will try to make him acknowledge the wrong he has done me, and so put it away from him.

===Chinese===

但愿神学家们在这类事上像孩子们那样接近真理。*病态幻想！*那孩子知道、*并且意识到自己知道*她在做错事，因为那事曾被禁止。*她的惧怕有理性的根据。*耶稣会怎样接纳这宝贝的认罪呢？*他*不会对她说她傻、“别放在心上”。她虽是个孩子，他岂不会对她说：“我不定你的罪；去吧，从此不要再犯罪了”吗？
为到达达于我们目标所必需的第一个立场，我要探究神的赦免意味着什么。为了自然地到达这一点，我要先问人的赦免意味着什么；因为，道成肉身若有任何意义，我们正是必须借着人性爬升到神性。
我不认为回到希腊文或英文字义去求这行动的原初观念有多大用处——一个意思是“打发走”，另一个意思是“给出去”。我们只消看看与所谓“赦免”之行使相伴的情感就够了。
一个人会说：“*我*赦免，但我忘不了。别让那家伙再出现在我眼前。”这样的赦免达到了什么？达到了受害方相信自己有权向施害方索取之刑罚的免除或打发。
*但那过犯本身并没有从他们中间被打发走。*
又一个人会说：“他做了一件很卑鄙的事，但他自己吃了更大的亏，因为他居然做得出来。我看不起他，都懒得报复。我不计较。我赦免他。我不在乎。”
这里同样没有把那过犯从他们中间打发走——没有对罪的“免除”。
第三个人会说：“我想我必须赦免他；因为我不赦免他，神也不赦免我。”
这人*稍稍*更接近真理，因为在冒犯者与他之间，一种同感的基础——尽管只是共同之罪的基础——被承认了。
还有一个人会说：“他严重地亏负了我。他做了这事，对我是可怕的事，对他自己更是可怕得多。他伤了我，却几乎杀了他自己。我要尽我所能救他，不让他再受这事的伤害。我暂时还不能对他有从前的感觉；但我要努力使他承认他对我所犯的错，从而把它从他身上除去。

===Original===

Then, perhaps, I shall be able to feel towards him as I used to feel. For this end I will show him all the kindness I can, not forcing it upon him, but seizing every fit opportunity; not, I hope, from a wish to make myself great through bounty to him, but because I love him so much that I want to love him more in reconciling him to his true self. I would destroy this evil deed that has come between us. I send it away. And I would have him destroy it from between us too, by abjuring it utterly.”
Which comes nearest to the divine idea of forgiveness? nearest, though with the gulf between, wherewith the heavens are higher than the earth?
For the Divine creates the Human, has the creative power in excess of the Human. It is the Divine forgiveness that, originating itself, creates our forgiveness, and therefore can do so much more. It can take up all our wrongs, small and great, with their righteous attendance of griefs and sorrows, and carry them away from between our God and us.
Christ is God’s Forgiveness.
Before we approach a little nearer to this great sight, let us consider the human forgiveness in a more definite embodiment﻿—as between a father and a son. For although God is so much more to us, and comes so much nearer to us than a father can be or come, yet the fatherhood is the last height of the human stair whence our understandings can see him afar off, and where our hearts can first know that he is nigh, even in them.
There are various kinds and degrees of wrongdoing, which need varying kinds and degrees of forgiveness. An outburst of anger in a child, for instance, scarcely wants forgiveness. The wrong in it may be so small, that the parent has only to influence the child for self-restraint, and the rousing of the will against the wrong. The father will not feel that such a fault has built up any wall between him and his child. But suppose that he discovered in him a habit of sly cruelty towards his younger brothers, or the animals of the house, how differently would he feel! Could his forgiveness be the same as in the former case? Would not the different evil require a different *form* of forgiveness? I mean, would not the forgiveness have to take the form of that kind of punishment fittest for restraining, in the hope of finally rooting out, the wickedness? Could there be true love in any other kind of forgiveness than this?

===Chinese===

那样，也许我就能重新像从前那样待他。为这个目的，我要对他显出我所能的一切恩慈，不强加于他，却抓住每一个合适的机会；我希望不是出于借对他的慷慨抬高自己的愿望，而是因为我如此爱他，以至我想在使他与自己真实的自己和好中更爱他。我要除灭这件横亘在我们之间的恶行。我把它打发走。我也要他借彻底弃绝它，把它从我们中间除灭。”
哪一个最接近神对赦免的观念呢？最接近——尽管其间仍有鸿沟，如天之高于地？
因为属神的创造属人的，且拥有超过人性的创造之能。是神的赦免自己发端，创造了我们的赦免，因此能行的远更多。它能把我们一切的过犯、无论大小、连同它们公义相随的忧伤哀痛，都担起来，从我们的神与我们中间带走。
基督就是神的赦免。
在稍近距离靠近这大异象之前，让我们以一个更明确的体现来思想人的赦免——父与儿子之间的赦免。因为尽管神对我们远不止于此、也远比一位父亲所能更亲近我们，父性仍是人类阶梯的最后一级高度，从那里我们的悟性能远远望见他，我们的心也能初次知道他临近——甚至就在我们心里。
过错有种种种类与程度，需要种种种类与程度的赦免。譬如孩子一时发怒，几乎不需要赦免。其中的错可能如此之小，父亲只需引导孩子自我克制、激发意志抵挡那错。父亲不会觉得这样的过犯在他与孩子之间筑起了什么墙。但假设他发现孩子对弟弟妹妹或家中的动物有阴毒残忍的习惯，他的感受何等不同！他的赦免能和前一情形一样吗？不同的恶岂不需要不同*形式*的赦免吗？我的意思是，赦免岂不必须采取那种最适于遏制、并指望最终根除恶行的惩罚形式吗？除此以外的任何赦免，其中还能有真实的爱吗？

===Original===

A passing-by of the offence might spring from a poor human kindness, but never from divine love. It would not be “remission.” Forgiveness can never be indifference. Forgiveness is love towards the unlovely.
Let us look a little closer at the way a father might feel, and express his feelings. One child, the moment the fault was committed, the father would clasp to his bosom, knowing that very love in its own natural manifestation would destroy the fault in him, and that, the next moment, he would be weeping. The father’s hatred of the sin would burst forth in his pitiful tenderness towards the child who was so wretched as to have done the sin, and so destroy it. The fault of such a child would then cause no interruption of the interchange of sweet affections. The child is forgiven at once. But the treatment of another upon the same principle would be altogether different. If he had been guilty of baseness, meanness, selfishness, deceit, self-gratulation in the evil brought upon others, the father might *say* to himself: “I cannot forgive him. This is beyond forgiveness.” He might *say* so, and keep saying so, while all the time he was striving to let forgiveness find its way that it might lift him from the gulf into which he had fallen. His love might grow yet greater because of the wandering and loss of his son. For love is divine, and then most divine when it loves according to *needs* and not according to *merits*. But the forgiveness would be but in the process of making, as it were, or of drawing nigh to the sinner. Not till his opening heart received the divine flood of destroying affection, and his own affection burst forth to meet it and sweep the evil away, could it be said to be finished, to have arrived, could the son be said to “be” forgiven.
God is forgiving us every day﻿—sending from between him and us our sins and their fogs and darkness. Witness the shining of his sun and the falling of his rain, the filling of their hearts with food and gladness, that he loves them that love him not. When some sin that we have committed has clouded all our horizon, and hidden him from our eyes, he, forgiving us, ere we are, and that we may be, forgiven, sweeps away a path for this his forgiveness to reach our hearts, that it may by causing our repentance destroy the wrong, and make us able even to forgive ourselves.

===Chinese===

对过犯的轻轻放过，可能出于贫乏的人间善意，却绝不会出于属神的爱。那不是“免除”。赦免永远不可能是漠不关心。赦免是对不可爱者的爱。
让我们更贴近一点看一位父亲可能的感受与表达方式。对某个孩子，过犯一犯下，父亲就会把他搂进怀中，知道那爱本身自然的流露就会除灭他里面的过犯，知道下一刻他就会痛哭。父亲对罪的恨，会向他那因犯了罪而如此可怜的孩子化作怜悯的温柔爆发出来，从而除灭那罪。这样一个孩子的过犯便不会中断彼此甜蜜情感的交流。孩子立刻得了赦免。但对另一个孩子，基于同样的原则，对待却完全不同。他若犯了卑鄙、小气、自私、欺骗，或因加于别人的祸患而自鸣得意的罪，父亲可能会*对自己*说：“我不能赦免他。这超出赦免的范围。”他可能这样说，并且一直这样说，同时却始终在竭力让赦免找到路，好把他从堕入的深渊里提起来。他的爱可能因儿子的流浪与失丧而愈发深挚。因为爱是属神的，并且当它按*需要*而不是按*功德*去爱的时候，最为属神。但那赦免可以说还只是在制成之中，或在临近罪人的途中。直到他敞开的心接受了那除灭罪恶之爱的大水，他自己的爱也爆发出来迎上去、把恶冲走，那赦免才可以说成了、到了，那儿子才可以说是“得了”赦免。
神天天在赦免我们——从他与我们中间打发走我们的罪和它们的雾与暗。看哪，他的太阳照耀，他的雨水降下，他以食物和欢喜充满人心——他爱那不爱他的人。当我们所犯的某个罪遮蔽了我们全部的地平线、把我们的眼与他隔开时，他赦免我们——在我们得赦免之先、也为了使我们得赦免——为他的赦免扫出一条到达我们心的路，好叫它借引出我们的悔改而除灭那过犯，使我们甚至能赦免自己。

===Original===

For some are too proud to forgive themselves, till the forgiveness of God has had its way with them, has drowned their pride in the tears of repentance, and made their heart come again like the heart of a little child.
But, looking upon forgiveness, then, as the perfecting of a work ever going on, as the contact of God’s heart and ours, in spite and in destruction of the intervening wrong, we may say that God’s love is ever in front of his forgiveness. God’s love is the prime mover, ever seeking to perfect his forgiveness, which latter needs the human condition for its consummation. The love is perfect, working out the forgiveness. God loves where he cannot yet forgive﻿—where forgiveness in the full sense is as yet simply impossible, because no contact of hearts is possible, because that which lies between has not even begun to yield to the besom of his holy destruction.
Some things, then, between the Father and his children, as between a father and his child, may comparatively, and in a sense, be made light of﻿—I do not mean made light of in themselves: away they must go﻿—inasmuch as, evils or sins though they be, they yet leave room for the dwelling of God’s Spirit in the heart, forgiving and cleansing away the evil. When a man’s evil is thus fading out of him, and he is growing better and better, that is the forgiveness coming into him more and more. Perfect in God’s will, it is having its perfect work in the mind of the man. When the man hath, with his whole nature, cast away his sin, there is no room for forgiveness any more, for God dwells in him, and he in God. With the voice of Nathan, “Thou art the man,” the forgiveness of God laid hold of David, the heart of the king was humbled to the dust; and when he thus awoke from the moral lethargy that had fallen upon him, he found that he was still with God. “When I awake,” he said, “I am still with thee.”
But there are two sins, not of individual deed, but of spiritual condition, which “cannot be forgiven”; that is, as it seems to me, which cannot be excused, passed by, made little of by the tenderness even of God, inasmuch as they will allow no forgiveness to come into the soul, they will permit no good influence to go on working alongside of them; they shut God out altogether. Therefore the man guilty of these can never receive into himself the holy renewing saving influences of God’s forgiveness.

===Chinese===

因为有些人太骄傲，不能赦免自己，直到神的赦免在他们身上行了它的事，把他们的骄傲淹没在悔改的眼泪里，使他们的心重新变成小孩子的心。
于是，把赦免看作一件正在进行之工的完成，看作神的心与我们的心在对抗并除灭间隔之过犯中的相触，我们可以说：神的爱永远走在他的赦免之前。神的爱是原动力，总在寻求成全他的赦免；而后者需要人的状态来达于成全。爱是完全的，在作成着赦免。神在他还不能赦免的地方爱着——在那里，完全意义上的赦免还根本不可能，因为心与心的相触不可能，因为那间隔之物甚至还没开始向他圣洁除灭的扫帚屈服。
那么，有些事，在父（the Father）与他的儿女之间，如同在父亲与他的孩子之间，比较上、在某种意义上可以从轻发落——我不是说它们本身可以从轻：它们必须除去——因为它们虽是恶、是罪，却仍给神的灵在心里的居住留出余地，赦免并清净地除去那恶。当一个人的恶这样渐渐从他身上消退、他变得越来越好，那就是赦免越来越多地进入他。赦免在神的旨意里是完全的，正在人的心里成全它的工。当那人以其全部天性抛掉他的罪，就再没有赦免的余地，因为神住在他里面，他也在神里面。拿单以“你就是那人”的声音发出时，神的赦免抓住了大卫；王的心谦卑到尘土；当他这样从落在自己身上的道德麻木中醒来时，他发现他仍与神同在。“我醒来的时候，”他说，“仍与你同在。”
但有两种罪，不是个别的行为，而是属灵光景之罪，“不能得赦免”；照我看来，就是说，连神的温柔也不能原谅它们、放过它们、看轻它们，因为它们不容赦免进入灵魂，不容任何美善的影响力在它们旁边继续作工；它们把神完全关在门外。所以犯这罪的人，永远不能在自己里面领受神赦免之圣洁更新拯救的影响力。

===Original===

God is outside of him in every sense, save that which springs from his creating relation to him, by which, thanks be to God, he yet keeps a hold of him, although against the will of the man who will not be forgiven. The one of these sins is against man; the other against God.
The former is unforgivingness to our neighbour; the shutting of him out from our mercies, from our love﻿—so from the universe, as far as we are a portion of it﻿—the murdering therefore of our neighbour. It may be an infinitely less evil to murder a man than to refuse to forgive him. The former may be the act of a moment of passion: the latter is the heart’s choice. It is *spiritual* murder, the worst, to hate, to brood over the feeling that excludes, that, in our microcosm, kills the image, the idea of the hated. We listen to the voice of our own hurt pride or hurt affection (only the latter without the suggestion of the former, thinketh no evil) to the injury of the evildoer. In as far as we can, we quench the relations of life between us; we close up the passages of possible return. This is to shut out God, the Life, the One. For how are we to receive the forgiving presence while we shut out our brother from our portion of the universal forgiveness, the final restoration, thus refusing to let God be All in all? If God appeared to us, how could he say, “I forgive you,” while we remained unforgiving to our neighbour? Suppose it possible that he should say so, his forgiveness would be no good to us while we were uncured of our unforgivingness. It would not touch us. It would not come near us. Nay, it would hurt us, for we should think ourselves safe and well, while the horror of disease was eating the heart out of us. Tenfold the forgiveness lies in the words, “If ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your heavenly Father forgive your trespasses.” Those words are kindness indeed. God holds the unforgiving man with his hand, but turns his face away from him. If, in his desire to see the face of his Father, he turns his own towards his brother, then the face of God turns round and seeks his, for then the man may look upon God and not die. With our forgiveness to our neighbour, in flows the consciousness of God’s forgiveness to us; or even with the effort, we become capable of believing that God can forgive us.

===Chinese===

在一切意义上，神都在他之外——除了那出于神与他创造关系的意义；靠这关系——感谢神——他仍握着他、抓着他，尽管那不愿被赦免的人自己并不愿意。这两种罪，一种是对人犯的，一种是对神犯的。
前者是对邻人的不赦免；把他关在我们的怜悯之外、我们的爱之外——既然我们是宇宙的一部分，也就把他关在宇宙之外——因此是对邻人的谋杀。拒绝赦免一个人，可能比谋杀他更是无限的恶。前者可能是一时激情的行为：后者却是心的选择。那是*属灵的*谋杀，是最坏的谋杀——怀恨、怀抱那排拒之感、在我们的微观宇宙里杀死所恨者的形象与观念。我们听从自己受伤的骄傲或受伤的情感的声音（唯有后者没有前者的掺和时才不计算人的恶），去加害于作恶者。我们尽我们所能地熄灭我们之间生命的关联；我们封死一切可能回转的通路。这就是把神、把生命、把那一位关在门外。因为我们既把弟兄关在普遍赦免、最终复原之外，拒绝让神在一切之中作一切，又怎能领受那赦免的同在呢？神若向我们显现，我们若仍不肯赦免邻人，他怎能说“我赦免你”呢？假定他可能这样说，他的赦免在我们未医好不赦免之病以前，也于我们无益。它摸不着我们。它就近不了我们。不，它还要害我们，因为我们自以为安稳无恙，而疾病的恐怖正在啃蚀我们的心。“你们不饶恕人的过犯，你们的天父也必不饶恕你们的过犯”——这话里有十倍的赦免。这些话实在是恩慈。神用手握着那不赦免的人，脸却向他转开。他若因渴望见父的面而把自己的脸转向弟兄，神的脸就转过来寻他的脸，因为那时这人可以见神而不死。随着我们对邻人的赦免，神赦免我们的意识便流入；甚至随着这努力，我们变得能够相信神肯赦免我们。

===Original===

No man who will not forgive his neighbour, can believe that God is willing, yea, wanting to forgive him, can believe that the dove of God’s peace is hovering over a chaotic heart, fain to alight, but finding no rest for the sole of its foot. For God to say to such a man, “I cannot forgive you,” is love as well as necessity. If God said, “I forgive you,” to a man who hated his brother, and if (as is impossible) that voice of forgiveness should reach the man, what would it mean to him? How would the man interpret it? Would it not mean to him, “You may go on hating. I do not mind it. You have had great provocation, and are justified in your hate”? No doubt God takes what wrong there is, and what provocation there is, into the account; but the more provocation, the more excuse that can be urged for the hate, the more reason, if possible, that the hater should be delivered from the hell of his hate, that God’s child should be made the loving child that he meant him to be. The man would think, not that God loved the sinner, but that he forgave the sin, which God never does. Every sin meets with its due fate﻿—inexorable expulsion from the paradise of God’s Humanity. He loves the sinner so much that he cannot forgive him in any other way than by banishing from his bosom the demon that possesses him, by lifting him out of that mire of his iniquity.
No one, however, supposes for a moment that a man who has once refused to forgive his brother, shall therefore be condemned to endless unforgiveness and unforgivingness. What is meant is, that while a man continues in such a mood, God cannot be with him as his friend; not that he will not be his friend, but the friendship being all on one side﻿—that of God﻿—must take forms such as the man will not be able to recognize as friendship. Forgiveness, as I have said, is not love merely, but love *conveyed as love* to the erring, so establishing peace towards God, and forgiveness towards our neighbour.
To return then to our immediate text: Is the refusal of forgiveness contained in it a condemnation to irrecoverable impenitence? Strange righteousness would be the decree, that because a man has done wrong﻿—let us say has done wrong so often and so much that he *is* wrong﻿—he shall forever remain wrong!

===Chinese===

凡不肯赦免邻人的人，都不能相信神愿意、甚至渴望赦免他，不能相信神和平的鸽正盘旋在一颗混乱的心上，想要落下，却找不着落脚之地。神对这样的人说“我不能赦免你”，既是爱，也是必需。神若对一个恨弟兄的人说“我赦免你”，而那赦免之声（这是不可能的）竟能到达那人，它对那人意味着什么呢？那人会怎样理解它呢？岂不会理解为“你可以继续恨。我不介意。你受了很大的刺激，你的恨有理”吗？无疑，神会把一切存在的错、一切存在的刺激计算在内；但刺激越多、能为恨辩护的理由越多，那恨人者就——若可能的话——越有理由该从他的恨之地狱（hell）里被救出来，神的儿女就该被造成神所定意要他成为的那个爱的孩子。那人想到的将不是神爱罪人，而是神赦免了罪——而神从不赦免罪。每一件罪都遭逢它命定的结局——从神之人性的乐园里被无情逐出。他如此爱罪人，以致他无法以别的方式赦免他，只能把附着他身上的鬼从他怀里逐出，把他从罪的泥沼中提起来。
然而，没有人会有一刻以为：一个曾拒绝赦免弟兄的人，就要因此被判无尽的不得赦免与不赦免。这意思乃是：只要人停留在这等心境里，神就不能作他的朋友与他同在；不是他不愿作他的朋友，而是友谊既全在神的一边，就必采取这人所不能认出为友谊的形式。赦免，如我所说，不只是爱，而是*作为爱被传递*给犯错者的爱，从而确立对神的平安和对邻人的赦免。
那么回到我们眼前的经文：经文里所含的拒绝赦免，是对无可挽回之不悔改的定罪吗？说一个人因为行了错——姑且说他行错又多又频繁，以致他这个人*就是*错——他就要求远错下去，这样的判决是何等奇怪的义（righteousness）！

===Original===

Do not tell me the condemnation is only negative﻿—a leaving of the man to the consequences of his own will, or at most a withdrawing from him of the Spirit which he has despised. God will not take shelter behind such a jugglery of logic or metaphysics. He is neither schoolman nor theologian, but our Father in heaven. He knows that that in him would be the same unforgivingness for which he refuses to forgive man. The only tenable ground for supporting such a doctrine is, that God *cannot* do more; that Satan has overcome; and that Jesus, amongst his own brothers and sisters in the image of God, has been less strong than the adversary, the destroyer. What then shall I say of such a doctrine of devils as that, even if a man did repent, God would not or could not forgive him?
Let us look at “*the* unpardonable sin,” as this mystery is commonly called, and see what we can find to understand about it.
All sin is unpardonable. There is no compromise to be made with it. We shall not come out except clean, except having paid the uttermost farthing. But the special unpardonableness of those sins, the one of which I have spoken and that which we are now considering, lies in their shutting out God from his *genial*, his especially spiritual, influences upon the man. Possibly in the case of the former sin, I may have said this too strongly; possibly the love of God may have some part even in the man who will not forgive his brother, although, if he continues unforgiving, that part must decrease and die away; possibly resentment against our brother, might yet for a time leave room for some divine influences by its side, although either the one or the other must speedily yield; but the man who denies truth, who consciously resists duty, who says there is no truth, or that the truth he sees is not true, who says that which is good is of Satan, or that which is bad is of God, supposing him to know that it is good or is bad, denies the Spirit, shuts out the Spirit, and therefore cannot be forgiven. For without the Spirit no forgiveness can enter the man to cast out the satan. Without the Spirit to witness with his spirit, no man could know himself forgiven, even if God appeared to him and said so. The full forgiveness is, as I have said, when a man feels that God is forgiving him; and this cannot be while he opposes himself to the very essence of God’s will.

===Chinese===

不要对我说这定罪只是消极的——只是任凭那人承受自己意志的后果，或至多是收回他所轻看的圣灵。神不会躲藏在这样一套逻辑或形而上学的戏法后面。他既不是经院学者，也不是神学家，而是我们在天上的父。他知道，那样做在他里面，就正是他所拒绝用以赦免人的那种不赦免。支撑这样一套教义唯一站得住的根据是：神*不能*做得更多；撒但已经得胜；耶稣在他自己按神形象所造的弟兄姊妹中间，竟不如那仇敌、那毁灭者刚强。那么，对这样一套鬼魔的教义——说即使人真悔改了，神也不肯或不能赦免他——我还有什么可说的呢？
让我们看看这通常所谓“*那*不得赦免的罪”的奥秘，看看我们能从中理解到什么。
一切的罪都是不得赦免的。与罪没有折中可讲。我们除非完全干净、除非还清了最后一文钱，就不能出来。但那两种罪——我已经讲过的一种和我们正在思想的这种——特殊的不得赦免性，在于它们把神关在他对人之*亲切的*、尤其属灵的影响力之外。就前一种罪而言，可能我说得太重了；神的爱或许在那不肯赦免弟兄的人里面也有一部分——尽管他若持续不赦免，那部分必减少而消逝；对弟兄的怨恨，或许一时还能在旁边给某些属神的影响力留出余地——尽管二者必有一方速速退让；但那否认真理的人、那明知故犯地抵挡本分的人、那说没有真理或说他所见的真理不是真理的人、那说是善的属撒但或说是恶的属神的人（假定他知道那是善或是恶），就是否认圣灵、把圣灵关在门外，因此不能被赦免。因为没有圣灵，就没有赦免能进入那人里面把撒但赶出去。没有圣灵与他的灵同证，即使神向他显现并这样说，也没有人能知道自己得了赦免。完全的赦免，如我所说，是人感觉到神正在赦免他；而这不可能，只要他还抵挡神旨意的本质本身。

===Original===

As far as we can see, the men of whom this was spoken were men who resisted the truth with some amount of perception that it was the truth; men neither led astray by passion, nor altogether blinded by their abounding prejudice; men who were not excited to condemn one form of truth by the love which they bore to another form of it; but men so set, from selfishness and love of influence, against one whom they saw to be a good man, that they denied the goodness of what they knew to be good, in order to put down the man whom they knew to be good, because He had spoken against them, and was ruining their influence and authority with the people by declaring them to be no better than they knew themselves to be. Is not this to be Satan? to be in hell? to be corruption? to be that which is damned? Was not this their *condition* unpardonable? How, through all this mass of falsehood, could the pardon of God reach the essential humanity within it? Crying as it was for God’s forgiveness, these men had almost separated their humanity from themselves, had taken their part with the powers of darkness. Forgiveness while they were such was an impossibility. No. Out of that they must come, else there was no word of God for them. But the very word that told them of the unpardonable state in which they were, was just the one form the voice of mercy could take in calling on them to repent. They must hear and be afraid. I dare not, cannot think that they refused the truth, knowing all that it was; but I think they refused the truth, knowing that it was true﻿—not carried away, as I have said, by wild passion, but by cold self-love, and envy, and avarice, and ambition; not merely doing wrong knowingly, but setting their whole natures knowingly against the light. Of this nature must the sin against the Holy Ghost surely be. “This is the condemnation,” (not the sins that men have committed, but the condition of mind in which they choose to remain), “that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” In this sin against the Holy Ghost, I see no single act alone, although it must find expression in many acts, but a wilful condition of mind,

> As far removed from God and light of heaven,

As from the centre thrice to the utmost pole.

===Chinese===

就我们所能看的，这些话所指的人，是在相当程度上感知到那是真理却仍抵挡真理的人；不是被激情引偏、也不是全然被充塞的偏见弄瞎的人；不是因为热爱真理的一种形式而激动去定罪另一种形式的人；而是这样的人——出于自私和权欲，执意敌对一个他们明知是好人的人，以致否认他们明知为善之事的善，为要打倒他们明知为善的那人，因为他曾指摘他们，并且向民众揭露他们并不比他们自知的那样更好，从而毁掉了他们的影响力和权柄。这岂不就是作撒但吗？岂不就是处身地狱吗？岂不就是朽坏吗？岂不就是那被定罪之物吗？他们这种*光景*岂不就是不得赦免的吗？穿过这一大团的虚谎，神的赦免怎能触及其中本质的人性呢？这些人虽呼求着神的赦免，却几乎已把自己的人性与自己分离，已站到黑暗权势那一边去了。他们仍是这样的时候，赦免是不可能的。不能。他们必须从那里面出来，否则对他们就没有神的道。但那告诉他们身处不得赦免之境的道，恰恰正是怜悯之声呼唤他们悔改所能取的唯一形式。他们必须听见而惧怕。我不敢、也不能认为他们拒绝真理时明白真理的全部；但我认为他们拒绝真理时知道那是真的——如我所说，不是被狂放的激情卷走，而是被冷酷的自爱、嫉妒、贪婪和野心；不单是明知而作恶，更是明知道而以全人性敌挡光。干犯圣灵的罪必是这种性质的。“光来到世间，世人因自己的行为是恶的，爱黑暗胜于爱光——定罪的就是这个”（不是人所犯的那些罪，而是他们选择停留的心境）。在这干犯圣灵的罪里，我看不到单独哪一个行为，虽然它必在许多行为中显明，我看到的是一个任性的心境，

> 远离神和天上的光，

如从中心三度到极点那样遥远。

===Original===

For this there could be no such excuse made as that even a little light might work beside it; for there light could find no entrance and no room; light was just what such a mind was set against, almost because it was what it was. The condition was utterly bad.
But can a man really fall into such a condition of spiritual depravity?
That is my chief difficulty. But I think it may be. And wiser people than I, have thought so. I have difficulty in believing it, I say; yet I think it must be so. But I do not believe that it is a fixed, a final condition. I do not see why it should be such any more than that of the man who does not forgive his neighbour. If you say it is a worse offence, I say, Is it too bad for the forgiveness of God?
But is God able to do anything more with the man? Or how is the man ever to get out of this condition? If the Spirit of God is shut out from his heart, how is he to become better?
The Spirit of God is the Spirit whose influence is known by its witnessing with our spirit. But may there not be other powers and means of the Spirit preparatory to this its highest office with man? God who has made us can never be far from any man who draws the breath of life﻿—nay, must be in him; not necessarily in his heart, as we say, but still in him. May not then one day some terrible convulsion from the centre of his being, some fearful earthquake from the hidden gulfs of his nature, shake such a man so that through all the deafness of his death, the voice of the Spirit may be faintly heard, the still small voice that comes after the tempest and the earthquake? May there not be a fire that even such can feel? Who shall set bounds to the consuming of the fire of our God, and the purifying that dwells therein?
The only argument that I can think of, which would with me have weight against this conclusion, is, that the revulsion of feeling in anyone who had thus sinned against the truth, when once brought to acknowledge his sin, would be so terrible that life would never more be endurable, and the kindest thing God could do would be to put such a man out of being, because it had been a better thing for him never to have been born. But he who could make such a man repent, could make him so sorrowful and lowly, and so glad that he had repented, that he would wish to live ever that he might ever repent and ever worship the glory he now beheld.

===Chinese===

因为对这罪，连“一点微光可在它旁边作工”这样的托辞都无从说起；因为光在那里找不到入口和余地；光恰恰是这种心所敌挡的，几乎正因为它就是它本是的那个。这光景是全然败坏的。
但人真的能堕入这样属灵败坏的光景吗？
这是我主要的难题。但我认为可能。比我更有智慧的人也这样认为。我说，我难于相信它；然而我认为必是如此。但我不相信它是固定的、终局的光景。我不明白它为什么比那不赦免邻人者的光景更是终局的。你若说它是更重的罪，我问：它坏到神赦免不了的地步了吗？
但神对这人还能作什么吗？这人又怎能从这光景中出来呢？若神的灵被他关在心外，他怎能变好呢？
神的灵，就是以其与我们灵同证而被认知其影响的那灵。但难道没有圣灵其他的权能与途径，作为它对人这最高职事之前的预备吗？造了我们的神，永远不会离任何呼吸生命之气的人太远——不，必定在他里面；不一定如我们所说的在他心里，却仍在他里面。那么，岂不终有一日，某种从他那存有之中心而来的可怕震动、某种从他那本性隐秘深渊而来的骇人地震，把这样的人摇撼，以致穿过他那死亡的一切聋聩，圣灵的声音仍能隐约听见——那在暴风和地震之后才来的微小安静之声？岂不能有一团连这样的人也能感觉到的火吗？谁能给我们神的火之烧灭、和住在其中的炼净设定界限呢？
我唯一想得到的、对我有分量来反对这结论的论据是：一个这样干犯了真理的人，一旦被带到承认己罪的地步，其情感的剧烈反转将如此可怕，以致生命再不可忍受，神所能行的最仁慈之事就是把这样的人除灭，因为他不如从未出生过。但那位能使这样的人悔改的，也能使他如此忧伤谦卑、又为他已悔改而如此欢喜，以致他愿意永远活着，好永远悔改、永远敬拜他如今所瞻望的荣耀。

When a man gives up self, his past sins will no longer oppress him. It is enough for the good of life that God lives, that the All-perfect exists, and that we can behold him.
“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do,” said the Divine, making excuse for his murderers, not after it was all over, but at the very moment when he was dying by their hands. Then Jesus had forgiven them already. His prayer the Father must have heard, for he and the Son are one. When the Father succeeded in answering his prayer, then his forgiveness in the hearts of the murderers broke out in sorrow, repentance, and faith. Here was a sin dreadful enough surely﻿—but easy for our Lord to forgive. All that excuse for the misled populace! Lord Christ be thanked for that! That was like thee! But must we believe that Judas, who repented even to agony, who repented so that his high-prized life, self, soul, became worthless in his eyes and met with no mercy at his own hand﻿—must we believe that he could find no mercy in such a God? I think, when Judas fled from his hanged and fallen body, he fled to the tender help of Jesus, and found it﻿—I say not how. He was in a more hopeful condition now than during any moment of his past life, for he had never repented before. But I believe that Jesus loved Judas even when he was kissing him with the traitor’s kiss; and I believe that he was his Saviour still. And if any man remind me of his words, “It had been good for that man if he had not been born,” I had not forgotten them, though I know that I now offer nothing beyond a conjectural explanation of them when I say: Judas had got none of the good of the world into which he had been born. He had not inherited the earth. He had lived an evil life, out of harmony with the world and its God. Its love had been lost upon him. He had been brought to the very Son of God, and had lived with him as his own familiar friend; and he had not loved him more, but less than himself. Therefore it had been all useless. “It had been good for that man if he had not been born”; for it was all to try over again, in some other way﻿—inferior perhaps, in some other world, in a lower school. He had to be sent down the scale of creation which is ever ascending towards its Maker. But I will not, cannot believe, O my Lord, that thou wouldst not forgive thy enemy, even when he repented, and did thee right.

人一旦舍弃了自己，过去的罪就不再压迫他。神活着、那完全者存在、我们能瞻望他——这就够作生命的良善了。
“父啊，赦免他们，因为他们所做的，他们不晓得。”那属神者在为他杀他的人开脱时这样说——不是在一切结束之后，而是在正死于他们之手的时刻。那时耶稣已经赦免了他们。他的祷告（prayer）父必定垂听了，因为父与子原为一。当父成功地应允了他的祷告，他的赦免就在凶手们心里爆发为忧伤、悔改与信心（faith）。这确实是一件够可怕的罪——却容易为我们主所赦免。一切都是为了给受蒙骗的民众开脱！主基督啊，为此感谢你！这才像你！但我们难道必须相信，那连痛苦都悔改了的犹大（Judas），那悔改到他把至为珍贵的生命、自己、灵魂都看得毫无价值、亲手不予怜惜的犹大——我们难道必须相信，他在这样一位神那里寻不到怜悯吗？我想，当犹大从他吊死的躯体逃开时，他是逃向耶稣的温柔救助，并且寻着了——至于如何，我不说。他如今处于他一生任何时刻都更有盼望的光景，因为他从前从未悔改。而我信，连犹大以卖主之亲吻他的时候，耶稣也爱他；我信，他仍是他的救主。若有人向我提起他的话——“那人没有生下来倒好”——我并没有忘记它们，尽管我知道我现在对它们所能提供的不过是一个推测性的解释：犹大并没有把他所生入的这个世界的任何益处得着。他没有承受这地。他过了一种邪恶的生活，与这世界和它的神不和谐。这世界的爱在他身上失落了。他被带到神儿子的面前，与他同住如亲密的朋友；而他爱他不是更多，而是比爱自己更少。因此这一切都落空了。“那人没有生下来倒好”；因为一切都要从头再来——用别的方式，或许更低一等的方式，在别的世界，在更低级的学校。他必须被送下那永远向着造它者上升的创造之梯。但主啊，我不肯、也不能相信：连他悔改了、向你行了义的时候，你还不赦免你的仇敌。

===Original===

Nor will I believe that thy holy death was powerless to save thy foe﻿—that it could not reach to Judas. Have we not heard of those, thine own, taught of thee, who could easily forgive their betrayers in thy name? And if thou forgivest, will not thy forgiveness find its way at last in redemption and purification?
Look for a moment at the clause preceding my text: “He that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.” What does it mean? Does it mean﻿—“Ah! you are mine, but not of my sort. You denied me. Away to the outer darkness”? Not so. “It shall be forgiven to him that speaketh against the Son of man”; for He may be but the truth revealed *without* him. Only he must have shame before the universe of the loving God, and may need the fire that burneth and consumeth not.
But for him that speaketh against the Spirit of Truth, against the Son of God revealed *within* him, he is beyond the teaching of that Spirit now. For how shall he be forgiven? The forgiveness would touch him no more than a wall of stone. Let him know what it is to be without the God he hath denied. Away with him to the Outer Darkness! Perhaps *that* will make him repent.
My friends, I offer this as only a contribution towards the understanding of our Lord’s words. But if we ask him, he will lead us into all truth. And let us not be afraid to think, for he will not take it ill.
But what I have said must be at least a part of the truth.
No amount of discovery in his words can tell us more than *we* have discovered, more than we have seen and known to be true. For all the help the best of his disciples can give us is only to discover, to see for ourselves. And beyond all our discoveries in his words and being, there lie depths within depths of truth that we cannot understand, and yet shall be ever going on to understand. Yea, even now sometimes we seem to have dim glimpses into regions from which we receive no word to bring away.
The fact that some things have become to us so much more simple than they were, and that great truths have come out of what once looked common, is ground enough for hope that such will go on to be our experience through the ages to come.

我也不信你圣死的拯救对你的仇敌是无能的——信它够不着犹大。我们岂不曾听说你自己的门徒、受过你教导的人，能轻易地奉你的名赦免那出卖他们的人吗？你既赦免，你的赦免岂不终要在救赎与炼净中找到路吗？
请看片刻我经文前面那一子句：“在人面前不认我的，人子在神的使者面前也必不认他。”这是什么意思呢？是——“啊！你是属我的，却不是我这类的。你不认我。去外边黑暗（the outer darkness）吧”——吗？不是如此。“说话干犯人子的还可得赦免”；因为他所抵挡的，可能只是在他*之外*启示的真理。只是他必须在慈爱神的全宇宙面前蒙羞，并且可能需要那焚烧却不烧灭的火。
至于那抵挡真理之灵、抵挡在他*之内*启示的神子的，他如今已在那灵的教导之外。因为他怎能被赦免呢？赦免临到他，不会比临到一堵石墙更多。让他知道否认了他的那位神不在，是什么滋味。把他赶到外边黑暗去吧！也许*那*会使他悔改。
我的朋友们，我提出这些，只是为理解我们主的话所作的一份贡献。但我们若求他，他必引导我们进入一切的真理。让我们不要怕思想，因为他不会见怪。
但我所说过的，至少必是真理的一部分。
在他的话语里再多的发现，也不能告诉我们多于*我们*已经发现的、多于我们已经看见并知道为真的东西。因为他门徒中最优秀者所能给我们的一切帮助，也只是帮助我们自己去发现、亲眼看见。而在我们对他话语与存有的一切发现之外，还有真理的深而又深，是我们不能明白、却要永远继续去明白的。是的，甚至此刻有时我们似乎对某些境界有朦胧的一瞥，却没有从那里带回任何话语。
有些事情对我们已变得比从前简单得多、有些伟大真理从曾经看似平凡之物中显出来——这事实，就是盼望的充分根据：在将来的世代里，这也必继续成为我们的经历。
