===Chinese===

我们从从前的无知中前进的距离，只能量度横在我们与他的成年之间、我们与他的爱之间、我们的朦胧与他浩大异象之间那必永远横亘之距离的一小段。愿我们不久都归向他——都是孩子，仍是孩子，比以往更甚地是孩子——从他手中领受那*白石，石上写着新名，除了那领受的人，没有人能认识*。

### The New Name / 新名
===Original===

> To him that overcometh, I will give a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.

Whether the Book of the Revelation be written by the same man who wrote the Gospel according to St. John or not, there is, at least, one element common to the two﻿—the mysticism.
I use the word *mysticism* as representing a certain mode of embodying truth, common, in various degrees, to almost all, if not all, the writers of the New Testament. The attempt to define it thoroughly would require an essay. I will hazard but one suggestion towards it: A mystical mind is one which, having perceived that the highest expression of which the truth admits, lies in the symbolism of nature and the human customs that result from human necessities, prosecutes thought about truth so embodied by dealing with the symbols themselves after logical forms. This is the highest mode of conveying the deepest truth; and the Lord himself often employed it, as, for instance, in the whole passage ending with the words, “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!”
The mysticism in the Gospel of St. John is of the simplest, and, therefore, noblest nature. No dweller in this planet can imagine a method of embodying truth that shall be purer, loftier, truer to the truth embodied. There may be higher modes in other worlds, or there may not﻿—I cannot tell; but of all our modes these forms are best illustrations of the highest. Apparently the mysticism of St. John’s own nature enabled him to remember and report with sufficient accuracy the words of our Lord, always, it seems to me, of a recognizably different kind from those of any of the writers of the New Testament﻿—chiefly, perhaps, in the simplicity of their poetical mysticism.
But the mysticism in the Book of the Revelation is more complicated, more gorgeous, less poetic, and occasionally, I think, perhaps arbitrary, or approaching the arbitrary; *reminding* one, in a word, of the mysticism of Swedenborg.

===Chinese===

> 得胜的，我要赐他一块白石，石上写着新名，除了那领受的人，没有人能认识。

《启示录》是否出自《约翰福音》同一位作者之手，姑且不论；至少有一点是两书共通的——神秘主义。
我用*神秘主义*一词，指一种体现真理的特定方式，新约的几乎全部作者（若非全部）都在不同程度上共有它。要彻底界定它需要一整篇文章。我只冒昧提出一个指向：神秘的心灵，是这样一个心灵——它既已察见真理所能有的最高表达，在于自然的象征、以及出于人类必需而产生的人类习俗之中，就照逻辑的形式处理这些象征本身，来推进对如此体现之真理的思考。这是传达最深真理的最高方式；主自己也常常使用它，例如在以“所以你里面的光若是暗了，那黑暗是何等大呢”结束的整段话里。
约翰福音中的神秘主义属于最简单、因而也最高贵的性质。住在这星球上的没有人能想出一种更纯净、更高超、更忠于所体现之真理的体现方式。别的世界也许有更高的方式，也许没有——我不知道；但在我们的一切方式中，这些形式是那最高者的最佳例证。显然，约翰本人天性中的神秘主义，使他能够以足够的准确记住并传报我们主的话——那些话在我看来，总与任何别的新约作者的话有可辨认的不同——或许主要就在其诗性神秘主义的单纯。
但《启示录》中的神秘主义更复杂、更华丽、较少诗意，而且我想，有时或许是任意的，或接近任意；一句话，它令人想起斯韦登堡（Swedenborg）的神秘主义。

===Original===

Putting aside both historical and literary criticism, in neither of which with regard to the authorship of these two books have I a right even to an opinion, I would venture to suggest that possibly their difference in tone is just what one might expect when the historian of a mystical teacher and the recorder of his mystical sayings, proceeds to embody his own thoughts, feelings, and inspirations; that is, when the revelation flows no longer from the lips of the Master, but through the disciple’s own heart, soul, and brain. For surely not the most idolatrous of our Bible-worshipping brothers and sisters will venture to assert that the Spirit of God could speak as freely by the lips of the wind-swayed, reed-like, rebukable Peter, or of the Thomas who could believe his own eyes, but neither the word of his brethren, nor the nature of his Master, as by the lips of Him who was blind and deaf to everything but the will of him that sent him.
Truth is truth, whether from the lips of Jesus or Balaam. But, in its deepest sense, *the truth* is a condition of heart, soul, mind, and strength towards God and towards our fellow﻿—not an utterance, not even a *right* form of words; and therefore such truth coming forth in words is, in a sense, the person that speaks. And many of the utterances of truth in the Revelation, commonly called of St. John, are not merely lofty in form, but carry with them the conviction that the writer was no mere “trumpet of a prophecy,” but spoke that he did know, and testified that he had seen.
In this passage about the gift of the white stone, I think we find the essence of religion.
What the notion in the mind of the writer with regard to the white stone was, is, I think, of comparatively little moment. I take the stone to belong more to the arbitrary and fanciful than to the true mystical imagery, although for the bringing out of the mystical thought in which it is concerned, it is of high and honourable dignity. For fancy itself will subserve the true imagination of the mystic, and so be glorified. I doubt if the writer himself associated any essential meaning with it. Certainly I will not allow that he had such a poor notion in it as that of a voting pebble﻿—white, because the man who receives it is accepted or chosen. The word is used likewise for a precious stone set as a jewel.

===Chinese===

撇开历史考证和文学考证不谈——对这两本书的作者问题，我在哪一方面都无权持有意见——我冒昧提示：两书语调之不同，或许正是一个神秘教师的史家、又兼他神秘话语的记录者，进而体现他自己的思想、情感与灵感时，我们所能预期的样子；就是说，当启示不再从主的口中流出，而是流经门徒自己的心、魂与脑。因为确实连我们那些拜圣经的弟兄姊妹中最拜偶像的，也不敢断言：神的灵能借着风中摇摆、芦苇般、可受责备的彼得（Peter）的口，或借着只信自己眼睛、却不信弟兄的话、不信主人本性的多马的口，像借着那位对一切都盲都聋、唯独对差他来者的旨意不盲不聋之主的口，一样自由地说话。
真理就是真理，无论出自耶稣之口还是巴兰之口。但*那真理*在其最深的意义上，是一种向着神、向着同伴的心、魂、意、力的光景——不是一句话语，甚至不是一个*正确的*言辞形式；因此这样从话语中出来的真理，在某种意义上，就是说话的那个人。而《启示录》——通常归于圣约翰名下——中许多真理的话语，不单形式崇高，还带着一种确信：写的人不只是一支“预言的号筒”，而是把他知道的说了出来，为他看见的作了见证。
在关于白石之赐的这段经文里，我想我们找到了宗教的本质。
写作者心中关于白石的观念是什么，我认为比较无关紧要。我认为这石头与其属于真正的神秘意象，不如属于任意与想象；尽管为要带出它所涉的神秘思想，它具有高贵可敬的尊严。因为想象本身也会服务于神秘主义者的真实想象，并因此得荣耀。我怀疑写作者自己是否把它与任何本质的意义相联。当然我不容许说它里面的观念贫乏到只是一枚投票的小圆石——白色，因为领受它的人蒙了悦纳或蒙了拣选。这词同样用来指镶作宝石的贵重石头。

===Original===

And the writer thought of it mystically, a mode far more likely to involve a reference to nature than to a political custom. What his mystic meaning may be, must be taken differently by different minds. *I* think he sees in its whiteness purity, and in its substance indestructibility. But I care chiefly to regard the stone as the vehicle of the name﻿—as the form whereby the name is represented as passing from God to the man, and what is involved in this communication is what I wish to show. If my reader will not acknowledge my representation as St. John’s meaning, I yet hope so to set it forth that he shall see the representation to be true in itself, and then I shall willingly leave the interpretation to its fate.
I say, in brief, the giving of the white stone with the new name is the communication of what God thinks about the man to the man. It is the divine judgment, the solemn holy doom of the righteous man, the “Come, thou blessed,” spoken to the individual.
In order to see this, we must first understand what is the idea of a name﻿—that is, what is the perfect notion of a name. For, seeing the mystical energy of a holy mind here speaks of God as giving something, we must understand that the essential thing, and not any of its accidents or imitations, is intended.
A name of the ordinary kind in this world, has nothing essential in it. It is but a label by which one man and a scrap of his external history may be known from another man and a scrap of his history. The only names which have significance are those which the popular judgment or prejudice or humour bestows, either for ridicule or honour, upon a few out of the many. Each of these is founded upon some external characteristic of the man, upon some predominant peculiarity of temper, some excellence or the reverse of character, or something which he does or has done well or ill enough, or at least, singularly enough, to render him, in the eyes of the people, worthy of such distinction from other men. As far as they go, these are real names, for, in some poor measure, they express individuality.
The true name is one which expresses the character, the nature, the being, the *meaning* of the person who bears it. It is the man’s own symbol﻿—his soul’s picture, in a word﻿—the sign which belongs to him and to no one else. Who can give a man this, his own name? God alone.

===Chinese===

而写作者是照神秘的意义思想它的——这种方式远更可能涉及对自然的指涉，而非一项政治习俗。它的神秘意义是什么，必因各人心灵的不同而不同。*我*认为写作者在其白色中看见纯净，在其质料中看见不朽。但我主要愿把石头看作名的载体——看作名被表达为从神传给人所借的形式；而我想表明的，是这传达中所含的东西。若我的读者不肯承认我的表述是圣约翰的意思，我仍盼望把它陈明得使他看见这表述本身为真，然后我就甘愿把这解释交给它的命运。
简言之，我说：赐白石与新名，就是神对这人的看法传达给这人。这是神的审判（the judgment），是义人严肃圣洁的定局，是对个体说的“你这蒙福的，来吧”。
要看见这一点，我们必须先明白名是什么观念——就是说，名的完全观念是什么。因为，一个圣洁心灵的神秘能力在此既说到神赐下某物，我们就必须明白，所指的是那本质之物，而不是它的任何偶然或仿效。
世上普通的名字，里面没有任何本质的东西。它不过是一个标签，借以把一个人连同他外史的一角，与另一个人连同他的历史一角区别开来。唯有那些出于大众的判断或偏见或趣味、为嘲弄或尊荣而赐给少数人的名字，才有意义。这些名字各基于那人的某个外在特征、某种主导的脾气特性、品格上的某种优异或相反、或他做得够好或够坏、至少够奇特而配得民众眼中与他人不同的某种东西。就其范围而论，这些是真实的名字，因为它们以某种贫乏的程度表达了个体性。
真名是表达那背负它之人的品格、本性、存有、*意义*的名。它是那人自己的符号——一言以蔽之，他灵魂的画像——属于他、不属于任何别人的记号。谁能给人这个、他自己的名？唯独神。

===Original===

For no one but God sees what the man is, or even, seeing what he is, could express in a name-word the sum and harmony of what he sees. To whom is this name given? To him that overcometh. When is it given? When he has overcome. Does God then not know what a man is going to become? As surely as he sees the oak which he put there lying in the heart of the acorn. Why then does he wait till the man has become by overcoming ere he settles what his name shall be? He does not wait; he knows his name from the first. But as﻿—although repentance comes because God pardons﻿—yet the man becomes aware of the pardon only in the repentance; so it is only when the man has become his name that God gives him the stone with the name upon it, for then first can he understand what his name signifies. It is the blossom, the perfection, the completion, that determines the name; and God foresees that from the first, because he made it so; but the tree of the soul, before its blossom comes, cannot understand what blossom it is to bear, and could not know what the word meant, which, in representing its own unarrived completeness, named itself. Such a name cannot be given until the man *is* the name.
God’s name for a man must then be the expression in a mystical word﻿—a word of that language which all who have overcome understand﻿—of his own idea of the man, that being whom he had in his thought when he began to make the child, and whom he kept in his thought through the long process of creation that went to realize the idea. To tell the name is to seal the success﻿—to say, “In thee also I am well pleased.”
But we are still in the region of symbol. For supposing that such a form were actually observed between God and him that overcometh, it would be no less a symbol﻿—only an acted one. We must therefore look deeper still for the fullness of its meaning. Up to this point little has been said to justify our expectations of discovery in the text. Let us, I say, look deeper. We shall not look long before we find that the mystic symbol has for its centre of significance the fact of the personal individual relation of every man to his God. That every man has affairs, and those his first affairs, with God, stands to the reason of every man who associates any meaning or feeling with the words, Maker, Father, God.

===Chinese===

因为除了神，没有人看见那人是什么；即使看见了是什么，也没有人能用一个名字的词，表达他所看见的总和与和谐。这名赐给谁？赐给那得胜的。何时赐下？当他得胜了。难道神不知道一个人将要成为什么吗？正如他看见他放进橡子心里的那棵橡树那样确实。那么他为什么要等到那人借得胜成为那样，才定他的名是什么？他并不等；他从起初就知道他的名。但正如——悔改虽因神赦免而来——人却只在悔改中才察觉那赦免；照样，只有当那人已成为他的名时，神才把写着名的石头赐给他，因为那时他才能第一次明白他的名意味着什么。是花朵、是完全、是成全决定了名；神从起初就预见它，因为是他造成这样；但灵魂之树在花开之前，不能明白它要开什么花，也不能明白那个代表它自己尚未到达之完全、因而命名了它自己的词是什么意思。这样的名，只有当那人*就是*这名时，才能赐下。
神给一个人的名，因而必是一个神秘之词的表达——用那一切得胜者都懂的语言之词——表达神自己关于这人的观念：就是他起意造这孩子时心中怀有的那位存有，也是他经过实现这观念的漫长创造过程始终怀在心中的那位。告知这名，就是盖印确认成功——就是说：“我喜悦你。”
但我们仍在象征的领域。因为假定这样一个形式真的在神与得胜者之间被遵守，它也仍是一个象征——只是一个行出来的象征。所以我们还得往更深处看它意义的丰满。到目前为止，为证实我们在经文中发现的期望，说得还很少。让我们，我说，往深处看。我们不用看多久，就会发现这神秘象征的意义中心，正是每个人与他神之间那亲身个别的关系。每个人都有与神的事务、且那是他首要的事务——这对一切把任何意义或情感与造物者、父、神这些词相连的人，都是不证自明的。

===Original===

Were we but children of a day, with the understanding that someone had given us that one holiday, there would be something to be thought, to be felt, to be done, because we knew it. For then our nature would be according to our fate, and we could worship and die. But it would be only the praise of the dead, not the praise of the living, for death would be the deepest, the lasting, the overcoming. We should have come out of nothingness, not out of God. He could only be our Maker, not our Father, our Origin. But now we know that God cannot be the God of the dead﻿—must be the God of the living; inasmuch as to know that we died, would freeze the heart of worship, and we could not say Our God, or feel him worthy of such worth-ship as we could render. To him who offers unto this God of the living his own self of sacrifice, to him that overcometh, him who has brought his individual life back to its source, who knows that he is *one* of God’s children, *this* one of the Father’s making, he giveth the white stone. To him who climbs on the stair of all his God-born efforts and God-given victories up to the height of his being﻿—that of looking face to face upon his ideal self in the bosom of the Father﻿—God’s “him,” realized in him through the Father’s love in the Elder Brother’s devotion﻿—to him God gives the new name written.
But I leave this, because that which follows embraces and intensifies this individuality of relation in a fuller development of the truth. For the name is one “which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.” Not only then has each man his individual relation to God, but each man has his peculiar relation to God. He is to God a peculiar being, made after his own fashion, and that of no one else; for when he is perfected he shall receive the new name which no one else can understand. Hence he can worship God as no man else can worship him﻿—can understand God as no man else can understand him. This or that man may understand God more, may understand God better than he, but no other man can understand God as he understands him. God give me grace to be humble before thee, my brother, that I drag not my simulacrum of thee before the judgment-seat of the unjust judge, but look up to thyself for what revelation of God thou and no one else canst give.

===Chinese===

我们纵然只是一日的孩子，知道有人给了我们这唯一的假日，也因知道这一点而有可想、可感、可做的事。因为那时我们的本性就与我们的命运相符，我们能敬拜，也能死。但那只是死人的赞美，不是活人的赞美，因为死才是最深的、持久的、得胜的。我们是从虚无里出来，不是从神里出来。他就只能是我们造物者，不是我们的父、我们的本源。但如今我们知道，神不能是死人的神——必须是活人的神（the God of the living）；因为知道我们会死，会冻结敬拜的心，我们就不能说“我们的神”，也不能觉他配得我们所能献上的那样敬拜。凡向这活人的神献上自己为祭的、那得胜的、那把自己个别的生命带回源头、知道自己*是*神儿女中的一个、*这*一位父手所造之人的，神就赐他白石。凡攀登他一切神生之努力与神赐之得胜的阶梯、上到他存有的高峰——就是在父怀中面对面瞻望他理想自己之高峰——神的“他”，借长兄的奉献成于父的爱，实现在他里面——神就赐他写着的新名。
但这且搁下，因为接下来的话，以更丰满的真理展开，拥抱并强化了这种关系的个体性。因为这名是“除了那领受的人，没有人能认识的”。那么，不仅每个人与神有个别的关系，而且每个人与神有他独特的关系。他对神是一个独特的存有，按神自己的样式而造、不按任何别人的样式；因为他得完全时，要领受没有别人能明白的新名。因此他能敬拜神，像没有别人能敬拜的那样——能明白神，像没有别人能明白的那样。这人那人也许比他明白神更多、明白得更好，但没有别人能像他那样明白神。神啊，赐我恩典在你面前谦卑，我的弟兄，好叫我不把我对你的幻像拖到那不义之审判官的审判（the judgment）座前，而是仰望你自己，仰望你、且唯独你能给的关于神的启示。

===Original===

As the fir-tree lifts up itself with a far different need from the need of the palm-tree, so does each man stand before God, and lift up a different humanity to the common Father. And for each God has a different response. With every man he has a secret﻿—the secret of the new name. In every man there is a loneliness, an inner chamber of peculiar life into which God only can enter. I say not it is *the innermost chamber*﻿—but a chamber into which no brother, nay, no sister can come.
From this it follows that there is a chamber also﻿—(O God, humble and accept my speech)﻿—a chamber in God himself, into which none can enter but the one, the individual, the peculiar man﻿—out of which chamber that man has to bring revelation and strength for his brethren. This is that for which he was made﻿—to reveal the secret things of the Father.
By his creation, then, each man is isolated with God; each, in respect of his peculiar making, can say, “*my* God”; each can come to him alone, and speak with him face to face, as a man speaketh with his friend. There is no *massing* of men with God. When he speaks of gathered men, it is as a spiritual *body*, not a *mass*. For in a body every smallest portion is individual, and therefore capable of forming a part of the body.
See, now, what a significance the symbolism of our text assumes. Each of us is a distinct flower or tree in the spiritual garden of God﻿—precious, each for his own sake, in the eyes of him who is even now making us﻿—each of us watered and shone upon and filled with life, for the sake of his flower, his completed being, which will blossom out of him at last to the glory and pleasure of the great gardener. For each has within him a secret of the Divinity; each is growing towards the revelation of that secret to himself, and so to the full reception, according to his measure, of the divine. Every moment that he is true to his true self, some new shine of the white stone breaks on his inward eye, some fresh channel is opened upward for the coming glory of the flower, the conscious offering of his whole being in beauty to the Maker. Each man, then, is in God’s sight worth. Life and action, thought and intent, are sacred. And what an end lies before us! To have a consciousness of our own ideal being flashed into us from the thought of God!

===Chinese===

正如冷杉以全然不同于棕榈的需要向上生长，每个人也这样站在神面前，向共同的父举起一种不同的人性。而对每一个，神有一个不同的回应。他与每个人之间有一个秘密——新名的秘密。每个人里面都有一种孤独、一个独特生命的内容，唯独神能进入。我不是说那是*最内的内室*——而是一个任何弟兄、不、任何姊妹都不能进入的内室。
由此推论，神自己里面也有一个内室——（神啊，使我的话谦卑并蒙悦纳）——除了那一位、那个别的人、那独特的人，没有谁能进入的内室——而那人必须从这内室带出启示与力量给他的弟兄。这正是他被造的目的——显明父的隐秘之事。
因着他的被造，每个人就与神单独相对；每一个人，就他独特的受造而言，都能说“*我的*神”；每一个都能单独就近他，与他面对面说话，好像人与朋友说话一般。在神那里没有对人的*堆聚*。他说到聚集的人时，是当作一个属灵的*身体*，不是一个*团块*。因为在身体里，最小的每一部分都是个别的，因此才能构成身体的一部分。
现在看，我们经文的象征具有了怎样的意义。我们每一个人，都是神属灵园子里一株独特的花或树——在正造着我们的他眼中，各因自己的缘故而宝贵——我们每一个人都被浇灌、被照耀、被充满生命，都是为了他的花、他那将要最后从我们里面绽放出来、归给那大园丁的荣耀与喜悦的完全存有。因为每个人里面都怀有神性的一个秘密；每个人都在向着向自己启示那秘密生长，从而按着他的量度，完全领受那属神的。他忠于他真实自己的每一刻，白石就有某道新的光华照在他内里的眼上，就有一条新的通路为那花的将临荣耀向上敞开——他的全存有有意识地以美丽献给造物者。每个人在神眼中就如此有价值。生命与行动、思想与意图，都是神圣的。而摆在我们面前的目标是何等的终点！得着一个从神的思想闪入我们里面的、对我们自己理想存有的意识！

===Original===

Surely for this may well give way all our paltry self-consciousnesses, our self-admirations and self-worships! Surely to know what he thinks about us will pale out of our souls all our thoughts about ourselves! and we may well hold them loosely now, and be ready to let them go. Towards this result St. Paul had already drawn near, when he who had begun the race with a bitter cry for deliverance from the body of his death, was able to say that he judged his own self no longer.
“But is there not the worst of all dangers involved in such teaching﻿—the danger of spiritual pride?” If there be, are we to refuse the spirit for fear of the pride? Or is there any other deliverance from pride except the spirit? Pride springs from supposed success in the high aim: with attainment itself comes humility. But here there is no room for ambition. Ambition is the desire to be above one’s neighbour; and here there is no possibility of comparison with one’s neighbour: no one knows what the white stone contains except the man who receives it. Here is room for endless aspiration towards the unseen ideal; none for ambition. Ambition would only be higher than others; aspiration would be high. Relative worth is not only unknown﻿—to the children of the kingdom it is unknowable. Each esteems the other better than himself. How shall the rose, the glowing heart of the summer heats, rejoice against the snowdrop risen with hanging head from the white bosom of the snow? Both are God’s thoughts; both are dear to him; both are needful to the completeness of his earth and the revelation of himself. “God has cared to make me for himself,” says the victor with the white stone, “and has called me that which I like best; for my own name must be what I would have it, seeing it is myself. What matter whether I be called a grass of the field, or an eagle of the air? a stone to build into his temple, or a Boanerges to wield his thunder? I am his; his idea, his making; perfect in my kind, yea, perfect in his sight; full of him, revealing him, alone with him. Let him call me what he will. The name shall be precious as my life. I seek no more.”
Gone then will be all anxiety as to what his neighbour may think about him. It is enough that God thinks about him. To be something to God﻿—is not that praise enough?

===Chinese===

为了这个，我们一切鄙陋的自我意识、自赏自拜，尽可以让位了！知道他对我们的想法，必使我们一切对自己的想法从灵魂里褪色！我们现在就可以轻握着它们，随时准备放手。圣保罗已经接近了这结果：那以痛苦呼求脱离这取死身体开始那赛程的人，后来竟能说他不再审判自己了。
“但这样的教导岂不包含最坏的危机——属灵骄傲的危机吗？”若有，我们就要因怕骄傲而拒绝那灵吗？除了那灵，还有别的拯救脱离骄傲的途径吗？骄傲生于自以为在高目标上成功：随着真实的达致而来的是谦卑。而在这里没有野心的余地。野心是想高过邻人；而这里根本不可能与邻人比较：除了领受白石的人，没有别人知道白石里是什么。这里有向着未见之理想的无穷升腾的余地；没有野心的余地。野心只想高过别人；升腾只想高。相对的价值不仅无人知晓——对这国（the kingdom）的儿女，它根本不可知。各人看别人比自己强。玫瑰，那夏日炎热的灼灼之心，岂能对着从雪的洁白胸怀里垂头升起的雪滴花夸胜？两者都是神的思想；两者都为他所爱；两者都为他大地的完全、为他自己的启示所必需。“神顾念为我造了我归他自己，”那持白石得胜的说，“又用我最喜欢的称呼我；因为我自己的名必是我所要的，既然它就是我自己。我被称为田间的一棵草、或空中的一只鹰，有什么要紧？被称为砌入他殿的一块石头、或挥动他雷霆的一位雷子，有什么要紧？我是他的；是他的意念、他的造物；在我的类中完全，是的，在他眼中完全；满了他，启示他，与他独处。随他怎样称呼我。这名必如我的生命般宝贵。我别无所求。”
那时，对邻人怎样想他的一切焦虑都消失了。神想着他，这就够了。对神是某样东西——这岂不是够多的称赞？

===Original===

To be a thing that God cares for and would have complete for himself, because it is worth caring for﻿—is not that life enough?
Neither will he thus be isolated from his fellows. For that we say of one, we say of all. It is as *one* that the man has claims amongst his fellows. Each will feel the sacredness and awe of his neighbour’s dark and silent speech with his God. Each will regard the other as a prophet, and look to him for what the Lord hath spoken. Each, as a high priest returning from his Holy of Holies, will bring from his communion some glad tidings, some gospel of truth, which, when spoken, his neighbours shall receive and understand. Each will behold in the other a marvel of revelation, a present son or daughter of the Most High, come forth from him to reveal him afresh. In God each will draw nigh to each.
Yes, there will be danger﻿—danger as everywhere; but he giveth more grace. And if the man who has striven up the heights should yet fall from them into the deeps, is there not that fire of God, the consuming fire, which burneth and destroyeth not?
To no one who has not already had some speech with God, or who has not at least felt some aspiration towards the fount of his being, can all this appear other than foolishness. So be it.
But, Lord, help them and us, and make our being grow into thy likeness. If through ages of strife and ages of growth, yet let us at last see thy face, and receive the white stone from thy hand. That thus we may grow, give us day by day our daily bread. Fill us with the words that proceed out of thy mouth. Help us to lay up *treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt*.

===Chinese===

作一件神顾念、并要为他自己使之完全的东西，因为它配得顾念——这岂不是够多的生命？
他也不会因此与同伴隔绝。因为我们对一个人说的，我们对所有人说。人正是作为*一个*而在同伴中间有他的权利。各人都要感受他邻人与他的神之间那暗而无声之言语的神圣与可畏。各人都要把对方看作先知，仰望他等候主所已说的话。各人像一位从至圣所出来的大祭司，必从他的相通中带出某些好消息、某些真理的福音，一说出来，邻人就要领受并明白。各人都要在对方身上看见一个启示的奇观、至高者眼前的一位儿子或女儿、从他出来、把他重新启示。在神里面，各人要彼此亲近。
是的，会有危险——像处处都有的危险；但他赐更多的恩典。而那奋力登上高峰的人若竟从那里坠入深处，不是还有神的那火、那烈火、那烧而不毁的火吗？
对凡还没有与神有过某种相通、或至少还没有对作他存有之源泉存过某种渴慕的人，这一切只能是愚拙。就这样吧。
但主啊，帮助他们，也帮助我们，使我们的存有长成你的像。纵使要经过争扎的世代、生长的世代，愿我们至终见你的面，从你手中领受白石。为叫我们这样生长，求你日日赐我们日用的饮食。用你口中出的话语充满我们。帮助我们积攒*财宝在天上，那里没有虫子咬、没有锈坏*。

### The Heart with the Treasure / 怀宝之心
===Original===

> Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal. But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

===Chinese===

> 不要为自己积攒财宝在地上，地上有虫子咬、有锈坏，也有贼挖窟窿来偷；只要积攒财宝在天上，天上没有虫子咬、没有锈坏，也没有贼挖窟窿来偷。因为你的财宝在哪里，你的心也在哪里。

===Original===

To understand the words of our Lord is the business of life. For it is the main road to the understanding of The Word himself. And to receive him is to receive the Father, and so to have Life in ourselves. And Life, the higher, the deeper, the simpler, the original, is the business of life.
The Word is that by which we live, namely, Jesus himself; and his words represent, in part, in shadow, in suggestion, himself. Any utterance worthy of being called “a truth,” is human food: how much more “The Word,” presenting no abstract laws of our being, but the vital relation of soul and body, heart and will, strength and rejoicing, beauty and light, to Him who first gave birth to them all! The Son came forth to *be*, before our eyes and in our hearts, that which he had made us for, that we might behold “the truth” in him, and cry out for the living God, who, in the highest sense of all is The Truth, not as understood, but as understanding, living, and being, doing and creating the truth. “I am the truth,” said our Lord; and by those who are in some measure like him in being the truth, the Word can be understood. Let us try to understand him.
Sometimes, no doubt, the Saviour would have spoken after a different *fashion* of speech, if he had come to Englishmen, instead of to Jews. But the lessons he gave would have been the same; for even when questioned about a matter for its passing import, his reply contained the enunciation of the great human principle which lay in it, and *that* lies changeless in every variation of changeful circumstance. With the light of added ages of Christian experience, it ought to be easier for us to understand his words than it was for those who heard him.
What, I ask now, is here the power of his word “For”: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also”? The meaning of the reason thus added is not obvious upon its surface. It has to be sought for because of its depth at once and its simplicity. But it is so complete, so imaginatively comprehensive, so immediately operative on the conscience through its poetic suggestiveness, that when it is once understood, there is nothing more to be said, but everything to be done.
“Why not lay up for ourselves treasures upon earth?”
“Because there the moth and rust and the thief come.”
“And so we should lose those treasures!”
“Yes; by the moth and the rust and the thief.”

===Chinese===

明白我们主的话，是生命的正事。因为这是明白那道（the Word）本身的主要途径。领受他就是领受父（the Father），从而在我们自己里面有生命。而生命——那更高、更深、更单纯、更原本的生命——就是生命的正事。
道就是我们借以活着的那位，即耶稣自己；他的话部分地、以影子、以提示，代表他自己。任何配称“一个真理”的话语，都是人的食物；何况“那道”——它所呈现的，不是我们存有的抽象法则，而是灵魂与身体、心与意志、力量与喜乐、美与光，对那位首先生出这一切者的活泼关系！子出来，要在我们眼前、在我们心中*成为*他造我们为之的那位，好叫我们在他身上看见“真理”，并呼求那活的神——他在一切最高的意义上就是那真理：不是被理解的真理，而是理解着、活着、存有着、行着并创造着真理的那位。“我就是真理，”我们主说；而那在成为真理上有几分像他的人，就能明白这道。让我们努力明白他。
无疑，救主若来到英国人中间，而不是犹太人中间，有时会用不同的言语*方式*说话。但他所给的教训会是一样的；因为即使被人问及一事的暂时意义时，他的回答也总含有其中那伟大人性原则的宣告，而*那原则*在多变环境的一切变迁中恒久不变。加上此后诸世代基督徒经验之光，我们理解他的话，本该比当年听他的人更容易。
现在我要问，这里他这“因为”一词的能力何在：“因为你的财宝在哪里，你的心也在哪里”？这样附加的理由，其意义并不浮在表面。必须因它兼具的深度与单纯而去寻求。但它是如此完全、如此富于想象地周全、如此借着诗意暗示即刻作用于良心，以致一旦明白，就再没有什么可说的，只有一切待行。
“为什么不可为自己积攒财宝在地上呢？”
“因为那里有虫子、锈坏和贼来。”
“那样我们就会失去那些财宝了！”
“是的；被虫子、锈坏和贼夺去。”

===Original===

“Does the Lord then mean that the *reason* for not laying up such treasures is their transitory and corruptible nature?”
“No. He adds a ‘For’: ‘For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.’ ”
“Of course the heart will be where the treasure is; but what has that to do with the argument?”
This: that what is with the treasure must fare as the treasure; that the heart which haunts the treasure-house where the moth and rust corrupt, will be exposed to the same ravages as the treasure, will itself be rusted and moth-eaten.
Many a man, many a woman, fair and flourishing to see, is going about with a rusty moth-eaten heart within that form of strength or beauty.
“But this is only a figure.”
True. But is the reality intended, less or more than the figure? Does not “the rust and the moth” mean more than disease? And does not “the heart” mean more than the heart? Does it not mean a deeper heart, the heart of your own self, not of your body? of the “self” that suffers, not pain, but misery? of the self whose end is not comfort, or enjoyment, but blessedness, yea, ecstasy? a heart which is the inmost chamber wherein springs the divine fountain of your being? a heart which God regards, though you may never have known its existence, not even when its writhings under the gnawing of the moth and the slow fire of the rust have communicated a dull pain to that outer heart which sends the blood to its appointed course through your body? If God sees that heart corroded with the rust of cares, riddled into caverns and films by the worms of ambition and greed, then your heart is as God sees it, for God sees things as they are. And one day you will be compelled to see, nay, to *feel* your heart as God sees it; and to know that the cankered thing which you have within you, a prey to the vilest of diseases, is indeed the centre of your being, your very heart.
Nor does the lesson apply to those only who worship Mammon, who give their lives, their best energies to the accumulation of wealth: it applies to those equally who in any way worship the transitory; who seek the praise of men more than the praise of God; who would make a show in the world by wealth, by taste, by intellect, by power, by art, by genius of any kind, and so would gather golden opinions to be treasured in a storehouse of earth.

===Chinese===

“那么主的意思是，不积攒这类财宝的*理由*，在于它们短暂易朽的本性吗？”
“不是。他加了一个‘因为’：‘因为你的财宝在哪里，你的心也在哪里。’”
“心当然会在财宝那里；可这与论证有什么相干？”
相干在这里：与财宝同在的，必遭逢财宝所遭逢的；那常出入于虫蛀锈坏之宝库的心，必暴露在与财宝同样的毁坏之下，自己也要生锈、被虫蛀。
多少男人、多少女人，外表看来健美兴旺，在那力量或美丽的形体里面，却揣着一颗锈了、虫蛀了的心。
“但这只是一个比喻。”
真的。但所意指的实体，是比这比喻更少还是更多呢？“锈和虫”岂不意味着比疾病更多？“心”岂不意味着比心脏更多？它岂不意味着一颗更深的心，你自己的自我之心，不是你身体之心？那受苦的不是疼痛、而是悲惨的“自我”之心？那以舒适或享乐为终点、而以福乐、是的、以狂喜为终点的自我？一颗作为你最内之内室、你存有之神性源泉从中涌起的心？一颗神所注视的心——尽管你可能从未知道它的存在，甚至当它在虫的啃噬和锈的慢火之下的翻腾，把一种钝痛传给那推动血液循行你身体的外层之心的时候。神若看见那心被忧虑的锈蚀坏，被野心与贪婪的虫蛀成洞穴和薄壳，那你的心就是神所看见的那样，因为神看事物照它们的本相。有一日你将被迫看见、不、*感觉*你的心像神所看见的那样；并知道你里面那溃烂之物、那最卑劣疾病之猎物，确是你存有的中心、你真正的心。
这教训也不单适用于那些拜玛门的、把生命和最好的精力用于积攒财富的人：它同样适用于一切以任何方式敬拜短暂之物的人；那寻求人的称赞过于神的称赞的人；那想借财富、品味、才智、权力、艺术、任何一种天才在世上炫耀、从而把金色的舆论积进一座地上仓房的人。

===Original===

Nor to such only, but surely to those as well whose pleasures are of a more evidently transitory nature still, such as the pleasures of the senses in every direction﻿—whether lawfully or unlawfully indulged, if the joy of being is centred in them﻿—do these words bear terrible warning. For the hurt lies not in this﻿—that these pleasures are false like the deceptions of magic, for such they are not: pleasures they are; nor yet in this﻿—that they pass away, and leave a fierce disappointment behind: that is only so much the better; but the hurt lies in this﻿—that the immortal, the infinite, created in the image of the everlasting God, is housed with the fading and the corrupting, and clings to them as its good﻿—clings to them till it is infected and interpenetrated with their proper diseases, which assume in it a form more terrible in proportion to the superiority of its kind, that which is mere decay in the one becoming moral vileness in the other, that which fits the one for the dunghill casting the other into the outer darkness; creeps, that it may share with them, into a burrow in the earth, where its budded wings wither and damp and drop away from its shoulders, instead of haunting the open plains and the high-uplifted tablelands, spreading abroad its young pinions to the sun and the air, and strengthening them in further and further flights, till at last they should become strong to bear the God-born into the presence of its Father in Heaven. Therein lies the hurt.
He whose heart is sound because it haunts the treasure-house of heaven may *be tempted of the devil*, but will be first *led up of the Spirit into the wilderness*.

===Chinese===

也不单适用于这些人，同样也适用于那些喜乐显然更属短暂性质的人，就是那些感官之乐的人——无论放纵得合法还是不合法，只要存有的喜乐以它们为中心——这些话都带着可怕的警告。因为伤害不在于——这些快乐像魔术的骗局一样是假的，因为它们并非如此：它们是快乐；也不在于——它们会过去，留下惨烈的失望：那倒反而更好；伤害乃在于——那不朽的、无限的、按永生神形象所造的，竟与易凋与朽坏者同住一处，并以它们为它的善——紧抓着它们，直到被它们特有的疾病感染浸透；这些疾病在它里面取得的形式，按其种类之优越而愈加可怕：在一边不过是腐朽的东西，在另一边成了道德的卑劣；使一边只配堆肥的东西，把另一边抛进了外边黑暗（the outer darkness）；它为要与它们同分，爬进地里的一个洞穴，它初萌的翅膀在肩上枯萎、潮湿、脱落，而不是出没于开阔的平原和高耸的台地，把年轻的翅膀向太阳和空气张开，在越飞越远的翱翔中强健它们，直到它们终于强壮到足以背负这神生之子进入他天父面前。伤害就在这里。
那心因常出入天上宝库而健全的人，可能*被魔鬼试探*，却必先*被圣灵引到旷野*。

### The Temptation in the Wilderness / 旷野的试探
===Original===

> Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness, to be tempted of the devil. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungered. And when the tempter came to him, he said, if thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread. But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple, and saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down; for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee, and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone. Jesus said unto him, It is written again, thou shall not tempt the Lord thy God. Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and showeth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them: and saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me. Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan; for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Then the devil leaveth him; and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.

===Chinese===

> 当时，耶稣被圣灵引到旷野，受魔鬼的试探。他禁食四十昼夜，后来就饿了。那试探人的进前来，对他说：你若是神的儿子，可以吩咐这些石头变成食物。耶稣却回答说：经上记着说：人活着，不是单靠食物，乃是靠神口里所出的一切话。魔鬼就带他进了圣城，叫他站在殿顶上，对他说：你若是神的儿子，可以跳下去，因为经上记着说：主要为你吩咐他的使者用手托着你，免得你的脚碰在石头上。耶稣对他说：经上又记着说：不可试探主你的神。魔鬼又带他上了一座极高的山，将世上的万国与万国的荣华都指给他看，对他说：你若俯伏拜我，我就把这一切都赐给你。耶稣说：撒但，退去吧！因为经上记着说：当拜主你的神，单要事奉他。于是魔鬼离了耶稣，有天使来伺候他。

===Original===

This narrative must have one of two origins. Either it is an invention, such as many tales told of our Lord in the earlier periods of Christianity; or it came from our Lord himself, for, according to the story, except the wild beasts, of earthly presence there was none at his Temptation.
As to the former of the two origins: The story bears upon it no sign of human invention. The man who could see such things as are here embodied, dared not invent such an embodiment for them. To one in doubt about the matter it will be helpful, I think, to compare this story with the best of those for which one or other of the apocryphal gospels is our only authority﻿—say the grand account of the Descent into Hell in the Gospel according to Nicodemus.
If it have not this origin, there is but the other that it can have﻿—Our Lord himself. To this I will return presently.
And now, let us approach the subject from another side.
With this in view, I ask you to think how much God must know of which we know nothing. Think what an abyss of truth was our Lord, out of whose divine darkness, through that revealing countenance, that uplifting voice, those hands whose tenderness has made us great, broke all holy radiations of human significance. Think of his understanding, imagination, heart, in which lay the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Must he not have known, felt, imagined, rejoiced in things that would not be told in human words, could not be understood by human hearts? Was he not always bringing forth out of the light inaccessible? Was not his very human form a veil hung over the face of the truth that, even in part by dimming the effulgence of the glory, it might reveal? What could be conveyed must be thus conveyed: an infinite More must lie behind. And even of those things that might be partially revealed to men, could he talk to his Father and talk to his disciples in altogether the same forms, in altogether the same words? Would what he said to God on the mountaintops, in the dim twilight or the gray dawn, never be such that his disciples could have understood it no more than the people, when the voice of God spoke to him from heaven, could distinguish that voice from the inarticulate thunderings of the element?
There is no attempt made to convey to us even the substance of the battle of those forty days.

===Chinese===

这段记述必有两个来源之一。要么它是一种虚构，像基督教早期流传的许多关于我们主的故事；要么它出于我们主自己，因为照故事所记，他的受试探，除了野兽，没有任何属地的在场者。
至于两个来源中的前者：这故事身上没有任何人工虚构的痕迹。能看见此处所体现之事物的人，不敢为它们编造这样一个体现。对这事存疑的人，我想，把这故事与那些唯以某卷旁经福音书为据的最佳故事比较一下，会有帮助——比如《尼哥底母福音》里那篇下到阴间的宏伟记述。
它若不是这个来源，就只能有另一个——我们主自己。这点我稍后回来说。
现在，让我们从另一面接近这主题。
为此，我请你们思想：神所知道的、我们所不知道的，必有多少。想想我们的主曾是何等一个真理的深渊——从他那神性的幽暗里，透过那启示的面容、那激励人的声音、那双手——它们的温柔使我们成为尊大——迸发出一切人性意义的圣洁光辉。想想他的悟性、想象、心，其中藏着智慧与知识的宝藏。他岂不必然知道、感受、想象、并喜乐于那些不能以人言讲述、不能为人心明白的事？他岂不是一直在从那不可靠近之光中带出东西来？他那属人的形体本身，岂不就是一幅蒙在真理面上的幔子——甚至要借部分地柔化那荣耀的强光来启示？能传递的必这样传递：无限的“更多”必藏在背后。而即使是那些可以部分向人启示的事，他对他父说话与他门徒说话，能用完全相同的形式、完全相同的言辞吗？他在山巅上、在朦胧的黄昏或灰白的黎明对神所说的，难道永不会像神从天上对他说话时那样——百姓分辨不出那声音与元素的含混雷声——是他的门徒也同样不能明白的吗？
那四十日争战的内容本身，甚至都没有尝试传达给我们。

===Original===

Such a conflict of spirit as for forty days absorbed all the human necessities of *The Man* in the cares of the Godhead could not be rendered into forms intelligible to us, or rather, could not be in itself intelligible to us, and therefore could not take any form of which we could lay hold. It is not till the end of those forty days that the divine event begins to dawn out from the sacred depths of the eternal thought, becomes human enough to be made to appear, admits of utterance, becomes capable of being spoken in human forms to the ears of men, though yet only in a dark saying, which he that hath ears to hear may hear, and he that hath a heart to understand may understand. For the mystery is not left behind, nor can the speech be yet clear unto men.
At the same moment when the approaching event comes within human ken, may from afar be dimly descried by the God-upheld intelligence, the same humanity seizes on the Master, and he is an hungered. The first sign that he has come back to us, that the strife is approaching its human result, is his hunger. On what a sea of endless life do we float, are our poor necessities sustained﻿—not the poorest of them dissociated from the divine! Emerging from the storms of the ocean of divine thought and feeling into the shallower waters that lave the human shore, bearing with him the treasures won in the strife, our Lord is straightway an hungered; and from this moment the temptation is human, and can be in some measure understood by us.
But could it even then have been conveyed to the human mind in merely intellectual forms? Or, granting that it might, could it be so conveyed to those who were only beginning to have the vaguest, most error-mingled and confused notions about our Lord and what he came to do? No. The inward experiences of our Lord, such as could be conveyed to them at all, could be conveyed to them only in a parable. For far plainer things than these, our Lord chose this form. The form of the parable is the first in which truth will admit of being embodied. Nor is this all: it is likewise the fullest; and to the parable will the teacher of the truth ever return.

===Chinese===

这样一场灵里的冲突——四十天之久，把*那人*一切属人的必需都吸进神性的挂虑之中——不可能被表达为我们能懂的形态；或者说，它本身对我们就是不可懂的，因此不可能取得任何我们能把握的形态。直到那四十日的末了，那属神的事件才开始从永恒思想的圣洁深处破晓而出，变得够属人而可以显现、可以言说、可以用人的形态向人的耳朵述说——尽管还只是在一个暗喻里，有耳可听的可以听，有心可懂的可以懂。因为奥秘并未被抛在后面，那言语对人还不能清楚。
就在那临近的事件进入人的认识范围、被神所扶持的悟性远远隐约望见的同一时刻，同样的人性抓住了主，他就饿了。他已回到我们这里的第一个记号、争战临近其人性结果的第一个记号，就是他的饥饿。我们漂浮在怎样一片无尽生命的海上，我们贫乏的必需怎样得着供养——连其中最贫乏的也不与属神的分离！我们的主从神性思想与感受之大洋的风暴中浮现出来，进入冲刷人性之岸的浅水，带着他在争战中赢得的珍宝，随即就饿了；从这一刻起，试探是属人的，能被我们部分地明白了。
但即便那时，它能仅以智性的形态传达给人的心思吗？或者，即使能，它能这样传达给那些对我们主和他来要作的事、刚开始有最模糊、最掺杂错误、最混乱观念的人吗？不能。我们主的内在经历，凡能传达给他们的，只能以一个比喻传达。对比这些远为浅显的事，我们主尚且选用这形式。比喻的形式，是真理最先容许自己被体现于其中的形式。还不止此：它也是最丰满的形式；而真理的教师永远要回到比喻。

===Original===

Is he who asserts that the passage contains a simple narrative of actual events, prepared to believe, as the story, so interpreted, indubitably gives us to understand, that a visible demon came to our Lord and, himself the prince of worldly wisdom, thought, by quoting Scripture after the manner of the priests, to persuade a good man to tempt God; thought, by the promise of power, to prevail upon him to cast aside every claim he had upon the human race, in falling down and worshipping one whom he knew to be the adversary of Truth, of Humanity, of God? How could Satan be so foolish? or, if Satan might be so foolish, wherein could such temptation so presented have tempted our Lord? and wherein would a victory over such be a victory for the race?
Told as a parable, it is as full of meaning as it would be bare if received as a narrative.
Our Lord spake then this parable unto them, and so conveyed more of the truth with regard to his temptation in the wilderness, than could have been conveyed by any other form in which the truth he wanted to give them might have been embodied. Still I do not think it follows that we have it exactly as he told it to his disciples. A man will hear but what he can hear, will see but what he can see, and, telling the story again, can tell but what he laid hold of, what he seemed to himself to understand. His effort to reproduce the impression made upon his mind will, as well as the impression itself, be liable to numberless altering, modifying, even, in a measure, discomposing influences. But it does not, therefore, follow that the reproduction is false. The mighty hosts of life-bearing worlds, requiring for the freedom of their courses, and the glory of their changes, such awful abysses of space, dwindle in the human eye to seeds of light sown upon a blue plain. How faint in the ears of man is the voice of their sphere-born thunder of adoration! Yet are they lovely indeed, uttering speech and teaching knowledge. So this story may not be just as the Lord told it, and yet may contain in its mirror as much of the truth as we are able to receive, and as will afford us sufficient scope for a life’s discovery. The modifying influences of the human channels may be essential to God’s revealing mode. It is only by seeing them first from afar that we learn the laws of the heavens.

===Chinese===

那断言这段经文是对实际事件之单纯记述的人，可曾准备好相信——如这故事照那样解释所无疑要我们明白的——一个看得见的魔鬼来到我们主面前，身为属世智慧之君，竟想照祭司们的样子引用圣经，劝一个好人去试探神；想借权能的应许，劝服他抛开他对人类的一切权利，俯伏敬拜一位他明知是真理之敌、人类之敌、神之敌的？撒但怎么会这样愚蠢？或者，撒但即使可以这样愚蚌，这样一个呈现出来的试探又在哪里能试探我们的主？而胜过这样一个试探，又在哪里是全族的一场胜利？
作为一个比喻来讲，它意味丰满；若当作记事来领受，它便意味全失。
我们主于是对他们讲了这比喻，从而关于他旷野受试探的真理，他所要给他们的，以这形式比任何别的形式传达得都多。但我仍不认为，我们手里这故事就精确是他讲给门徒时的样子。人只能听见他所能听的，只能看见他所能看的；再讲这故事时，只能讲出他所把握的、他自己以为明白的。他重现心中印象的努力，与那印象本身一样，容易受无数改变、修改、甚至在某种程度上扰乱的影响。但由此并不能推出那重现是虚假的。那载着生命的大军——众世界，为了它们运行的白由与其变化的荣耀，需要何等可畏的空间深渊——在人眼里缩成撒在蓝色平原上的光的种子。它们那随球而生的敬拜雷声，在人耳中何其微弱！然而它们确实可爱，“发出言语，传扬知识”。照样，这故事可以不像主讲的原样，却仍可以在它的镜子里含着我们所能领受的那么多真理，足以供我们一生的发现。人之渠道的这些修改影响，可能正是神启示方式的必需。我们唯有先从远处看见诸天，才能学习诸天的律法。

===Original===

And now arises the question upon the right answer to which depends the whole elucidation of the story: *How could the Son of God be tempted*?
If anyone say that he was not moved by those temptations, he must be told that then they were no temptations to him, and he was not tempted; nor was his victory of more significance than that of the man who, tempted to bear false witness against his neighbour, abstains from robbing him of his goods. For human need, struggle, and hope, it bears no meaning; and we must reject the whole as a fantastic folly of crude invention; a mere stage-show; a lie for the poor sake of the fancied truth; a doing of evil that good might come; and, with how many fragments soever of truth its mud may be filled, not in any way to be received as a divine message.
But asserting that these were real temptations if the story is to be received at all, am I not involving myself in a greater difficulty still? For how could the Son of God be tempted with evil﻿—with that which must to him appear in its true colours of discord, its true shapes of deformity? Or how could he then be the Son of his Father who cannot be tempted with evil?
In the answer to this lies the centre, the essential germ of the whole interpretation: He was not tempted with Evil but with Good; with inferior forms of good, that is, pressing in upon him, while the higher forms of good held themselves aloof, biding their time, that is, God’s time. I do not believe that the Son of God could be tempted with evil, but I do believe that he could be tempted with good﻿—to yield to which temptation would have been evil in him﻿—ruin to the universe. But does not all evil come from good?
Yes; but it has come *from* it. It is no longer good. A good corrupted is no longer a good. Such could not tempt our Lord. Revenge may originate in a sense of justice, but it is revenge not justice; an evil thing, for it would be fearfully unjust. Evil is evil whatever it may have come from. The Lord could not have felt tempted to take vengeance upon his enemies, but he might have felt tempted to destroy the wicked from the face of the earth﻿—to destroy them from the face of the earth, I say, not to destroy them forever. To that I do not think he could have felt tempted.
But we shall find illustration enough of what I mean in the matter itself.

===Chinese===

现在产生一个问题，对它的正确回答系着整个故事的阐明：*神的儿子怎能被试探*？
若有人说他没有被动于那些试探，就必须告诉他：那样它们对他就不是试探，他也没有受试探；他的胜利也不比那受试探要作伪证害邻舍、却克制不抢他财物之人的胜利更有意义。对人的需要、争扎与盼望，它毫无意义；我们就必须把整个故事当作粗劣虚构的荒唐物加以拒绝；一场舞台表演；为想象的真理之可怜缘故而说的谎；作恶以求善成；而且无论它的泥里塞着多少真理的碎片，绝不可当作属神的信息来领受。
但既断言这些若是真试探故事才可领受，我不是让自己陷入一个更大的难题吗？因为神的儿子怎能被恶试探——被那在他眼中必显出其冲突本色、其畸形真形的东西试探？那样他又怎能是不能被恶试探之父的儿子？
答案里藏着整个解释的中心、本质的胚芽：他不是被恶试探，而是被善试探；被较低形式的善，就是说，在他身上施压，而较高形式的善却持身远引、静候其时——即神的时辰。我不信神的儿子能被恶试探，但我信他能被善试探——而向这试探屈服，在他就是恶——是宇宙的毁灭。但一切恶岂不都出于善吗？
是的；但它已经*从*善里出来了。它不再是善。被腐化的善不再是善。这样的东西不能试探我们的主。报复可能源于正义感，但它是报复不是正义；是恶物，因为它会可怕地不义。恶就是恶，无论它从什么出来。主不可能受试探要向仇敌复仇，但他可能受试探要把恶人从地上除灭——我说，从地面上除灭，不是永远除灭。对后者我不认为他会受试探。
但我们将在事情本身中找到足够的例证。

===Original===

Let us look at the individual temptations represented in the parable.
The informing idea which led to St. Matthew’s arrangement seems to me superior to that showing itself in St. Luke’s. In the two accounts, the closes, while each is profoundly significant, are remarkably different.
Now let us follow St. Matthew’s record.
And we shall see how the devil tempted him *to* evil, but not *with* evil.
First, He was hungry, and the devil said, “Make bread of this stone.”
The Lord had been fasting for forty days﻿—a fast impossible except during intense mental absorption. Let no one think to glorify this fast by calling it miraculous. Wonderful such fasts are on record on the part of holy men; and inasmuch as the Lord was more of a man than his brethren, insomuch might he be farther withdrawn in the depths of his spiritual humanity from the outer region of his physical nature. So much the slower would be the goings on of that nature; and fasting in his case might thus be extended beyond the utmost limits of similar fasts in others. This, I believe, was all﻿—and this all infinite in its relations. This is the grandest, simplest, and most significant, and, therefore, the divinest way of regarding his fast. Hence, at the end of the forty days, it was not hunger alone that made food tempting to him, but that exhaustion of the whole system, wasting itself all the time it was forgotten, which, reacting on the mind when the mind was already worn out with its own tension, must have deadened it so, that (speaking after the experience of his brethren, which alone will explain his), it could for the time see or feel nothing of the spiritual, and could only *believe in* the unfelt, the unseen. What a temptation was here! There is no sin in wishing to eat; no sin in procuring food honestly that one may eat. But it rises even into an awful duty, when a man knows that to eat will restore the lost vision of the eternal; will, operating on the brain, and thence on the mind, render the man capable of hope as well as of faith, of gladness as well as of confidence, of praise as well as of patience. Why then should he not eat? Why should he not put forth the power that was in him that he might eat? Because such power was his, not to take care of himself, but to work the work of him that sent him.

===Chinese===

让我们看比喻中所代表的各次试探。
导致圣马太那种排列顺序的主导观念，在我看来优于圣路加所显出的。两个记载的收尾，虽各有深意，却显著不同。
现在让我们跟随圣马太的记述。
我们将看见魔鬼怎样引他*向*恶，却不是*用*恶。
第一，他饿了，魔鬼说：“吩咐这些石头变成食物。”
主已经禁食了四十天——除非在极深的心神专注中，这样的禁食是不可能的。谁也不要想把这禁食称作神迹来荣耀它。圣徒们有记载在案的可惊叹的类似禁食；而既然主比他的弟兄更是人，他就更能在他的属灵人性深处，远离他生理本性的外层区域。那样，那本性的运行就愈发缓慢；他身上的禁食便可能超过别人类似禁食的极限。我相信，这就是全部——而这一“全部”在其诸般关系上是无限的。这是看他禁食的最宏大、最单纯、最有意义、因而也最属神的方式。因此，四十天末了，使他觉得食物可慕的，不只是饥饿，而是整个系统的耗竭——它一直在被忘记中消耗自己——当心神已被自身的紧张耗尽时，这耗竭反作用于心神，必使它如此麻木，以致（照他弟兄们的经历来说——唯有这能解释他的经历），它一时对属灵之事看不见、感觉不到什么，只能*信*那未感到、未看见的。这是何等的试探！想吃没有罪；诚实获取食物来吃没有罪。而当一个人知道，吃能恢复那失去的永恒异象，能作用于大脑、进而作用于心神，使人重新能盼望如能信心、能喜乐如能笃定、能赞美如能忍耐时——这甚至升华为一个可畏的本分。那他为什么不 吃？为什么不运用他里面的能力、好使自己得吃？因为这能力属于他，不是为照顾自己，而是为作那差他来者的工。

===Original===

Such power was his not even to honour his Father save as his Father chose to be honoured, who is far more honoured in the ordinary way of common wonders, than in the extraordinary way of miracles. Because it was God’s business to take care of him, his to do what the Father told him to do. To make that stone bread would be to take the care out of the Father’s hands, and turn the divinest thing in the universe into the merest commonplace of self-preservation.
And in nothing was he to be beyond his brethren, save in faith. No refuge for him, any more than for them, save in the love and care of the Father. Other refuge, let it be miraculous power or what you will, would be but hell to him. God is refuge. God is life. “Was he not to eat when it came in his way? And did not the bread come in his way, when his power met that which could be changed into it?”
Regard that word “changed.” The whole matter lies in that. Changed from what? From what God had made it. Changed into what? Into what he did not make it. Why changed? Because the Son was hungry, and the Father would not feed him with food convenient for him! The Father did not give him a stone when he asked for bread. It was Satan that brought the stone and told him to provide for himself. The Father said, That is a stone. The Son would not say, That is a loaf. No one creative *fiat* shall contradict another. The Father and the Son are of one mind. The Lord could hunger, could starve, but would not change into another thing what his Father had made one thing.1
If we regard the answer he gave the devil, we shall see the root of the matter at once: “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” Yea even by the word which made that stone that stone. Everything is all right. It is life indeed for him to leave that a stone, which the Father had made a stone. It would be death to him to alter one word that He had spoken.
“Man shall not live by bread alone.” There are other ways of living besides that which comes by bread. A man will live by the word of God, by what God says to him, by what God means between Him and him, by the truths of being which the Father alone can reveal to his child, by the communion of love between them. Without the bread he will die, as men say; but he will not find that he dies.

===Chinese===

这能力属于他，甚至不是用来尊荣他的父——除非照他父所选定的方式被尊荣；父在寻常平常的奇事里所受的尊荣，远多于在非凡的神迹方式里。因为照顾他是神的事，他的事是行父所告诉他的。把那石头变成食物，就是把照顾从父手里夺过来，把宇宙中最属神的事变成最平庸的自保。
他在任何事上都不该越过他的弟兄，除了在信心上。他没有避难所——和他们一样没有——除了父的爱与照顾。别的避难所，无论是行神迹的权能还是别的什么，对他都无非地狱。神就是避难所。神就是生命。“食物来到他面前时，他不是可以吃吗？而他的能力既遇见可以变成食物的东西，食物岂不就来到他面前了吗？”
细想“变成”这个词。整个关键就在这里。从什么变成？从神所造的那个东西。变成什么？变成他没有造的那个东西。为什么要变？因为子饿了，而父不愿用适合他的食物喂他！父在他求饼时没有给他石头。是撒但拿来石头、叫他自谋生计的。父说，那是石头。子不会说，那是一个面包。没有一个创造的*命令*当与另一个矛盾。父与子同心一意。主可以饥饿，可以饿死，却不肯把他父造为一物的东西变成另一物。1
我们若看他给魔鬼的回答，就会立刻看见问题的根：“人活着，不是单靠食物，乃是靠神口里所出的一切话。”是的，甚至靠那造这石头为石头的道。一切都是对的。让父所造为石头的仍作石头，这对他就是真实的生命。改动他已说的一个字，对他就是死亡。
“人活着，不是单靠食物。”除了靠食物而来的，还有别的活法。人要靠神的道而活，靠神对他说的话，靠神在他与他自己之间的意思，靠唯有父能向他孩子启示的存有的诸真理，靠他们之间爱的相通。没有饼，他会死，如人们所说；但他将发现自己并没有死。

===Original===

He will only find that the tent which hid the stars from him is gone, and that he can see the heavens; or rather, the earthly house will melt away from around him, and he will find that he has a palace-home about him, another and loftier word of God clothing upon him. So the man lives by the word of God even in refusing the bread which God does not give him, for, instead of dying because he does not eat, he rises into a higher life even of the same kind.
For I have been speaking of the consciousness of existence, and not of that higher spiritual life on which all other life depends. That of course can for no one moment exist save from the heart of God. When a man tries to live by bread and not by the word that comes out of that heart of God, he may think he lives, but he begins to die or is dead. Our Lord says, “I can do without the life that comes of bread: without the life that comes of the word of my Father, I die indeed.” Therefore he does not think twice about the matter. That God’s will be done is all his care. That done, all will be right, and all right with him, whether he thinks about himself or not. For the Father does not forget the child who is so busy trusting in him, that he cares not even to pray for himself.
In the higher aspect of this first temptation, arising from the fact that a man cannot feel the things he believes except under certain conditions of physical well-being dependent upon food, the answer is the same: A man does not live by his feelings any more than by bread, but by the Truth, that is, the Word, the Will, the uttered Being of God.
I am even ashamed to yield here to the necessity of writing what is but as milk for babes, when I would gladly utter, if I might, only that which would be as bread for men and women. What I must say is this: that, by *the Word of God*, I do not understand *The Bible*. The Bible is *a* Word of God, the chief of his written words, because it tells us of The Word, the Christ; but everything God has done and given man to know is a word of his, a will of his; and inasmuch as it is a will of his, it is a necessity to man, without which he cannot live: the reception of it is man’s life. For inasmuch as God’s utterances are a whole, every smallest is essential: he speaks no foolishness﻿—there are with him no vain repetitions.

But by *the word* of the God and not Maker only, who is God just because he *speaks* to men, I must understand, in the deepest sense, every revelation of Himself in the heart and consciousness of man, so that the man knows that God is there, nay, rather, that he is here. Nor, moreover, can the man know that any one of them is the word of God, save as it comes thus to him, is a revelation of God in him. It is *to* him that it may be *in* him; but till it is *in* him he cannot *know* that it was *to* him. God must be God *in* man before man can know that he is God, or that he has received aright, and for that for which it was spoken, any one of his words.2
If, by any will of God﻿—that is, any truth in him﻿—we live, we live by it tenfold when that will has become a word to us. When we receive it, his will becomes our will, and so we live by God. It is the Truth itself, that which God is, known by what goeth out of his mouth, that man lives by. And when he can no longer *feel* the truth, he shall not therefore die. He lives because God is true; and he is able to know that he lives because he knows, having once understood the word, that God is truth. He believes in the God of former vision, lives by that word therefore, when all is dark and there is no vision.

而*道*——属于那位不仅是造物者、更是神的；他正是因向人*说话*才是神——在最深的意义上，我必须理解为他在人心与意识中对自我的每一个启示，以致那人知道神在那里，不、更确切地说，他在这里。连基督自己，在最深的意义上也不是*对一个人*而言的神之道，直到他成为神对这人的启示——直到作为道中之意的那灵临到他——直到那言语不是雷鸣之声，而是话语的声音；因为一个字（道）不只是一个发声——它是一个当被理解的声音。我说，没有一句话在成为*对*人的道之前，是完全的神之道——直到人在其中认出神。这正是话说出来的目的。神的话如沙如星——不能数算；但一切和每一个的终点都是这个——启示神。而且，人也不能知道它们中任何一个是神的话，除非它这样临到他、是神在他里面的一个启示。它是*对*他的，好成为*在*他里面的；但在它*在*他里面之前，他不能*知道*它曾是*对*他的。神必须先*在*人里面作神，人才能知道他是神，才知道自己已正确地、按那话被说的目的领受了它的任何一句。2
我们若靠神的任何旨意——即他里面的任何真理——活着，当那旨意成为对我们说的道时，我们就十倍地靠它活。我们领受它时，他的旨意成为我们的旨意，这样我们就靠神活着。但神的道一旦被明白，人就必须靠对神之所是的信心而活，而不是靠自己的感觉——即使对神的感觉。人靠以活着的，是真理本身，是神之所是，借他口中所出的而被认识。当他不再能*感觉*真理时，他也不会因此死。他活着，因为神是真的；他能知道自己活着，因为他既已明白了那道，就知道神是真理。他信那曾显现之神，因此在全然黑暗、没有异象时，靠那道活着。

For thou knowest thou dost not look like what thou sayest thou art.”
Again, with a written word, in return, the Lord meets him. And he does not quote the scripture for logical purposes﻿—to confute Satan intellectually, but as giving even Satan the reason of his conduct. Satan quotes Scripture as a verbal authority; our Lord meets him with a Scripture by the truth in which he regulates his conduct.
If we examine it, we shall find that this answer contains the same principle as the former, namely this, that to the Son of God the will of God is Life. It was a temptation to show the powers of the world that he was the Son of God; that to him the elements were subject; that he was above the laws of Nature, because he was the Eternal Son; and thus stop the raging of the heathen, and the vain imaginations of the people. It would be but to show them the truth. But he was the *Son* of God: what was his *Father’s* will? Such was not the divine way of convincing the world of sin, of righteousness, of judgment. If the Father told him to cast himself down, that moment the pinnacle pointed naked to the sky. If the devil threw him down, let God send his angels; or, if better, allow him to be dashed to pieces in the valley below. But never will he forestall the divine will. The Father shall order what comes next. The Son will obey. In the path of his work he will turn aside for no stone. There let the angels bear him in their hands if need be. But he will not choose the path because there is a stone in it. He will not choose at all. He will go where the Spirit leads him.
I think this will throw some light upon the words of our Lord, “If ye have faith and doubt not, if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.” Good people, amongst them John Bunyan, have been tempted to tempt the Lord their God upon the strength of this saying, just as Satan sought to tempt our Lord on the strength of the passage he quoted from the Psalms. Happily for such, the assurance to which they would give the name of faith generally fails them in time. Faith is that which, knowing the Lord’s will, goes and does it; or, not knowing it, stands and waits, content in ignorance as in knowledge, because God wills; neither pressing into the hidden future, nor careless of the knowledge which opens the path of action.

我们若细察，就会发现这回答含有与前一回答相同的原则，即：对神的儿子，神的旨意就是生命。这是一个试探：要向世上的权势显明他是神的儿子；万有都服他；他在自然律之上，因为他是永恒之子；从而止息外邦的愤怒和民的谋算虚妄的事。那不过是向他们显明真理。但他是神的*子*：他*父*的旨意是什么？那不是神说服世界知罪、知义（righteousness）、知审判的属神方式。父若吩咐他跳下去，那一刻殿尖便赤裸裸地指向天空。魔鬼若把他扔下去，就让神差遣使者；或者，若更好的话，容他在下面谷中摔得粉碎。但他绝不抢先于神的旨意。下一步由父吩咐。子要顺服（obedience）。在工作的路上，他不因任何石头拐弯。在那里，若有需要，就让使者用手托住他。但他不会因为路上有一块石头而选择那条路。他根本不作选择。圣灵引他到哪里，他就到哪里。
我想这会照亮我们主的话：“你们若有信心，不疑惑，对这座山说：挪开此地，投在海里，也必成就。”好人，其中包括约翰·班扬（Bunyan），曾受试探要凭这话的力量试探主他们的神，正如撒但想凭他从诗篇引的那段经文试探我们主。所幸，他们愿称之为信心的那把握，总是及时失效。信心（faith）就是那知道主旨意就去行出来的；或者，不知道时，就站着等候，在无知中如在知识中一样知足，因为神愿意；既不闯入隐藏的未来，也不轻忽那开启行动之路的知识。

It is its noblest exercise to act with uncertainty of the result, when the duty itself is certain, or even when a course seems with strong probability to be duty.3 But to put God to the question in any other way than by saying, What wilt thou have me to do? is an attempt to compel God to declare himself, or to hasten his work. This probably was the sin of Judas. It is presumption of a kind similar to the making of a stone into bread. It is, as it were, either a forcing of God to act where he has created no need for action, or the making of a case wherein he shall seem to have forfeited his word if he does not act. The man is therein dissociating himself from God so far that, instead of acting by the divine will from within, he acts in God’s face, as it were, to see what he will do. Man’s first business is, “What does God want me to do?” not “What will God do if I do so-and-so?” To tempt a parent after the flesh in such a manner would be impertinence: to tempt God so is the same vice in its highest form﻿—a natural result of that condition of mind which is worse than all the so-called cardinal sins, namely, spiritual pride, which attributes the tenderness and love of God not to man’s being and man’s need, but to some distinguishing excellence in the individual himself, which causes the Father to love him better than his fellows, and so pass by his faults with a smile. Not thus did the Son of God regard his relation to his Father. The faith which will remove mountains is that confidence in God which comes from seeking nothing but his will. A man who was thus faithful would die of hunger sooner than say to the stone, “Be bread”; would meet the scoffs of the unbelieving without reply and with apparent defeat, sooner than say to the mountain, “Be thou cast into the sea,” even if he knew that it would be torn from its foundations at the word, except he knew first that God would have it so.
And thus I am naturally brought to consider more fully how this should be a real temptation to the Son of Man. It would be good to confound his adversaries; to force conviction upon them that he was the God-supported messenger he declared himself. Why should he have Adversaries a moment longer to interfere between him and the willing hearts which would believe if they could?

当本分本身确定、甚至当一条路线极可能是本分时，怀着对结果的不确定而行动，是信心最高贵的运用。3但以任何别的方式向神提问——不是问“你要我做什么？”——就是企图强逼神表明自己，或催促他的工。这大概就是犹大（Judas）的罪。这是一种与把石头变成食物相似的擅专。它或者是强逼神在他没有创造行动需要的地方行动，或者是制造一个若他不行动就好像失信的案子。人在其中与神分离到这样的地步：不是从里面凭属神的旨意行动，而是当着神的面行动，仿佛要看他会做什么。人的第一本分是：“神要我做什么？”不是“我若这样那样做，神会做什么？”照这样试探肉身的父母是失礼：照这样试探神，是同一恶习的最高形式——那种比一切所谓七宗大罪更坏的心境的自然结果，即属灵的骄傲：它把神的温柔慈爱不归于人的存有与人的需要，而归于个人自己某种出众的优异，以为是它使父爱他胜过爱同伴，从而含笑放过他的过失。神的儿子不是这样看他与父的关系的。能移山的信心，是那种无所求、唯独神旨意的对神的信靠。这样忠信的人宁可饿死，也不对石头说“变饼”；宁可受不信者的嘲笑而不还口、看似失败，也不对山说“投在海里”——即使他知道一出口它就会被连根拔起——除非他先知道神要它如此。
这样，我就自然地被引到更全面地思想：这怎能对人子是一个真实的试探。使他的对头们羞惭混乱，迫使他们确信他就是自己宣称的那位神所扶持的使者，那岂不好？他的对头们为什么还该多留一刻，拦在他与那些若能就愿信的甘心人心之间？

The answer to all this was plain to our Lord, and is plain to us now: It was not the way of the Father’s will. It would not fall in with that gradual development of life and history by which the Father works, and which must be the way to breed free, God-loving wills. It would be violent, theatrical, therefore poor in nature and in result﻿—not Godlike in any way. Everything in God’s doing comes harmoniously with and from all the rest. Son of Man, his history shall be a man’s history, shall be The Man’s history. Shall that begin with an exception? Yet it might well be a temptation to Him who longed to do all he could for men. He was the Son of God: why should not the sons of God know it?
But as this temptation in the wilderness was an epitome and type of the temptations to come, against which for forty days he had been making himself strong, revolving truth beyond our reach, in whose light every commonest duty was awful and divine, a vision fit almost to oppress a God in his humiliation, so we shall understand the whole better if we look at his life in relation to it. As he refused to make stones bread, so throughout that life he never wrought a miracle to help himself; as he refused to cast himself from the temple to convince Satan or glory visibly in his Sonship, so he steadily refused to give the sign which the human Satans demanded, notwithstanding the offer of conviction which they held forth to bribe him to the grant. How easy it seems to have confounded them, and strengthened his followers! But such conviction would stand in the way of a better conviction in his disciples, and would do his adversaries only harm. For neither could not in any true sense be convinced by such a show: it could but prove his power. It might prove so far the presence of a God; but would it prove that God? Would it bring him nearer to them, who could not see him in the face of his Son? To say *Thou art God*, without knowing what the *Thou* means﻿—of what use is it? God is a name only, except we know *God*. Our Lord did not care to be so acknowledged.
On the same principle, the very miracles which from their character did partially reveal his character to those who already had faith in him, he would not do where unbelief predominated. He often avoided cities and crowds, and declined mighty works because of unbelief.

这一切的答案，对我们主是清楚的，如今对我们也是清楚的：那不是父旨意的方式。它与父所行的、生命与历史逐渐展开的方式不合；而那方式必是养育自由、爱神之意志的方式。那会是暴烈的、戏剧化的，因而在性质与结果上都贫乏——毫无神的样子。神行事中的一切，都与其余一切和谐地同来、并从其余一切而来。人子，他的历史必是人的历史，必是*那*人的历史。那岂能以一个例外开场？但对那渴望为人为到底的他，这确够得上一个试探。他是神的儿子：神的儿子们为什么不该知道？
但这旷野的试探既是将来一切试探的缩影与类型——为抵挡它们，他四十天之久使自己刚强，盘旋于我们够不着的真理之上，在那些真理的光中，每一个最平常的本分都可畏而属神，一个几乎足以压住一位自卑之神的异象——所以，我们若把他的生平与它联系起来看，就会更明白整体。他怎样拒绝把石头变成饼，照样在那一生中，他从未行一个神迹来帮助自己；他怎样拒绝从殿顶跳下来说服撒但、或可见地荣耀他的儿子名分，照样他坚定地拒绝给出那些属人的撒但们所要求的神迹记号——尽管他们抛出确信的许诺来诱他应允。羞辱他们、坚固他的跟从者，看似何等容易！但那样的确信会挡住门徒们一种更好的确信，对他的对头们也只有害处。因为后者在任何真实意义上都不能被这样一场表演说服：它至多证明他的权能。它或许可以证明到某程度有一位神在场；但它能证明*那*位神吗？它能把他带到那些在他儿子面上都看不见他的人更近处吗？说*你是神*，却不知道*你*是什么意思——有什么用呢？神只是一个名字，除非我们认识*神*。我们主不要这样的承认。
基于同样的原则，那些因性质确实部分向已有信心者启示了他性情的神迹，他在不信占上风的地方就不行。他常回避城市和人群，因不信而辞谢大工。

Except for the loving help they gave the distressed, revealing him to their hearts as the Redeemer from evil, I doubt if he would have wrought a single miracle. I do not think he cared much about them. Certainly, as regarded the onlookers, he did not expect much to result from those mighty deeds. A mere marvel is practically soon forgotten, and long before it is forgotten, many minds have begun to doubt the senses, their own even, which communicated it. Inward sight alone can convince of truth; signs and wonders never. No number of signs can do more than convey a probability that he who shows them knows that of which he speaks. They cannot convey the truth. But the vision of the truth itself, in the knowledge of itself, a something altogether beyond the region of signs and wonders, is the power of God, is salvation. This vision was in the Lord’s face and form to the pure in heart who were able to see God; but not in his signs and wonders to those who sought after such. Yet it is easy to see how the temptation might for a moment work upon a mind that longed to enter upon its labours with the credentials of its truth. How the true heart longs to be received by its brethren﻿—to be known in its truth! But no. The truth must show itself in God’s time, in and by the labour. The kingdom must come in God’s holy human way. Not by a stroke of grandeur, but by years of love, yea, by centuries of seeming bafflement, by aeons of labour, must he grow into the hearts of the sons and daughters of his Father in heaven. The Lord himself *will* be bound by the changeless laws which are the harmony of the Father’s being and utterance. He will *be*, not seem. He will be, and thereby, not therefore, seem. Yet, once more, even on him, the idea of asserting the truth in holy power such as he could have put forth, must have dawned in grandeur. The thought was good: to have yielded to it would have been the loss of the world; nay, far worse﻿—ill inconceivable to the human mind﻿—the God of obedience had fallen from his throne, and﻿—all is blackness.
But let us not forget that the whole is a faint parable﻿—faint I mean in relation to the grandeur of the reality, as the ring and the shoes are poor types (yet how dear!) of the absolute love of the Father to his prodigal children.
We shall now look at the third temptation.

===Chinese===

若不是它们给困苦者所上的慈爱帮助、向他们的心启示他为救赎主，我怀疑他是否会行一个神迹。我想他不怎么在乎它们。当然，就旁观者而言，他不期望这些大事产生多少结果。单是奇观，实际上很快被遗忘；而在被遗忘之前许久，许多心思已开始怀疑传达它的感官——甚至自己的感官。唯独内在的看见能说服人信真理；神迹奇事永不能。多少神迹也不能多于传达一个可能性：显神迹的那位知道他所说的事。它们不能传达真理。但对真理本身在自知中的看见——一样全然在神迹奇事范围之外的东西——乃是神的大能，乃是救恩。这看见在主的面容与形体里，向那能看见神的清心之人；却不在他的神迹奇事里，向那些追求奇事的人。然而，很容易看出，对一个渴望带着真理的凭证进入其劳作的心思，这试探会怎样一时作工。真实的心何等渴望被弟兄们接受——渴望在它的真实中被认识！但是不。真理必须在神的时间、借着并在劳作之中显明自己。这国（the kingdom）必须以神圣洁属人的方式来临。不是借一击之宏伟，而是借多年的爱，是的，借多个看似受挫的世纪，借万古的劳作，他必须长进他天上儿女的心里。主自己*愿意*受那不变法则的约束——那法则是父存有与言语的和谐。他要*是*，不要似乎。他要“是”，从而——不是“因此”——似乎。然而，再一次，即使在他身上，以他所能施展的圣洁权能断言真理的念头，也必曾以宏伟的样式破晓。这念头是好的：向它屈服就会是世界的丧亡；不，远比那更坏——人心无法想象的恶——顺服的神从他宝座坠落，而——一切都黑暗了。
但让我们不要忘记，整体是一个黯淡的比喻——黯淡，我是说相对于实际之宏伟，正如戒指与鞋（何等宝贝，却何等贫乏地）预表父对他浪子儿女绝对的爱。
我们现在看第三个试探。

===Original===

The first was to help himself in his need; the second, perhaps, to assert the Father; the third to deliver his brethren.
To deliver them, that is, after the fashion of men﻿—from the outside still. Indeed, the whole Temptation may be regarded as the contest of the seen and the unseen, of the outer and inner, of the likely and the true, of the show and the reality. And as in the others, the evil in this last lay in that it was a temptation to save his brethren, instead of doing the Will of his Father.
Could it be other than a temptation to think that he might, if he would, lay a righteous grasp upon the reins of government, leap into the chariot of power, and ride forth conquering and to conquer? Glad visions arose before him of the prisoner breaking jubilant from the cell of injustice; of the widow lifting up the bowed head before the devouring Pharisee; of weeping children bursting into shouts at the sound of the wheels of the chariot before which oppression and wrong shrunk and withered, behind which sprung the fir-tree instead of the thorn, and the myrtle instead of the brier. What glowing visions of holy vengeance, what rosy dreams of human blessedness﻿—and all from his hand﻿—would crowd such a brain as his!﻿—not like the castles-in-the-air of the aspiring youth, for he builds at random, because he knows that he cannot realize; but consistent and harmonious as well as grand, because he knew them within his reach. Could he not mould the people at his will? Could he not, transfigured in his snowy garments, call aloud in the streets of Jerusalem, “Behold your King?” And the fierce warriors of his nation would start at the sound; the ploughshare would be beaten into the sword, and the pruning-hook into the spear; and the nation, rushing to his call, learn war yet again indeed﻿—a grand, holy war﻿—a crusade﻿—no; we should not have had *that* word; but a war against the tyrants of the race﻿—the best, as they called themselves﻿—who trod upon their brethren, and would not suffer them even to look to the heavens.﻿—Ah! but when were his garments white as snow? When, through them, glorifying them as it passed, did the light stream from his glorified body? Not when he looked to such a conquest; but when, on a mount like this, he “spake of the decease that he should *accomplish* at Jerusalem”! Why should this be “the sad end of the war”?

===Chinese===

第一个是要在他缺乏中自助；第二个或许是要断言父；第三个是要拯救他的弟兄。
拯救他们，就是说，照人的方式——仍旧从外面。的确，整个试探可以看作是可见的与不可见的之争、外面的与里面的之争、看似可能的与真实的之争、表演与实体之争。而如在其他试探中一样，这最后一个的恶在于：它试探他去救他的弟兄，而不是行他父的旨意。
想到他若愿意，就能以义的手掌握住治理的缰绳、跃上权能的战车、出去征服且再胜——这怎能不是一个试探？欢喜的异象在他面前升起：囚徒从冤狱的牢房欢然破出；寡妇在吞噬人的法利赛人面前抬起垂下的头；哭泣的孩童在战车车轮声里迸发欢呼——车前，压迫与冤屈萎缩枯凋；车后，杉树代替荆棘长出，番石榴代替蒺藜。何等炽热的圣洁复仇的异象、何等玫瑰色的人类福乐之梦——都出于他的手——会挤满他这样的头脑！——不像有志少年那些空中楼阁——他随手乱建，因为他知道自己实现不了——而是既宏伟又一致和谐，因为他知道它们在他力所能及的范围。他难道不能随意塑造这民？他难道不能，在雪白衣袍中变化形容，在耶路撒冷街市上高呼：“看哪，你们的王？”他本国的勇猛战士必闻声而起；犁头打成刀剑，镰刀打成长矛；那民涌向他的呼召，再次真实地学会战争——一场宏伟、圣洁的战争——一场讨伐——不，我们本不会有*那个*词；而是一场对那自称为最优等者的族类暴君之战——他们践踏弟兄，不容他们甚至仰望诸天。——啊！但他的衣裳何时白如雪？何时有光从他荣耀的身体流出、穿过衣裳、使衣裳得荣耀？不是在他指望这样的征服之时；而是在这样一座山上，他“谈论他将在耶路撒冷*成全*的去世”之时！为什么这该是“战争的悲惨结局”呢？

===Original===

“Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.” Not even thine own visions of love and truth, O Saviour of the world, shall be thy guides to thy goal, but the will of thy Father in heaven.
But how would he, thus conquering, be a servant of Satan? Wherein would this be a falling-down and a worshipping of him (that is, an acknowledging of the worth of him) who was the lord of misrule and its pain?
I will not inquire whether such an enterprise could be accomplished without the worship of Satan﻿—whether men could be managed for such an end without more or less of the trickery practised by every ambitious leader, every self-serving conqueror﻿—without double-dealing, tact, flattery, finesse. I will not inquire into this, because, on the most distant supposition of our Lord being the leader of his country’s armies, these things drop out of sight as impossibilities. If these were necessary, such a career for him refuses to be for a moment imagined. But I will ask whether to know better and do not so well, is not a serving of Satan;﻿—whether to lead men on in the name of God as towards the best when the end is not the best, is not a serving of Satan;﻿—whether to flatter their pride by making them conquerors of the enemies of their nation instead of their own evils, is not a serving of Satan;﻿—in a word, whether, to desert the mission of God, who knew that men could not be set free in that way, and sent him to be a man, a true man, the one man, among them, that his life might become their life, and that so they might be as free in prison or on the cross, as upon a hillside or on a throne﻿—whether, so deserting the truth, to give men over to the lie of believing other than spirit and truth to be the worship of the Father, other than love the fulfilling of the law, other than the offering of their best selves the service of God, other than obedient harmony with the primal love and truth and law, freedom﻿—whether, to desert God thus, and give men over thus, would not have been to fall down and worship the devil. Not all the sovereignty of God, as the theologians call it, delegated to the Son, and administered by the wisdom of the Spirit that was given to him without measure, could have wrought the kingdom of heaven in one corner of our earth.

===Chinese===

“当拜主你的神，单要事奉他。”世界的救主啊，连你自己那些爱与真理的异象，也不可作你达于目标的向导；作向导的，惟有你天上父的旨意。
但他若这样征服，怎会是撒但的仆人呢？这在哪一点上是向他俯伏敬拜（即承认他的价值）呢——他是那乱治之主、及其痛苦之主？
我不去追问这样一番事业能否不经对撒但的敬拜而成就——人能否为这样的目的被驾驭，而不用每个野心家和自私征服者都多少使用的权术——不用两面手腕、机变、谄媚、诡计。我不追问这个，因为哪怕在最遥远的假设里——我们主作他本国军队的统帅——这些事都作为不可能而退场。这些若必需，那样一条道路他就一刻不容想象。但我要问：明知更好而行得更差，岂不是事奉撒但？——以神的名把人引向所谓最好的、而终点并非最好，岂不是事奉撒但？——借使他们作民族仇敌的征服者、而非自己罪恶的征服者来奉承他们的骄傲，岂不是事奉撒但？——一言以蔽之：离弃神的使命——那使命知道人不能那样得自由，并差他来在他们中间作一个人、一个真实的人、那独一的人，好叫他的生命成为他们的生命，叫他们因此或在监里、或在十字架上，都如在山坡上、在宝座上一样自由——这样离弃真理、把人交给那谎言——叫他们相信除了灵与真理还有别的是对父的敬拜、除了爱还有别的是律法的成全、除了献上自己最好的自己还有别的是对神的事奉、除了与元初的爱、真理、律法和谐的顺服还有别的是自由——这样离弃神、又这样交出人，岂不正是俯伏敬拜魔鬼。神学家们所谓的神的一切主权，就算都委托给子、并由那无限量赐给他之圣灵的智慧来施行，也不能在我们大地上的一角造出天国。

===Original===

Nothing but the obedience of the Son, the obedience unto the death, the absolute *doing* of the will of God because it was the truth, could redeem the prisoner, the widow, the orphan. But it would redeem them by redeeming the conquest-ridden conqueror too, the stripe-giving jailer, the unjust judge, the devouring Pharisee himself with the insatiable moth-eaten heart. The earth should be free because Love was stronger than Death. Therefore should fierceness and wrong and hypocrisy and God-service play out their weary play. He would not pluck the spreading branches of the tree; he would lay the axe to its root. It would take time; but the tree would be dead at last﻿—dead, and cast into the lake of fire. It would take time; but his Father had time enough and to spare. It would take courage and strength and self-denial and endurance; but his Father could give him all. It would cost pain of body and mind, yea, agony and torture; but those he was ready to take on himself. It would cost him the vision of many sad and, to all but him, hopeless sights; he must see tears without wiping them, hear sighs without changing them into laughter, see the dead lie, and let them lie; see Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted; he must look on his brothers and sisters crying as children over their broken toys, and must not mend them; he must go on to the grave, and they not know that thus he was setting all things right for them. His work must be one with and completing God’s Creation and God’s History. The disappointment and sorrow and fear he could, he would bear. The will of God should be done. Man should be free﻿—not merely man as he thinks of himself, but man as God thinks of him. The divine idea shall be set free in the divine bosom; the man on earth shall see his angel face to face. He shall grow into the likeness of the divine thought, free not in his own fancy, but in absolute divine fact of being, as in God’s idea. The great and beautiful and perfect will of God *must* be done.
“Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.”
It was when Peter would have withstood him as he set his face steadfastly to meet this death at Jerusalem, that he gave him the same kind of answer that he now gave to Satan, calling him Satan too.

===Chinese===

唯有子的顺服（obedience）、顺服以至于死、对神旨意那绝对的*遵行*——因为它就是真理——才能救赎那囚徒、那寡妇、那孤儿。而这救赎，也要借救赎那被征服欲辖制的征服者、那施鞭刑的狱卒、那不义的法官、连那吞噬人的法利赛人自己——那颗被虫蛀透、贪得无厌的心——来成就。大地必得自由，因为爱比死更强。所以，凶暴、冤屈、伪善与奉神之名的事，要演完它们疲乏的戏。他不折断树伸展的枝条；他要把斧子放在树根上。这需要时间；但树至终必死——死了，被丢进火湖。这需要时间；但他的父有的是时间，绰绰有余。这需要勇气、力量、舍己（self-denial）与忍耐；但他的父能赐他一切。这要付上身心之痛，是的，苦痛与折磨；但这些他甘愿担在自己身上。这要他目睹许多悲伤、且除了他无人能指望的景象；他必须看见眼泪而不擦，听见叹息而不化为欢笑，看见死者躺着、且任他们躺着；看见拉结哭她的儿女、不肯受安慰；他必须看着他的弟兄姊妹像孩子一样为摔坏的玩具哭喊，却不得修补；他必须走向坟墓，而他们不知道他正这样为他们把一切摆正。他的工必须与神的创造、神的历史为一，并成全它们。失望、忧伤与恐惧，凡他担当得起的，他都愿担当。神的旨意要成就。人要得自由——不仅是人自己所想的人，更是神所想的人。属神的观念要在属神的怀里得释放；地上的人要面对面见他的使者。他要长成属神思想的样子，自由——不在自己的幻想里，而在绝对属神的存在事实里，如在神的观念中。神的伟大、美善、完全的旨意*必须*成就。
“撒但，退去吧！因为经上记着说：当拜主你的神，单要事奉他。”
正是在彼得（Peter）想拦阻他、而他定意向耶路撒冷去迎这场死的时候，他给了彼得与如今给撒但同样的回答，也称呼他作撒但。

===Original===

“Then the devil leaveth him, and behold angels came and ministered unto him.”
So saith St. Matthew. They brought him the food he had waited for, walking in the strength of the word. He would have died if it had not come now.
“And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.”
So saith St. Luke.
Then Satan ventured once more. When?
Was it then, when at the last moment, in the agony of the last faint, the Lord cried out, “Why hast thou forsaken me?” when, having done the great work, having laid it aside clean and pure as the linen cloth that was ready now to infold him, another cloud than that on the mount overshadowed his soul, and out of it came a voiceless persuasion that, after all was done, God did not care for his work or for him?
Even in those words the adversary was foiled﻿—and forever. For when he seemed to be forsaken, his cry was still, “*My God! my God!*”

===Chinese===

“于是魔鬼离了耶稣，有天使来伺候他。”
圣马太这样说。他们把他等候的食物带来了——他一直是靠那道之力量的行走。食物这时若不来，他就死了。
“魔鬼用完了各样的试探，就暂时离开耶稣。”
圣路加这样说。
后来撒但又冒险再来一次。是什么时候？
是在那时吗——在最后一刻、在最后昏厥的痛苦中，主喊出“为什么离弃我”的时候？在他作成了大工、把它像如今预备好裹他的细麻布一样洁白纯净地放妥之后，另一片乌云——不是山上那片——笼罩了他的灵魂，从其中出来一种无声的劝说：毕竟一切已成，神却不在乎他的工、也不在乎他？
即使在那些话里，仇敌也被挫败了——且永远被挫败。因为在他似乎被离弃之时，他的呼喊仍是：“*我的神！我的神！*”

### The *Eloi* / 以罗伊（Eloi）
===Original===

> “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?”

I do not know that I should dare to approach this, of all utterances into which human breath has ever been moulded, most awful in import, did I not feel that, containing both germ and blossom of the final devotion, it contains therefore the deepest practical lesson the human heart has to learn. The Lord, the Revealer, hides nothing that can be revealed, and will not warn away the foot that treads in naked humility even upon the ground of that terrible conflict between him and Evil, when the smoke of the battle that was fought not only with garments rolled in blood but with burning and fuel of fire, rose up between him and his Father, and for the one terrible moment ere he broke the bonds of life, and walked weary and triumphant into his arms, hid God from the eyes of his Son. He will give us even to meditate the one thought that slew him at last, when he could bear no more, and fled to the Father to know that he loved him, and was well-pleased with him. For Satan had come at length yet again, to urge him with his last temptation; to tell him that although he had done his part, God had forgotten his; that although he had lived by the word of his mouth, that mouth had no word more to speak to him; that although he had refused to tempt him, God had left him to be tempted more than he could bear; that although he had worshipped none other, for that worship God did not care.
