There is so much associated with it to swell out the self of his consciousness, that the difficulty of casting it from him as the mere ugly shadow of the self God made, is vastly increased.
None can know how difficult it is to enter into the kingdom of heaven, but those who have tried﻿—tried hard, and have not ceased to try. I care not to be told that one may pass at once into all possible sweetness of assurance; it is not assurance I desire, but the thing itself; not the certainty of eternal life, but eternal life. I care not what other preachers may say, while I know that in St. Paul the spirit and the flesh were in frequent strife. They only, I repeat, know how hard it is to enter into life, who are in conflict every day, are growing to have this conflict every hour﻿—nay, begin to see that no moment is life, without the presence that maketh strong.

===Chinese===

他们必须得着的是生命；没有*生命*，存在就无法忍受。他们以为*只要能永远活着，永生可以不要*！凡知道永生是什么意思的人，都算那为唯一的恐怖：没有它而活下去。
那么这样取主的话：“孩子们，要进神的国，何等难哪！”这很像是他说话的方式。先叫他们思想每个人进神国本有的难处，再以更强的话重申富人的难处：“骆驼穿过针的眼，比财主进神的国还容易呢。”进天国从来难、永远难。连信人都必须从上头生——必须进入一种新的、未知的意识，都难。谨守律法的犹太人、礼仪的基督徒，畏缩于那自我灭没、那恩典与真理的生命、那天上喜乐的高天空气、那成全律法又将其放下的普及之爱。他们不能接受一种本身即永生的存有光景。这生命难信，也就难进。多难？难到救恩的夫子所能找到表达其难的话：“人到我这里来，若不恨……连自己的生命也恨，就不能作我的门徒。”而富人必比别人更难恨自己的生命。与生命关联的东西太多，胀大他意识中的自我，以致要把它当作神所造自我那单纯的丑陋影子抛开，难处就大增。
没有人知道进天国何等难，除非那些试过的——拼命试过、且不曾停止试的。谁对我说人可以立刻进入一切可能的甘甜确据，我不在乎；我要的不是确据，而是那东西本身；不是永生的确定性，而是永生。不管别的传道人怎么说，我知道圣保罗里面灵与肉体屡屡相争。我重复：唯有那些天天争战、渐渐要时时刻刻争战——不，开始看见没有那使人刚强的同在、没有一瞬是生命——的人，才知道进生命何等难。

===Original===

Let any tell me of peace and content, yea, joy unspeakable as the instant result of the new birth; I deny no such statement, refuse no such testimony; all I care to say is, that, if by salvation they mean less than absolute oneness with God, I count it no salvation, neither would be content with it if it included every joy in the heaven of their best imagining. If they are not righteous even as he is righteous, they are not saved, whatever be their gladness or their content; they are but on the way to be saved. If they do not love their neighbour﻿—not as themselves: that is a phrase ill to understand, and not of Christ, but﻿—as Christ loves him, I cannot count them entered into life, though life may have begun to enter into them. Those whose idea of life is simply an eternal one, best know how hard it is to enter into life. The Lord said, “Children how hard is it to enter into the kingdom!” the disciples little knew what was required of them!
Demands unknown before are continually being made upon the Christian: it is the ever fresh rousing and calling, asking and sending of the Spirit that worketh in the children of obedience. When he thinks he has attained, then is he in danger; when he finds the mountain he has so long been climbing show suddenly a distant peak, radiant in eternal whiteness, and all but lost in heavenly places, a peak whose glory-crowned apex it seems as if no human foot could ever reach﻿—then is there hope for him; proof there is then that he has been climbing, for he beholds the yet unclimbed; he sees what he could not see before; if he knows little of what he is, he knows something of what he is not. He learns ever afresh that he is not in the world as Jesus was in the world; but the very wind that breathes courage as he climbs is the hope that one day he shall be like him, seeing him as he is.
Possessions are *Things*, and *Things* in general, save as affording matter of conquest and means of spiritual annexation, are very ready to prove inimical to the better life. The man who for consciousness of well-being depends upon anything but life, the life essential, is a slave; he hangs on what is less than himself. He is not perfect who, deprived of every *thing*, would not sit down calmly content, aware of a well-being untouched; for none the less would he be possessor of all things, the child of the Eternal.

===Chinese===

谁对我说重生的直接结果是平安、知足、乃至说不出的喜乐，我不否认这样的说法，不拒绝这样的见证；我只想说：若他们所谓救恩少于与神绝对的为一，我就不称之为救恩；即便它含着他们最好想象之天上的一切喜乐，我也不满足于此。他们若不像他那样义（righteousness），就没有得救，无论他们多高兴多知足；他们不过在得救的路上。他们若不爱邻舍——不是如己：那话难解，也不是基督的——而是如基督爱他，我就不能算他们已进入生命，尽管生命可能已开始进入他们。那些以为生命不过是永远活着的人，最知道进入生命何等难。主说：“孩子们，进神的国何等难哪！”门徒们何等不知道所要求于他们的是什么！
前所未知的要求不断向基督徒提出：这是那运行在顺服（obedience）儿女里面之灵的永远新鲜的激动与呼召、询问与差遣。他以为自己已经达到了，那时他就在危险中；当他长久攀登的山忽然显出一个远峰，在永恒的洁白中放光，几乎隐没于诸天，一个荣耀加冕、其巅仿佛无人脚能及的峰——那时他就有盼望；那时就有了他一直在攀登的凭据，因为他望见了尚未攀登的；他看见了他从前看不见的；他对自己是什么所知虽少，对自己不是什么却知道了一点。他不断重新学知：他不像耶稣那样在世上；但他攀登时给他鼓勇的那阵风，就是那盼望：有一日他必像他，因为必见他他的真体。
所有物是*物*，而*物*——除非作为征服的材料与属灵兼并的凭借——总非常容易证明与更美生命为敌。凡安乐意识依赖生命以外任何东西的人，就是奴仆；他悬挂在低于自己的东西上。那被夺去每一*样*东西、仍能安然知足而坐、晓得安乐未受触动的人，才是不完全之外的人；因为他仍是万有的拥有者、永恒者的孩子。

===Original===

*Things* are given us, this body first of things, that through them we may be trained both to independence and true possession of them. We must possess them; they must not possess us. Their use is to mediate﻿—as shapes and manifestations in lower kind of the things that are unseen, that is, in themselves unseeable, the things that belong, not to the world of speech, but the world of silence, not to the world of showing, but the world of being, the world that cannot be shaken, and must remain. These things unseen take form in the things of time and space﻿—not that they may exist, for they exist in and from eternal Godhead, but that their being may be known to those in training for the eternal; these things unseen the sons and daughters of God must possess. But instead of reaching out after them, they grasp at their forms, reward the things seen as the things to be possessed, fall in love with the bodies instead of the souls of them. There are good people who can hardly believe that, if the young man had consented to give up his wealth, the Lord would not then have told him to keep it; they too seem to think the treasure in heaven insufficient as a substitute. They cannot believe he would have been better off without his wealth. “Is not wealth power?” they ask. It is indeed power, and so is a wolf hid in the robe; it is power, but as of a brute machine, of which the owner ill knows the handles and cranks, valves and governor. The multitude of those who read the tale are of the same mind as the youth himself﻿—in his worst moment, as he turned and went﻿—with one vast difference, that they are not sorrowful.
*Things* can never be really possessed by the man who cannot do without them﻿—who would not be absolutely, divinely content in the consciousness that the cause of his being is within it﻿—and *with him*. I would not be misunderstood: no man can have the consciousness of God with him and not be content; I mean that no man who has not the Father so as to be eternally content in him alone, can possess a sunset or a field of grass or a mine of gold or the love of a fellow-creature according to its nature﻿—as God would have him possess it﻿—in the eternal way of inheriting, having, and holding. He who has God, has all things, after the fashion in which he who made them has them.

===Chinese===

*物*赐给我们——这身体为物之首——是要借它们训练我们既独立又真占有它们。我们必须占有它们；它们不可占有我们。它们的用处是作中保——作那不可见之事、就是本身不可见之事在较低类中的形状与彰显；那些事不属于言语的世界，而属于沉默的世界，不属于显示的世界，而属于存有的世界，那不能震动、必须长存的世界。那些不可见之事在时空之物的形态——不是为存在，因为它们本在永恒神格中存在、从永恒神格存在——而是叫它们的存有被那些受训入永恒的人知道；神的儿女必须占有这些不可见之事。但他们不是伸手取它们，而是抓住它们的形态，把可见之物当作当占之物来报偿，爱上它们的身体而不是它们的灵魂。有好人几乎不信：那青年若同意放弃财富，主就不会叫他留着它；他们也似乎觉得天上的财宝作为替代品不够。他们不能相信，没有财富他反而境况更好。“财富不是力量吗？”他们问。它确是力量，正如藏在袍中的狼是力量；它是力量，但如同一台牲口机器，其主人对它的把手与曲柄、阀门与调速器都不甚了了。读这故事的大多数人，与那青年自己——在他最坏的一刻、转身走去之时——怀着同一心思，只差一点大大的不同：他们不忧愁。
*物*永不能真被那离不了它们的人占有——那人不能在“我存有的因由在其内、且*与他同在*”的意识中绝对、属神地知足。我不要被误解：凡有神与他同在的意识的人没有不知足的；我的意思是：凡不以得着父（the Father）、以致在他里面永远知足的人，就不能照一件东西的本性——照神要他占有的方式，照那永远的承继、得着、持守的方式——占有一次日落、一片草场、一座金矿、或一个同类的爱。有神的人，就有万物，按造它们者拥有它们的方式拥有。

===Original===

To man, woman, and child, I say﻿—if you are not content, it is because God is not with you as you need him, not with you as he would be with you, as you *must* have him; for you need him as your body never needed food or air, need him as your soul never hungered after joy, or peace, or pleasure.
It is imperative on us to get rid of the tyranny of *things*. See how imperative: let the young man cling with every fibre to his wealth, what God can do he will do; his child shall not be left in the hell of possession! Comes the angel of death!﻿—and where are the things that haunted the poor soul with such manifold hindrance and obstruction! The world, and all that is in the world, drops and slips, from his feet, from his hands, carrying with it his body, his eyes, his ears, every pouch, every coffer, that could delude him with the fancy of possession.
“Is the man so freed from the dominion of things? does Death so serve him﻿—so ransom him? Why then hasten the hour? Shall not the youth abide the stroke of Time’s clock﻿—await the Inevitable on its path to free him?”
Not so!﻿—for then first, I presume, does the man of things become aware of their tyranny. When a man begins to abstain, then first he recognizes the strength of his passion; it may be, when a man has not a thing left, he will begin to know what a necessity he had made of things; and if then he begin to contend with them, to cast out of his soul what Death has torn from his hands, then first will he know the full passion of possession, the slavery of prizing the worthless part of the precious.
“Wherein then lies the service of Death? He takes the sting, but leaves the poison!”
In this: it is not the fetters that gall, but the fetters that soothe, which eat into the soul. When the fetters of gold are gone, on which the man delighted to gaze, though they held him fast to his dungeon-wall, buried from air and sunshine, then first will he feel them in the soreness of their lack, in the weary indifference with which he looks on earth and sea, on space and stars. When the truth begins to dawn upon him that those fetters were a horror and a disgrace, then will the good of saving death appear, and the man begin to understand that having never was, never could be well-being; that it is not by possessing we live, but by life we possess.

===Chinese===

对男人、女人、孩子，我说——你若不知足，是因为神不照你的需要与你同在，不照他愿与你同在的方式、不照你*必须*有他的方式与你同在；因为你需要他，如你的身体从未需要食物或空气；需要他，如你的灵魂从未切慕过喜乐、平安或快乐。
摆脱*物*的辖制，于我们是当务之急。看何等当务之急：让那青年每一根纤维紧抓他的财富，神能作的他必作；他的孩子不可被留在占有的地狱（hell）里！死亡的使者来了！——那些曾以如此重重拦阻与障碍萦缠这可怜灵魂的东西，在哪里呢？世界和世上的一切，从他脚上、从他手中滑落、坠下，连带他的身体、他的眼、他的耳、每一个口袋、每一口箱子——凡能以占有的幻觉欺哄他的，都去了。
“这人就这样从物的主宰下得释了吗？死亡就这样服事他——这样赎他吗？那为什么催促那时刻？那青年不也可以等候时辰之钟的一击——在路上等候那不可避免的来释放他吗？”
不然！——因为我想，正是那时，这物之人才初次察觉它们的辖制。人开始禁戒时，才认出他情欲的力量；也许，当一个人一样东西都不剩时，他才开始知道他曾把物造成了何等的必需；若那时他开始与它们相争，把死亡从手中撕去的东西从灵魂里也赶出去，那时他才初次知道占有的全部情欲、把珍贵之物的无价值部分奉为至宝的奴役。
“那么死亡的服务在哪里？它拔去刺，却留下毒！”
在这里：磨伤灵魂的，不是那磨脚镣，而是那柔顺的脚镣。金的脚镣——人乐于注视的，虽然它们把他锁在牢墙上、与空气阳光隔绝——当它们去了，他才在失去它们的酸痛中、在他看地与海、看空间与星辰的厌倦冷漠中，初次感觉到它们。当真理开始向他破晓——那些脚镣原是恐怖与耻辱——那时拯救性死亡的好处就显出，人开始明白：拥有从来不是、也永不能是安乐；我们不是靠占有而活，乃是靠生命而占有。

===Original===

In this way is the loss of the things he thought he had, a motioning, hardly *towards*, yet in favour of deliverance. It may seem to the man the first of his slavery when it is in truth the beginning of his freedom. Never soul was set free without being made to feel its slavery; nothing but itself can enslave a soul, nothing without itself free it.
When the drunkard, free of his body, but retaining his desire unable to indulge it, has time at length to think, in the lack of the means of destroying thought, surely there dawns for him then at last a fearful hope!﻿—not until, by the power of God and his own obedient effort, he is raised into such a condition that, be the temptation what it might, he would not yield for an immortality of unrequited drunkenness﻿—all its delights and not one of its penalties﻿—is he saved.
Thus death may give a new opportunity﻿—with some hope for the multitude counting themselves Christians, who are possessed by *things* as by a legion of devils; who stand well in their church; whose lives are regarded as stainless; who are kind, friendly, give largely, believe in the redemption of Jesus, talk of the world and the church; yet whose care all the time is to heap up, to make much into more, to add house to house and field to field, burying themselves deeper and deeper in the ash-heap of *Things*.
But it is not the rich man only who is under the dominion of things; they too are slaves who, having no money, are unhappy from the lack of it. The man who is ever digging his grave is little better than he who already lies mouldering in it. The money the one has, the money the other would have, is in each the cause of an eternal stupidity. To the one as to the other comes the word, “*How is it that ye do not understand?*”

===Chinese===

这样，那自以为有之物的失去，虽算不得是朝向释放、却是利于释放的一动。人在它看去是他奴役之始，其实是他自由之始。从来没有一个灵魂不经感觉自己为奴而得释放；除它自己以外，没有什么能奴役一个灵魂；没有它自己，也没有什么能释放它。
当那酒鬼脱离了身体、却存着无法放纵的欲、终于有了时间思想——在缺乏毁灭思想之手段的时刻——确实那时终有一线可畏的盼望向他破晓！——直到借着神的大能与他自己顺服的努力，他被提升到这样一种光景——无论试探是什么，哪怕拿永不落空的酗酒——其全部快乐而无一份惩罚——作交换，他也不肯屈服——他才得救。
这样，死亡可能给一个新的机会——给那被*物*占有、如被一群鬼附的自认为基督徒的大众，一点盼望；他们在教会里站得良好；他们的生活被看为无瑕；他们仁慈、友好、大量施与、信耶稣的救赎、谈论世界与教会；然而他们一切的挂虑，都是堆积、把多变多、房连房田连田，把自己在*物*的灰堆里越埋越深。
但受物辖制的不只是富人；那些没有钱、却因缺钱而不快乐的人，同样是奴仆。那不断为自己掘墓的人，比已躺在墓中朽坏的人好不了多少。一人所有的钱、另一人所想要的钱，在各人里面都是永恒愚蠢之因。对这一人如对那一人，这话都临到：“*你们怎么还不明白呢？*”

### The Cause of Spiritual Stupidity / 属灵迟钝的原因
===Original===

> “How is it that ye do not understand?”

After feeding the four thousand with seven loaves and a few small fishes, on the east side of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus, having crossed the lake, was met on the other side by certain Pharisees, whose attitude towards him was such that he betook himself again to the boat, and recrossed the lake. On the way the disciples bethought them that they had in the boat but a single loaf: probably while the Lord was occupied with the Pharisees, one of them had gone and bought it, little thinking they were about to start again so soon. Jesus, still occupied with the antagonism of the leaders of the people, and desirous of destroying their influence on his disciples, began to warn them against them. In so doing he made use of a figure they had heard him use before﻿—that of leaven as representing a hidden but potent and pervading energy: the kingdom of heaven, he had told them, was like leaven hid in meal, gradually leavening the whole of it. He now tells them to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. The disciples, whose minds were occupied with their lack of provisions, the moment they heard the word leaven, thought of bread, concluded it must be because of its absence that he spoke of leaven, and imagined perhaps a warning against some danger of defilement from Pharisaical cookery: “It is because we have taken no bread!” A leaven like that of the Pharisees was even then at work in their hearts; for the sign the Pharisees sought in the mockery of unbelief, they had had a few hours before, and had already, in respect of all that made it of value, forgotten.
It is to the man who is trying to live, to the man who is obedient to the word of the Master, that the word of the Master unfolds itself. When we understand the outside of things, we think we have them: the Lord puts his things in subdefined, suggestive shapes, yielding no satisfactory meaning to the mere intellect, but unfolding themselves to the conscience and heart, to the man himself, in the process of life-effort. According as the new creation, that of reality, advances in him, the man becomes able to understand the words, the symbols, the parables of the Lord. For life, that is, action, is alone the human condition into which the light of the Living can penetrate; life alone can assimilate life, can change food into growth. See how the disciples here fooled themselves!

===Chinese===

> “你们怎么还不明白呢？”

在加利利海东岸用七个饼和几条小鱼给四千人吃饱之后，耶稣渡到湖那边，被几个法利赛人迎上；他们对他的态度使他重新上船，又渡回湖那边去。路上，门徒们想起船上只有一个饼：大概当主与法利赛人周旋时，他们中有人去买了一个，没想到这么快又要开船。耶稣仍想着民众领袖们的敌意，想要摧毁他们对门徒的影响，就开始警戒他们提防。这样作时，他用了一个他们从前听他用过的比喻——酵，代表一种隐藏却有力、弥漫的能力：天国，他曾告诉他们，好比酵藏在面里，渐渐使全团都发起来。他现在告诉他们要防备法利赛人的酵。门徒们心里正想着食物的缺乏，一听见“酵”字，就想到饼，断定必是因为没有饼他才说酵，也许还以为是提防法利赛人烹饪沾染污秽的警戒：“这是因为我们没有带饼吧！”一种像法利赛人的酵那样的酵，那时已在他们心里作工；因为法利赛人在不信的讥诮中所求的神迹，他们几个钟头前刚刚有过，而在一切使它有价值的事上，他们已经忘了。
夫子的话，是向那努力活着的人、向那顺服夫子之道的人展开的。当我们懂得了事物的外表，就以为得着了它们；主却把他的事放在未完成的、暗示性的形状里，对纯粹的智性不给满意的意义，却在生命努力的过程中，向良心与心、向人自己展开。随着那新的创造——真实的创造——在他里面推进，人就变得能明白夫子的话、象征与比喻。因为生命，就是行动，才是活者之光能透入的唯一人的光景；唯独生命能同化生命，能把食物变为生长。看门徒们在这里怎样自欺！

===Original===

See how the Lord calls them to their senses. He does not tell them in so many words where they are wrong; he attacks instead the cause in themselves which led to their mistake﻿—a matter always of infinitely more consequence than any mistake itself: the one is a live mistake, an untruth in the soul, the other a mere dead blunder born of it. The word-connection therefore between their blunder and our Lord’s exhortation, is not to be found; the logic of what the Lord said, is not on the surface. Often he speaks not to the words but to the thought; here he speaks not even to the thought, but to the whole mode of thinking, to the thought-matrix, the inward condition of the men.
He addresses himself to rouse in them a sense of their lack of confidence in God, which was the cause of their blunder as to his meaning. He reminds them of the two miracles with the loaves, and the quantity of fragments left beyond the need. From one of these miracles they had just come; it was not a day behind them; yet here they were doubting already! He makes them go over the particulars of the miracles﻿—hardly to refresh their memories﻿—they were tenacious enough of the marvel, but to make their hearts dwell on them; for they had already forgotten or had failed to see their central revelation﻿—the eternal fact of God’s love and care and compassion. They knew the number of the men each time, the number of the loaves each time, the number of the baskets of fragments they had each time taken up, but they forgot the Love that had so broken the bread that its remnants twenty times outweighed its loaves.
Having thus questioned them like children, and listened as to the answers of children, he turns the light of their thoughts upon themselves, and, with an argument to the man which overleaps all the links of its own absolute logic, demands, “How is it that ye do not understand?” Then they did understand, and knew that he did not speak to them of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees. He who trusts can understand; he whose mind is set at ease can discover a reason.
How otherwise than by rebuking and quelling their anxiety, could those words have made them see what then they saw? What connection was there between “How many baskets took ye up?” and “How is it that ye do not understand?”

===Chinese===

看主怎样叫他们醒悟。他没有直说他们错在哪里；他攻击的，是他们自己里面导致错误的原因——这永远比任何错误本身重要无限倍：一个是活的错误、灵魂里的不真，另一个只是由它而生的死的过失。所以他们的过失与我们主的劝诫之间，找不到字面的联系；主所说的话的逻辑，不在表面。他常常不是对言语说话，而是对思想说话；在这里，他连思想都不是对之说话，而是对整个思维方式、对思想之母、对人的内在光景说话。
他着手唤醒他们里面一种对神缺乏信靠的感觉——那就是他们对主用意误解的原因。他提醒他们那两个分饼的神迹，以及吃剩零碎的数量。他们刚从其中一个神迹那里来；它就在身后不到一日；可他们已经又疑惑了！他让他们一一数说神迹的细节——倒不是为唤起记忆——神迹本身他们记得牢——而是叫他们的心驻留其上；因为他们已经忘了、或从未看见它们的中心启示——神的爱、眷顾与怜悯这永恒的事实。他们记得每次的人数、每次的饼数、每次收拾的篮数，却忘了那爱——它擘饼擘得零碎比饼还多出二十倍。
这样像对孩子一样问过他们、又像听孩子回答一样听过，他把他们思想的光转向他们自己，用一个越过其自身绝对逻辑一切环节的论证，质问：“你们怎么还不明白呢？”那时他们就明白了，知道他说的不是饼的酵，乃是法利赛人和撒都该人的教训。信靠的人能明白；心得安顿的人能找出理由。
若不借着斥责并平息他们的焦虑，那些话又怎能叫他们看见当时所看见的？“你们收拾了多少篮子”与“你们怎么还不明白”之间有什么联系呢？

===Original===

What had the miracles to do with their discovering that when he spoke of leaven, it was not of the leaven of bread? If not of the leaven of bread, how did the reference to those miracles of bread make them recognize the fact?
The lesson he would have had them learn from the miracle, the natural lesson, the only lesson worthy of the miracle, was, that God cared for his children, and could, did, and would provide for their necessities. This lesson they had not learned. No doubt the power of the miracle was some proof of his mission, but the love of it proved it better, for it made it worth proving: it was a throb of the Father’s heart. The ground of the Master’s upbraiding is not that they did not understand him, but that they did not trust God; that, after all they had seen, they yet troubled themselves about bread. Because we easily imagine ourselves in want, we imagine God ready to forsake us. The miracles of Jesus were the ordinary works of his Father, wrought small and swift that we might take them in. The lesson of them was that help is always within God’s reach when his children want it﻿—their design, to show what God is﻿—not that Jesus was God, but that his Father was God﻿—that is, was what he was, for no other kind of God could be, or be worth believing in, no other notion of God be worth having. The mission undertaken by the Son, was not to show himself as having all power in heaven and earth, but to reveal his Father, to show him to men such as he is, that men may know him, and knowing, trust him. It were a small boon indeed that God should forgive men, and not give himself. It would be but to give them back themselves; and less than God just as he is will not comfort men for the essential sorrow of their existence. Only God the gift can turn that sorrow into essential joy: Jesus came to give them God, who is eternal life.
Those miracles of feeding gave the same lesson to their eyes, their hands, their mouths, that his words gave to their ears when he said, “seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind; for your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things”; “Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.” So little had they learned it yet, that they remembered the loaves but forgot the Father﻿—as men in their theology forget the very *θεοῦ λόγος*.

===Chinese===

神迹与他们发现“他说酵时不是指饼的酵”这件事有什么相干？若不是指饼的酵，提及那些饼的神迹又怎样使他们认出这事实？
他要他们从神迹学的功课——那自然的功课、唯一配得上神迹的功课——乃是：神眷顾他的儿女，能、曾、且必供给他们的需用。这功课他们没有学。无疑神迹的大能在某种程度上证明了他的使命，但神迹的爱证明得更好，因为它使这使命值得证明：那是父（the Father）心的一跳。夫子责备的根据，不在于他们不明白他，而在于他们不信靠神；在于见了这一切之后，他们还为自己的饼挂虑。因为我们很容易想象自己缺乏，就想象神随时要丢弃我们。耶稣的神迹是他父寻常的工作，作得又小又快，好叫我们领受。它们的功课是：他的儿女需要时，帮助总在神的手边——它们的设计，是显明神是怎样的一位——不是显明耶稣是神，而是显明他的父是神——就是说，显明他是他所是的那位；因为别的种类的神不能存在，也不值得信，别的神的观念不值得一有。子所承担的使命，不是显明自己握有天上地下所有的权柄，而是启示他的父，把他照他的本相显给人，叫人认识他，认识而信靠他。神若赦免人却不把自己给人，那实在算不得什么恩惠。那不过把人还给他们自己；而少于神自己的本相，安慰不了人存在的本质忧伤。唯有神这恩赐能把那忧伤转为本质的喜乐：耶稣来，是要把神——就是永生——赐给他们。
那些吃饱的神迹，给他们的眼、他们的手、他们的口的功课，正如他的话给他们耳的功课：“不要为生命忧虑吃什么，喝什么，也不要挂心；你们的父知道你们需要这些”；“要先求他的国和他的义，这些东西都要加给你们了。”他们学得何其少，以致记住了饼，却忘了父——正如人在他们的神学里忘了那真正的*神的道*。

===Original===

Thus forgetting, they were troubled about provision for the day, and the moment leaven was mentioned, thought of bread. *What else could he mean? The connection was plain!* The Lord reminds them of the miracle, which had they believed after its true value, they would not have been so occupied as to miss what he meant. It had set forth to them the truth of God’s heart towards them; revealed the loving care without which he would not be God. Had they learned this lesson, they would not have needed the reminder; for their hearts would not have been so filled with discomfort as to cause them mistake his word. Had they but said with themselves that, though they had but one loaf, they had him who makes all the loaves, they would never have made the foolish blunder they did.
The answer then to the Lord’s reproach, “How is it that ye do not understand?” is plainly this: their minds were so full of care about the day’s bread, that they could not think with simplicity about anything else; the mere mention of leaven threw them floundering afresh in the bog of their unbelief. When the Lord reminded them of what their eyes had seen, so of what he was and what God was, and of the foolishness of their care﻿—the moment their fear was taught to look up, that moment they began to see what the former words of the Lord must have meant: their minds grew clear enough to receive and reflect in a measure their intent.
The care of the disciples was care for the day, not for the morrow; the word “morrow” must stand for any and every point of the future. The next hour, the next moment, is as much beyond our grasp and as much in God’s care, as that a hundred years away. Care for the next minute is just as foolish as care for the morrow, or for a day in the next thousand years﻿—in neither can we do anything, in both God is doing everything. Those claims only of the morrow which have to be prepared today are of the duty of today; the moment which coincides with work to be done, is the moment to be minded; the next is nowhere till God has made it.

===Chinese===

这样忘了，他们为当日的食物忧烦，一提到酵，就想到饼。*不然他还能指什么？联系明摆着！*主提醒他们那神迹；他们若照它的真价值信了它，就不会那样心事重重，以致听不出他的意思。那神迹向他们陈明了神对他们的心之真理；启示了那没有它神就不成其为神的慈爱眷顾。他们若学了这功课，就不需要这提醒；因为他们的心就不会那样被不安充满，以致误解他的话。他们若曾对自己说：虽然我们只有一个饼，我们却有那造一切饼的他——他们就不会犯下所犯的那愚蠢过失。
所以对主那责备——“你们怎么还不明白呢？”——的答案，明摆着是：他们的心思满了对当日之饼的挂虑，以致不能单纯地想别的事；一提到酵，就使他们重新跌进不信的泥沼。当主提醒他们眼睛所见的，也就提醒了他是谁、神是谁、以及他们挂虑的愚昧——他们的惧怕一被教导向上看，那一刻他们就开始明白主先前那些话必是指什么：他们的心思清明到足以领受并在一定程度上反映那些话的用意。
门徒的挂虑是为当日，不是为明日；“明日”一词必须代表未来的任何一个、每一个点。下一小时、下一刻，与百年之后的那一刻，同样在我们把握之外，同样在神的看顾之中。为下一分钟的挂虑，与为明日、或为下一千年中某一天的挂虑同样愚昧——两者我们都不能作什么，两者神都在作一切。唯那些必须在今天预备的明日之要求，才属于今天的本分；与当作之工相重合的那一刻，才是当留心的那一刻；下一刻在神造它之前，并不存在。

===Original===

Their lack of bread seems to have come from no neglect, but from the immediacy of the Lord’s re-embarkation; at the same time had there been a want of foresight, that was not the kind of thing the Lord cared to reprove; it was not this and that fault he had come to set right, but the primary evil of life without God, the root of all evils, from hatred to discourtesy. Certain minor virtues also, prudence amongst the rest, would thus at length be almost, if not altogether, superseded. If a man forget a thing, God will see to that: man is not lord of his memory or his intellect. But man is lord of his will, his action; and is then verily to blame when, remembering a duty, he does not do it, but puts it off, and so forgets it. If a man lay himself out to do the immediate duty of the moment, wonderfully little forethought, I suspect, will be found needful. That forethought only is right which has to determine duty, and pass into action. To the foundation of yesterday’s work well done, the work of the morrow will be sure to fit. Work done is of more consequence for the future than the foresight of an archangel.
With the disciples as with the rich youth, it was *Things* that prevented the Lord from being understood. Because of possession the young man had not a suspicion of the grandeur of the call with which Jesus honoured him. He thought he was hardly dealt with to be offered a patent of Heaven’s nobility﻿—he was so very rich! *Things* filled his heart; things blocked up his windows; things barricaded his door, so that the very God could not enter. His soul was not empty, swept, and garnished, but crowded with meanest idols, among which his spirit crept about upon its knees, wasting on them the gazes that belonged to his fellows and his Master. The disciples were a little further on than he; they had left all and followed the Lord; but neither had they yet got rid of *Things*. The paltry solitariness of a loaf was enough to hide the Lord from them, to make them unable to understand him. Why, having forgotten, could they not trust? Surely if he had told them that for his sake they must go all day without food, they would not have minded! But they lost sight of God, and were as if either he did not see, or did not care for them.

===Chinese===

他们缺饼看来并非出于疏忽，而是出于主重新上船的突然；同时，即便有欠远虑，那也不是主所在意责备的事；他来要矫正的，不是这样那样的过失，而是没有神的生命这一根本的恶——一切恶的根，从恨到失礼。某些次要的美德，包括远虑，届时也将几乎（若非全然）被取代。人若忘了一件事，神会负责：人不是他记忆或智性的主。但人是他意志的主、他行动的主；当他记得一样本分却不作、拖延以致忘记时，他才真是可责的。人若专心作眼前当下的本分，我猜，所需的远虑会少得惊人。唯有那须决定本分、并化入行动的远虑才是正当的。在昨日之工作得好完成的根基上，明日的工作必恰好合式。完成了的工作，对未来比一位天使长的预见更紧要。
门徒们与那富有的青年一样，是*物*拦阻了他们明白主。因为占有，那青年对耶稣加给他尊荣的呼召之宏伟毫无感觉。他以为自己受了苛待——竟被赐予一份天国贵族的册封——他是这么富！*物*充满了他的心；物堵住了他的窗；物封锁了他的门，以致神自己都进不来。他的灵魂不是空着、扫净、粉饰好的，而是挤满了最鄙陋的偶像，他的灵在其间膝行爬动，把本属于他同伴与他夫子的凝望，浪费在它们身上。门徒们比他稍靠前些；他们已撇下一切跟从了主；但他们也还没有摆脱*物*。一个饼那点可怜的孤单，就足以把主向他们隐藏，使他们不能明白他。既然忘了，为什么不能信靠？确实，他若告诉他们：为他的缘故他们必须终日无食，他们也不会在意！但他们忘了神，表现得仿佛神要么看不见、要么不顾念他们。

===Original===

In the former case it was the possession of wealth, in the latter the not having more than a loaf, that rendered incapable of receiving the word of the Lord: the evil principle was precisely the same. If it be *Things* that slay you, what matter whether things you have, or things you have not? The youth, not trusting in God, the source of his riches, cannot brook the word of his Son, offering him better riches, more direct from the heart of the Father. The disciples, forgetting who is lord of the harvests of the earth, cannot understand his word, because filled with the fear of a day’s hunger. He did not trust in God as having given; they did not trust in God as ready to give. We are like them when, in *any* trouble, we do not trust him. It is hard on God, when his children will not let him give; when they carry themselves so that he must withhold his hand, lest he harm them. To take no care that they acknowledge whence their help comes, would be to leave them worshippers of idols, trusters in that which is not.
Distrust is atheism, and the barrier to all growth. Lord, we do not understand thee, because we do not trust thy Father﻿—wholehearted to us, as never yet was mother to her firstborn! Full of care, as if he had none, we think this and that escapes his notice, for this and that he does not think! While we who are evil would die to give our children bread to eat, we are not certain the only Good will give us anything of what we desire! The things of thy world so crowd our hearts, that there is no room in them for the things of thy heart, which would raise ours above all fear, and make us merry children in our Father’s house! Surely many a whisper of the watching Spirit we let slip through brooding over a need not yet come to us! Tomorrow makes today’s whole head sick, its whole heart faint. When we should be still, sleeping or dreaming, we are fretting about an hour that lies a half sun’s-journey away! Not so doest thou, Lord! thou doest the work of thy Father! Wert thou such as we, then should we have good cause to be troubled! But thou knowest it is difficult, *things* pressing upon every sense, to believe that the informing power of them is in the unseen; that out of it they come; that, where we can descry no hand directing, a will, nearer than any hand, is moving them from within, causing them to fulfil his word!

===Chinese===

前一例是财富的占有，后一例是不多于一个饼的缺乏，使主的话不能被领受：其恶的原则完全相同。若杀死你的是*物*，是你所有的物、还是你所没有的物，有什么要紧？那青年既不信靠神——他财富的源头，就受不住神之子的话，那给他更好财富、更直接出于父心的话。门徒们既忘了谁是地上庄稼的主，就不能明白他的话，因为满了对一日饥饿的惧怕。他不是作为已赐予者信靠神；他们不是作为乐赐者信靠神。我们在*任何*患难中不信靠他时，就像他们一样。这对神是难堪的：他的儿女不让他给；他们行事为人使他不得不缩回手，惟恐害了他们。若不管他们是否承认帮助从何而来，就等于任他们作拜偶像的、信那不是的。
不信是无神论，是一切生长的障碍。主啊，我们不明白你，因为我们不信靠你的父——他对我们全心全意，正如从未有母亲对她的头生子那样！我们满腹挂虑，仿佛他毫无挂虑；我们以为这那逃过了他的注意，为这那他不想！我们这些邪恶的人尚且肯死、为给儿女饼吃，却不能确定那唯一的良善者会给我们任何所愿之物！你世界的*物*这样挤满我们的心，以致其中没有地方容纳你心的事——那会使我们的心胜过一切惧怕、使我们在父家中作快乐孩子的事！确实，那守望之灵的许多低语，都因我们盘算着尚未临到的需用而漏失了！明日使今日整头发昏、整心发颤。我们本该安静、睡眠或作梦的时候，却在为一个隔半日之程的钟点焦躁！你不这样，主！你作你父的工！你若像我们一样，我们倒真有理由烦恼了！但你知道，*物*挤压着每一个感官，要相信那赋形于物的能力在不可见者里面、物从它出来、在我们看不见有手引导之处有一个比任何手都近的意志从里面运行、使它们成全他的话——这实在是难的。

===Original===

Help us to obey, to resist, to trust.
The care that is filling your mind at this moment, or but waiting till you lay the book aside to leap upon you﻿—that need which is no need, is a demon sucking at the spring of your life.
“No; mine is a reasonable care﻿—an unavoidable care, indeed!”
“Is it something you have to do this very moment?”
“No.”
“Then you are allowing it to usurp the place of something that is required of you this moment!”
“There is nothing required of me at this moment.”
“Nay, but there is﻿—the greatest thing that can be required of man.”
“Pray, what is it?”
“Trust in the living God. His will is your life.”
“He may not will I should have what I need!”
“Then you only think you need it. Is it a good thing?”
“Yes, it is a good thing.”
“Then why doubt you shall have it?”
“Because God may choose to have me go without it.”
“Why should he?”
“I cannot tell.”
“Must it not be in order to give you something instead?”
“I want nothing instead.”
“I thought I was talking to a Christian!”
“I can consent to be called nothing else.”
“Do you not, then, know that, when God denies anything a child of his values, it is to give him something *he* values?”
“But if I do not want it?”
“You are none the less miserable just because you do not have it. Instead of his great possessions the young man was to have the company of Jesus, and treasure in heaven. When God refused to deliver a certain man from a sore evil, concerning which he three times besought him, unaccustomed to be denied, he gave him instead his own graciousness, consoled him in person for his pain.”
“Ah, but that was St. Paul!”
“True; what of that?”
“He was one by himself!”
“God deals with all his children after his own father-nature. No scripture is of private interpretation even for a St. Paul. It sets forth God’s way with man. If thou art not willing that God should have his way with thee, then, in the name of God, be miserable﻿—till thy misery drive thee to the arms of the Father.”
“I do trust him in spiritual matters.”
“Everything is an affair of the spirit. If God has a way, then that is the only way. Every little thing in which you would have your own way, has a mission for your redemption; and he will treat you as a naughty child until you take your Father’s way for yours.”

帮助我们顺服，帮助我们抵挡，帮助我们信靠。

“不；我的挂虑是合理的——实在是无法避免的！”

“在属灵的事上我信靠他。”

There will be this difference, however, between the rich that loves his riches and the poor that hates his poverty﻿—that, when they die, the heart of the one will be still crowded with things and their pleasures, while the heart of the other will be relieved of their lack; the one has had his good things, the other his evil things. But the rich man who held his *things* lightly, nor let them nestle in his heart; who was a channel and no cistern; who was ever and always forsaking his money﻿—starts, in the new world, side by side with the man who accepted, not hated, his poverty. Each will say, “I am free!”
For the only air of the soul, in which it can breathe and live, is the present God and the spirits of the just: that is our heaven, our home, our all-right place. Cleansed of greed, jealousy, vanity, pride, possession, all the thousand forms of the evil self, we shall be God’s children on the hills and in the fields of that heaven, not one desiring to be before another, any more than to cast that other out; for ambition and hatred will then be seen to be one and the same spirit.﻿—“What thou hast, I have; what thou desirest, I will; I give to myself ten times in giving once to thee. My want that thou mightst have, would be rich possession.” But let me be practical; for thou art ready to be miserable over trifles, and dost not believe God good enough to care for thy care: I would reason with thee to help thee rid of thy troubles, for they hide from thee the thoughts of thy God.
The things readiest to be done, those which lie not at the door but on the very table of a man’s mind, are not merely in general the most neglected, but even by the thoughtful man, the oftenest let alone, the oftenest postponed. The Lord of life demanding high virtue of us, can it be that he does not care for the first principles of justice? May a man become strong in righteousness without learning to speak the truth to his neighbour? Shall a man climb the last flight of the stair who has never set foot on the lowest step? Truth is one, and he who does the truth in the small thing is of the truth; he who will do it only in a great thing, who postpones the small thing near him to the great thing farther from him, is not of the truth.

===Chinese===

然而，爱财的富人与恨贫的穷人之间将有这样的不同：死的时候，前者的心仍挤满了物及其快乐，而后者的心则从缺乏中得了释放；一个得了他的好东西，一个得了他的恶东西。而那把*物*看得很轻、不容它们在心里筑巢的富人；那作渠道而不作水池的；那始终不断撇弃他金钱的——将在新世界里，与那接受（而非恨恶）自己贫穷的人并肩起步。两个都要说：“我自由了！”
因为灵魂唯一能在其中呼吸存活的空气，乃是现在的神与义人的灵：那是我们的天堂、我们的家、我们一切安妥之地。洗净了贪婪、嫉妒、虚荣、骄傲、占有，以及恶我的千百种形态，我们将作神的儿女，在那天堂的山上、田间，没有一个想凌驾于另一个之上，正如没有一个想把另一个赶出去；因为那时野心与仇恨要被看作同一个灵。——“你所有的，我也有；你所愿的，我也愿；我给一次你，就是给自己十次。我愿你有而我缺，将是富足的拥有。”但让我实际一点；因为你随时准备为琐事痛苦，也不信神好到顾念你的挂虑：我愿与你讲理，帮助你脱去烦恼，因为它们向你隐藏你神的思想。
那些最易作的事——那些不是躺在人心门口、而是摆在人心桌面上的事——不仅在总体上最受忽略，连那有思想的人也最常搁下它们、最常推延它们。生命之主既向我们要求高超的美德，难道他会在乎不到公义的首要原则吗？人能不学会向邻舍说真话，就在义中刚强吗？从未踏过最低一级的人，能攀登最后一程楼梯吗？真理是一；在小事上行真理的人，就属乎真理；只愿在大事上行真理、把近处的小事推给远处的大事的，不属乎真理。

===Original===

Let me suggest some possible parallels between ourselves and the disciples maundering over their one loaf﻿—with the Bread of Life at their side in the boat. We too dull our understandings with trifles, fill the heavenly spaces with phantoms, waste the heavenly time with hurry. To those who possess their souls in patience come the heavenly visions. When I trouble myself over a trifle, even a trifle confessed﻿—the loss of some little article, say﻿—spurring my memory, and hunting the house, not from immediate need, but from dislike of loss; when a book has been borrowed of me and not returned, and I have forgotten the borrower, and fret over the missing volume, while there are thousands on my shelves from which the moments thus lost might gather treasure holding relation with neither moth, nor rust, nor thief; am I not like the disciples? Am I not a fool whenever loss troubles me more than recovery would gladden? God would have me wise, and smile at the trifle. Is it not time I lost a few things when I care for them so unreasonably? This losing of things is of the mercy of God; it comes to teach us to let them go. Or have I forgotten a thought that came to me, which seemed of the truth, and a revealment to my heart? I wanted to keep it, to have it, to use it by and by, and it is gone! I keep trying and trying to call it back, feeling a poor man till that thought be recovered﻿—to be far more lost, perhaps, in a notebook, into which I shall never look again to find it! I forget that it is live things God cares about﻿—live truths, not things set down in a book, or in a memory, or embalmed in the joy of knowledge, but things lifting up the heart, things active in an active will. True, my lost thought might have so worked; but had I faith in God, the maker of thought and memory, I should know that, if the thought was a truth, and so alone worth anything, it must come again; for it is in God﻿—so, like the dead, not beyond my reach: kept for me, I shall have it again.
“These are foolish illustrations﻿—not worth writing!”
If such things are not, then the mention of them is foolish. If they are, then he is foolish who would treat them as if they were not. I choose them for their smallness, and appeal especially to all who keep house concerning the size of trouble that suffices to hide word and face of God.

===Chinese===

让我提出几个我们与门徒之间可能有的平行——他们为着一个饼唠叨不休，而生命的粮就在船上他们身旁。我们也用琐事钝化我们的悟性，用幻影填满天上的空间，用匆忙浪费天上的时间。凡以忍耐拥有自己灵魂的，天上的异象就临到他们。当我为一件琐事烦恼——哪怕是一件认了的琐事，比如丢了什么小物件——翻搅记忆、翻遍全屋，不为当下的需要，只为厌恶损失；当有人借了我的书不还、我又忘了借者，为那失踪的一卷烦躁，而我书架上有成千卷书、那些失去的时光本可从中收取与虫、锈、贼都无关的珍宝；我岂不像那些门徒吗？每当损失之扰我甚于复得之乐，我岂不是个愚人？神要我智慧，对琐事一笑置之。我既然这样不合理地顾念它们，岂不正是该丢几件东西的时候吗？这丢东西是出于神的怜悯；它来教我们放手。或者，我忘了一个临到我的思想，它似乎出于真理、是我心的一个启示？我想留住它、拥有它、日后用它，它却没了！我一再试着召回它，在收回它之前自觉贫穷——而收回后也许在笔记本里失丧得更彻底，因为我再不会去翻那本子找它！我忘了神所在意的是活的东西——活的真理，不是记在书里、或记忆里、或封存在知识之乐里的东西，而是举起心来的东西、在活泼意志里活泼的东西。真的，我失去的思想或许本可这样作工；但我若信靠那思想与记忆的造者，我就知道，那思想若是一个真理、因而才有点价值，它必再来；因为它在神里面——所以像死者一样，并非够不到：它为我存留，我必再得着它。
“这些都是愚蠢的例子——不值一写！”
若这些事不存在，提起它们就是愚蠢。若它们存在，那把它们当作不存在看待的人才是愚蠢的。我特意选它们，正因其小，并特别请问一切当家的人：多小的烦恼就足以隐藏神的话与神的脸？

===Original===

With every haunting trouble then, great or small, the loss of thousands or the lack of a shilling, go to God, and appeal to him, the God of your life, to deliver you, his child, from that which is unlike him, therefore does not belong to you, but is antagonistic to your nature. If your trouble is such that you cannot appeal to him, the more need you should appeal to him! Where one cannot go to God, there is something specially wrong. If you let thought for the morrow, or the next year, or the next month, distress you; if you let the chatter of what is called the public, peering purblind into the sanctuary of motive, annoy you; if you seek or greatly heed the judgment of men, capable or incapable, you set open your windows to the mosquitoes of care, to drown with their buzzing the voice of the Eternal!
If you tell me that but for care, the needful work of the world would be ill done﻿—“What work,” I ask, “can that be, which will be better done by the greedy or anxious than by the free, fearless soul? Can care be a better inspirer of labour than the sending of God? If the work is not his work, then, indeed, care may well help it, for its success is loss. But is he worthy the name of man who, for the fear of starvation, will do better work than for the joy that his labour is not in vain in the Lord? I know as well as you that you are not likely to get rich that way; but neither will you block up the gate of the kingdom of heaven against yourself.”
Ambition in every shape has to do with *Things*, with outward advantages for the satisfaction of self-worship; it is that form of pride, foul shadow of Satan, which usurps the place of aspiration. The sole ambition that is of God is the ambition to rise above oneself; all other is of the devil. Yet is it nursed and cherished in many a soul that thinks itself devout, filling it with petty cares and disappointments, that swarm like bats in its air, and shut out the glory of God. The love of the praise of men, the desire of fame, the pride that takes offence, the puffing-up of knowledge, these and every other form of Protean self-worship﻿—we must get rid of them all. We must be free. The man whom another enslaves may be free as God; to him who is a slave in himself, God will not enter in; he will not sup with him, for he cannot be his friend.

===Chinese===

那么，每逢缠人的烦恼，无论大小——损失千万或缺少一先令——都到神那里去，向他呼吁，你这生命之神，救你这孩子脱离那不像他的东西——因此不属于你、且与你本性为敌的东西。你的烦恼若是那种无法向他呼吁的，那就更需要你向他呼吁！人不能到神那里去的地方，就有特别不对的东西。你若容为明日、为明年、为下月的思想使你痛苦；你若容那所谓公众的 chatter——斜眼窥探动机之圣所——搅扰你；你若寻求或过于在意人的审判（the judgment），无论有能的不能的，你就是向挂虑的蚊群敞开你的窗，让它们的嗡鸣淹灭永恒者的声音！
你若告诉我，没有挂虑，世上必需的工作就会作不好——“什么工作，”我问，“贪婪者或焦虑者会作得比自由无畏的灵魂更好？挂虑岂能比神的差遣更好地激发劳动？若那工作不是他的工作，那么挂虑倒真能帮它，因为它的成功就是损失。但那配称人的人，岂能因惧怕饿死而作的工，比因‘劳碌在主里面不是徒然’的喜乐而作的工更好？我同你一样清楚，那样你发不了财；但你也不会把天国的门向自己堵死。”
野心在一切形态上都与*物*打交道，与满足自我崇拜的外在优势打交道；它是骄傲的那一形态——撒但的秽影——篡夺了渴慕之位。唯一属神的野心，是超越自己的野心；其余一切都出于魔鬼。然而它却被许多自以为虔诚的灵魂哺育珍爱，使其充满琐屑的挂虑与失望，如蝙蝠成群飞满它的天空，把神的荣耀关在外面。对人称的爱、对名声的欲、易怒的骄傲、知识的自高——这些和一切其他形态的变形自我崇拜——我们都必须摆脱。我们必须自由。被别人奴役的人可以像神一样自由；而对自己里面的奴仆，神必不进去；不同他坐席，因为不能作他的朋友。

===Original===

He will sit by the humblest hearth where the daily food is prepared; he will not eat in a lumber-room, let the lumber be thrones and crowns. *Will not*, did I say? *Cannot*, I say. Men full of things would not once partake with God, were he by them all the day.
Nor will God force any door to enter in. He may send a tempest about the house; the wind of his admonishment may burst doors and windows, yea, shake the house to its foundations; but not then, not so, will he enter. The door must be opened by the willing hand, ere the foot of Love will cross the threshold. He watches to see the door move from within. Every tempest is but an assault in the siege of love. The terror of God is but the other side of his love; it is love outside the house, that would be inside﻿—love that knows the house is no house, only a place, until it enter﻿—no home, but a tent, until the Eternal dwell there. *Things* must be cast out to make room for their souls﻿—the eternal truths which in things find shape and show.
But who is sufficient to cast them out? If a man take courage and encounter the army of bats and demon-snakes that infests the place of the Holy, it is but to find the task too great for him; that the temple of God will not be cleansed by him; that the very dust he raises in sweeping is full of corruptive forces. Let such as would do what they must yet cannot, be what they must yet cannot, remember, with hope and courage, that he who knows all about our being, once *spake a parable to the end that they ought always to pray, and not to faint*.

===Chinese===

他要坐在最卑微的炉边，那里备着每日的饮食；他不在堆满杂物的屋里进食，哪怕那杂物是宝座与冠冕。我说*不愿*？我说*不能*。满腹是物的人，即使神终日与他们同在，也不会与神分享一次。
神也不会强闯任何门进去。他可以在房屋四围掀起暴风；他训诫之风可以吹破门窗，是的，把房子摇到根基；但不是那时、不是那样，他进去。门必须由甘愿的手打开，爱的脚才跨过门槛。他守望，要看门从里面动。每一场暴风都只是爱之围城的一次进攻。神的可畏只是他的爱的另一面；是屋外的爱，想要成为屋内的爱——那知道房屋在它进去之前不是房屋、只是处所——不是家、只是帐棚、直到永恒者住进——的爱。必须把*物*抛出去，为它们的灵魂——那些在物里找到形状与显示的永恒真理——腾出地方。
但谁配得把它们抛出去呢？人若鼓起勇气，迎战那侵扰圣地之处的蝙蝠群与鬼蛇，结果只会发现任务对他太重；神的殿不会被他洁净；他扫地扬起的尘土本身也满是败坏的力量。让那些必须作却作不到、必须是却作不到的人，怀着盼望与勇气记住：那位全知我们存有的主，曾*设一个比喻，要人常常祷告，不可灰心*。

### The Word of Jesus on Prayer / 耶稣论祷告的话
===Original===

> “They ought always to pray.”

The impossibility of doing what we would as we would, drives us to look for help. And this brings us to a new point of departure. Everything difficult indicates something more than our theory of life yet embraces, checks some tendency to abandon the strait path, leaving open only the way ahead. But there is a reality of being in which all things are easy and plain﻿—oneness, that is, with the Lord of Life; to pray for this is the first thing; and to the point of this prayer every difficulty hedges and directs us. But if I try to set forth something of the reasonableness of all prayer, I beg my readers to remember that it is for the sake of action and not speculation; if prayer be anything at all, it is a thing to be done: what matter whether you agree with me or not, if you do not pray? I would not spend my labour for that; I desire it to serve for help to pray, not to understand how a man might pray and yet be a reasonable soul.
First, a few words about the parable itself.
It is an instance, by no means solitary, of the Lord’s use of a tale about a very common or bad person, to persuade, reasoning *a fortiori*, of the way of the All-righteous. Note the points: “Did the unrighteous judge, to save himself from annoyance, punish one with whom he was not offended, for the sake of a woman he cared nothing about? and shall not the living Justice avenge his praying friends over whose injuries he has to exercise a long-suffering patience towards their enemies?”﻿—for so I would interpret the phrase, as correctly translated in the Revision, “and he is long-suffering over them.”﻿—“I say unto you, that he will avenge them speedily. Howbeit when the Son of Man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?”
Here then is a word of the Lord about prayer: it is a comfort that he recognizes difficulty in the matter﻿—sees that we need encouragement to go on praying, that it looks as if we were not heard, that it is no wonder we should be ready to faint and leave off. He tells a parable in which the suppliant has to go often and often to the man who can help her, gaining her end only at the long last. Actual delay on the part of God, we know from what follows, he does not allow; the more plain is it that he recognizes how the thing must look to those whom he would have go on praying.

===Chinese===

> “人应当常常祷告。”

不能照所愿的行所愿的，驱我们寻求帮助。这就把我们带到一个新的出发点。每一件难事都指明生命理论尚未涵盖的东西，拦阻某种离弃窄路的倾向，只留下前路。但有一种存有的实际，其中万事都容易而显明——就是与生命之主的合一；为此祷告是第一件事；而每一次难处都围着这祷告指向我们。但我若要陈说一切祷告的合理性之万一，我求读者记住：这是为行动，不是为思辨；祷告若算得什么，它是一件当行的事：你若不祷告，你同不同意我，有什么要紧？我不愿为此花费劳力；我愿它用于帮助人祷告，而不是帮助人理解一个人怎能祷告而仍作理性的灵魂。
先就比喻本身说几句。
这是主用一个极平常或很坏之人的故事、借“更况且”的推理、劝人信服全义者之方式的一个例子——并非孤例。注意要点：“那不义的官，为免骚扰自己，为他所不恼怒的一方、为一个他毫不关切的妇人伸冤了；何况那活的公义，岂不更要为他祷告的朋友们伸冤——对伤害他们的人，他正得长久忍耐？”——因为修订译本正确译作“他为他们恒久忍耐”，我就是这样解这话的。——“我告诉你们，他要快快地给他们伸冤了。然而人子来的时候，遇得见世上有信心吗？”
这就是主关于祷告的一句话：他承认这事有难处，这是一个安慰——他看见我们需要鼓励去继续祷告，看见事情看去仿佛未蒙垂听，看见我们难怪会灰心放弃。他讲了一个比喻，其中那恳求者得一再去、再去，到那能帮助她的人那里，直到最后最后才达到目的。至于神方面的实际迟延，我们从下文知道，他不容许；他承认这事在那些他要他们继续祷告的人眼中必是什么样子，就显得更明白。

===Original===

Here as elsewhere he teaches us that we must not go by the look of things, but by the reality behind the look. A truth, a necessity of God’s own willed nature, is enough to set up against a whole army of appearances. It looks as if he did not hear you: never mind; he does; it must be that he does; go on as the woman did; you too will be heard. She is heard at last, and in virtue of her much going; God hears at once, and will avenge speedily. The unrighteous judge cared nothing for the woman; those who cry to God are his own chosen﻿—plain in the fact that they cry to him. He has made and appointed them to cry: they do cry: will he not hear them? They exist that they may pray; he has chosen them that they may choose him; he has called them that they may call him﻿—that there may be such communion, such interchange as belongs to their being and the being of their Father. The gulf of indifference lay between the poor woman and the unjust judge; God and those who seek his help, are closer than two hands clasped hard in love: he will avenge them speedily. It is a bold assertion in the face of what seems great delay﻿—an appearance acknowledged in the very groundwork of the parable. Having made it, why does he seem to check himself with a sigh, adding, “Howbeit when the Son of Man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?” After all he had said, and had yet to say, after all he had done, and was going on to do, when he came again, after time given for the holy leaven to work, would he find men trusting the Father? Would he find them, even then, beyond the tyranny of appearances, believing in spite of them? Would they be children enough towards God to know he was hearing them and working for them, though they could not hear him or see him work?﻿—to believe the ways of God so wide, that even on the breadth of his track was room for their understanding to lose its way﻿—what they saw, so small a part of what he was doing, that it could give them but little clue to his end? that it was because the goal God had in view for them was so high and afar, that they could detect no movement of approach thereto? The sigh, the exclamation, never meant that God might be doing something more than he was doing, but that the Father would have a dreary time to wait ere his children would know, that is, trust in him.

===Chinese===

在这里也如别处一样，他教导我们：不可凭事物的外观，要凭外观背后的实际。一个真理、一种神自己意志本性中的必然，就足以抵挡整整一支外观的大军。看去仿佛他不听你：不要紧；他听着；必是他在听着；像那妇人那样继续去；你也必蒙垂听。她最后蒙了垂听，凭着她的一再去；神立刻垂听，且要快快伸冤。那不义的官不顾念那妇人；那些向神呼求的，是他自己的选民——他们向他呼求，这事实就显明了。他造他们、派定他们呼求：他们确实呼求：他岂不垂听？他们存在，为要祷告；他拣选他们，为要他们拣选他；他呼召他们，为要他们呼召他——为要有那样的相通、那样的交流，属于他们的存有与他们父的存有。冷漠的鸿沟隔在那可怜妇人与不义之官中间；神与那些寻求他帮助的人，却比相爱紧握的两只手更近：他要快快给他们伸冤。这是在看似大延迟面前的一个大胆断言——这外观在比喻的根基处就被承认了。既作了这断言，他为何又似乎叹一口气拦住自己，加上说：“然而人子来的时候，遇得见世上有信心吗？”在他所说的一切、还要说的一切之后，在他所作的一切、还要继续作的一切之后，当他再来时，在给了圣洁之酵作工的时间之后，他会发现人信靠父吗？会发现他们那时也在外观的暴虐之外、不顾外观而信吗？他们会够作神的孩子、知道他正垂听他们、正为他们作工——尽管他们听不见他、看不见他作工吗？——会信神的道路如此之广，甚至他行踪的宽度上也有他们悟性迷路的空间——他们所看见的，只是他所作之工如此小的一部分，以至几乎不能给他们他目标的线索吗？会信正因神为他们所定的目标那么高、那么远，以致他们察觉不出任何接近的动态吗？那叹息、那感叹，从不是指神可能在作比他正在作更多的什么，而是指父要有一段凄凉的等候，他的儿女才知道——就是说，才信靠他。

===Original===

The utterance recognizes the part of man, his slowly yielded part in faith, and his blame in troubling God by not trusting in him. If men would but make haste, and stir themselves up to take hold on God! They were so slow of heart to believe! They could but would not help it and do better!
He seems here to refer to his second coming﻿—concerning the time of which, he refused information; concerning the mode of which, he said it would be unexpected; but concerning the duty of which, he insisted it was “to be ready”: we must be faithful, and at our work. Do those who say, lo here or lo there are the signs of his coming, think to be too keen for him, and spy his approach? When he tells them to watch lest he find them neglecting their work, they stare this way and that, and watch lest he should succeed in coming like a thief! So throughout: if, instead of speculation, we gave ourselves to obedience, what a difference would soon be seen in the world! Oh, the multitude of so-called religious questions which the Lord would answer with, “strive to enter in at the strait gate”! Many eat and drink and talk and teach in his presence; few do the things he says to them! Obedience is the one key of life.
I would meet difficulties, not answer objections; I would remove stumbling-blocks from the path of him who would pray; I would help him to pray. If, seeing we live not by our own will, we live by another will, then is there reason, and then only can there be reason in prayer. To him who refuses that other will, I have nothing to say. The hour may come when he will wish there were someone to pray to; now he is not of those whom I can help.
If there be a God, and I am his creature, there may be, there should be, there must be some communication open between him and me. If anyone allow a God, but one scarce good enough to care about his creatures, I will yield him that it were foolish to pray to such a God; but the notion that, with all the good impulses in us, we are the offspring of a cold-hearted devil, is so horrible in its inconsistency, that I would ask that man what hideous and cold-hearted disregard to the truth makes him capable of the supposition! To such a one God’s terrors, or, if not his terrors, then God’s sorrows yet will speak; the divine something in him will love, and the love be left moaning.

===Chinese===

这话承认了人的份——他在信心上迟迟交出的份，和他因不信靠而烦扰神的罪责。人若肯赶快，奋发抓住神就好了！他们信得何等迟钝！他们能、却不肯自救而作得更好！
他这里似乎是指他的再来——关于其时候，他拒绝告知；关于其方式，他说必是意想不到的；但关于其本分，他坚持是“要警醒”：我们必须忠心，且在我们的工上。那些说看哪这里、看哪那里是他再来之兆的人，想比他更敏锐、窥探他的临近吗？他叫他们警醒、惟恐发现他们疏忽工作，他们却东张西望，警醒惟恐他真像贼一样来到！处处皆然：我们若以顺服（obedience）代替思辨，世上很快会有何等的不同！哦，那许许多多所谓宗教问题，主都只用一句回答：“要努力进窄门”！许多人在他面前又吃又喝、又谈论又教训；少有人行他对他们说的话！顺服是生命唯一的钥匙。
我愿应对难处，不愿回答异议；我愿从那要祷告之人的路上挪去绊脚石；我愿帮助他祷告。我们既见我们不是凭自己的意志活着，而是凭另一个意志活着，那么祷告才有理性，也唯有这时才能有理性。对那拒绝那另一个意志的人，我无话可说。时候也许会来，那时他会盼望有个可祷告的对象；现在他还不在我能帮助的人中。
若有一位神，而我是他的受造者，那么他与我之间，可能有、应该有、必定有某种敞开的相通。谁若容一位神，却难得好到顾念他的受造者，我承认向这样一位神祷告是愚妄；但“我们里面既有这一切良善的冲动，却是一个冷心魔鬼的后裔”这观念，其不自洽如此可怖，以致我要问那人：是怎样丑恶而冷心的不顾真理，使他能够作这假设！对这样的人，神的可畏——或者，若不是他的可畏，那必是神的忧伤——终要说话；他里面那属神的某物要爱，而那爱要留下哀鸣。

===Original===

If I find my position, my consciousness, that of one from home, nay, that of one in some sort of prison; if I find that I can neither rule the world in which I live nor my own thoughts or desires; that I cannot quiet my passions, order my likings, determine my ends, will my growth, forget when I would, or recall what I forget; that I cannot love where I would, or hate where I would; that I am no king over myself; that I cannot supply my own needs, do not even always know which of my seeming needs are to be supplied, and which treated as impostors; if, in a word, my own being is everyway too much for me; if I can neither understand it, be satisfied with it, nor better it﻿—may it not well give me pause﻿—the pause that ends in prayer? When my own scale seems too large for my management; when I reflect that I cannot account for my existence, have had no poorest hand in it, neither, should I not like it, can do anything towards causing it to cease; when I think that I can do nothing to make up to those I love, any more than to those I hate, for evils I have done them and sorrows I have caused them; that in my worst moments I disbelieve in my best, in my best loathe my worst; that there is in me no wholeness, no unity; that life is not a good to me, for I scorn myself﻿—when I think all or any such things, can it be strange if I think also that surely there ought to be somewhere a being to account for me, one to account for himself, and make the round of my existence just; one whose very being accounts and is necessary to account for mine; whose presence in my being is imperative, not merely to supplement it, but to make to myself my existence a good? For if not rounded in itself, but dependent on that which it knows not and cannot know, it cannot be to itself a good known as a good﻿—a thing of reason and well-being: it will be a life longing for a *logos* to be the interpretative soul of its *cosmos*﻿—a *logos* it cannot have. To know God present, to have the consciousness of God where he is the essential life, must be absolutely necessary to that life! He that is made in the image of God must know him or be desolate: the child must have the Father! Witness the dissatisfaction, yea desolation of my soul﻿—wretched, alone, unfinished, without him!

===Chinese===

我若发现自己的处境、自己的意识，是一个离乡之人的——不，是一个某种意义上在监里之人的；我若发现自己既不能治理我所生活的世界，也不能治理自己的思想或欲望；不能平息我的激情、整理我的好恶、决定我的目标、意愿我的生长、在愿忘时忘掉、或召回所忘的；不能在愿爱处爱、在愿恨处恨；不是我自己的王；不能供给自己的需用，甚至不总知道我那些看似的需要哪些当供给、哪些当视作骗子；总而言之，我若自己的存有在每方面都非我所能应付；既不能明白它、满足于它，也不能改良它——这岂不很可能叫我停下——那止于祷告的一停？当我自己的规模看来大得非我所能经营；当我想到我不能解释自己的存在，对它从未出过最微薄的一手，而且，就算我不喜欢它，也不能作什么使它止息；当我想到对那些我所爱的、正如对那些我所恨的，我都不能为他们所受的恶、所遭的忧作什么补偿；我在最坏的时刻不信我最好的自己，在最好的时刻厌恶我最坏的自己；我里面没有整全、没有统一；生命于我不是善，因为我鄙视自己——当我想着这一切或任何一件这样的事，我若也想着：确然应当有一位为我负责的存有、一位为他自己负责的存有、使我存在的整个圆周成为正当；一位其存有本身就解释了、且是必需来解释我的存有的；其在我存有中的临在是不可缺——不只是补充它，而是使我的存在对我成为善——岂会奇怪吗？因为它若不在自身内圆满，而系于它所不认识、也不能认识的，它就不能对自己成为一个被认知为善的善——一件有理性并安乐的东西：它将是一个渴慕着道（logos）来作它宇宙（cosmos）解释性灵魂的生命——一个它无法拥有的道。认识神的同在、在他乃本质生命之处有神的意识，对那生命必是绝对必需的！照神形象受造的，必认识他，否则就是荒凉：孩子必须有父！看哪，我灵魂的不满——是的，荒凉——没有他，可怜、孤独、未得成全！

===Original===

It cannot act from itself, save in God; acting from what seems itself without God, is no action at all, it is a mere yielding to impulse. All within is disorder and spasm. There is a cry behind me, and a voice before; instincts of betterment tell me I must rise above my present self﻿—perhaps even above all my possible self: I see not how to obey, how to carry them out! I am shut up in a world of consciousness, an unknown *I* in an unknown world: surely this world of my unwilled, unchosen, compelled existence, cannot be shut out from him, cannot be unknown to him, cannot be impenetrable, impermeable, unpresent to him from whom I am! nay, is it not his thinking in which I think? is it not by his consciousness that I am conscious? Whatever passes in me must be as naturally known to him as to me, and more thoroughly, even to infinite degrees. My thought must lie open to him: if he makes me think, how can I elude him in thinking? “If I should spread my wings toward the dawn, and sojourn at the last of the sea, even there thy hand would lead me, and thy right hand would hold me!” If he has determined the being, how shall any mode of that being be hidden from him? If I speak to him, if I utter words ever so low; if I but think words to him; nay, if I only think to him, surely he, my original, in whose life and will and no otherwise I now think concerning him, hears, and knows, and acknowledges! Then shall I not think to him? Shall I not tell him my troubles﻿—how he, even he, has troubled me by making me?﻿—how unfit I am to be that which I am?﻿—that my being is not to me a good thing yet?﻿—that I need a law that shall account to me for it in righteousness﻿—reveal to me how I am to make it a good﻿—how I am to *be* a good, and not an evil? Shall I not tell him that I need him to comfort me? his breath to move upon the face of the waters of the Chaos he has made? Shall I not cry to him to be in me rest and strength? to quiet this uneasy motion called life, and make me live indeed? to deliver me from my sins, and make me clean and glad? Such a cry is of the child to the Father: if there be a Father, verily he will hear, and let the child know that he hears! Every need of God, lifting up the heart, is a seeking of God, is a begging for himself, is profoundest prayer, and the root and inspirer of all other prayer.

===Chinese===

它不能凭自己行动，唯有在神里面；凭看似的自己而无神行动，根本不是行动，只是屈服于冲动。里面尽是紊乱与痉挛。我身后有呼喊，我面前有声音；改良的本能告诉我，我必须升到我现在的自己之上——也许甚至升到我一切可能的自己之上：我看不出怎样顺从、怎样成全它们！我被关在一个意识的世界里，一个未知的*我*在一个未知的世界：确然，我这非我所愿、非我所选、被迫存在的世界，不可能向他关闭，不可能不为他所知，不可能对那位我所从出者不可透、不可渗、不临在——不，我的思想岂不是在他思想里思想？我岂不是凭他的意识而意识？凡在我里面经过的，必如自然地为他所知，如为我所知，且更透彻，直到无限度。我的思想必向他敞开：他若使我思想，我怎能在思想里躲避他？“我若展开清晨的翅膀，飞到海极居住，就是在那里，你的手必引导我，你的右手也必扶持我！”他既定了那存有，那存有的任何方式怎能向他隐藏？我若向他说话，无论声音多低；我若只向他默想话语；不，我若只向他存念，确然他——我的本原，我如今正是在他的生命与意志里、且唯独在其中思想到他的——必垂听、知道、回应！那么我岂可不向他存念？我岂可不以我的困苦告诉他——他，正是他，怎样借造我而困住了我？——我多么不宜于作我所是的这个？——我的存有于我还不是一件善事？——我需要一条律法，在义（righteousness）中向我说明它——向我启示我怎样使它成为善——我怎样*作*一个善、而不是一个恶？我岂可告诉他，我需要他安慰我？需要他的运行在他所造之混沌的水面上？我岂可不向他呼求，求他在我里面作安息与力量？安抚这名为生命的不安之动，使我真实地活？救我脱离我的罪，使我洁净而喜乐？这样的呼喊是孩子向父的：若有一位父，他必垂听，并叫孩子知道他垂听！对神的每一需要，只要举起心，就是对神的寻求、对他自己的乞求、是最深的祷告，且是一切别的祷告的根与启示者。

===Original===

If it be reasonable for me to cry thus, if I cannot but cry, it is reasonable that God should hear, he cannot but hear. A being that could not hear or would not answer prayer, could not be God.
“But, I ask, all this admitted﻿—is what you call a necessary truth an existent fact? You say, ‘It must be so;’ I say, ‘What if there is no God!’ Convince me that prayer is heard, and I shall know. Why should the question admit of doubt? Why should it require to be reasoned about? We know that the wind blows: why should we not know that God answers prayer?”
I reply, What if God does not care to have you know it at second hand? What if there would be no good in that? There is some testimony on record, and perhaps there might be much were it not that, having to do with things so immediately personal, and generally so delicate, answers to prayer would naturally not often be talked about; but no testimony concerning the thing can well be conclusive; for, like a reported miracle, there is always some way to daff it; and besides, the conviction to be got that way is of little value; it avails nothing to know the thing by the best of evidence.
As to the evidence itself, adduction of proof is scarce possible in respect of inward experience, and to this class belongs the better part of the evidence: the testimony may be truthful, yet the testifier utterly self-deceived! How am I to know the thing as he says he knows it? How am I to judge of it? There is king David:﻿—Poetry!﻿—old poetry!﻿—and in the most indefinite language in the world! Doubtless he is little versed in the utterance of the human soul, who does not recognize in many of the psalms a cry as true as ever came from depth of pain or height of deliverance; but it may all have been but now the jarring and now the rhythmical movement of the waves of the psychical aether!﻿—I lay nothing upon testimony for my purpose now, knowing the things that can be said, and also not valuing the bare assent of the intellect. The sole assurance worth a man’s having, even if the most incontestable evidence were open to him from a thousand other quarters, is that to be gained only from personal experience﻿—that assurance in himself which he can least readily receive from another, and which is least capable of being transmuted into evidence for another. The evidence of Jesus Christ could not take the place of that.

===Chinese===

我这样呼喊若是合理的，我若不能不呼喊，那么神垂听也是合理的，他不能不垂听。一位不能垂听、或不肯应允祷告的存有，不能是神。
“但我要问，这一切都认了——你所谓必然的真理，是一件存在的事实吗？你说‘必是如此’；我说‘若没有神呢！’你若能使我信祷告蒙垂听，我就知道了。这问题为何容许怀疑？为何需要推理？我们知道风吹：我们为何不知道神应允祷告？”
我回答：若神不愿你间接地知道它呢？若那样并无益处呢？记载上有一些见证，若非因所涉之事如此切身、且通常如此微妙，本或许有许多——蒙应允的祷告自然地不常被谈论；但关于这事的任何见证都难作决定性的；因为像一桩被报道的神迹，总有办法把它挥开；何况，那样得来的确信价值甚微；凭最好的证据知道这事，也毫无用处。
至于证据本身，就内在经历而言，举证几乎不可能，而证据的更好部分正属此类：见证者可能诚实，却完全自欺！我怎能照他说的那样知道这事？我怎能判断它？有大卫王在：——诗！——古诗！——且是用世上最不确定的语言！无疑，谁若不认出许多诗篇里的呼喊真实如历来从痛苦之深或拯救之高发出的呼喊，谁就很少谙熟人类灵魂的言说；但这一切或许不过是心理以太之波时而刺耳、时而合拍的动荡！——我现在不把任何分量放在见证上，因为我知道所能被说的话，也不看重智性的空口同意。唯一配人拥有的确据——即便从一千个别的方面有最无可争辩的证据向他敞开——是唯有从个人经历才能得着的确据：那种在他自己里面的确据，他最难从别人领受，也最不能转化为给别人的证据。耶稣基督的证据也代替不了它。

===Original===

A truth is of enormous import in relation to the life﻿—that is the heart, and conscience, and will; it is of little consequence merely as a fact having relation to the understanding. God may hear all prayers that ever were offered to him, and a man may believe that he does, nor be one whit the better for it, so long as God has no prayers of his to hear, he no answers to receive from God. Nothing in this quarter will ever be gained by investigation. Reader, if you are in any trouble, try whether God will not help you; if you are in no need, why should you ask questions about prayer? True, he knows little of himself who does not know that he is wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked; but until he begins at least to suspect a need, how can he pray? And for one who does not want to pray, I would not lift a straw to defeat such a one in the argument whether God hears or does not hear prayer: for me, let him think what he will! it matters nothing in heaven or in earth: whether in hell I do not know.
As to the so-called scientific challenge to prove the efficacy of prayer by the result of simultaneous petition, I am almost ashamed to allude to it. There should be light enough in science itself to show the proposal absurd. A God capable of being so moved in one direction or another, is a God not worth believing in﻿—could not be the God believed in by Jesus Christ﻿—and he said he knew. A God that should fail to hear, receive, attend to one single prayer, the feeblest or worst, I cannot believe in; but a God that would grant every request of every man or every company of men, would be an evil God﻿—that is no God, but a demon. That God should hang in the thought-atmosphere like a windmill, waiting till men enough should combine and send out prayer in sufficient force to turn his outspread arms, is an idea too absurd. God waits to be gracious not to be tempted. A man capable of proposing such a test, could have in his mind no worthy representative idea of a God, and might well disbelieve in any: it is better to disbelieve than believe in a God unworthy.
“But I want to believe in God. I want to know that there is a God that answers prayer, that I may believe in him. There was a time when I believed in him. I prayed to him in great and sore trouble of heart and mind, and he did not hear me. I have not prayed since.”

===Chinese===

一条真理，就其与生命——就是心、良心、意志——的关系而言，意义重大；仅作为与悟性相关的事实，则无关紧要。神可能垂听历来向他献上的一切祷告，一个人也可能信他垂听，却不见得好一丝一毫——只要神没有他的祷告可垂听、他没有从神而来的应答可领受。在这一领域，靠研究将永远一无所获。读者啊，你若在任何患难中，试试神会不会帮助你；你若没有需用，为什么要问关于祷告的问题？真的，不认识自己可怜、贫穷、瞎眼、赤身的，就很少认识自己；但直到他至少开始疑心一种需要，他怎能祷告？而对于一个不想祷告的人，神垂听或不垂听祷告这争论，我一根草也不愿举起来驳倒他：至于我，随他怎么想！这在天上地上都无关紧要：在地狱（hell）里是否如此，我不知道。
至于那所谓科学的挑战——要用同时集体的祈求的结果证明祷告的功效——我几乎羞于提及它。科学本身就该有足够的光照出这提议的荒谬。一位能这样被朝这方向或那方向推动的神，是一位不值得信的神——不可能是耶稣基督所信的神——而他说过他认识。一位会漏听、不接、忽略一个祷告——哪怕最微弱、最坏的祷告——的神，我不能信；但一位会应允每个人、每群人的每个请求的神，将是一位恶神——那不是神，是鬼魔。神悬挂在思想的大气里像一架风车，等足够多的人联合起来、以足够强的祷告之力转动他张开的手臂——这观念实在荒谬。神等候施恩，而不等候被试探。一个能提出这种试验的人，他心里对神必没有一个配得的代表观念，大可以什么神都不信：与其信一位不配的神，不如不信。
“可我想信神。我想知道有一位应允祷告的神，好叫我信他。曾有一时我信他。我在心灵极大极痛的患难中向他祷告，他没有垂听我。此后我没有再祷告。”

===Original===

How do you know that he did not hear you?
“He did not give me what I asked, though the weal of my soul hung on it.”
In your judgment. Perhaps he knew better.
“I am the worse for his refusal. I would have believed in him if he had heard me.”
Till the next desire came which he would not grant, and then you would have turned your God away. A desirable believer you would have made! A worthy brother to him who thought nothing fit to give the Father less than his all! You would accept of him no decision against your desire! That ungranted, there was no God, or not a good one! I think I will not argue with you more. This only I will say: God has not to consider his children only at the moment of their prayer. Should he be willing to give a man the thing he knows he would afterwards wish he had not given him? If a man be not fit to be refused, if he be not ready to be treated with love’s severity, what he wishes may perhaps be given him in order that he may wish it had not been given him; but barely to give a man what he wants because he wants it, and without farther purpose of his good, would be to let a poor ignorant child take his fate into his own hands﻿—the cruelty of a devil. Yet is every prayer heard; and the real soul of the prayer may require, for its real answer, that it should not be granted in the form in which it is requested.
“To have a thing in another shape, might be equivalent to not having it at all.”
If you knew God, you would leave that to him. He is not mocked, and he will not mock. But he knows you better than you know yourself, and would keep you from fooling yourself. He will not deal with you as the child of a day, but as the child of eternal ages. You shall be satisfied, if you will but let him have his way with the creature he has made. The question is between your will and the will of God. He is not one of those who give readiest what they prize least. He does not care to give anything but his best, or that which will prepare for it. Not many years may pass before you confess, “Thou art a God who hears prayer, and gives a better answer.” You may come to see that the desire of your deepest heart would have been frustrated by having what seemed its embodiment then.

===Chinese===

你怎么知道他没有垂听你？
“他没有把我所求的给我，虽然我灵魂的福祉系于其上。”
按你的判断。也许他知道得更好。
“他的拒绝使我更坏了。他若垂听了我，我就信他了。”
直到下一个他不肯应允的愿望来到，那时你又要送走你的神。你倒会是个可取的信者！真配作那认为只有把一切给父才算馈赠之人的弟兄！你不愿接受他任何违背你愿望的决定！那不给成，就没有神，或没有好神！我想我不再与你争了。我只说一句：神不是只在儿女祷告的那一刻才考虑他们。一件他知道那人日后会巴望不曾得着的东西，他该给他吗？人若不宜被拒绝、若没有预备好受爱的严厉对待，他所愿的也许会被给他，好叫他巴望不曾得着它；但仅仅因为人要就给他所要的、而不顾及他的益处，就是任一个无知的孩子把命运握在自己手里——魔鬼的残忍。然而每一个祷告都被垂听；而祷告的真实灵魂，可能正需要不照所求的形式应允，才是它真实的回答。
“以另一个形状得一样东西，可能等于根本没有它。”
你若认识神，就会把这事留给他。他不受愚弄，他也不愚弄人。但他认识你胜过你认识自己，并要保守你不自欺。他不把你当作一日之子待，而当作永恒世代之子待。你必得满足，只要你肯让他照他的意思待他所造的。问题在你的意志与神的旨意（the will of God）之间。他不是那种把最不宝爱的给得最爽快的人。除了他的至善、或那为至善作预备的，他不愿给别的。不出几年，你或许就会承认：“你是一位垂听祷告的神，且给更好的回答。”你也许会看见：你心底的愿望，若按它当时看似的形体得着，反倒受了挫。

===Original===

That God should as a loving father listen, hear, consider, and deal with the request after the perfect tenderness of his heart, is to me enough; it is little that I should go without what I pray for. If it be granted that any answer which did not come of love, and was not for the final satisfaction of him who prayed, would be unworthy of God; that it is the part of love and knowledge to watch over the wayward, ignorant child; then the trouble of seemingly unanswered prayers begins to abate, and a lovely hope and comfort takes its place in the childlike soul. To hear is not necessarily to grant﻿—God forbid! but to hear is necessarily to attend to﻿—sometimes as necessarily to refuse.
“Concerning this thing,” says St. Paul, “I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he hath said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee; power is made perfect in weakness.” God had a better thing for Paul than granting his prayer and removing his complaint: he would make him strong; the power of Christ should descend and remain upon him; he would make him stronger than his suffering, make him a sharer in the energy of God. Verily, if we have God, we can do without the answer to any prayer.
“But if God is so good as you represent him, and if he knows all that we need, and better far than we do ourselves, why should it be necessary to ask him for anything?”
I answer, What if he knows prayer to be the thing we need first and most? What if the main object in God’s idea of prayer be the supplying of our great, our endless need﻿—the need of himself? What if the good of all our smaller and lower needs lies in this, that they help to drive us to God? Hunger may drive the runaway child home, and he may or may not be fed at once, but he needs his mother more than his dinner. Communion with God is the one need of the soul beyond all other need; prayer is the beginning of that communion, and some need is the motive of that prayer. Our wants are for the sake of our coming into communion with God, our eternal need. If gratitude and love immediately followed the supply of our needs, if God our Saviour was the one thought of our hearts, then it might be unnecessary that we should ask for anything we need.

===Chinese===

神作为慈父倾听、垂听、思量，并照他心的完全温柔对待请求，于我就足够了；我得不着我所求的，是小事。若承认：凡不出于爱、不为祷告者最终满足的应允，都不配神；看顾任性无知的孩子，正是爱与知识的份——那么，看似未蒙应允之祷告的烦恼便开始消减，一份可爱的盼望与安慰占据孩子般的心。垂听不必然是应允——万万不可！但垂听必然是关注——有时也必然是拒绝。
“为这件事，”圣保罗说，“我三次求过主，叫它离开我。他对我说：我的恩典够你用的；我的能力是在人的软弱上得以完全。”神给保罗的，比应允他的祷告、除去他的苦楚更好：他要使他刚强；基督的能力要降下并停留在他身上；他要使他强过他的受苦，使他有分于神的大能。真的，我们若有神，就可以不需要任何祷告的应允。
“但神若真如你所说那样好，又知道我们一切所需，远比我们自己知道得更清楚，为什么还必须向他求什么呢？”
我回答：若他知道祷告正是我们首先且最需要的呢？若神的祷告观念中主要的目标，就是供应我们那大的、无穷的需要——对他自己的需要呢？若我们一切较小较低的需要的好处正在于此：它们助长、驱我们到神面前呢？饥饿可以把逃跑的孩子赶回家，他到家或许吃得上饭、或许吃不上，但他需要他的母亲过于他的晚餐。与神相通是灵魂超越一切别需的唯一需要；祷告是那相通的开端，而某种需要是那祷告的动机。我们的诸需，是为了我们得以进入与神的相通、我们永恒的需要。若感恩与爱立即随着我们需要的供应而来，若神我们的救主是我们心中唯一的思想，那么我们为任何所需祈求，或许多余。

===Original===

But seeing we take our supplies as a matter of course, feeling as if they came out of nothing, or from the earth, or our own thoughts, instead of out of a heart of love and a will which alone is force, it is needful that we should be made feel some at least of our wants, that we may seek him who alone supplies all of them, and find his every gift a window to his heart of truth. So begins a communion, a talking with God, a coming-to-one with him, which is the sole end of prayer, yea, of existence itself in its infinite phases. We must ask that we may receive; but that we should receive what we ask in respect of our lower needs, is not God’s end in making us pray, for he could give us everything without that: to bring his child to his knee, God withholds that man may ask.
In regard, however, to the high necessities of our nature, it is in order that he may be able to give that God requires us to ask﻿—requires by driving us to it﻿—by shutting us up to prayer. For how can he give into the soul of a man what it needs, while that soul cannot receive it? The ripeness for receiving is the asking. The blossom-cup of the soul, to be filled with the heavenly dews, is its prayer. When the soul is hungry for the light, for the truth﻿—when its hunger has waked its higher energies, thoroughly roused the will, and brought the soul into its highest condition, that of action, its only fitness for receiving the things of God, that action is prayer. Then God can give; then he can be as he would towards the man; for the glory of God is to give himself.﻿—We thank thee, Lord Christ, for by thy pain alone do we rise towards the knowledge of this glory of thy Father and our Father.
And even in regard to lower things﻿—what it may be altogether unfit to do for a man who does not recognize the source of his life, it may be in the highest sense fit to grant him when he comes to that source to ask for it. Even in the case of some individual desire of one who in the main recognizes the Father, it may be well to give him asking whom, not asking, it would not benefit. For the real good of every gift it is essential, first, that the giver be in the gift﻿—as God always is, for he is love﻿—and next, that the receiver know and receive the giver in the gift. Every gift of God is but a harbinger of his greatest and only sufficing gift﻿—that of himself.

===Chinese===

但我们既把供应当作理所当然，觉得它们仿佛出自虚无、或出自地、或出自我们自己的思想，而不是出自一颗爱的心和一个独为力量的意志，我们就需要被叫来感觉至少某些我们的需要，好寻求那位独一的供应者，并发现他的每件礼物都是通向他真理之心的窗。这样就开始了一种相通、一种与神的对话、一种与他的合一——这是祷告唯一的目的，是的，是存在本身在其无限诸相中的唯一目的。我们必须求，才能得着；但我们照较低的需要得着所求的，并不是神叫我们祷告的目的，因为不求他也能把一切给我们：为把孩子带到膝前，神留着不给，使人求。
然而，就我们本性的高需而言，神要求我们求——借着驱我们到那里、借着把我们关进祷告——正是为了他能够给。因为他怎能把他所需要的给进一个人的灵魂，而那灵魂还不能领受它呢？领受的成熟就是那求。灵魂那要盛满天来之露的花杯，就是它的祷告。当灵魂饿慕光、饿慕真理——当它的饥饿唤醒了它较高的能量、彻底唤起了意志、把灵魂带进它最高的光景、行动的光景、它领受神之事的唯一合宜状态时——那行动就是祷告。那时神能给；那时他能照他所愿对待那人；因为神的荣耀就是把自己给人。——主基督啊，我们感谢你，因为唯有借你的痛苦，我们才得以升向你父我们父这荣耀的认识。
即使在较低的事上——对那不认生命之源的人全然不宜作的事，等他来到那源头求它时，给他或许在最高的意义上是合宜的。即使在某个大体上认识父之人的个别愿望上，问而给他、不问而不给他，或许都是好的。因为每件礼物真实的好处，首要在于赐者在礼物中——神总是如此，因为他是爱；其次在于受者认识并在礼物中领受赐者。神的每件礼物，都不过是他那最大、唯一足够的礼物——他自己——的前驱。

===Original===

No gift unrecognized as coming from God is at its own best; therefore many things that God would gladly give us, things even that we need because we are, must wait until we ask for them, that we may know whence they come: when in all gifts we find him, then in him we shall find all things.
Sometimes to one praying will come the feeling rather than question: “Were it not better to abstain? If this thing be good, will he not give it me? Would he not be better pleased if I left it altogether to him?” It comes, I think, of a lack of faith and childlikeness﻿—taking form, perhaps, in a fear lest, asking for what was not good, the prayer should be granted. Such a thought has no place with St. Paul; he says, “Casting all your care upon him, for he careth for you”; “In everything making your request known unto him.” It may even come of ambition after spiritual distinction. In every request, heart and soul and mind ought to supply the low accompaniment, “Thy will be done”; but the making of any request brings us near to him, into communion with our Life. Does it not also help us to think of him in all our affairs, and learn in everything to give thanks? Anything large enough for a wish to light upon, is large enough to hang a prayer upon: the thought of him to whom that prayer goes will purify and correct the desire. To say, “Father, I should like this or that,” would be enough at once, if the wish were bad, to make us know it and turn from it. Such prayer about things must of necessity help to bring the mind into true and simple relation with him; to make us remember his will even when we do not see what that will is. Surely it is better and more trusting to tell him all without fear or anxiety. Was it not thus the Lord carried himself towards his Father when he said, “If it be possible, let this cup pass from me”? But there was something he cared for more than his own fear﻿—his Father’s will: “Nevertheless, not my will, but thine be done.” There is no apprehension that God might be displeased with him for saying what he would like, and not leaving it all to his Father. Neither did he regard his Father’s plans as necessarily so fixed that they could not be altered to his prayer. The true son-faith is that which comes with boldness, fearless of the Father doing anything but what is right fatherly, patient, and full of loving-kindness.

===Chinese===

凡不被认作来自神的礼物，都未达到它自身的最好；因此许多神乐意给我们的东西——甚至因我们存在而需要的东西——必须等我们求了才来，好叫我们知道它们从何而来：当我们在一切礼物中找到他，我们就在他里面找到万事。
有时，一个祷告的人会来一种感觉，多于问题：“不如不求吧？这事若是善的，他岂不会给我？我若全然把它留给他，他岂不更喜悦？”这感觉，我想，出于信心与孩子气的缺乏——或许成形为一种害怕：求了不善的，祷告反蒙应允。这样的念头在圣保罗那里没有位置；他说：“你们要将一切的忧虑卸给他，因为他顾念你们”；“凡事借着祷告……将你们所要的告诉神”。它甚至可能出于对属灵卓越的野心。在每一个请求里，心、魂、意都当配上那低音：“愿你的旨意成全”；而发出任何请求，都把我们带到他近前、带到与我们生命的相通里。它岂不也帮助我们在一切事务中想到他、在凡事上学习谢恩吗？凡大得可以让一个愿望落上去的，就大得可以让一个祷告挂上去：对那祷告所归之神的思想，必净化并纠正那愿望。说“父啊，我愿意这个或那个”，若那愿望是坏的，就足以立刻叫我们知道它而转离它。这样关于事物的祷告，必帮助我们使心思与他进入真实单纯的关系；叫我们即使在看不出他旨意是什么时也记念他的旨意。确然，毫无恐惧或焦虑地把一切告诉他，是更好、更信靠的。主对他的父岂不正是这样，当他说“若可行，叫这杯离开我”？但有一样他顾念过于自己的惧怕——父的旨意：“然而不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思。”他不担心父会因他说出所愿、而非全然留给父而不喜悦他。他也不认为父的计划必已定死、不能照他的祷告更改。真正的儿子信心，是放胆而来的那种，不怕父作任何不是正当父性、忍耐、满有慈爱的事。

===Original===

We must not think to please him by any asceticism even of the spirit; we must speak straight out to him. The true child will not fear, but lay bare his wishes to the perfect Father. The Father may will otherwise, but his grace will be enough for the child.
There could be no riches but for need. God himself is made rich by man’s necessity. By that he is rich to give; through that we are rich by receiving.
As to any notion of prevailing by entreaty over an unwilling God, that is heathenish, and belongs to such as think him a hard master, or one like the unjust judge. What so quenching to prayer as the notion of unwillingness in the ear that hears! And when prayer is dull, what makes it flow like the thought that God is waiting to give, wants to give us everything! “Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.” We shall be refused our prayer if that be better; but what is good our Father will give us with divine good will. The Lord spoke his parable “to the end that they ought always to pray, *and not to faint*.”
