我们不要想以任何苦修——甚至属灵的苦修——讨他喜悦；我们要向他直说。真孩子不会惧怕，却要向那完全的父袒露他的愿望。父或许另有旨意，但他的恩典对孩子总是够用的。
若没有需要，就没有丰富。神自己因人的必需而成为富。借此他富于施给；借此我们因领受而富。
至于以为可以借恳求胜过一位不情愿的神，那是异教的想法，属于那些把他看作忍心主人、或像那不义之官的人。没有什么比“垂听之耳的不情愿”这念头更熄灭祷告了！而当祷告沉滞时，有什么比“神正等候着要给、要给我们一切”这思想更能叫它涌流！“所以我们只管坦然无惧地来到施恩的宝座前，为要得怜恤，蒙恩惠，作随时的帮助。”若那样更好，我们的祷告会被拒绝；但凡善的，我们的父必以神圣的美意赐给我们。主讲他那比喻，正是“要人常常祷告，*不可灰心*”。

### Man’s Difficulty Concerning Prayer / 人关于祷告的难处
===Original===

> “﻿—and not to faint.”

“How should any design of the All-wise be altered in response to prayer of ours!” How are we to believe such a thing?
By reflecting that he is the All-wise, who sees before him, and will not block his path. Such objection springs from poorest idea of God in relation to us. It supposes him to have cares and plans and intentions concerning our part of creation, irrespective of us. What is the whole system of things for, but our education? Does God care for suns and planets and satellites, for divine mathematics and ordered harmonies, more than for his children? I venture to say he cares more for oxen than for those. He lays no plans irrespective of his children; and, his design being that they shall be free, active, live things, he sees that space be kept for them: they need room to struggle out of their chrysalis, to undergo the change that comes with the waking will, and to enter upon the divine sports and labours of children in the house and domain of their Father. Surely he may keep his plans in a measure unfixed, waiting the free desire of the individual soul! Is not the design of the first course of his children’s education just to bring them to the point where they shall pray? and shall his system appointed to that end be then found hard and fast, tooth-fitted and inelastic, as if informed of no live causing soul, but an unself-knowing force﻿—so that he cannot answer the prayer because of the system which has its existence for the sake of the prayer? True, in many cases, the prayer, far more than the opportunity of answering it, is God’s end; but how will the further end of the prayer be reached, which is oneness between the heart of the child and of the Father? how will the child go on to pray if he knows the Father cannot answer him? “Will not” may be for love, but how with a self-imposed “cannot”? How could he be Father, who creating, would not make provision, would not keep room for the babbled prayers of his children? Is his perfection a mechanical one? Has he himself no room for choice﻿—therefore can give none? There must be a Godlike region of choice as there is a human, however little we may be able to conceive it. It were a glory in such system that its suns themselves wavered and throbbed at the pulse of a new child-life.

===Chinese===

> “——不可灰心。”

“全智者的任何设计，怎会因我们的祷告而更改！”我们怎能相信这样的事？
借思想他是那位全智者——他看清前路，不会挡住自己的路。这样的反对，出于关于神与我们关系的最贫乏的神观。它假设他对我们这部分创造怀有挂虑、计划与意图，却与我们无关。整个事物的体系若不是为了我们的教育，是为了什么？神顾念日月星辰、行星卫星，顾念属神的数学与有序的和声，过于顾念他的儿女吗？我敢说，他顾念牛过于顾念那些。他不制定撇开儿女的计划；而他的设计既是要他们作自由、活泼、活着的存有，他就看顾为他们留出空间：他们需要地方挣出他们的茧，经受那随苏醒之意志而来的改变，并在他们父的家与疆域里开始孩子们属神的游戏与劳作。确实，他可以把他的计划保持在某种未定状态，等候个别灵魂的自由愿望！他儿女教育首段课程的设计，岂不正是要把他们带到那开始祷告的地步？而为此目的设立的系统，届时岂会被发现僵硬死板、齿轮咬死、毫无弹性，仿佛其中没有一个活的起因之灵，只有一个不自知的力量——以致他因那为祷告而存在的系统而不能应允祷告？诚然，在许多情形里，祷告本身远过于应允它的机会，才是神的目的；但祷告更进一步的目的——孩子的心与父的心合一——又怎能达到？孩子若知道父不能应允他，还怎会继续祷告？“不肯”可以出于爱，但一个自加的“不能”又怎样？一位创造却不预备、不为儿女牙牙的祷告留余地的那位，怎能作父？他的完全是机械的吗？他自己竟没有选择的余地——因此给不出余地？必有一个属神的选择领域，正如有一个属人的，无论我们多么难以设想它。一个系统，其诸日竟随一个新孩童生命的脉搏而摇撼跳动，于那系统正是荣耀。

===Original===

What perfection in a dwelling would it be that its furniture and the paths between were fitted as the trays and pigeonholes of a cabinet? What stupidity of perfection would that be which left no margin about God’s work, no room for change of plan upon change of fact﻿—yea, even the mighty change that, behold now at length, his child is praying! See the freedom of God in his sunsets﻿—never a second like one of the foregone!﻿—in his moons and skies﻿—in the ever-changing solid earth!﻿—all moving by no dead law, but in the harmony of the vital law of liberty, God’s creative perfection﻿—all ordered from within. A divine perfection that were indeed, where was no liberty! where there could be but one way of a thing! I may move my arm as I please: shall God be unable so to move his? If but for himself, God might well desire no change, but he is God for the sake of his growing creatures; all his making and doing is for them, and change is the necessity of their very existence. They need a mighty law of liberty, into which shall never intrude one atom of chance. Is the one idea of creation the begetting of a free, grand, divine will in us? and shall that will, praying with the will of the Father, find itself cramped, fettered, manacled by foregone laws? Will it not rather be a newborn law itself, working new things? No man is so tied by divine law that he can nowise modify his work: shall God not modify his? Law is but mode of life-action. Is it of his perfection that he should have no scope, no freedom? Is he but the prisoned steam in the engine, pushing, escaping, stopped﻿—his way ordered by valve and piston? or is he an indwelling, willing, ordering power? Law is the slave of Life. Is not a man’s soul, as it dwells in his body, a dim-shadowing type of God in and throughout his universe? If you say, he has made things to go, set them going, and left them﻿—then I say, If his machine interfered with his answering the prayer of a single child, he would sweep it from him﻿—not to bring back chaos, but to make room for his child. But order is divine, and cannot be obstructive to its own higher ends; it must subserve them. Order, free order, neither chaos, nor law unpossessed and senseless, is the home of Thought.

===Chinese===

一座居所，若其家具与其间的路径像柜子的抽屉与鸽笼般一一契定，那算什么完全？一种完全，若在神的工四围不留余裕、不随事实之变留改计之余地——是的，甚至那大变：看哪，他的孩子如今终于祷告了！——那算什么愚拙的完全？看神在他日落中的自由——从未有一次与已往的任何一次相同！——在他的月与天空——在恒变的坚实大地！——一切并非循死律而动，而是循自由之生命律的和声，神创造的完全——一切从里面受调度。一种属神的完全若是里面没有自由、一件事只能有一种作法，那算什么！我可以随意挥动我的手臂：神竟不能这样挥动他的吗？即使单为自己，神尽可以不欲改变；但他为着他成长中的受造者的缘故作神；他一切的造作与行事都是为了他们，而改变是他们存在本身的必需。他们需要一条自由的大律，其中永不容一粒偶然的原子闯入。创造的唯一观念，岂不就是在里面生出一个自由、宏大、属神的意志？而那意志与父的意志一同祷告时，竟发现自己被既成的律法束缚、桎梏、上镣？它岂不更当自己就是一条新生的律，行出新事？没有人被神的律捆得完全不能修改自己的工：神岂不能修改他的？律不过是生命行动的样式。他竟没有施展的余地、没有自由，这算是他的完全吗？他不过是引擎里被囚的蒸汽，推挤、逃逸、被止住——他的路由阀与活塞安排？还是他是一位内住、有意志、有调度的大能？律是生命的奴仆。人的灵魂住在他身体里，岂不就是神在他整个宇宙中、并贯穿他宇宙的一个朦胧投影？你若说：他造好万物叫它们运转、发动了它们、就撇下不管——那么我说：他的机器若妨碍他应允一个孩子的祷告，他会把它扫开——不是要带回混沌，而是要为他的孩子腾出地方。但秩序是属神的，不能阻碍它自己更高的目的；它必服务于它们。秩序，自由的秩序——既非混沌、也非无主而无意义的律法——才是思想的家园。

If you say There can be but one perfect way, I answer, Yet the perfect way to bring a thing so far, to a certain crisis, can ill be the perfect way to carry it on after that crisis: the plan will have to change then. And as this crisis depends on a will, all cannot be in exact, though in live preparation for it. We must remember that God is not occupied with a grand toy of worlds and suns and planets, of attractions and repulsions, of agglomerations and crystallizations, of forces and waves; that these but constitute a portion of his workshops and tools for the bringing out of righteous men and women to fill his house of love withal. Would he have let his Son die for a law of nature, as we call it? These doubtless are the outcome of willed laws of his own being; but they take their relations in matter only for the sake of the birth of sons and daughters, that they may yet again be born from above, and into the higher region whence these things issue; and many a modification of the ideal, rendering it less than complete, must be given to those whose very doom being to grow or perish implies their utter inability to lay hold of the perfect. The best *means* cannot be the ideal Best. The embodiment of uplifting truth for the low, cannot be equal to that for the higher, else it will fail, and prove for its object not good; but, as the low ascend, their revelation will ascend also.
That God cannot interfere to modify his plans, interfere without the change of a single law of his world, is to me absurd. If we can change, God can change, else is he less free than we﻿—his plans, I say, not principles, not ends: God himself forbid!﻿—change them after divine fashion, above our fashions as the heavens are higher than the earth. And as in all his miracles Jesus did only in miniature what his Father does ever in the great﻿—in far wider, more elaborate, and beautiful ways, I will adduce from them an instance of answer to prayer that has in it a point bearing, it seems to me, most importantly on the thing I am now trying to set forth.

===Chinese===

你若说：只能有一条完全的路。我回答：然而把一件事带到某危机为止的完全之路，很难也是那危机之后继续它的完全之路：届时计划将不得不改变。而这危机既系于一个意志，一切便不能（虽在活泼的预备中）精确就位。我们必须记住：神所忙的不是一个由世界、太阳、行星、吸引与排斥、凝聚与结晶、力与波组成的大玩偶；这些不过是他的工场与工具的一部分，为要造出义人义女来充满他爱的家。他岂会为一条自然律——如我们所称的——让他的儿子死？这些无疑出于他存有之意志诸律的流发；但它们在物质中的诸关系，只是为了儿女的出生，好叫他们得以从上头再生、进入这些事物所自出的更高境界；而理想的许多修改——使它不及完全——必须给予那些其命运既是生长或灭亡就注定无力抓住完全的人。最好的*手段*不能就是那理想的至善。为低者设计之提升性真理的体现，不能等于为高者设计的，否则就会失败，对其对象证明为非善；但随着低者的上升，他们的启示也将上升。
说神不能干预修改他的计划、不能在不变更他世界任何一条律的情况下干预，在我看来是荒谬的。我们既能改变，神就能改变，否则他就少于我们的自由——我说的是他的计划，不是他的原理，不是他的目的：神自己不容许！——以属神的方式改它们，高过我们的方式，如天之高于地。而耶稣在一切神迹中所作的，不过是把他的父在宏大中永远在作的事作了个缩影——以远更宽广、更精巧、更美的方式——我就要从其中举一个蒙应允之祷告的例子，其中有一点，在我看来，与我现在力图陈明的事有最重要的关系。

===Original===

Poor, indeed, was the making of the wine in the earthen pots of stone, compared with its making in the lovely growth of the vine with its clusters of swelling grapes﻿—the live roots gathering from the earth the water that had to be borne in pitchers and poured into the great vases; but it is precious as the interpreter of the same, even in its being the outcome of our Lord’s sympathy with ordinary human rejoicing. There is however an element in its origin that makes it yet more precious to me﻿—the regard of our Lord to a wish of his mother. Alas, how differently is the tale often received! how misunderstood!
His mother had suggested to him that here was an opportunity for appearing in his own greatness, the potent purveyor of wine for the failing feast. It was not in his plan, as we gather from his words; for the Lord never pretended anything, whether to his enemy or his mother; he is The True. He lets her know that he and she have different outlooks, different notions of his work: “What to me and thee, woman?” he said: “my hour is not yet come”; but there was that in his look and tone whence she knew that her desire, scarce half-fashioned into request, was granted. What am I thence to conclude, worthy of the Son of God, and the Son of Mary, but that, at the prayer of his mother, he made room in his plans for the thing she desired? It was not his wish then to work a miracle, but if his mother wished it, he would! He did for his mother what for his own part he would rather have let alone. Not always did he do as his mother would have him; but this was a case in which he could do so, for it would interfere nowise with the will of his Father. Was the perfect son, for, being perfect, he must be perfect every way, to be the only son of man who needed do nothing to please his mother﻿—nothing but what fell in with his plan for the hour? Not so could he be the root, the living heart of the great response of the children to the Father of all! not so could the idea of the grand family ever be made a reality! Alas for the son who would not willingly for his mother do something which in itself he would rather not do! If it would have hurt his mother, if it had been in any way turning from the will of his Father in heaven, he would not have done it: that would have been to answer her prayer against her. His yielding makes the story doubly precious to my heart.

===Chinese===

确实，比较在葡萄可爱的生长中——活的根从地里吸取那得用水瓶带来、倒进大缸的水，连同它串串饱满的葡萄——造酒，在石缸里造酒是贫乏的；但作为同一件事的解释者，它是宝贵的，甚至在它是我们主对寻常人间喜庆之同情的产物这一点上。然而它起源中有一个因素，于我更宝贵——我们主对他母亲一个愿望的顾念。唉，这故事常被多么不同地领受！多么被误解！
他母亲向他提示：这里有一个机会显出他自己的伟大，作那节筵席告罄时的大能供酒者。照他的话推断，那不在他的计划里；因为主从不假装什么，无论对他的仇敌还是他的母亲；他就是那真实。他让她知道，他与她有不同的视野、对他的工作有不同的观念：“妇人，我与你有什么相干？”他说，“我的时候还没有到”；但他神色语气中有一种东西，使她知道她的愿望——才勉强成形的请求——已经蒙了应允。我从这里当得出什么结论，配于神子、也配于马利亚之子的结论，岂不就是：应他母亲的祷告，他在他的计划里为她所愿的事腾出了地方？他那时本不愿行神迹，但他母亲若愿，他就愿！他为母亲作了他自己宁可不作的事。他并非总照他母亲所要的去作；但这是他能这样作的一个情形，因为它毫不妨碍他父的旨意。那完全的儿子——既完全，就必在每方面完全——难道要作人子中唯一不必作什么讨母亲喜悦的儿子——除了那落在他当刻计划之内的事？若这样，他怎能作众儿女对万有之父那伟大回应的根、那活的心！怎能叫那大家族的观念终成实际！唉，那不肯为母亲甘愿作一件自己本宁可不作之事的儿子！它若会伤他母亲，若在任何方面偏离他天上父的旨意，他就不会作：那将是逆着她的祷告应允她。他的顺从使这故事在我心里加倍宝贵。

The Son then could change his intent, and spoil nothing: so, I say, can the Father; for the Son does nothing but what he sees the Father do.
Finding it possible to understand, however, that God may answer prayers to those who pray for themselves, what are we to think concerning prayer for others? One may well say, It would surely be very selfish to pray only for ourselves! but the question is of the use, not of the character of the action: if there be any good in it, let us pray for all for whom we feel we can pray; but is there to be found in regard to prayer for others any such satisfaction as in regard to prayer for ourselves? The ground is changed﻿—if the fitness of answering prayer lies in the praying of him who prays: the attitude necessary to reception does not belong to those *for* whom prayer is made, but to him *by* whom it is made. What fitness then can there be in praying for others? Will God give to another for our asking what he would not give without it? Would he not, if it could be done without the person’s self, do it without a second person? If God were a tyrant, one whose heart might be softened by the sight of anxious love; or if he were one who might be informed, enlightened, reasoned with; or one in whom a setting forth of character, need, or claim might awake interest; then would there be plain reason in prayer for another﻿—which yet, however disinterested and loving, must be degrading, as offered to one unworthy of prayer. But if we believe that God is the one unselfish, the one good being in the universe, and that his one design with his children is to make them perfect as he is perfect; if we believe that he not only would once give, but is always giving himself to us for our life; if we believe﻿—which once I heard a bishop decline to acknowledge﻿—that God does his best for *every* man; if also we believe that God knows every man’s needs, and will, for love’s sake, not spare one pang that may serve to purify the soul of one of his children; if we believe all this, how can we think he will in any sort alter his way with one because another prays for him? The prayer would arise from nothing in the person prayed for; why should it initiate a change in God’s dealing with him?
The argument I know not how to answer.

===Chinese===

子既能改变他的意图而不损坏什么：照样，我说，父也能；因为子除了他看见父所作的，什么也不作。
既发现有可能理解神会应允那些为自己祷告之人的祷告，那么我们当怎样看为别人的祷告呢？人满可以说：只为自己祷告确实很自私！但问题在这行动的用处，不在其品格：若其中有善，就让我们为一切我们觉得能为之祷告的人祷告；但关于为别人的祷告，是否找得到如为自己祷告那样的合理根据？根据变了——若应允祷告的合宜性在于祷告者的祷告：领受所需的姿态不属于那些*为其*代求的人，而属于那*借其*代求的人。那么为别人祷告还有什么合宜性？神会因我们的求而给另一个人他本来不给的东西吗？若这事能不经那人自己作成，他岂不会不经第二个人就作成吗？神若是一位暴君——一位见了焦灼之爱会心软的；或是一位可以被告知、被启发、可以与之讲理的；或是一位陈明品格、需要或主张就能唤起其兴趣的——那么为别人祷告就有明白的理性——然而这样的祷告，无论多么无私、多么有爱，献于一位不配祷告的对象，必是贬降。但我们若信神是宇宙中唯一无私的、唯一善的存有，他对他儿女的唯一设计是要他们完全如他完全；我们若信他不仅曾一次赐下、而且一直把自己赐给我们作生命；我们若信——这话我曾听一位主教拒绝承认——神为*每一个*人作他最好的；我们又若信神知道每个人的需要，且为爱的缘故，不免去任何一样可用来炼净他一个儿女之灵魂的痛苦；我们若信这一切，又怎能想他会因另一个人为他祷告而以任何方式改变他待他的方式？那祷告将不出于被代求者里面的任何东西；它为什么该发起神待他方式的一个改变？
这论证我不知怎样回答。

I can only, in the face of it, and feeling all the difficulty, say, and say again, “Yet I believe I may pray for my friend﻿—for my enemy﻿—for anybody! Yet and yet, there is, there must be some genuine, essential good and power in the prayer of one man for another to the maker of both﻿—and that just because their maker is perfect, not less than very God.” I shall not bring authority to bear, for authority can at best but make us believe reason there, it cannot make us see it. The difficulty remains the same even when we hear the Lord himself pray to his Father for those the Father loves because they have received his Son﻿—loves therefore with a special love, as the foremost in faith, the elect of the world﻿—loves not merely because they must die if he did not love them, but loves from the deeps of divine approval. Those who believe in Jesus will be satisfied, in the face of the incomprehensible, that in what he does reason and right must lie; but not therefore do we understand. At the same time, though I cannot explain, I can show some ground upon which, even had he not been taught to do so, but left alone with his heart, a man might yet, I think, pray for another.
If God has made us to love like himself, and like himself long to help; if there are for whom we, like him, would give our lives to lift them from the evil gulf of their ungodliness; if the love in us would, for the very easing of the love he kindled, gift another﻿—like himself who chooses and cherishes even the love that pains him; if, in the midst of a sore need to bless, to give, to help, we are aware of an utter impotence; if the fire burns and cannot out; and if all our hope for ourselves lies in God﻿—what is there for us, what can we think of, what do, but go to God?﻿—what but go to him with this our own difficulty and need? And where is the natural refuge, there must be the help. There can be no need for which he has no supply. The best argument that he has help, is that we have need. If I can be helped through my friend, I think God will take the thing up, and do what I cannot do﻿—help my friend that I may be helped﻿—perhaps help me to help him. You see, in praying for another we pray for ourselves﻿—for the relief of the needs of our love; it is not prayer for another alone, and thus it comes under the former kind.

===Chinese===

我只能面对它、感受全部难处，还是说、再说：“然而我信我可以为我的朋友祷告——为我的仇敌祷告——为任何人祷告！然而、然而，在一个人为另一个人向两者的造者所作的祷告里，有、也必有某种真实的、本质的善与大能——恰恰因为他们的造者是完全的，不少于非常之神。”我不愿引权威压阵，因为权威至多只能叫我们信那里有理性，不能叫我们看见它。难处依旧，即使我们听见主自己向父为那些人祷告——父爱他们，因为他们领受了他的子；因此是以特殊的爱爱他们，作为信心之首、世界的选民；爱他们不只是因为他们若不被爱就必须死，而是从属神嘉许的深处爱他们。信耶稣的人面对不可领悟之事会满足于：他所行的里面必有理性与正当；但我们并不因此就明白。同时，虽不能解释，我能指出一个根据，使一个人纵未受教导、只与自己的心独处时，我想，也仍会为别人祷告。
神既造我们像他那样爱、像他那样切慕帮助；既然有那样一些人，我们像他一样，肯舍命把他们从他们不敬虔的恶渊里提起；既然我们里面的爱，为缓释他所点燃的那爱的缘故，肯恩赐另一个人——像他自己那样，连那使他痛苦的爱也拣选、也珍爱；既然在极切的祝福、给予、帮助的需要中，我们察觉全然的无能；火既燃烧而不能出；我们为自己的一切盼望既都在神里——我们还有什么可作的、可想的，除了到神那里去？——除了带着我们自己的难处与需要到他那里去？哪里是天然的避所，哪里就必有帮助。他不会有一个需用是没有供应的。他有帮助的最好论证，就是我们有需要。我若能借我的朋友得帮助，我想神会把这事接过去，作我所不能作的——帮助我的朋友、叫我可以得帮助——或许帮助我去帮助他。你看，为别人祷告时我们正为自己祷告——为我们爱之需要的舒缓祷告；它不只是单为别人的祷告，因而归入前一类。

Would God give us love, the root of power, in us, and leave that love, whereby he himself creates, altogether helpless in us? May he not at least expedite something for our prayers? Where he could not alter, he could perhaps expedite, in view of some help we might then be able to give. If he desires that we should work with him, that work surely helps him!
There are some things for which the very possibility of supposing them are an argument; but I think I can go a little farther here, and imagine at least the *where* if not the *how*, the divine conditions in which the help for another in answer to prayer is born, the divine region in which its possibility must dwell.
God is ever seeking to lift us up into the sharing of his divine nature; God’s kings, such men, namely, as with Jesus have borne witness to the truth, share his glory even on the throne of the Father. See the grandeur of the creative love of the Holy! nothing less will serve it than to have his children, through his and their suffering, share the throne of his glory! If such be the perfection of the Infinite, should that perfection bring him under bonds and difficulties, and not rather set him freer to do the thing he would in the midst of opposing forces? If his glory be in giving himself, and we must share therein, giving ourselves, why should we not begin here and now? If he would have his children fellow-workers with him; if he has desired and willed that not only by the help of his eternal Son, but by the help also of the children who through him have been born from above, other and still other children shall be brought to his knee, to his fireside, to the plenty of his house, why should he not have kept some margin of room wherein their prayers may work for those whom they have to help, who are of the same life as they? I cannot tell how, but may not those prayers in some way increase God’s opportunity for working his best and highest will? Dealing with his children, the good ones may add to his power with the not yet good﻿—add to his means of helping them. One way is clear: the prayer will react upon the mind that prays, its light will grow, will shine the brighter, and draw and enlighten the more. But there must be more in the thing.

But will not any good parent find some way of granting the prayer of the child who comes to him, saying, “Papa, this is my brother’s birthday: I have nothing to give him, and I do love him so! could you give me something to give him, or give him something for me?”
“Still, could not God have given the gift without the prayer? And why should the good of anyone depend on the prayer of another?”
I can only answer with the return question, “Why should my love be powerless to help another?” But we must not tie God to our measures of time, or think he has forgotten that prayer even which, apparently unanswered, we have forgotten. Death is not an impervious wall; through it, beyond it, go the prayers. It is possible we may have some to help in the next world because we have prayed for them in this: will it not be a boon to them to have an old friend to their service? I but speculate and suggest. What I see and venture to say is this: If in God we live and move and have our being; if the very possibility of loving lies in this, that we exist in and by the live air of love, namely God himself, we must in this very fact be nearer to each other than by any bodily proximity or interchange of help; and if prayer is like a pulse that sets this atmosphere in motion, we must then by prayer come closer to each other than are the parts of our body by their complex nerve-telegraphy. Surely, in the Eternal, hearts are never parted! surely, through the Eternal, a heart that loves and seeks the good of another, must hold that other within reach! Surely the system of things would not be complete in relation to the best thing in it﻿—love itself, if love had no help in prayer. If I love and cannot help, does not my heart move me to ask him to help who loves and can?﻿—him without whom life would be to me nothing, without whom I should neither love nor care to pray!﻿—will he answer, “Child, do not trouble me; I am already doing all I can”?

===Chinese===

祷告在其完全的观念里，既是升入永恒者的意志，父的帮助岂不能与孩子的祷告合为一，并且为着他怀中之人的祷告，出去到那还不愿被举到他怀抱之人的身上？神自己不能一下子把儿女带进他怀中，且除非借他自己的与他们的受苦，全然不能。但哪位好父母不会想法应允那来到他面前的孩子的祷告：“爸爸，今天是我哥哥的生日：我没有东西给他，我又那么爱他！你能不能给我一样东西让我给他，或者替我给他一样东西？”
“可是，神岂不能不借祷告就把礼物给了？又为什么该有谁的好处系于另一个人的祷告？”
我只能以反问回答：“为什么我的爱该无力帮助另一个人？”但我们不可把神捆在我们对时间的量度上，也不可以为他忘了那看来未蒙应允、连我们也忘了的祷告。死亡不是一堵不透水的墙；祷告穿过它、越过它而行。有可能，我们在来世会有一些人要帮助，因为我们今生为他们祷告过：对他们，有一位旧友可供差遣，岂非恩惠？我不过是猜测与提示。我所看见、所敢说的是：我们若在神里面生活、动作、存留；若爱的可能性正在于我们存在于、且凭借爱的活空气——就是神自己——那么我们必在这事实本身里，比任何身体的临近或帮助的交换更彼此相近；而祷告若像一道使这大气运动的脉搏，那么我们借祷告彼此相近，必过于我们身体各部分借其复杂的神经电报而相近。确实，在永恒者里面，心从不分离！确实，借永恒者，一颗爱着、寻求另一人之善的心，必把那人持在可及之内！确实，事物的系统若就其中最好的东西——爱本身——而言，倘若爱在祷告中没有帮助，便不完整。我若爱而不能帮助，我的心岂不催我求那爱而又能的帮助者？——求那位没有他生命于我便为虚无、没有他我既不会爱也不会想祷告的？——他会回答说：“孩子，不要搅扰我；我已经在作我一切所能作的”吗？

===Original===

If such answer came, who that loved would not be content to be nowhere in the matter? But how if the eternal, limitless Love, the unspeakable, self-forgetting God-devotion, which, demanding all, gives all, should say, “Child, I have been doing all I could; but now you are come, I shall be able to do more! here is a corner for you, my little one: push at this thing to get it out of the way”! How if he should answer, “Pray on, my child; I am hearing you; it goes through me in help to him. We are of one mind about it; I help and you help. I shall have you all safe home with me by and by! There is no fear, only we must work, and not lose heart. Go, and let your light so shine before men that they may see your good things, and glorify me by knowing that I am light and no darkness”!﻿—what then? Oh that lovely picture by Michelangelo, with the young ones and the little ones come to help God to make Adam!
But it may be that the answer to prayer will come in a shape that seems a refusal. It may come even in an increase of that from which we seek deliverance. I know of one who prayed to love better: a sore division came between﻿—out of which at length rose a dawn of tenderness.
Our vision is so circumscribed, our theories are so small﻿—the garment of them not large enough to wrap us in; our faith so continually fashions itself to the fit of our dwarf intellect, that there is endless room for rebellion against ourselves: we must not let our poor knowledge limit our not so poor intellect, our intellect limit our faith, our faith limit our divine hope; reason must humbly watch over all﻿—reason, the candle of the Lord.
There are some who would argue for prayer, not on the ground of any possible answer to be looked for, but because of the good to be gained in the spiritual attitude of the mind in praying. There are those even who, not believing in any ear to hear, any heart to answer, will yet pray. They say it does them good; they pray to nothing at all, but they get spiritual benefit.
I will not contradict their testimony. So needful is prayer to the soul that the mere attitude of it may encourage a good mood. Verily to pray to that which is not, is in logic a folly; yet the good that, they say, comes of it, may rebuke the worse folly of their unbelief, for it indicates that prayer is natural, and how could it be natural if inconsistent with the very mode of our being?

===Chinese===

若这样的回答来到，凡爱着的谁不甘愿在这事上毫无地位？但若那位永恒无限的爱、那说不出的、忘我的神圣挚爱——要求一切又给出一切——说：“孩子，我一直在作我一切所能的；如今你来了，我就能作更多了！这里有一个角落给你，我的小家伙：来推这东西，把它挪开”！他若回答说：“继续祷告，我的孩子；我正垂听你；它穿过我、化为对他人的帮助。我们在此事上同心；我帮助，你也帮助。不久我要把你们全都平安带回家！不要怕，只要我们必须作工、不可灰心。去吧，让你们的光这样照在人前，叫他们看见你们的好行为，便借着认识我是光、不是黑暗来荣耀我”！——那又如何？哦，米开朗基罗那幅可爱的画：少年们与孩童们来帮神造亚当！
但祷告的回答或会取一个看似拒绝的形状。它甚至或会以我们所求解脱之事的加增而来。我认识一个人祷告求爱得更好：一场痛苦的分裂随之而来——从其中终于升起一抹温柔的曙光。
我们的视野如此受限，我们的理论如此之小——它们的衣裳不够大，裹不住我们；我们的信心如此不断地按我们侏儒智力的尺寸裁剪自己，以致总有无限余地反抗我们自己：我们不可让我们贫乏的知识限制我们不那么贫乏的智力，让智力限制我们的信心，让信心限制我们属神的盼望；理性必须谦卑地看顾一切——理性，主的烛。
有人为祷告辩护，不是根据任何可期待的应允，而是根据祷告时心思的属灵姿态可得的益处。甚至有人不信有耳垂听、有心应允，却仍祷告。他们说祷告于他们有益；他们向虚无祷告，却得到属灵的好处。
我不反驳他们的见证。祷告于灵魂如此必需，以致单单它的姿态也能扶持一种好的心境。向那不存在者祷告，在逻辑上确实是愚妄；但他们说从中出来的善，可以责备他们不信的更重愚妄，因为它表明祷告是自然的；而它若与我们存有的根本方式不一致，又怎能是自然的？

===Original===

Theirs is a better way than that of those who, believing there is a God, but not believing that he will give any answer to their prayers, yet pray to him; that is more foolish and more immoral than praying to the No-god. Whatever the God be to whom they pray, their prayer is a mockery of him, of themselves, of the truth.
On the other hand, let God give no assent to the individual prayer, let the prayer even be for something nowise good enough to be a gift of God, yet the soul that prays will get good of its prayer, if only in being thereby brought a little nearer to the Father, and making way for coming again. Prayer does react in good upon the praying soul, irrespective of answer. But to pray for the sake of the prayer, and without regard to there being no one to hear, would to me indicate a nature not merely illogical but morally false, did I not suspect a vague undetected apprehension of a Something diffused through the All of existence, and some sort of shadowiest communion therewith.
There are moods of such satisfaction in God that a man may feel as if nothing were left to pray for, as if he had but to wait with patience for what the Lord would work; there are moods of such hungering desire, that petition is crushed into an inarticulate crying; and there is a communion with God that asks for nothing, yet asks for everything. This last is the very essence of prayer, though not petition. It is possible for a man, not indeed to believe in God, but to believe that there is a God, and yet not desire to enter into communion with him; but he that prays and does not faint will come to recognize that to talk with God is more than to have all prayers granted﻿—that it is the end of all prayer, granted or refused. And he who seeks the Father more than anything he can give, is likely to have what he asks, for he is not likely to ask amiss.
Even such as ask amiss may sometimes have their prayers answered. The Father will never give the child a stone that asks for bread; but I am not sure that he will never give the child a stone that asks for a stone. If the Father say, “My child, that is a stone; it is no bread”; and the child answer, “I am sure it is bread; I want it”; may it not be well he should try his bread?

===Chinese===

他们的路，比那些信有神、却不信他会给他们的祷告任何应允、却仍向他祷告之人的路更好；那比向无神祷告更愚妄、更不道德。无论他们向什么神祷告，他们的祷告是对他、对他们自己、对真理的嘲弄。
另一方面，即使神不给个别祷告以同意，即使那祷告甚至是全然配不上作神之礼物的东西，那祷告的灵魂仍将从它的祷告得着益处，哪怕只在借此稍稍靠近父、为再来开路这一点上。祷告确实以善反作用于祷告的灵魂，无论应允与否。但为祷告本身的缘故祷告、而不顾没有谁在垂听，于我而言将表明一种不仅不合逻辑、而且在道德上虚假的天性——若非我猜想有一种朦胧未察的领会，领会到某种弥漫于存在之万有的东西、以及与它某种最影影绰绰的相通。
有那样在神里满足的心境，人可以觉得仿佛再没有什么可求的，仿佛只需耐心等候主要成全的；也有那样饥慕的心境，祈求被压成不成声的呼喊；还有一种与神的相通，无所求、却无所不求。这最后一种正是祷告的本质，虽不是祈求。一个人可能——确实不信神，而信有一位神——却不渴望进入与他的相通；但那祷告而不灰心的人，终将认识：与神交谈，比一切祷告蒙应允更宝贵——它是祷告一切的目的，无论应允或拒绝。凡寻求父过于他所能给之任何物的，多半要得着所求的，因为他多半不会妄求。
连妄求的人有时也蒙应允。孩子求饼，父永不会给他石头；但孩子求石头，父是否永不给石头，我不敢肯定。父若说：“我的孩子，那是石头；不是饼”；孩子若回答：“我确信是饼；我要它”；让他试试他的饼，岂不好吗？

===Original===

But now for another point in the parable, where I think I can give some help﻿—I mean the Lord’s apparent recognition of delay in the answering of prayer: in the very structure of the parable he seems to take delay for granted, and says notwithstanding, “He will avenge them speedily!”
The reconciling conclusion is, that God loses no time, though the answer may not be immediate.
He may delay because it would not be safe to give us at once what we ask: we are not ready for it. To give ere we could truly receive, would be to destroy the very heart and hope of prayer, to cease to be our Father. The delay itself may work to bring us nearer to our help, to increase the desire, perfect the prayer, and ripen the receptive condition.
Again, not from any straitening in God, but either from our own condition and capacity, or those of the friend for whom we pray, time may be necessary to the working out of the answer. God is limited by regard for our best; our best implies education; in this we must ourselves have a large share; this share, being human, involves time. And perhaps, indeed, the better the gift we pray for, the more time is necessary to its arrival. To give us the spiritual gift we desire, God may have to begin far back in our spirit, in regions unknown to us, and do much work that we can be aware of only in the results; for our consciousness is to the extent of our being but as the flame of the volcano to the world-gulf whence it issues: in the gulf of our unknown being God works behind our consciousness. With his holy influence, with his own presence, the one thing for which most earnestly we cry, he may be approaching our consciousness from behind, coming forward through regions of our darkness into our light, long before we begin to be aware that he is answering our request﻿—has answered it, and is visiting his child. To avenge speedily must mean to make no delay beyond what is absolutely necessary, to begin the moment it is possible to begin. Because the Son of Man did not appear for thousands of years after men began to cry out for a Saviour, shall we imagine he did not come the first moment it was well he should come? Can we doubt that to come a moment sooner would have been to delay, not to expedite, his kingdom? For anything that needs a process, to begin to act at once is to be speedy.

===Chinese===

但现在谈比喻中的另一点，我想我能给些帮助——我指主对祷告应允之迟延的表面承认：在比喻的结构本身里，他似乎把迟延视为当然，却仍说：“他要快快地给他们伸冤了！”
调和的结论是：神不耽误一刻，虽然回答未必即刻。
他可能迟延，因为立刻给我们所求的并不安全：我们还没有预备好。在我们还不能真实领受之先就给，会毁掉祷告的心与盼望，他就不再作我们的父。迟延本身或许正作用来把我们带到帮助更近，加增愿望，成全祷告，使领受的状态成熟。
再者，不是由于神有任何窘迫，而是由于我们自己的光景与容量、或我们为之祷告之朋友的光景与容量，时间或许为回答的作成所必需。神受他对我们至善的顾念所限；我们的至善意味着教育；在其中我们自己必须承担大份；这份既属人，就涉及时间。而确实，或许我们祷告所求的礼物越好，它的到达所需的时间就越多。要给我们所愿的属灵礼物，神或许必须从我们灵里很靠后的地方、在我们不认识的境界里开始，作许多我们只能从结果察觉的工；因为我们的意识，就我们存有的范围而言，不过如火山口的火焰之于它所自出的世界深渊：在我们未知存有的深渊里，神在我们的意识后面作工。以他圣洁的影响、以他自己的同在——我们最恳切呼求的那一样——他或许正从后面接近我们的意识，穿过我们黑暗的诸境界进入我们的光，远在我们开始察觉他在应允我们的请求——已经应允了、正在眷访他的孩子——之前。快快伸冤必是指：不作绝对必要之外的迟延，在可以开始的那一刻开始。人子既在人类开始呼求救主之后数千年才显现，我们就该想象他没有在宜于来临的第一刻来临吗？我们能否认早来一刻会是迟延、而非加速他的国吗？凡需要过程的事，立刻开始行动就是快。

===Original===

God does not put off like the unrighteous judge; he does not delay until irritated by the prayers of the needy; he will hear while they are yet speaking; yea, before they call he will answer.
The Lord uses words without anxiety as to the misuse of them by such as do not search after his will in them; and the word “avenge” may be simply retained from the parable without its special meaning therein; yet it suggests a remark or two.
Of course, no prayer for any revenge that would gratify the selfishness of our nature, a thing to be burned out of us by the fire of God, needs think to be heard. Be sure, when the Lord prayed his Father to forgive those who crucified him, he uttered his own wish and his Father’s will at once: God will never punish according to the abstract abomination of sin, as if men knew what they were doing. “Vengeance is mine,” he says: with a right understanding of it, we might as well pray for God’s vengeance as for his forgiveness; that vengeance is, to destroy the sin﻿—to make the sinner abjure and hate it; nor is there any satisfaction in a vengeance that seeks or effects less. The man himself must turn against himself, and so be for himself. If nothing else will do, then hellfire; if less will do, whatever brings repentance and self-repudiation, is God’s repayment.
Friends, if any prayers are offered against us; if the vengeance of God be cried out for, because of some wrong you or I have done, God grant us his vengeance! Let us not think that we shall get off!
But perhaps the Lord was here thinking, not of persecution, or any form of human wrong, but of the troubles that most trouble his true disciple; and the suggestion is comforting to those whose foes are within them, for, if so, then he recognizes the evils of self, against which we fight, not as parts of ourselves, but as our foes, on which he will avenge the true self that is at strife with them. And certainly no evil is, or ever could be, of the essential being and nature of the creature God made! The thing that is not good, however associated with our being, is against that being, not of it﻿—is its enemy, on which we need to be avenged. When we fight, he will avenge. Till we fight, evil shall have dominion over us, a dominion to make us miserable; other than miserable can no one be, under the yoke of a nature contrary to his own.

===Chinese===

神不像那不义之官那样拖延；他不等到被穷乏人的祷告惹烦才垂听；他们还说话的时候他就垂听；是的，他们还没求告，他就应允。
主使用词语，并不担心那不寻求他旨意的人滥用它们；“伸冤”一词或许只是沿自比喻、未带其中特殊的意义；然而它提示一两句评语。
当然，凡为满足我们天性之自私的任何复仇——一件要被神的火从我们里面烧掉的东西——所作的祷告，休想蒙垂听。可以确信，当主求父赦免那些钉他的人时，他同时说出了自己的愿望与父的旨意：神永不会按罪的抽象可憎来刑罚，仿佛人知道自己在作什么。“伸冤在我，”他说：对它有正当的理解，我们求神的伸冤与求他的赦免同样可以；那伸冤就是：毁掉罪——使罪人弃绝它、恨恶它；少于这的伸冤，既不寻求这个也不成全这个，其中没有任何满足。人自己必须转过来反对自己，从而才是为着自己。若非这样不行，那么地狱（hell）之火；若较少即可，凡带来悔改与自我弃绝的，都是神的报偿。
朋友们，若有祷告是反对我们的；若因你我所作的某桩错事而有人呼求神的伸冤，愿神赐我们他的伸冤！不要以为我们能逃脱！
但或许主在这里所想的不是逼迫或任何形式的人间错待，而是最搅扰他真门徒的那些苦难；而这提示安慰了那些仇敌在他们里面的人，因为若如此，他就承认自我的诸恶——我们与之争战的——不是我们自己的部分，而是我们的仇敌，他要为那与它们交战的真自我向它们伸冤。而确实，没有任何恶是、或曾经能是神所造之受造物的本质存有与本性！那不善之物，无论与我们的存有关联多深，是敌对那存有，不是属于它——是它的仇敌，我们需要向它伸冤。当我们争战，他要伸冤。我们不争战，恶就必辖制我们，一个使我们悲惨的辖制；凡在一个与自己本性相反的轭下，没有人能不悲惨。

===Original===

Comfort thyself then, who findest thine own heart and soul, or rather the things that move therein, too much for thee: God will avenge his own elect. He is not delaying; he is at work for thee. Only thou must pray, and not faint. Ask, ask; it shall be given you. Seek most the best things; to ask for the best things is to have them; the seed of them is in you, or you could not ask for them.
But from whatever quarter come our troubles, whether from the world outside or the world inside, still let us pray. In his own right way, the only way that could satisfy us, for we are of his kind, will God answer our prayers with help. He will avenge us of our adversaries, and that speedily. Only let us take heed that we be adversaries to no man, but fountains of love and forgiving tenderness to all. And from no adversary, either on the way with us, or haunting the secret chamber of our hearts, let us hope to be delivered till we *have paid the last farthing*.

===Chinese===

那么，你若发现自己的心与灵魂——或毋宁说在其中运行的诸事物——非你所能应付，就以此自慰：神要为他自己的选民伸冤。他没有迟延；他正为你作工。只是你必须祷告，不可灰心。求，求；就必给你。最要寻求至善之物；求至善之物就是拥有它们；它们的种子在你里面，否则你不能求它们。
但无论我们的烦恼从哪一方来——从外面的世界还是里面的世界——让我们仍然祷告。神必以他自己正当的方式——那唯一能满足我们的方式，因为我们出于他的类——以帮助回答我们的祷告。他要为我们向我们的对头伸冤，而且快快地。只要我们小心不作任何人的对头，而作对一切人的爱与赦免之温柔的泉源。而无论对哪个对头——在路上与我们同行的、或在心中密室萦缠的——在我们还清最后一文钱（the last farthing）之前，不要指望得解脱。

### The Last Farthing / 最后一文钱
===Original===

> “Verily I say unto thee, thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.”

There is a thing wonderful and admirable in the parables, not readily grasped, but specially indicated by the Lord himself﻿—their unintelligibility to the mere intellect. They are addressed to the conscience and not to the intellect, to the will and not to the imagination. They are strong and direct but not definite. They are not meant to explain anything, but to rouse a man to the feeling, “I am not what I ought to be, I do not the thing I ought to do!” Many maundering interpretations may be given by the wise, with plentiful loss of labour, while the child who uses them for the necessity of walking in the one path will constantly receive light from them. The greatest obscuration of the words of the Lord, as of all true teachers, comes from those who give themselves to interpret rather than do them. Theologians have done more to hide the gospel of Christ than any of its adversaries. It was not for our understandings, but our will, that Christ came. He who does that which he sees, shall understand; he who is set upon understanding rather than doing, shall go on stumbling and mistaking and speaking foolishness. He has not that in him which can understand that kind. The gospel itself, and in it the parables of the Truth, are to be understood only by those who walk by what they find. It is he that runneth that shall read, and no other. It is not intended by the speaker of the parables that any other should know intellectually what, known but intellectually, would be for his injury﻿—what knowing intellectually he would imagine he had grasped, perhaps even appropriated. When the pilgrim of the truth comes on his journey to the region of the parable, he finds its interpretation. It is not a fruit or a jewel to be stored, but a well springing by the wayside.

There has been much cherishing of the evil fancy, often without its taking formal shape, that there is some way of getting out of the region of strict justice, some mode of managing to escape doing *all* that is required of us; but there is no such escape. Thou must be good; neither death nor any admittance into good company will make thee good; though, doubtless, if thou be willing and try, these and all other best helps will be given thee. There is no clothing in a robe of imputed righteousness, that poorest of legal cobwebs spun by spiritual spiders. To me it seems like an invention of well-meaning dullness to soothe insanity; and indeed it has proved a door of escape out of worse imaginations. It is apparently an old “doctrine”; for St. John seems to point at it where he says, “Little children, let no man lead you astray; he that doeth righteousness is righteous even as he is righteous.” Christ is our righteousness, not that we should escape punishment, still less escape being righteous, but as the live potent creator of righteousness in us, so that we, with our wills receiving his spirit, shall like him resist unto blood, striving against sin; shall know in ourselves, as he knows, what a lovely thing is righteousness, what a mean, ugly, unnatural thing is unrighteousness. He *is* our righteousness, and that righteousness is no fiction, no pretence, no imputation.

「你的本分——你的债。这件事你全弄错了。那人给不给你权利，对你（to you）是小事；你给不给他他的权利，对你是生死攸关。他还不还你以为他所欠的，你却必被追讨，还清你欠他的一切。你若欠他一镑，他欠你一百万，那么无论他还不还你那一百万，你必须还他那一镑；这里没有生意上的对抵。他若欠你爱却给你恨，你欠他爱，就仍须把爱还上。他未付你的爱、未行给你的公义、未给你的称赞、加于你的无凭判断，都不能豁免你所欠的未付之爱、未行之义、未给之称赞、妄下的判断这些债：这些极小的一文钱——更不必说世界自己也视为重害的诸债——无论他还不还你，你都必须还他。」
我们获赐相当一段时日去偿还，但危机必来——终究来得快——对那些未预备好的人，它总来得比预期更快——到了那危机，要求未蒙应允，监牢随之而至。
对神的每一样要求，道理相同：人拒付，就为自己造出一位必追讨他的对头——这是为人自己的缘故。你或你的生命若说「我不肯」，他就要亲自料理。有一座监牢，而我们对那监牢唯一知道的是：不等到完全清偿、还清最后一文钱，它的门不开。
神所追讨的主要债务，是那一切正当之根本的债——我们在心思、灵魂、存在里所欠的。我们里面凡能作对头或能造成对头的，凡能拦阻我们遵行神的旨意（the will of God）、或拦阻我们与同伴和好的，都必须交出。我们对神、对同伴的每一样关系，都必须诚心承认，当作真实去面对。较小的债——若有债可算小的话——自然随之而来。

===Original===

If the man acknowledge, and would pay if he could but cannot, the universe will be taxed to help him rather than he should continue unable. If the man accepts the will of God, he is the child of the Father, the whole power and wealth of the Father is for him, and the uttermost farthing will easily be paid. If the man denies the debt, or acknowledging does nothing towards paying it, then﻿—at last﻿—the prison! God in the dark can make a man thirst for the light, who never in the light sought but the dark. The cells of the prison may differ in degree of darkness; but they are all alike in this, that not a door opens but to payment. There is no day but the will of God, and he who is of the night cannot be forever allowed to roam the day; unfelt, unprized, the light must be taken from him, that he may know what the darkness is. When the darkness is perfect, when he is totally without the light he has spent the light in slaying, then will he know darkness.
I think I have seen from afar something of the final prison of all, the innermost cell of the debtor of the universe; I will endeavour to convey what I think it may be.
It is the vast outside; the ghastly dark beyond the gates of the city of which God is the light﻿—where the evil dogs go ranging, silent as the dark, for there is no sound any more than sight. The time of signs is over. Every sense has its signs, and they were all misused: there is no sense, no sign more﻿—nothing now by means of which to believe. The man wakes from the final struggle of death, in absolute loneliness﻿—such a loneliness as in the most miserable moment of deserted childhood he never knew. Not a hint, not a shadow of anything outside his consciousness reaches him. All is dark, dark and dumb; no motion﻿—not the breath of a wind! never a dream of change! not a scent from far-off field! nothing to suggest being or thing besides the man himself, no sign of God anywhere. God has so far withdrawn from the man, that he is conscious only of that from which he has withdrawn. In the midst of the live world he cared for nothing but himself; now in the dead world he is in God’s prison, his own separated self.

===Chinese===

人若承认，并愿意偿还只是无力偿还，那么与其让他继续无力，整个宇宙都必倾力相助。人若接受神的旨意，他就是父（the Father）的孩子，父全部的权能与财富都是为他的，那极小的一文钱必轻易还清。人若否认那债，或虽承认却不偿付分毫，那么——终究——监牢！在黑暗中，神能叫一个在光明里只寻求黑暗的人渴想光明。那监牢的各囚室昏暗程度或不同；但这一点上全都一样：非付款不开一门。除了神的旨意别无白昼；属黑夜的人不能永远被容许在白昼游荡；那光既无感觉、不受珍惜，就必从他夺去，使他知道黑暗是什么。当黑暗完全、当他全然失去那光——他曾耗费那光去杀害光——那时他将认识黑暗。
我想我远远望见了那终极监狱的一斑——宇宙债务人的最内囚室；我要努力把我以为它可能的情形传达出来。
那是浩瀚的外面；那以神为光之城的城门外可怖的黑暗——恶狗游荡之地，静默如黑暗，因为那里没有声音，正如没有视觉。记号的时代过去了。每种感官原有它的记号，而它们全被滥用了：不再有感官，不再有记号——如今再无凭以相信之物。那人从死亡的最后挣扎中醒来，处于绝对的孤独之中——那样的孤独，是他在被撇弃之童年最悲惨的时刻也不曾知道的。没有一丝暗示、一点阴影，是从他意识之外来的。全是黑暗，黑暗而哑寂；没有动静——没有一缕风息！绝无变化的梦影！没有远处田野的一缕气息！没有任何事物提示在他自己之外还有存在或事物，任何地方都没有神的记号。神从那人身上退隐到这般地步，以致他只意识到那已经退隐之物。在活的世界里他只顾自己；如今在死的世界里，他在神的监牢中——他自己那被隔绝的自我。

===Original===

He would not believe in God because he never saw God; now he doubts if there be such a thing as the face of a man﻿—doubts if he ever really saw one, ever anything more than dreamed of such a thing:﻿—he never came near enough to human being, to know what human being really was﻿—so may well doubt if human beings ever were, if ever he was one of them.
Next after doubt comes reasoning on the doubt: “The only one must be God! I know no one but myself: I must myself be God﻿—none else!” Poor helpless dumb devil!﻿—his own glorious lord god! Yea, he will imagine himself that same resistless force which, without his will, without his knowledge, is the law by which the sun burns, and the stars keep their courses, the strength that drives all the engines of the world. His fancy will give birth to a thousand fancies, which will run riot like the mice in a house but just deserted: he will call it creation, and *his*. Having no reality to set them beside, nothing to correct them by; the measured order, harmonious relations, and sweet graces of God’s world nowhere for him; what he thinks, will be, for lack of what God thinks, the man’s realities: what others can he have! Soon, misery will beget on imagination a thousand shapes of woe, which he will not be able to rule, direct, or even distinguish from real presences﻿—a whole world of miserable contradictions and cold-fever-dreams.
But no liveliest human imagination could supply adequate representation of what it would be to be left without a shadow of the presence of God. If God gave it, man could not understand it: he knows neither God nor himself in the way of the understanding. For not he who cares least about God was in this world ever left as God could leave him. I doubt if any man could continue following his wickedness from whom God had withdrawn.
The most frightful idea of what could, to his own consciousness, befall a man, is that he should have to lead an existence with which God had nothing to do. The thing could not be; for being that is caused, the causation ceasing, must of necessity cease. It is always in, and never out of God, that we can live and do. But I suppose the man so left that he seems to himself utterly alone, yet, alas!

===Chinese===

他从前不肯信神，因为他从未见过神；如今他怀疑是否有过人面这样的东西——怀疑自己是否真见过一张脸，还是不过梦见过这样的东西：——他从未与人类亲近到知道人类究竟是什么——所以尽可怀疑人类是否存在过，怀疑自己是否曾是其中一员。
怀疑之后，随之而来的是对怀疑的推理：「独一者必是神！除我自己我不认识任何存在：那么我自己必是神——别无他者！」可怜无助的哑巴魔鬼！——自己那荣耀的君王神！是啊，他还要把自己想象成那无可抗拒之力本身——不凭他的意志、不因他的认识，正是那力作太阳燃烧、众星守轨的法则，是推动世上一切机关的力量。他的幻想将生养千般幻想，像刚被遗弃的屋子里的老鼠那样横行：他要称之为创造，且是他自己的创造。没有实在可与之并列，没有可资校正之物；神之世界那有分寸的秩序、和谐的关系与甜美的恩典，于他无处可寻；于是，因缺乏神所思想的，他所思想的就成了此人的实在：除此之外他还能有什么！不久，苦难要在想象中生出千般祸殃之形，他将无力统御、指引，甚至无力把它们与真实的临在区分开来——一整个悲惨矛盾与寒热之梦的世界。
然而，即便最活跃的人类想象，也无法充分描画被撇下而毫无神临在之影会是怎样。神若将它给人，人也无从领会：他既不循悟性之路认识神，也不循悟性之路认识自己。因为在世上，连最不把神放在心上的人，也从未被撇弃到神所能撇弃的地步。我怀疑，神一旦退隐，是否还有人能继续行他的恶。
对人的自觉而言可能临到他的事，最可怖的观念莫过于：他不得不过一种与神毫无关涉的存在。这不可能成立；因为被造而有之物，其因既绝，必随之而绝。我们能生活能行事，始终是在神之内，从不在神之外。但我且设想那人被撇到自称绝对孤独的地步，然而，唉！

with himself﻿—smallest interchange of thought, feeblest contact of existence, dullest reflection from other being, impossible: in such evil case I believe the man would be glad to come in contact with the worst-loathed insect: it would be a shape of life, something beyond and besides his own huge, void, formless being! I imagine some such feeling in the prayer of the devils for leave to go into the swine. His worst enemy, could he but be aware of him, he would be ready to worship. For the misery would be not merely the absence of all being other than his own self, but the fearful, endless, unavoidable presence of that self. Without the correction, the reflection, the support of other presences, being is not merely unsafe, it is a horror﻿—for anyone but God, who is his own being. For him whose idea is God’s, and the image of God, his own being is far too fragmentary and imperfect to be anything like good company. It is the lovely creatures God has made all around us, in them giving us himself, that, until we know him, save us from the frenzy of aloneness﻿—for that aloneness is Self, Self, Self. The man who minds only himself must at last go mad if God did not interfere.
Can there be any way out of the misery? Will the soul that could not believe in God, with all his lovely world around testifying of him, believe when shut in the prison of its own lonely, weary all-and-nothing? It would for a time try to believe that it was indeed nothing, a mere glow of the setting sun on a cloud of dust, a paltry dream that dreamed itself﻿—then, ah, if only the dream might dream that it was no more! that would be the one thing to hope for. Self-loathing, and that for no sin, from no repentance, from no vision of better, would begin and grow and grow; and to what it might not come no soul can tell﻿—of essential, original misery, uncompromising self-disgust! Only, then, if a being be capable of self-disgust, is there not some room for hope﻿—as much as a pinch of earth in the cleft of a rock might yield for the growth of a pine? Nay, there must be hope while there is existence; for where there is existence there must be God; and God is forever good, nor can be other than good. But alas, the distance from the light! Such a soul is at the farthest verge of life’s negation!﻿—no, not the farthest!

只剩他自己——最微小的一点思想交流、最微弱的一点存在接触、从别的存在发来的最黯淡的一点反映，都不可能：处于这样凶恶的境地，我相信这人必乐于接触哪怕他最厌恶的虫豸：那将是一个生命的形——在他那庞大、空洞、无形的存在之外并之上的什么东西！我想，群鬼恳求进入猪群的那祷告（prayer）里，就有些这样的感受。他最大的仇敌，他若还能觉察到，他都几乎要敬拜了。因为那苦难不仅是失去自我以外的一切存在，更是那自我可怕的、无尽的、无从躲避的在场。没有别的临在的校正、反映与扶持，存在就不仅是不安全的——它是恐怖——对谁都如此，唯独对那自有永有的神除外。对那观念出于神、又是神之形像的人，他自己的存在太破碎、太不完全，绝不能算是好同伴。正是神在我们四围所造的那些可爱造物——在其中把他自己赐给我们——在我们认识他之前，救我们脱离独自一人的癫狂；因为那种独自就是自我、自我、自我。只顾自己的人，若神不干预，至终必发疯。
这苦难可有出路吗？那灵魂在神一切可爱世界的环绕见证之下尚且不能信神，如今被关在它自己孤独、疲竭的一切皆无之狱中，倒能信吗？有一阵它要竭力相信自己的确是虚无——不过是落日在尘云上的一抹余晖，一场梦见自己的鄙陋之梦——继而，啊，但愿这梦能梦见自己不复存在！那倒是唯一可指望的事了。自我厌憎——并非因罪，不因悔改，不因得见更美——要开始生长，越长越大；它能长到什么地步，没有魂能说尽——本质的、本源的苦难，决不妥协的自我厌弃！不过，一个存在若能有自我厌弃，岂不就有几分盼望的余地——如同石缝里的一撮土足供一棵松树生长那样？不，只要存在尚在，就必有盼望；因为哪里有存在，哪里就必有神；而神永远良善，也不能不良善。可是唉，离光何其远！这样的灵魂正处于生命之否定的最远边缘！——不，还不是最远的！

a man is nearer heaven when in deepest hell than just ere he begins to reap the reward of his doings﻿—for he is in a condition to receive the smallest show of the life that is, as a boon unspeakable. All his years in the world he received the endless gifts of sun and air, earth and sea and human face divine, as things that came to him because that was their way, and there was no one to prevent them; now the poorest thinning of the darkness he would hail as men of old the glow of a descending angel; it would be as a messenger from God. Not that he would think of God! it takes long to think of God; but hope, not yet seeming hope, would begin to dawn in his bosom, and the thinner darkness would be as a cave of light, a refuge from the horrid self of which he used to be so proud.
A man may well imagine it impossible ever to think so unpleasantly of himself! But he has only to let things go, and he will make it the real, right, natural way to think of himself. True, all I have been saying is imaginary; but our imagination is made to mirror truth; all the things that appear in it are more or less after the model of things that are; I suspect it is the region whence issues prophecy; and when we are true it will mirror nothing but truth. I deal here with the same light and darkness the Lord dealt with, the same St. Paul and St. John and St. Peter and St. Jude dealt with. Ask yourself whether the faintest dawn of even physical light would not be welcome to such a soul as some refuge from the dark of the justly hated self.
And the light would grow and grow across the awful gulf between the soul and its haven﻿—its repentance﻿—for repentance is the first pressure of the bosom of God; and in the twilight, struggling and faint, the man would feel, faint as the twilight, another thought beside his, another thinking Something nigh his dreary self﻿—perhaps the man he had most wronged, most hated, most despised﻿—and would be glad that someone, whoever, was near him: the man he had most injured, and was most ashamed to meet, would be a refuge from himself﻿—oh, how welcome!
So might I imagine a thousand steps up from the darkness, each a little less dark, a little nearer the light﻿—but, ah, the weary way! He cannot come out until he have paid the uttermost farthing! Repentance once begun, however, may grow more and more rapid!

人在最深的地狱里，反倒比他刚开始收割自己行为之报应的前一刻更接近天堂——因为他这时所处的境地，能领受那真实生命哪怕最微弱的一线显现，视之为无以言表的恩惠。在世上的一切年日里，他把阳光与空气、大地与海洋、以及人脸上属天的容光，这些无穷的恩赐，都当作照例落到他头上的东西照单全收，因为那些事物素来如此，也没有谁拦阻它们；如今，哪怕黑暗最微薄的一丝稀薄，他也要像古人迎候降临天使的光辉那样迎候它；那将如同从神那里差来的使者。倒不是说他就会想到神！想到神需要很长的时间；但盼望——虽还显不出是盼望——会开始在他胸中发亮，而那较为稀薄的黑暗将如同一穴光明，作他脱离那可憎之自我的避难所——那自我，他曾何等引以为豪。
人尽可以想，如此不快地想到自己是不可能的！但他只需放任自流，这就将成为他想到自己的真实的、正当的、自然而然的方式。诚然，我以上所说全是想象；但我们的想象力原是为映照真理而造的；其中显现的一切，多少都以实有之物为范本；我疑心它正是预言由此而出的疆域；而当我们真实无妄时，它将只映照真理。我在此论及的，正是主所论及的同一光与暗，圣保罗、圣约翰、圣彼得（Peter）与圣犹大所论及的同一光与暗。问问你自己：对这样一个灵魂，哪怕只是肉眼之光最微弱的破晓，岂不也会受它欢迎，当作躲避那理当憎恶之自我的黑暗的某种避难所？
而光将愈照愈亮，横越那隔在灵魂与其港湾——它的悔改——之间的可怖鸿沟；因为悔改是神的胸怀最初的贴近。在暮色中，挣扎而微弱，那人将感觉到——微弱如暮色——自己的念头之外还有另一个念头，另一个有思想的存在靠近他凄凉的自我——也许正是他亏负最深、憎恨最切、鄙夷最甚的那个人——而他将高兴有人在他身旁，不管那人是谁：他伤害最深、最羞于相见的那个人，将成为他躲避自己的避难所——哦，那是何等受欢迎啊！
这样，我可以想象出黑暗之上的一千级台阶，一级比一级稍亮，稍近光明——可是，啊，这疲倦的路程！不还清那极小的一文钱（the uttermost farthing），他总不得出来！然而悔改一经开始，就可能愈来愈迅疾！

If God once get a willing hold, if with but one finger he touch the man’s self, swift as possibility will he draw him from the darkness into the light. Out of the abyss into which he cast himself, refusing to be the heir of God, he must rise and be raised. To the heart of God, the one and only goal of the human race﻿—the refuge and home of all and each, he must set out and go, or the last glimmer of humanity will die from him. 神一旦得着一个乐意的把柄，哪怕只用一根指头触及那人的自我，他必快如可能，把他从黑暗中拉进光明。因为这孤苦、自取败亡的可怜人受造的目的，本是要作神的孩子，有分于神的性情，作神的后嗣，并与基督同作后嗣。从他因拒绝作神的后嗣而自投的深渊里，他必须起来，也必被举起。向神的心——人类唯一的目标，一切人并每一个人的避难所与家园——他必须动身前行，否则人性最后的一线微光必从他里面熄灭。凡要活着的，必须不再是奴仆，而成为神的孩子。没有一个可以与不敬虔调情而不至致命的中途歇脚之处。被投入我所力图想象的那种监狱的人，无论或多或少，人的灵魂无论身在其中或其外，都绝无别的拯救，唯有还清最后一文钱，成为谦卑、痛悔、舍己——如此领受儿子的名分，并学会呼喊：天父（Father）！

### Abba, Father! / 阿爸，父！
===Original===

> “﻿—the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.”

The hardest, gladdest thing in the world is, to cry *Father!* from a full heart. I would help whom I may to call thus upon the Father.
There are things in all forms of the systematic teaching of Christianity to check this outgoing of the heart﻿—with some to render it simply impossible. The more delicate the affections, the less easy to satisfy, the readier are they to be damped and discouraged, yea quite blown aside; even the suspicion of a cold reception is enough to paralyze them. Such a cold wind blowing at the very gate of heaven﻿—thank God, *outside* the gate!﻿—is the so-called doctrine of “Adoption.” When a heart hears﻿—and believes, or half believes﻿—that it is not the child of God by origin, from the first of its being, but may possibly be adopted into his family, its love sinks at once in a cold faint: where is its own father, and who is this that would adopt it? To myself, in the morning of childhood, the evil doctrine was a mist through which the light came struggling, a cloud-phantom of repellent mien﻿—requiring maturer thought and truer knowledge to dissipate it. But it requires neither much knowledge nor much insight to stand up against its hideousness; it needs but love that will not be denied, and courage to question the phantom.
A devout and honest scepticism on God’s side, not to be put down by anything called authority, is absolutely necessary to him who would know the liberty wherewith Christ maketh free. Whatever any company of good men thinks or believes, is to be approached with respect; but nothing claimed or taught, be the claimers or the teachers who they may, must come between the soul and the spirit of the father, who is himself the teacher of his children. Nay, to accept authority may be to refuse the very thing the “authority” would teach; it may remain altogether misunderstood just for lack of that natural process of doubt and inquiry, which we were intended to go through by him who would have us understand.
As no scripture is of private interpretation, so is there no feeling in human heart which exists in that heart alone, which is not, in some form or degree, in every heart; and thence I conclude that many must have groaned like myself under the supposed authority of this doctrine.

> “——儿子的灵，呼叫阿爸，父。”

世上最难、也最甘美的事，是从一颗满溢的心呼叫*父！*我愿帮助凡我能帮助的，来这样向父呼求。
基督教一切形式的系统教导里，都有拦阻这心之外流的东西——对有些人，甚至使它全然不可能。情感越细腻，越难满足，也就越容易被挫伤、被 discouraged，是的，被完全吹偏；连一点受冷遇的猜疑都足以使它们瘫瘓。这样一股冷风吹在天门——感谢神，在门*外*！——就是那所谓的“收养”教义。一颗心听见——并且信了、或半信了——它不是因出身、从它存有之起初就是神的孩子，而只是可能被收养进他的家，它的爱立刻在寒冷的昏厥中下沉：它自己的父亲在哪里，这个要收养它的又是谁？在我自己的童年之晨，这邪恶的教义是一层雾，光在其中挣扎而来，是一片面目可拒的云影——需要更成熟的思想与更真的知识来驱散它。但要抵挡它的丑恶，并不需要多少知识或洞察；只需要不肯被拒的爱，和质问那鬼影的勇气。
一种站在神一边的、虔诚而诚实的怀疑主义，不被任何所谓权威压倒，对凡要认识基督所赐自由的人，是绝对必需的。无论任何一群好人想什么、信什么，都当以敬意接近；但凡人所宣称或教导的——无论宣称者或教导者是谁——都不可站在灵魂与父的灵之间，他自己才是他儿女的教师。不，接受权威可能恰恰是拒绝那“权威”所要教的东西；它可能全然被误解，只因缺少那自然的怀疑与探究的过程——那正是要我们明白的那位定意要我们经过的。
正如没有经书是私意解经的，人心中也没有一种情感是单独存在于那心里的，没有一种不在每颗心里以某种形式、某种程度存在；由此我断定，许多人必曾像我一样，在这教义所谓的权威下呻吟过。

Paul did not intend “adoption”; and second, that if the Revisers had gone through what I have gone through because of the word, if they had felt it come between God and their hearts as I have felt it, they could not have allowed it to remain in their version.
Once more I say, the word used by St. Paul does not imply that God adopts children that are not his own, but rather that a second time he fathers his own; that a second time they are born﻿—this time from above; that he will make himself tenfold, yea, infinitely their father: he will have them back into the very bosom whence they issued, issued that they might learn they could live nowhere else; he will have them one with himself. It was for the sake of this that, in his Son, he died for them.
Let us look at the passage where he reveals his use of the word. It is in another of his epistles﻿—that to the Galatians: 4:1﻿–﻿7.
“But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a bondservant, though he is lord of all; but is under guardians and stewards until the term appointed of the father. So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the rudiments of the world: but when the fullness of the time came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, that he might redeem them which were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father. So that thou art no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.”
How could the Revisers choose this last reading, “an heir through God,” and keep the word “adoption”? From the passage it is as plain as St. Paul could make it, that, by the word translated “adoption,” he means the raising of a father’s own child from the condition of tutelage and subjection to others, a state which, he says, is no better than that of a slave, to the position and rights of a son. None but a child could become a son; the idea is﻿—a spiritual coming of age; *only when the child is a man is he really and fully a son*. The thing holds in the earthly relation. How many children of good parents﻿—good children in the main too﻿—never know those parents, never feel towards them as children might, until, grown up, they have left the house﻿—until, perhaps, they are parents themselves, or are parted from them by death!

不是“收养”；第二，若修订者们经历过我因这个词所经历的，若他们曾像我一样感到它隔在神与他们的心之间，他们就不会容它留在他们的译本里。

让我们看他揭示自己用法的段落。在他另一封书信里——致加拉太人书：4:1-7。
“但我说，那承受产业的虽然是孩童，却与奴仆毫无分别，直到父亲预定的时候来到。我们为孩童的时候，受管于世俗的小学之下，也是如此。及至时候满足，神就差遣他的儿子，为女子所生，且生在律法以下，要把律法以下的人赎出来，叫我们得着儿子的名分。你们既为儿子，神就差他儿子的灵进入你们的心，呼叫：阿爸，父。可见，从此你不是奴仆，乃是儿子了；既是儿子，就靠着神为后嗣。”
修订者们怎么会选择这最后的读法“靠着神为后嗣”，却保留“收养”一词？从这段经文看，再明白不过——圣保罗以那译作“收养”的词，所指的是把父亲自己的孩子从受监护、受制于他人的光景（他说那光景不比奴仆好）提升到儿子的地位与权利。唯有孩子能成为儿子；这观念是——一场属灵的成年；*唯有孩子成人时，他才真正而完全地是儿子*。这在属地的关系里也成立。多少好父母的孩子——大体上也是好孩子——从不认识那些父母、从不像孩子那样感受他们，直到长大离家——直到或许他们自己也作了父母，或直到死亡把他们分开！

To be a child is not necessarily to be a son or daughter. The childship is the lower condition of the upward process towards the sonship, the soil out of which the true sonship shall grow, the former without which the latter were impossible. God can no more than an earthly parent be content to have only children: he must have sons and daughters﻿—children of his soul, of his spirit, of his love﻿—not merely in the sense that he loves them, or even that they love him, but in the sense that they love like him, love as he loves. For this he does not adopt them; he dies to give them himself, thereby to raise his own to his heart; he gives them a birth from above; they are born again out of himself and into himself﻿—for he is the one and the all. His children are not his real, true sons and daughters until they think like him, feel with him, judge as he judges, are at home with him, and without fear before him because he and they mean the same thing, love the same things, seek the same ends. For this are we created; it is the one end of our being, and includes all other ends whatever. It can come only of unbelief and not faith, to make men believe that God has cast them off, repudiated them, said they are not, yea never were, his children﻿—and he all the time spending himself to make us the children he designed, foreordained﻿—children who would take him for their Father! He is our father all the time, for he is true; but until we respond with the truth of children, he cannot let all the father out to us; there is no place for the dove of his tenderness to alight. He is our father, but we are not his children. Because we are his children, we must become his sons and daughters. Nothing will satisfy him, or do for us, but that we be one with our father! What else could serve! How else should life ever be a good! Because we are the sons of God, we must become the sons of God.
There may be among my readers﻿—alas for such!﻿—to whom the word “Father” brings no cheer, no dawn, in whose heart it rouses no tremble of even a vanished emotion. It is hardly likely to be their fault.

是孩子，未必就是儿子或女儿。孩子名分是朝向儿子名分那向上过程的较低光景，是真儿子名分将从中长出的土壤——没有前者，后者不可能。神不能——正如属地的父母不能——满足于只有孩子：他必须有儿子有女儿——他魂的、他灵的、他爱的孩子——不只是他爱他们、甚至他们爱他的那种意义上，而是他们像他那样爱、照他那样爱的意义上。为这个，他不收养他们；他死，把自己给他们，借此把他自己的孩子举到心上；他给他们一次从上头的生；他们从他里面重生的、也生进他里面——因为他是独一、也是万有。他的孩子直到像他那样思想、与他同感、照他判断、在他跟前自在无惧——因为他与他们同指一意、同爱一物、同求一目的——才是他真实真确的儿子女儿。我们受造正是为此；这是我们存有的唯一目的，且包含其他一切目的。叫人信神已丢弃他们、否认了他们、说他们不是、从来不曾是他的孩子——而神始终倾尽自己、要把我们作成他所设计、所预定的孩子——会作他父的孩子！——这只能出于不信，不是信心。他始终是我们的父，因为他是真的；但直到我们以孩子的真回应，他不能把全部的父向我们敞开；他温柔的鸽没有落脚之地。他是我们的父，但我们不是他的孩子。因为我们本是他的孩子，我们必须成为他的儿子女儿。唯有我们与我们的父为一，才能满足他、也成全我们！别的有什么用！生命否则怎能成为善！因为我们本是神的众子，我们必须成为神的众子。

For though as children we seldom love up to the mark of reason; though we often offend; and although the conduct of some children is inexplicable to the parent who loves them; yet, if the parent has been but ordinarily kind, even the son who has grown up a worthless man, will now and then feel, in his better moments, some dim reflex of childship, some faintly pleasant, some slightly sorrowful remembrance of the father around whose neck his arms had sometimes clung. In my own childhood and boyhood my father was the refuge from all the ills of life, even sharp pain itself. Therefore I say to son or daughter who has no pleasure in the name “Father,” “You must interpret the word by all that you have missed in life. Every time a man might have been to you a refuge from the wind, a covert from the tempest, the shadow of a great rock in a weary land, that was a time when a father might have been a father indeed. Happy you are yet, if you have found man or woman such a refuge; so far have you known a shadow of the perfect, seen the back of the only man, the perfect Son of the perfect Father. All that human tenderness can give or desire in the nearness and readiness of love, all and infinitely more must be true of the perfect Father﻿—of the maker of fatherhood, the Father of all the fathers of the earth, specially the Father of those who have specially shown a father-heart.”
This Father would make to himself sons and daughters indeed﻿—that is, such sons and daughters as shall be his sons and daughters not merely by having come from his heart, but by having returned thither﻿—children in virtue of being such as whence they came, such as choose to be what he is. He will have them share in his being and nature﻿—strong wherein he cares for strength; tender and gracious as he is tender and gracious; angry where and as he is angry. Even in the small matter of power, he will have them able to do whatever his Son Jesus could on the earth, whose was the life of the perfect man, whose works were those of perfected humanity. Everything must at length be subject to man, as it was to The Man. When God can do what he will with a man, the man may do what he will with the world; he may walk on the sea like his Lord; the deadliest thing will not be able to hurt him:﻿—“He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater than these shall he do.”

因为虽然作孩子的，我们很少爱到理性的标准；虽然我们常冒犯；虽然有些孩子的行为对爱他们的父母来说无法理解；然而，只要父母曾有过寻常的仁慈，连那长成无用之人的儿子，也必在较好的时刻，偶尔感到孩子名分的一丝朦胧反映，对那位父亲有某种微弱甘甜、微带忧愁的记忆——他的手臂曾有时环过那父亲的颈项。在我自己的童年与少年，我父亲是一切人生之祸——连剧痛本身——的避难所。因此我对那在“父”之名中得不着喜乐的儿子或女儿说：“你必须用你在人生中所错过的一切来解释这个词。每一次本可以有人作你的避风处、暴雨的庇护所、疲乏之地大磐石的影子的时候，那本可以是一位父亲真作父亲的时刻。你若曾发现某位男人或女人是这样的避难所，你仍是有福的；到那地步，你已认识完全者的一影，见过那独一之人、那完全之父的完全之子的背影。人一切温柔所能在大爱之切近与随手中给或愿的，一切且无限更多，必真实属于那完全的父——父性的造作者、地上一切父亲之父、尤其是那些特别显出为父之心者的父。”
这位父要为自己造出真儿子真女儿——就是那些不仅因出自他心、且因已归回他心而作他儿女的——因他们是从哪里来的那种人、因他们选择作他所是的那种人而作的孩子。他要他们有分于他的存有与性情——在他看重刚强处刚强；照他温柔恩慈而温柔恩慈；在他发怒处、照他那样发怒。甚至在能力这件小事上，他也要他们能行他儿子耶稣在地上所能行的一切——那是完全之人的一生，他的工作是成全了的人性之作。万物至终必服于人，正如服于那人。当神能随己意对待一个人时，那人便能随己意对待世界；他能像他的主那样在海面上走；最致命之物不能伤他：——“信我的人，我所作的事，他也要作；并且要作比这更大的。”

> God, whose pleasure brought

As it were, an handbreath off, to give

He has made us, but we have to be. All things were made *through* the Word, but that which was made *in* the Word was life, and that life is the light of men: they who live by this light, that is, live as Jesus lived﻿—by obedience, namely, to the Father, have a share in their own making; the light becomes life in them; they are, in their lower way, alive with the life that was first born in Jesus, and through him has been born in them﻿—by obedience they become one with the godhead: “As many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God.” He does not *make* them the sons of God, but he gives them power to become the sons of God: in choosing and obeying the truth, man becomes the true son of the Father of lights.
It is enough to read with understanding the passage I have quoted from his epistle to the Galatians, to see that the word “adoption” does not in the least fit St. Paul’s idea, or suit the things he says. While we but obey the law God has laid upon us, without knowing the heart of the Father whence comes the law, we are but slaves﻿—not necessarily ignoble slaves, yet slaves; but when we come to think *with* him, when the mind of the son is as the mind of the Father, the action of the son the same as that of the Father, then is the son *of* the Father, then are we the sons of God. And in both passages﻿—this, and that which, from his epistle to the Romans, I have placed at the head of this sermon﻿—we find the same phrase, “Abba, Father,” showing, if proof were needful, that he uses the word *νἱοθεσία* the same sense in both: nothing can well be plainer, that needs consideration at all, than what that sense is. Let us glance at the other passages in which he uses the same word: as he alone of the writers of the New Testament does use it, so, for aught I know, he may have made it for himsef. One of them is in the same eighth chapter of the epistle to the Romans; this I will keep to the last. Another is in the following chapter, the fourth verse; in it he speaks of the *νἱοθεσία*, literally the “son-placing” (that is, the placing of sons in the true place of sons), as belonging to the Jews.

On this I have but to remark that “whose is the *νἱοθεσία*” cannot mean either that they had already received it, or that it belonged to the Jews more than to the Gentiles; it can only mean that, as the elder-brother-nation, they had a foremost claim to it, and would naturally first receive it; that, in their best men, they had always been nearest to it. It must be wrought out first in such as had received the preparation necessary; those were the Jews; of the Jews was the Son, bringing the *νἱοθεσία*, the sonship, to all. Therefore theirs was the *νἱοθεσία*, just as theirs was the gospel. It was to the Jew first, then to the Gentile﻿—though many a Gentile would have it before many a Jew. Those and only those who out of a true heart cry “*Abba, Father*,” be they of what paltry little so-called church, other than the body of Christ, they may, or of no other at all, are the sons and daughters of God.
St. Paul uses the word also in his epistle to the Ephesians, the first chapter, the fifth verse. “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself,” says the authorized version; “Having foreordained us unto adoption as sons through Jesus Christ unto himself,” says the revised﻿—and I see little to choose between them: neither gives the meaning of St. Paul. If there is anything gained by the addition of the words “of children” in the one case, and “as sons” in the other, to translate the word for which “adoption” alone is made to serve in the other passages, the advantage is only to the minus-side, to that of the wrong interpretation.
Children we were; true sons we could never be, save through The Son. He brothers us. He takes us to the knees of the Father, beholding whose face we grow sons indeed. Never could we have known the heart of the Father, never felt it possible to love him as sons, but for him who cast himself into the gulf that yawned between us. In and through him we were foreordained to the sonship: sonship, even had we never sinned, never could we reach without him. We should have been little children loving the Father indeed, but children far from the sonhood that understands and adores. “For as many as are led by the spirit of God, these are sons of God”; “If any man hath not the spirit of Christ, he is none of his”; yea, if we have not each other’s spirits, we do not belong to each other.

对此我只需说：“*νἱοθεσία*是他们的”既不能指他们已经领受了它，也不能指它属于犹太人多于外邦人；它只能指：作为长兄之民，他们对它有最前的主张，必自然最先领受；在他们最好的人身上，他们一直最接近它。它必须先在那些已受必要预备的人身上作成；那些人是犹太人；出于犹太人的是那位儿子，把*νἱοθεσία*、儿子名分带给万人。所以那是他们的*νἱοθεσία*，正如福音是他们的。先给犹太人，后给外邦人——尽管许多外邦人会在许多犹太人之先得着。那些、唯有那些从心里呼喊“*阿爸，父*”的人——无论他们属于哪个渺小可怜的所谓教会，只要不同于基督的身体，或根本不属于任何——才是神的儿子女儿。
圣保罗在他致以弗所人书里也用这词，第一章第五节。“又因爱我们，就按着自己意旨所喜悦的，预定我们借着耶稣基督得儿子的名分”，钦定本说；“又因爱我们，就按着自己意旨所喜悦的，预定我们借着耶稣基督得_着儿子名分归于他自己”，修订本说——我看两者差别不大：都没有给出圣保罗的意思。若在“收养”一词之外，一处加上“儿女”、一处加上“为儿子”算有所得，那益处也只在负侧、在错误解释的那侧。

There is no unity but having the same spirit. There is but one spirit, that of truth.
It remains to note yet another passage.
That never in anything he wrote was it St. Paul’s intention to contribute towards a system of theology, it were easy to show: one sign of the fact is, that he does not hesitate to use this word he has perhaps himself made, in different, and apparently opposing, though by no means contradictory senses: his meanings always vivify each other. His ideas are so large that they tax his utterance and make him strain the use of words, but there is no danger to the honest heart, which alone he regards, of misunderstanding them, though “the ignorant and unsteadfast wrest them” yet. At one time he speaks of the sonship as being the possession of the Israelite, at another as his who has learned to cry “Abba, Father”; and here, in the passage I have now last to consider, that from the 18th to the 25th verse of this same eighth chapter of his epistle to the Romans, he speaks of the *νἱοθεσία* as yet to come﻿—and as if it had to do, not with our spiritual, but our bodily condition. This use of the word, however, though not the same use as we find anywhere else, is nevertheless entirely consistent with his other uses of it.
The 23rd verse says, “And not only so, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.”
It is nowise difficult to discern that the ideas in this and the main use are necessarily associated and more than consistent. The putting of a son in his true, his foreordained place, has outward relations as well as inward reality; the outward depends on the inward, arises from it, and reveals it. When the child whose condition under tutors had passed away, took his position as a son, he would naturally change his dress and modes of life: when God’s children cease to be slaves doing right from law and duty, and become his sons doing right from the essential love of God and their neighbour, they too must change the garments of their slavery for the robes of liberty, lay aside the body of this death, and appear in bodies like that of Christ, with whom they inherit of the Father. But many children who have learned to cry “Abba, Father,” are yet far from the liberty of the sons of God.

还剩一个段落要看。
圣保罗在他所写的任何东西里，从无意于为一套神学体系作贡献，这很容易证明：这事实的一个迹象是，他不 hesitate 使用这个或许他自己造的词，用在不同、且表面相反——却绝不矛盾——的意义上：他的各层意义总是彼此赋活。他的观念太大，压_迫他的言辞，使他拉伸词语的用法；但对那唯一被他看重的诚实之心，没有误解它们的危险，尽管“无学问、不坚固的人”仍在强解。他一时说儿子名分是以色列人的产业，一时说是那学会呼叫“阿爸，父”之人的产业；而这里，在我现在要看的最后一段——罗马书同一第八章第18至25节——他说到*νἱοθεσία*尚未来到——而且仿佛与我们的属灵光景无关，倒与我们的身体光景有关。然而这个词的这用法，虽与别处的用法都不同，却与他一切别的用法完全一致。
第23节说：“不但如此，就是我们这有圣灵初结果子的，也是自己心里叹息，等候得着儿子的名分，乃是我们的身体得赎。”
不难看出，这里的意思与主要用法里的意思必然相联、且不止于一致。把儿子放进他真实、他预定的位置，既有向外的关系，也有向内的实际；向外者系于向内者、由它而生、并启示它。那受监护之光景已过去的孩子，就位为儿子时，自然要更换衣装与生活方式：当神的儿女不再是因律法与本分行义的奴仆，而成为因爱神爱邻舍之本而行义的儿子时，他们也要脱下奴役的衣裳、穿上自由的袍，脱下这取死的身体，穿上与基督相似的身体——他们与基督同承父业。但许多已学会呼叫“阿爸，父”的孩子，还远未得着神儿女的自由。

Paul means, I think, the same thing as here he means by the sonship which he puts in apposition with the redemption of the body:﻿—
Until our outward condition is that of sons royal, sons divine; so long as the garments of our souls, these mortal bodies, are mean﻿—torn and dragged and stained; so long as we groan under sickness and weakness and weariness, old age, forgetfulness, and all heavy things; so long we have not yet received the sonship in full﻿—we are but getting ready one day to creep from our chrysalids, and spread the great heaven-storming wings of the psyches of God. Such it shall be, when truth is strong enough in the sons of God to make it such﻿—for it is the soul that makes the body. When we are the sons of God in heart and soul, then shall we be the sons of God in body too: “we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.”
I care little to speculate on the kind of this body; two things only I will say, as needful to be believed, concerning it: first, that it will be a body to show the same self as before﻿—but, second, a body to show the being truly﻿—without the defects, that is, and imperfections of the former bodily revelation. Even through their corporeal presence shall we then know our own infinitely better, and find in them endlessly more delight, than before. These things we must believe, or distrust the Father of our spirits. Till this redemption of the body arrives, the *νἱοθεσία* is not wrought out, is only upon the way. Nor can it come but by our working out the salvation he is working in us.

所指的，我想，与他此处放在与身体得赎并列的儿子名分是同一件事：——
直到我们向外的光景是王者之子、属神之子的光景；只要我们灵魂的衣裳——这些必朽的身体——还是鄙陋的——撕裂、拖曳、玷污的；只要我们还在疾病、软弱、疲乏、衰老、健忘与一切沉重之物下叹息；我们就还没有全然领受儿子名分——我们不过在预备终有一日从茧中爬出、张开神之魂灵那搏击诸天的大翅。我们背负重担而叹息；我们叹息，等候儿子名分——就是身体的得赎——身体被举起、成为内住之灵合宜的居所与启示——不，像基督的身体那样，成为更深内住之神合宜的殿与启示。因为我们永远需要身体来彼此彰显启示——所以那时的身体要绝对真实地呈现并启示灵魂。因此第19节所说神众子的显明，与身体的得赎是同一件事；身体配得上神众子时，就是得赎之时；那时它就启示他们——这正是它受造的目的，且一直或多或少不完全地是的。当真理在神众子里面强到足以使它如此时，它必如此——因为使身体成形的正是灵魂。当我们在心与魂里是神的儿子，那时我们在身体里也必是：“我们必要像他，因为必见他他的真体。”
我不大多愿揣测这身体的类别；关于它，我只说两件必须相信的事：第一，它将是显出与从前同一个自己的身体——但第二，是真实显出那存有的身体——没有从前身体启示的缺陷与不完全。到那时，连借着他们身体的同在，我们对亲爱者的认识也必无限胜于从前、喜乐也必无限多于从前。这些事我们必须信，否则就是不信托我们灵之父。直到这身体的得赎来到，*νἱοθεσία*还未作成，只在路上。它也只能借着我们作成他在我们里面所作的救恩而来。

===Original===

This redemption of the body﻿—its deliverance from all that is amiss, awry, unfinished, weak, worn out, all that prevents the revelation of the sons of God, is called by the apostle, not certainly the “adoption,” but the *νἱοθεσία*, the sonship in full manifestation. It is the slave yet left in the sons and daughters of God that has betrayed them into even permitting the word “adoption” to mislead them!
To see how the whole utterance hangs together, read from the 18th verse to the 25th, especially noticing the 19th: “For the earnest expectation of the creation waiteth for the revealing” (*the outshining*) “of the sons of God.” When the sons of God show as they are, taking, with the character, the appearance and the place that belong to their sonship; when the sons of God sit with *the* Son of God on the throne of their Father; then shall they be in potency of fact the lords of the lower creation, the bestowers of liberty and peace upon it; then shall the creation, subjected to vanity for their sakes, find its freedom in their freedom, its gladness in their sonship. The animals will glory to serve them, will joy to come to them for help. Let the heartless scoff, the unjust despise! the heart that cries “Abba, Father,” cries to the God of the sparrow and the oxen; nor can hope go too far in hoping what that God will do for the creation that now groaneth and travaileth in pain because our higher birth is delayed. Shall not the judge of all the earth do right? Shall my heart be more compassionate than his?
If to any reader my interpretation be unsatisfactory, I pray him not to spend his strength in disputing my faith, but in making sure his own progress on the way to freedom and sonship. Only to the child of God is true judgment possible. Were it otherwise, what would it avail to prove this one or that right or wrong? Right opinion on questions the most momentous will deliver no man. Cure for any ill in me or about me there is none, but to become the son of God I was born to be. Until such I am, until Christ is born in me, until I am revealed a son of God, pain and trouble will endure﻿—and God grant they may! Call this presumption, and I can only widen my assertion: until you yourself are the son of God you were born to be, you will never find life a good thing. If I presume for myself, I presume for you also. But I do not presume.

要看整个教训怎样连贯，请读第18节至25节，特别留意第19节：“受造之物切望等候”（*昂然 shining出*）“神众子的显明。”当神的众子照他们的本相显出，随性情一并取得他们儿子名分所属的外貌与地位；当神的众子与*那*神子同坐他们父的宝座；那时他们就要在实际的效能上作低等受造界的主、向它颁赐自由与平安；那时那为他们的缘故服在虚空之下的受造界，要在他们的自由里找到它的自由、在他们的儿子名分里找到它的喜乐。动物要以服事他们为荣、乐于到他们那里求帮助。任凭无心者讥诮、不义者轻视！那呼叫“阿爸，父”的心，所呼叫的正是麻雀与牛群之神；盼望那位神要为如今因我们更高的出生被迟延而叹息劳苦的受造界作什么，盼望再多也不为过。审判全地的主岂不行公义吗？我的心岂能比他的更慈悲？
若有读者觉得我的解释不能满意，我求他不要把力气花在辩驳我的信心上，而花在确证自己那朝向自由与儿子名分之路的进程上。唯有神的孩子才能有真实的判断。若非如此，证明这个那个对错又有什么用？对最重大问题的正确意见救不了任何人。在我里面或我周围任何病患，除了一剂药无药可医：成为我受生所要作的神儿子。直到我如此，直到基督生在我里面，直到我显为神的儿子，痛苦与患难必存留——神啊，愿它们存留！你若说这是擅专，我只能扩大我的断言：直到你自己成为你受生所要作的神儿子，你永远不会发现生命是一件好事。我若为自己擅专，我也为你擅专。但我不是擅专。
