Thus have both Jesus Christ and his love-slave Paul represented God﻿—as a Father perfect in love, grand in self-forgetfulness, supreme in righteousness, devoted to the lives he has uttered. I will not believe less of the Father than I can conceive of glory after the lines he has given me, after the radiation of his glory in the face of his Son. He is the express image of the Father, by which we, his imperfect images, are to read and understand him: imperfect, we have yet perfection enough to spell towards the perfect.
It comes to this then, after the grand theory of the apostle:﻿—The world exists for our education; it is the nursery of God’s children, served by troubled slaves, troubled because the children are themselves slaves﻿—children, but not good children. Beyond its own will or knowledge, the whole creation works for the development of the children of God into the sons of God. When at last the children have arisen and gone to their Father; when they are clothed in the best robe, with a ring on their hands and shoes on their feet, shining out at length in their natural, their predestined sonship; then shall the mountains and the hills break forth before them into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. Then shall the wolf dwell with the lamb, and the leopard lie down with the kid and the calf, and the young lion and the fatling together, and a little child shall lead them. Then shall the fables of a golden age, which faith invented, and unbelief threw into the past, unfold their essential reality, and the tale of paradise prove itself a truth by becoming a fact. Then shall every ideal show itself a necessity, aspiration although satisfied put forth yet longer wings, and the hunger after righteousness know itself blessed. Then first shall we know what was in the Shepherd’s mind when he said, “*I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.*”

===Chinese===

耶稣基督和他爱的奴仆保罗，就是这样代表了神——一位爱中完全、忘我中宏伟、义中至上、倾心于他所说出的诸生命的父。我不肯对父信得少于我照他给我的线、照他荣耀在他儿子面上的辐射、所能构想的荣耀。他是父的本体真像，我们这些他不完全的形象，要借他读懂并认识他：虽不完全，我们仍有足够的不完全去拼向完全。
于是归结到这一点，照使徒的宏大理论：——世界为我们的教育而存在；它是神儿女的育儿所，由受苦的奴仆服事着——受苦，因为孩子们自己也是奴仆——是孩子，却不是好孩子。超出它自己的意愿或知识，整个受造界都在为神儿女长成神众子而作工。当孩子们终于起来回到他们父那里；当他们穿上那上好的袍子、手上戴着戒指、脚上穿着鞋、终于在他们的天然、他们预定的儿子名分中放出光来；那时大山小山必在他们面前发声歌唱、田野的树木也都拍掌。那时豺狼必与绵羊羔同居、豹子与山羊羔同卧、牛犊与肥畜同群、少壮狮子同眠、一个小孩子要牵引它们。那时信心所虚构、不信抛进过去的黄金时代寓言，要展开它们的本质实际；乐园的故事要以成为事实证明自己是真理。那时每一个理想都要显为必需，满足了的心虽满足、仍要展出更长的翅膀，饥渴慕义的心要知道自己是蒙福的。那时我们才初次知道牧者心里所存的，当他说：“*我来了，是要叫羊得生命，并且得的更丰盛。*”

### Life / 生命
===Original===

> “I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.”

In a word, He came to supply all our lack﻿—from the root outward; for what is it we need but more life? What does the infant need but more life? What does the bosom of his mother give him but life in abundance? What does the old man need, whose limbs are weak and whose pulse is low, but more of the life which seems ebbing from him? Weary with feebleness, he calls upon death, but in reality it is life he wants. It is but the encroaching death in him that desires death. He longs for rest, but death cannot rest; death would be as much an end to rest as to weariness: even weakness cannot rest; it takes strength as well as weariness to rest. How different is the weariness of the strong man after labour unduly prolonged, from the weariness of the sick man who in the morning cries out, “Would God it were evening!” and in the evening, “Would God it were morning!” Low-sunk life imagines itself weary of life, but it is death, not life, it is weary of. Never a cry went out after the opposite of life from any soul that knew what life is. Why does the poor, worn, outworn suicide seek death? Is it not in reality to escape from death?﻿—from the death of homelessness and hunger and cold; the death of failure, disappointment, and distraction; the death of the exhaustion of passion; the death of madness﻿—of a household he cannot rule; the death of crime and fear of discovery? He seeks the darkness because it seems a refuge from the death which possesses him. He is a creature possessed by death; what he calls his life is but a dream full of horrible phantasms.
“More life!” is the unconscious prayer of all creation, groaning and travailing for the redemption of its lord, the son who is not yet a son. Is not the dumb cry to be read in the faces of some of the animals, in the look of some of the flowers, and in many an aspect of what we call Nature? All things are possible with God, but all things are not easy. It is easy for him *to be*, for there he has to do with his own perfect will: it is not easy for him to create﻿—that is, after the grand fashion which alone will satisfy his glorious heart and will, the fashion in which he is now creating us. In the very nature of being﻿—that is, God﻿—it must be hard﻿—and divine history shows how hard﻿—to create that which shall be not himself, yet like himself.

===Chinese===

> “我来了，是要叫羊得生命，并且得的更丰盛。”

一言以蔽之，他来是要补足我们一切的匮乏——从根向外；因为除了更多的生命，我们还需要什么？婴孩除了更多的生命还需要什么？他母亲的胸怀给他的，除了丰盛的生命，还有什么？四肢无力、脉搏低微的老人，除了那看似正从他退潮的生命之更多，还需要什么？他疲于软弱，就呼唤死亡；但他真正要的，其实是生命。要死的只是他里面那渐渐侵入的死。他渴望安息，但死不能安息；死之于疲倦，正如之于安息，同样是终结：连软弱也不能安息；安息既需要疲乏、也需要力量。壮劳作过度之后的那种疲倦，与病人早晨呼喊“巴不得是晚上”、晚上呼喊“巴不得是早晨”的那种疲倦，何其不同！低沉的生命自以为厌倦了生命，其实它厌倦的是死，不是生命。没有一个知道生命是什么的灵魂，曾发出过追求生命之反面的呼喊。那可怜、耗竭、被耗尽的自杀者为什么寻死？岂不是实际上要逃脱死吗？——逃脱无家可归、饥饿与寒冷之死；失败、失望与心力交瘁之死；激情耗竭之死；疯狂之死——一个他管不了的家之死；犯罪与惧怕败露之死？他寻求黑暗，因为它看似一个脱离那占据他之死的避难所。他是一个被死占据的受造者；他所谓的生命不过是一场满布恐怖幻影的梦。
“更多的生命！”是一切受造之物无意识的祷告（prayer）——它正为它主的救赎、为那还不是儿子的儿子叹息劳苦。这无声的呼喊，岂不可以从一些动物的脸、一些花的神情、以及我们所谓自然的许多面相中读出来吗？在神凡事都能，但并非凡事都容易。他*存在*是容易的，因为那只关乎他自己完全的旨意：他创造却不容易——就是照那唯一能满足他荣耀心与旨意的宏大方式创造，他如今正以那方式创造我们。在存有的本性——就是神——里面，创造那既非他自己、却又像他自己的东西，必是难的——神圣的历史显出何等难。

===Original===

The problem is, so far to separate from himself that which must yet on him be ever and always and utterly dependent, that it shall have the existence of an individual, and be able to turn and regard him﻿—choose him, and say, “I will arise and go to my Father,” and so develop in itself the highest *Divine* of which it is capable﻿—the will for the good against the evil﻿—the will to be one with the life whence it has come, and in which it still is﻿—the will to close the round of its procession in its return, so working the perfection of reunion﻿—to shape in its own life the ring of eternity﻿—to live immediately, consciously, and active-willingly from its source, from its own very life﻿—to restore to the beginning the end that comes of that beginning﻿—to be the thing the maker thought of when he willed, ere he began to work its being.
I imagine the difficulty of doing this thing, of effecting this creation, this separation from himself such that will in the creature shall be possible﻿—I imagine, I say, the difficulty of such creation so great, that for it God must begin inconceivably far back in the infinitesimal regions of beginnings﻿—not to say before anything in the least resembling man, but eternal miles beyond the last farthest-pushed discovery in *protoplasm*﻿—to set in motion that division from himself which in its grand result should be individuality, consciousness, choice, and conscious choice﻿—choice at last pure, being the choice of the right, the true, the divinely harmonious. Hence the final end of the separation is not individuality; that is but a means to it; the final end is oneness﻿—an impossibility without it. For there can be no unity, no delight of love, no harmony, no good in being, where there is but one. Two at least are needed for oneness; and the greater the number of individuals, the greater, the lovelier, the richer, the diviner is the possible unity.
God is life, and the will-source of life. In the outflowing of that life, I know him; and when I am told that he is love, I see that if he were not love he would not, could not create. I know nothing deeper in him than love, nor believe there is in him anything deeper than love﻿—nay, that there can be anything deeper than love. The being of God is love, therefore creation. I imagine that from all eternity he has been creating.

===Chinese===

这难题是：要把那永远、始终、全然依赖他的东西，与他分开到如此地步，使它拥有一个个体的存在，能够回转而注视他——拣选他，并说“我要起来，到我父那里去”，从而在自己里面发展出它所能有的最高的*神性*——向善拒恶的意志——与它所自出、且仍在其中的生命为一的意志——以它的回归闭合它出来之环、从而作成重聚之完全的意志——在自己生命里铸成永恒之环——直接地、有意识地、以主动的意志从它的源头、从它自己的生命而活——把那出于起初的终点归还给起初——作那造它在动工以成其存有之前、心意中所想的那物。
我设想这事之难——成全这创造、这与他自己的分开、使受造者中的意志成为可能——我说，这创造之难如此之大，以致神必须从不可思议之遥的、初始的无穷小境界开始——不必说在任何略似人的东西之前，而且在*原生质*上最后推进到最远的发现之外还有永恒的里程——发动那与自己的分开，它在其宏大结果里要成为个体性、意识、选择、以及有意识的选择——最终成为纯净的选择，即对正当的、真的、属神和谐者的选择。因此分开的最终目的不是个体性；那只是手段；最终目的是一——没有它，一是不可能的。因为只有一个的地方，就没有合一、没有爱的喜悦、没有和谐、没有存有中的善。为一至少需要二；且个体的数目越多，那可能的一就越大、越可爱、越丰富、越属神。
神是生命，是生命意志的源头。在那生命的流出中，我认识他；当人告诉我他是爱，我就看见：他若不是爱，就不会、也不能创造。我在他里面不知道有比爱更深的，也不信他里面有什么比爱更深——不，不信能有什么比爱更深。神的存有就是爱，因此是创造。我设想他从永恒以来就一直在创造。

===Original===

As he saw it was not good for man to be alone, so has he never been alone himself;﻿—from all eternity the Father has had the Son, and the never-begun existence of that Son I imagine an easy outgoing of the Father’s nature; while to make other beings﻿—beings like us, I imagine the labour of a God, an eternal labour. Speaking after our poor human fashions of thought﻿—the only fashions possible to us﻿—I imagine that God has never been contented to be alone even with the Son of his love, the prime and perfect idea of humanity, but that he has from the first willed and laboured to give existence to other creatures who should be blessed with his blessedness﻿—creatures whom he is now and always has been developing into likeness with that Son﻿—a likeness for long to be distant and small, but a likeness to be forever growing: perhaps never one of them yet, though unspeakably blessed, has had even an approximate idea of the blessedness in store for him.
Let no soul think that to say God undertook a hard labour in willing that many sons and daughters should be sharers of the divine nature, is to abate his glory! The greater the difficulty, the greater is the glory of him who does the thing he has undertaken﻿—without shadow of compromise, with no half-success, but with a triumph of absolute satisfaction to innumerable radiant souls! He knew what it would cost!﻿—not energy of will alone, or merely that utterance and separation from himself which is but the first of creation, though that may well itself be pain﻿—but sore suffering such as we cannot imagine, and could only be God’s, in the bringing out, call it birth or development, of the God-life in the individual soul﻿—a suffering still renewed, a labour thwarted ever by that soul itself, compelling him to take, still at the cost of suffering, the not absolutely best, only the best possible means left him by the resistance of his creature. Man finds it hard to get what he wants, because he does not want the best; God finds it hard to give, because he would give the best, and man will not take it. What Jesus did, was what the Father is always doing; the suffering he endured was that of the Father from the foundation of the world, reaching its climax in the person of his Son. God provides the sacrifice; the sacrifice is himself. He is always, and has ever been, sacrificing himself to and for his creatures.

他既见人独居不好，他自己也从不独居；——从永恒以来，父就有了子，而那子的从未开始的存在，我想是父本性一次轻易的流出；至于造别的存有——像我们这样的存有，我想是一位神的劳作，一场永恒的劳作。照我们贫乏的人类思维方式——那对我们唯一可能的方式——来说，我想神即使与他爱的子、那人性的首要完全观念同在，也从不满足于独居，而是从起初就定意、就劳碌，要使别的受造者得存在、得以他的福乐为福乐——那些他如今、且一直都在发展成那子之相像的受造者——一种长久遥远而微小的相像，却是要永远生长的相像：他们中或许还没有一个、尽管蒙说不出的福，曾对存留给他的福乐有过哪怕近似的观念。
不要有灵魂以为：说神愿意许多儿女作神性的分享者、是承担了一桩艰难的劳作，就是减损他的荣耀！难处越大，那成全他所承担之事者的荣耀就越大——毫无妥协之影、毫无半成之功，只有一场使无数光辉灵魂绝对满足的胜利！他知道这将付上什么！——不只是意志的能量，或只是那言说与对己的分开——那不过是创造的第一步，虽然那本身就可能是痛——而是如此剧烈的受苦，我们无法想象，也只能是神的：把神的生命带出、生出或发展出在个别灵魂里——那受苦仍在更新，那劳作时时被那灵魂自己阻挠，迫使他仍然以受苦为代价，取那并非绝对至善、只是他的受造者之抵挡所留给他的最好可能手段。人觉得难得着他所要的，因为他不要至善；神觉得难以给，因为他要给至善，而人不肯接受。耶稣所作的，正是父一直在作的；他所受的苦，是从立世界的根基以来父的苦，在他儿子身上达到顶点。神预备祭物；那祭物就是他自己。他一直、且永远在向他的受造者、为他的受造者献上自己。

===Original===

It lies in the very essence of his creation of them. The worst heresy, next to that of dividing religion and righteousness, is to divide the Father from the Son﻿—in thought or feeling or action or intent; to represent the Son as doing that which the Father does not himself do. Jesus did nothing but what the Father did and does. If Jesus suffered for men, it was because his Father suffers for men; only he came close to men through his body and their senses, that he might bring their spirits close to his Father and their Father, so giving them life, and losing what could be lost of his own. He is God our Saviour: it is because God is our Saviour that Jesus is our Saviour. The God and Father of Jesus Christ could never possibly be satisfied with less than giving himself to his own! The unbeliever may easily imagine a better God than the common theology of the country offers him; but not the lovingest heart that ever beat can even reflect the length and breadth and depth and height of that love of God which shows itself in his Son﻿—one, and of one mind, with himself. The whole history is a divine agony to give divine life to creatures. The outcome of that agony, the victory of that creative and again creative energy, will be radiant life, whereof joy unspeakable is the flower. Every child will look in the eyes of the Father, and the eyes of the Father will receive the child with an infinite embrace.
The life the Lord came to give us is a life exceeding that of the highest undivine man, by far more than the life of that man exceeds the life of the animal the least human. More and more of it is for each who will receive it, and to eternity. The Father has given to the Son to have life in himself; that life is our light. We know life only as light; it is the life in us that makes us see. All the growth of the Christian is the more and more life he is receiving. At first his religion may hardly be distinguishable from the mere prudent desire to save his soul; but at last he loses that very soul in the glory of love, and so saves it; self becomes but the cloud on which the white light of God divides into harmonies unspeakable.
“In the midst of life we are in death,” said one; it is more true that in the midst of death we are in life.

这就在他创造他们的本质里。最大的异端——仅次于把宗教与义（righteousness）分开的——是把父与子分开——在思想、情感、行动或意图上分开；把子描绘成行父自己所不行之事的样子。耶稣所作的，无非父所作、所正在作的。耶稣若为人受苦，是因为他的父为人受苦；只是他借他的身体与他们的感官就近人，好把他们的灵带近他的父、他们的父，如此给他们生命，并失去他自己所能失去的。他是神我们的救主：正因神是我们的救主，耶稣才是我们的救主。耶稣基督的神与父，绝不可能满足于少于把自己给他自己的人！不信者很容易想象一个比这国家通行神学所提供的更好的神；但那从未跳动过的最富爱的心，也不能反映神那在他儿子身上显明之爱的长阔高深——那子与他为一、与他同一心意。整部历史是一场神圣的产难，要把神圣的生命给受造者。那产难的结果、那创造又再造之大能的胜利，将是光辉的生命，说不出的喜乐是它的花。每个孩子要注视父的眼，父的眼要以无限的拥抱接待孩子。
主来要给我们的生命，超过最高非神之人的生命，远过于那人的生命超过最少人性之动物的生命。凡愿领受的，都必有越来越多的它，直到永恒。父已赐子在自己里面有生命；那生命是我们的光。我们只在光中认识生命；是我们里面的生命使我们看见。基督徒全部的生长，就是他正在领受的越来越多的生命。起初他的宗教或许难以与那只想救自己灵魂的谨慎愿望区分；但至终他要在爱的荣耀里失去那灵魂，从而救了它；自我不过成为一朵云，神的白光在它上面分解成说不出的和谐。
“我们在生命中处于死亡里，”有人说过；更真实的是：我们在死亡中处于生命里。

===Original===

Life is the only reality; what men call death is but a shadow﻿—a word for that which cannot be﻿—a negation, owing the very idea of itself to that which it would deny. But for life there could be no death. If God were not, there would not even be nothing. Not even nothingness preceded life. Nothingness owes its very idea to existence.
One form of the question between matter and spirit is, which was first, and caused the other﻿—things or thoughts; whether things without thought caused thought, or thought without things caused things. To those who cannot doubt that thought was first, causally preceding the earliest material show, it is easily plain that death can be the cure for nothing, that the cure for everything must be life﻿—that the ills which come with existence, are from its imperfection, not of itself﻿—that what we need is more of it. We who *are*, have nothing to do with death; our relations are alone with life. The thing that can mourn can mourn only from lack; it cannot mourn because of being, but because of not enough being. We are vessels of life, not yet full of the wine of life; where the wine does not reach, there the clay cracks, and aches, and is distressed. Who would therefore pour out the wine that is there, instead of filling to the brim with more wine! All the being must partake of essential being; life must be assisted, upheld, comforted, every part, with life. Life is the law, the food, the necessity of life. Life is everything. Many doubtless mistake the joy of life for life itself; and, longing after the joy, languish with a thirst at once poor and inextinguishable; but even that thirst points to the one spring. These love self, not life, and self is but the shadow of life. When it is taken for life itself, and set as the man’s centre, it becomes a live death in the man, a devil he worships as his god; the worm of the death eternal he clasps to his bosom as his one joy!

===Chinese===

生命是唯一的实际；人所谓的死不过是一个影——一个指那不可能存在之物的词——一个否定，它连自身的观念都欠自那它要否定的。若没有生命，就没有死。神若不存在，连无也不会有。连虚无也不先于生命。虚无连自己的观念都欠自存在。
物质与灵之间那个问题的一个形式是：哪个在先、造成另一个——物还是思想；是无思想的物造成了思想，还是无物的思想造成了物。对那些不能怀疑思想在先、在因果上先于最早物质显示的人，很容易明白：死医不了任何病，万病的药必是生命——随存在而来的诸病，出于它的不完全，不出于它本身——我们所需要的是更多的生命。我们这些*存在着的*，与死毫无关系；我们的关系只与生命。能哀恸之物只能因缺乏而哀恸；它不能因为存在而哀恸，只能因为存在得不够而哀恸。我们是生命的器皿，还未满盛生命之酒；酒到不了的地方，陶土就开裂、疼痛、困窘。谁会因此倒掉已有的酒，而不添酒满到边沿呢！全部的存有都必须有分于本质的存有；生命必须被生命——每一部分——帮助、支撑、安慰。生命是生命的律、生命的粮、生命的必需。生命就是一切。许多人无疑把生命的喜乐误当生命本身；切慕那喜乐，就带着一种既贫乏又不能熄的渴虚弱下去；但连那渴也指向那独一的泉。这些人爱自我，不爱生命，而自我不过是生命之影。当它被当作生命本身、被立为人的中心，它就在人里面成为活的死亡、一个被他当作神敬拜的鬼魔；他把那永死之虫搂在怀里，当作他唯一的喜乐！

===Original===

The soul compact of harmonies has more life, a larger being, than the soul consumed of cares; the sage is a larger life than the clown; the poet is more alive than the man whose life flows out that money may come in; the man who loves his fellow is infinitely more alive than he whose endeavour is to exalt himself above him; the man who strives to be better, than he who longs for the praise of the many; but the man to whom God is all in all, who feels his life-roots hid with Christ in God, who knows himself the inheritor of all wealth and worlds and ages, yea, of power essential and in itself, that man has begun to be alive indeed.
Let us in all the troubles of life remember﻿—that our one lack is life﻿—that what we need is more life﻿—more of the life-making presence in us making us more, and more largely, alive. When most oppressed, when most weary of life, as our unbelief would phrase it, let us bethink ourselves that it is in truth the inroad and presence of death we are weary of. When most inclined to sleep, let us rouse ourselves to live. Of all things let us avoid the false refuge of a weary collapse, a hopeless yielding to things as they are. It is the life in us that is discontented; we need more of what is discontented, not more of the cause of its discontent. Discontent, I repeat, is the life in us that has not enough of itself, is not enough to itself, so calls for more. He has the victory who, in the midst of pain and weakness, cries out, not for death, not for the repose of forgetfulness, but for strength to fight; for more power, more consciousness of being, more God in him; who, when sorest wounded, says with Sir Andrew Barton in the old ballad:﻿—

> Fight on my men, says Sir Andrew Barton,

I am hurt, but I am not slain;

I’ll lay me down and bleed awhile,

And then I’ll rise and fight again;

===Chinese===

那由和谐组成的灵魂，比那被挂虑耗尽的灵魂有更多的生命、更大的存有；贤人是比小丑更大的生命；诗人比那把生命流出去好叫钱流进来的人更有活力；爱同伴的人比那力求高抬自己超过同伴的人，无限地更有活力；那努力求更好的，比那渴慕众人称赞的更有活力；而那以神为万有中之万有的、那感到自己的生命之根与基督一同藏在神里面的、那知道自己是万贯家财、万国万代的承受者、是的、是本质大能本身的承受者的——那样的人才真开始活了。
让我们在生命一切的烦难中记住——我们唯一的匮乏是生命——我们所需要的是更多的生命——更多那造生命的同在在我们里面，使我们更多、更广地活着。最受压制的时候、最厌倦生命的时候（照我们不信的说法），让我们想起：我们厌倦的其实是死的侵入与同在。最想睡的时候，让我们振作自己活。在一切事上，让我们避开那疲惫垮塌的假避难所、那对事物现状的无望屈从。是我们里面的生命在不满；我们需要更多那不满的，而不是更多它不满的原因。不满，我重复，是我们里面的生命，它自己不够、对自己不足，所以呼求更多。那在痛苦软弱中呼喊的——不求死、不求遗忘之安息、只求争战的力量、求更多的大能、更多的存有意识、更多神在他里面——的人，是得胜者；那受创最重时，同古谣曲里的安德鲁·巴顿爵士说：——

> 战斗吧我的人，安德鲁·巴顿爵士说，

我受了伤，却没有被杀；

我要躺下流一会儿血，

然后我要起来再战；

===Original===

—and that with no silly notion of playing the hero﻿—what have creatures like us to do with heroism who are not yet barely honest!﻿—but because so to fight is the truth, and the only way.
If, in the extreme of our exhaustion, there should come to us, as to Elijah when he slept in the desert, an angel to rouse us, and show us the waiting bread and water, how would we carry ourselves? Would we, in faint unwillingness to rise and eat, answer, “Lo I am weary unto death! The battle is gone from me! It is lost, or unworth gaining! The world is too much for me! Its forces will not heed me! They have worn me out! I have wrought no salvation even for my own, and never should work any, were I to live forever! It is enough; let me now return whence I came; let me be gathered to my fathers and be at rest!”? I should be loth to think that, if the enemy, in recognizable shape, came roaring upon us, we would not, like the red-cross knight, stagger, heavy sword in nerveless arm, to meet him; but, in the feebleness of foiled effort, it wants yet more faith to rise and partake of the food that shall bring back more effort, more travail, more weariness. The true man trusts in a strength which is not his, and which he does not feel, does not even always desire; believes in a power that seems far from him, which is yet at the root of his fatigue itself and his need of rest﻿—rest as far from death as is labour. To trust in the strength of God in our weakness; to say, “I am weak: so let me be: God is strong”; to seek from him who is our life, as the natural, simple cure of all that is amiss with us, power to do, and be, and live, even when we are weary﻿—this is the victory that overcometh the world. To believe in God our strength in the face of all seeming denial, to believe in him out of the heart of weakness and unbelief, in spite of numbness and weariness and lethargy; to believe in the wide-awake real, through all the stupefying, enervating, distorting dream; to will to wake, when the very being seems athirst for a godless repose;﻿—these are the broken steps up to the high fields where repose is but a form of strength, strength but a form of joy, joy but a form of love. “I am weak,” says the true soul, “but not so weak that I would not be strong; not so sleepy that I would not see the sun rise; not so lame but that I would walk!

===Chinese===

——而且不带任何逞英雄的蠢念——像我们这样连诚实都还差得远的受造者，与英雄主义有什么相干！——只因为这样争战是真实，是唯一的路。
若在我们耗竭的极处，有天使来唤醒我们——像以利亚睡在旷野时那样——向我们指明那等候的饼和水，我们会怎样自处？我们会不会在勉强不愿起身吃喝中回答：“看哪，我疲乏得要死！战斗已离我而去！它输了，或不值得赢！世界对我太重了！它的势力不理会我！它们把我磨垮了！我连为自己的人也作不成什么救恩，就算我活到永远也作不成！够了；让我如今回归我所从来之处；让我归到我的列祖那里安息吧！”？我不愿这样想：仇敌若以可辨认的形状向我们咆哮而来，我们必像那红十字骑士，拖着无力的手臂上沉重的剑，蹒跚着迎上去；但在努力受挫的软弱里，还需要更多的信心，才能起来吃那要带回更多努力、更多劳苦、更多疲乏的食物。真实的人信托一种不是自己的力量——他感觉不到、甚至不总渴望的力量；信一种看似离他遥远的大能，它却在他疲乏本身与他安息之需的根部——那安息离死与劳作同样遥远。在我们的软弱中信靠神的力量；说“我软弱：就让我软弱吧：神刚强”；向那作我们生命的，寻求大能去作、去是、去活——当作我们一切不对劲的自然简单的药——哪怕在我们疲乏时——这就是那胜了世界的信心（faith）。在一切看似否认面前信神是我们的力量，从软弱与不信的心坎里信他，不顾麻木、疲乏与昏沉；穿过那一切令人麻木、令人无力、令人变形的梦，信那完全醒着的实际；在那存有本身似乎渴慕一场无神安息之时，仍定意醒来；——这些是登上高处的破碎台阶，在那里安息不过是力量的一种形式，力量不过是喜乐的一种形式，喜乐不过是爱的一种形式。“我软弱，”真实的灵魂说，“但还没有软弱到不愿刚强；还没有困倦到不愿看日出；还没有瘸到不愿行走！

===Original===

Thanks be to him who perfects strength in weakness, and gives to his beloved while they sleep!”
If we will but let our God and Father work his will with us, there can be no limit to his enlargement of our existence, to the flood of life with which he will overflow our consciousness. We have no conception of what life might be, of how vast the consciousness of which we could be made capable. Many can recall some moment in which life seemed richer and fuller than ever before; to some, such moments arrive mostly in dreams: shall soul, awake or asleep, infold a bliss greater than its Life, the living God, can seal, perpetuate, enlarge? Can the human twilight of a dream be capable of generating or holding a fuller life than the morning of divine activity? Surely God could at any moment give to a soul, by a word to that soul, by breathing afresh into the secret caves of its being, a sense of life before which the most exultant ecstasy of earthly triumph would pale to ashes! If ever sunlit, sail-crowded sea, under blue heaven flecked with wind-chased white, filled your soul as with a new gift of life, think what sense of existence must be yours, if he whose thought has but fringed its garment with the outburst of such a show, take his abode with you, and while thinking the gladness of a God inside your being, let you know and feel that he is carrying you as a father in his bosom!
I have been speaking as if life and the consciousness of it were one; but the consciousness of life is not life; it is only the outcome of life. The real life is that which is of and by itself﻿—is life because it wills itself﻿—which is, in the active, not the passive sense: this can only be God. But in us there ought to be a life correspondent to the life that is God’s; in us also must be the life that wills itself﻿—a life in so far resembling the self-existent life and partaking of its image, that it has a share in its own being. There is an original act possible to the man, which must initiate the reality of his existence. He must live in and by willing to live.

感谢那位在软弱中成全力量、并在所爱之人睡着时赐给他们的！”
我们只要肯让我们的神与父照他的旨意在我们身上作工，他对我们存在的扩大、他以生命之洪漫过我们意识所能有的，就没有限量。我们全然无法设想生命可以是什么、我们所能承受的意识可以何等浩大。许多人能回忆某个生命显得比从前更丰富更充盈的时刻；对有些人，这样的时刻多在梦中：灵魂无论醒着睡着，能怀抱一种大于它生命——那活的神——所能盖印、永存、扩大的福吗？梦的人类微光，能生出或持守比神圣活动之早晨更充盈的生命吗？神当然能在任何时刻、借对那灵魂的一句话、借向它存有的隐秘洞穴重新吹气，给它一种生命感——地上凯旋最狂喜的陶醉在它面前也要淡成灰烬！若曾有过落日帆影的海洋、在点缀着风逐白云的蓝天下，如一份新生命之礼充满过你的灵魂，就想想：若那位其思想不过以其衣袍之缘迸发这样一场盛景的，来与你同住，且当他在你存有里面思想一位神的欢喜时，让你知道并感到他正像父亲一样把你抱在怀里——那时的存在感必是怎样！
我一直说得仿佛生命与生命的意识是一；但生命的意识不是生命；它只是生命的结果。真实的生命是那出于自己、凭自己而有的生命——是生命因为它意愿自己——在主动而非被动的意义上：这只能是神。但在我们里面，当有一种与神之生命相称的生命；在我们里面也必有那意愿自己的生命——一种在如此程度上类似那自有生命、有分其形象的生命，以致它在自己的存有中有份。人有可能作一个本原的行动，来开启他存在的实际。他必须靠着愿意活而活。

A tree lives; I hardly doubt it has some vague consciousness, known by but not to itself, only to the God who made it; I trust that life in its lowest forms is on the way to thought and blessedness, is in the process of that separation, so to speak, from God, in which consists the creation of living souls; but the life of these lower forms is not life in the high sense﻿—in the sense in which the word is used in the Bible: true life knows and rules itself; the eternal life is life come awake. The life of the most exalted of the animals is not such whatever it may become, and however I may refuse to believe their fate and being fixed as we see them. But as little as any man or woman would be inclined to call the existence of the dog, looking strange lack out of his wistful eyes, an existence to be satisfied with﻿—his life an end sufficient in itself, as little could I, looking on the human pleasure, the human refinement, the common human endeavour around me, consent to regard them as worthy the name of life. What in them is true dwells amidst an unchallenged corruption, demanding repentance and labour and prayer for its destruction. The condition of most men and women seems to me a life in death, an abode in unwhited sepulchres, a possession of withering forms by spirits that slumber, and babble in their dreams. That they do not feel it so, is nothing. The sow wallowing in the mire may rightly assert it her way of being clean, but theirs is not the life of the God-born. The day must come when they will hide their faces with such shame as the good man yet feels at the memory of the time when he lived like them. There is nothing for man worthy to be called life, but the life eternal﻿—God’s life, that is, after his degree shared by the man made to be eternal also. For he is in the image of God, intended to partake of the life of the most high, to be alive as he is alive. Of this life the outcome and the light is righteousness, love, grace, truth; but the life itself is a thing that will not be defined, even as God will not be defined: it is a power, the formless cause of form. It has no limits whereby to be defined. It shows itself to the soul that is hungering and thirsting after righteousness, but that soul cannot show it to another, save in the shining of its own light.

===Chinese===

一棵树活着；我几乎不怀疑它有某种模糊的意识——被那造它的神知道，却不被它自己知道；我信最低形态的生命正在走向思想与福乐，正处在——可以说——那与神分开的过程中，活魂的创造就在于此；但这些低形态的生命不是高意义上的生命——不是圣经里用这词的意义：真生命认识并治理自己；永生是醒过来的生命。最高动物的生命也不是这样的——无论它可能变成什么，无论我多么不肯信它们的命运与存有就定死在我们所见的样子。但正如没有哪个男人或女人会倾向于把狗那从凝望的眼里望出奇异匮乏的存在、称为可满足的存在——它的生命本身即为充分的目的；同样，我也不能看着周围的人间享乐、人间精致、寻常人间努力，就同意它们配得上生命之名。它们里面真实的东西，住在一片未受挑战的腐坏中，需要悔改、劳碌与祷告（prayer）来毁掉它。大多数人的光景在我看是死中之生、住在未粉刷的坟墓里、昏睡的灵拥着枯萎的形式、在梦中呓语。他们不觉得如此，无关紧要。在泥里打滚的母猪尽可以声称那是它洁净的方式，但他们的不是神生之人的生命。那日必来，那时他们要以那好人回忆自己像他们那样活着的时候仍感到的羞愧，遮住自己的脸。对人而言，没有配称生命的东西，唯有永生——神的生命，就是说，照他的度量、被那被造为也属永恒的人所分享的生命。因为他照神的形象受造，定意有分于至高者的生命、像他活着那样活着。这生命的结果与光是义（righteousness）、爱、恩慈、真理；但生命本身是一件不肯被定义的东西，正如神不肯被定义：它是一种大能，那无形之形的因。它没有可供定义的界限。它向那饥渴慕义的灵魂显明自己，但那灵魂不能把它示与别人，除非借它自己光的照耀。

===Original===

The ignorant soul understands by this life eternal only an endless elongation of consciousness; what God means by it is a being like his own, a being beyond the attack of decay or death, a being so essential that it has no relation whatever to nothingness; a something which is, and can never go to that which is not, for with that it never had to do, but came out of the heart of Life, the heart of God, the fountain of being; an existence partaking of the divine nature, and having nothing in common, any more than the Eternal himself, with what can pass or cease: God owes his being to no one, and his child has no lord but his Father.
This life, this eternal life, consists for man in absolute oneness with God and all divine modes of being, oneness with every phase of right and harmony. It consists in a love as deep as it is universal, as conscious as it is unspeakable; a love that can no more be reasoned about than life itself﻿—a love whose presence is its all-sufficing proof and justification, whose absence is an annihilating defect: he who has it not cannot believe in it: how should death believe in life, though all the birds of God are singing jubilant over the empty tomb! The delight of such a being, the splendour of a consciousness rushing from the wide open doors of the fountain of existence, the ecstasy of the spiritual sense into which the surge of life essential, immortal, increate, flows in silent fullness from the heart of hearts﻿—what may it, what must it not be, in the great day of God and the individual soul!
What then is our practical relation to the life original? What have we to do towards the attaining to the resurrection from the dead? If we did not make, could not have made ourselves, how can we, now we are made, do anything at the unknown roots of our being? What relation of conscious unity can be betwixt the self-existent God, and beings who live at the will of another, beings who could not refuse to be﻿—cannot even cease to be, but must, at the will of that other, go on living, weary of what is not life, able to assert their relation to life only by refusing to be content with what is not life?
The self-existent God is that other by whose will we live; so the links of the unity must already exist, and can but require to be brought together.

===Chinese===

无知的灵魂把这永生只理解为意识的无尽延长；神的意思却是：一种像他自己一样的存有、一种衰朽与死亡攻不动的存有、一种如此本质、以致与虚无毫无关系的存有；一样存在着、且永不能归于不存在的东西，因为它与不存在从无干系，而是从生命之心、神之心、存有之泉出来的；一种有分于神性的存在，与那能过去能止息的东西——正如永恒者自己一样——毫无共通之处：神的存在不欠谁，他的孩子除父之外没有别的主。
这生命、这永生，对人而言在于与神、与一切属神存有方式的绝对为一，与每一阶段之正当与和谐为一。它在于一种深如其广、如其所感而如其所不能言的爱；一种与生命本身一样无从论证的爱——一种其同在即是其自足的证明与正当、其缺席即是毁灭性缺损的爱：没有它的人不能信它：死怎能信生命，尽管神的众鸟正在空坟墓上欢唱！那样一个存有的喜乐、那意识从存有之泉敞开的众门奔涌而出的光辉、那属灵感官的狂喜——本质、不朽、非受造的生命之涌从心之心静静充盈而入——在神与个别灵魂之大日，它将是什么、必是什么！
那么，我们与那本原生命的实践关系是什么？我们当怎样作，以达到那从死里复活？我们既没有造自己、也不可能造自己，如今既已被造，怎能在这存有未知的根部作什么呢？在自存的神与那些凭另一者之意志而活的存有之间——那些不能拒绝存在、甚至不能停止存在、必须凭那另一者的意志继续活着、厌倦于那非生命之物、只能借着拒绝满足于非生命之物来主张其与生命之关系的存有之间——能有怎样有意识的一之关系呢？
那自存的神就是我们借其意志而活的那另一位；所以一之链环必已存在，只须被带到一起。

===Original===

For the link in our being wherewith to close the circle of immortal oneness with the Father, we must of course search the deepest of man’s nature: there only, in all assurance, can it be found. And there we do find it. For the *will* is the deepest, the strongest, the divinest thing in man; so, I presume, is it in God, for such we find it in Jesus Christ. Here, and here only, in the relation of the two wills, God’s and his own, can a man come into vital contact﻿—on the eternal idea, in no one-sided unity of completest dependence, but in willed harmony of dual oneness﻿—with the All-in-all. When a man can and does entirely say, “Not my will, but thine be done”﻿—when he so wills the will of God as to do it, then is he one with God﻿—one, as a true son with a true father. When a man wills that his being be conformed to the being of his origin, which is the life in his life, causing and bearing his life, therefore absolutely and only of its kind, one with it more and deeper than words or figures can say﻿—to the life which is itself, only more of itself, and more than itself, causing itself﻿—when the man thus accepts his own causing life, *and sets himself to live the will of that causing life*, humbly eager after the privileges of his origin﻿—thus receiving God, he becomes, in the act, a partaker of the divine nature, a true son of the living God, and an heir of all he possesses: by the obedience of a son, he receives into himself the very life of the Father. Obedience is the joining of the links of the eternal round. Obedience is but the other side of the creative will. Will is God’s will, obedience is man’s will; the two make one. The root-life, knowing well the thousand troubles it would bring upon him, has created, and goes on creating other lives, that, though incapable of self-being, they may, by willed obedience, share in the bliss of his essential self-ordained being. If we do the will of God, eternal life is ours﻿—no mere continuity of existence, for that in itself is worthless as hell, but a being that is one with the essential Life, and so within his reach to fill with the abundant and endless out-goings of his love. Our souls shall be vessels ever growing, and ever as they grow, filled with the more and more life proceeding from the Father and the Son, from God the ordaining, and God the obedient.

===Chinese===

为找到我们存有中那用来闭合与父不朽为一之环的链环，我们当然必须探究人性之最深处：唯有在那里，才能确定找得到它。而我们在那里确实找到了它。因为*意志*是人里面最深、最强、最属神的东西；我想，在神里面也是如此，因为我们在耶稣基督里发现它是这样。正在这里、也唯独在这里，在两个意志——神的与他自己的——的关系中，人才能进入活泼的接触——照永恒的观念，不在单单完满依赖的片面一里，而在双重之一意志的和谐里——与那在万有中作万有者相遇。当一个人能够并且完全说“不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思”——当他如此意愿神的旨意（the will of God）以至于行它——那时他就与神为一——像一个真儿子与一位真父亲那样为一。当一个人意愿他的存有符合于他本源之存有——那在他生命中的生命，造成并承载他生命的，因此绝对而唯独是它那一类，与它为一深过言语与比喻所能说——与那本身就是生命、只是更多它自己、又多于它自己、自因己的生命——当那人这样接受他那造成生命的生命，*并定意活出那造成生命的生命之旨意*，谦卑地切慕他本源的特权——这样领受神，他就在这行动中成为神性的分享者、永活真神的真儿子、与他一切所有的的承受者：借着一个儿子的顺服（obedience），他把父的生命本身接受进自己里面。顺服是永恒之环诸链环的接合。顺服不过是创造意志的另一面。意愿是神的意志，顺服是人的意志；两者合为一。那根生命明知它将带给他千般烦难，却创造了、且继续创造别的生命，好叫它们虽不能自有，却能借甘愿的顺服，有分于他本质自定存有的福。我们若行神的旨意，永生就是我们的——不是单纯的存在延续，因为那本身一文不值、如地狱（hell）一般，而是一种与本质生命为一的存有，从而在他所能及之内，以他爱的丰盛无尽流出充满我们。我们的灵魂要作不断长大的器皿，且随着长大，不断被从父与子、从定旨的神与顺服的神而来的越来越多的生命充满。

===Original===

What the delight of the being, what the abundance of the life he came that we might have, we can never know until we have it. But even now to the holy fancy it may sometimes seem too glorious to support﻿—as if we must die of very life﻿—of more being than we could bear﻿—to awake to a yet higher life, and be filled with a wine which our souls were heretofore too weak to hold! To be for one moment aware of such pure simple love towards but one of my fellows as I trust I shall one day have towards each, must of itself bring a sense of life such as the utmost effort of my imagination can but feebly shadow now﻿—a mighty glory of consciousness!﻿—not to be always present, indeed, for my love, and not my glory in that love, is my life. There would be, even in that one love, in the simple purity of a single affection such as we were created to generate, and intended to cherish, towards all, an expansion of life inexpressible, unutterable. For we are made for love, not for self. Our neighbour is our refuge; *self* is our demon-foe. Every man is the image of God to every man, and in proportion as we love him, we shall know the sacred fact. The precious thing to human soul is, and one day shall be known to be, every human soul. And if it be so between man and man, how will it not be betwixt the man and his maker, between the child and his eternal Father, between the created and the creating Life? Must not the glory of existence be endlessly redoubled in the infinite love of the creature﻿—for all love is infinite﻿—to the infinite God, the great one life, than whom is no other﻿—only shadows, lovely shadows of him!
Reader to whom my words seem those of inflation and foolish excitement, it can be nothing to thee to be told that I seem to myself to speak only the words of truth and soberness; but what if the cause why they seem other to thy mind be﻿—not merely that thou art not whole, but that thy being nowise thirsts after harmony, that thou art not of the truth, that thou hast not yet begun to live? How should the reveller, issuing worn and wasted from the haunts where the violent seize joy by force to find her perish in their arms﻿—how should such reveller, I say, break forth and sing with the sons of the morning, when the ocean of light bursts from the fountain of the east?

===Chinese===

那存有的喜乐、他来要我们得着的生命之丰盛，非得到它我们不能知道。但即使在如今，对圣洁的想象，它有时也显得太荣耀而难以承受——仿佛我们必死于纯粹的生命——死于多过我们所能承载的存有——醒入更高的生命、被盛满一种我们灵魂从前太弱而承受不起的酒！哪怕有一刻，觉察到对同伴中仅仅一人那样纯净单纯的爱——如我信我终有一日会向每一个人怀有的——其本身就必带来一种生命感，我想象的极致努力如今只能微弱地投影——一种意识的宏大荣耀！——确实不会常在，因为我的爱、不是我在那爱中的荣耀，才是我的生命。即使在那一单个的爱里，在那一种单纯纯粹的、如我们受造要向一切人生发并持守的情感里，也将有不可表达、不可言说的生命之扩张。因为我们是为爱受造，不是为自我。我们的邻舍是我们的避难所；*自我*是我们的鬼魔仇敌。每个人对每个人都是神的形象，且照我们爱他的程度，我们必认识这神圣的事实。于人魂珍贵的，且有一日必被认识为珍贵的，是每一个人的灵魂。人与人之间若尚且如此，人与造他者之间、孩子与他永恒之父之间、受造者与创造之生命之间，又将如何！在受造者对无限之神——那伟大的独一生命，除他以外无别——只有他可爱的影子！——的无限爱里，存在的荣耀岂不必无尽地加倍——因为一切爱都是无限的！
读者啊，若我的话在你听来是浮夸与愚妄的兴奋，我对你说“我自觉所说的不过是真实与清醒的话”，于你无益；但它们在你心思里显得别样，原因若不只是你不完整，而是你的存有毫不渴慕和谐、你不属于真理、你还没有开始活，又当如何？那寻欢者，从暴力之辈以强力夺乐、却发现乐在他们怀中消亡的巢穴里憔悴虚耗地出来——那寻欢者，我说，当光之海从东方之泉迸发时，怎能同早晨之子们一同放声歌唱？

===Original===

As little canst thou, with thy mind full of petty cares, or still more petty ambitions, understand the groaning and travailing of the creation. It may indeed be that thou art honestly desirous of saving thy own wretched soul, but as yet thou canst know but little of thy need of him who is *the first and the last and the living one*.

===Chinese===

你满心琐碎的挂虑、或更琐碎的野心，也照样不能明白受造之物的叹息与劳苦。也许你确实诚实地渴求救你自己那可怜的灵魂，但你到目前为止，只能极少认识你对那位*首先的、末后的、活着的*的需要。

### The Fear of God / 对神的敬畏
===Original===

> “And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as one dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying, Fear not; I am the first and the last and the Living one.”

It is not alone the first beginnings of religion that are full of fear. So long as love is imperfect, there is room for torment. That love only which fills the heart﻿—and nothing but love can fill any heart﻿—is able to cast out fear, leaving no room for its presence. What we find in the beginnings of religion, will hold in varying degree, until the religion, that is the love, be perfected.
The thing that is unknown, yet known to be, will always be more or less formidable. When it is known as immeasurably greater than we, and as having claims and making demands upon us, the more vaguely these are apprehended, the more room is there for anxiety; and when the conscience is not clear, this anxiety may well mount to terror. According to the nature of the mind which occupies itself with the idea of the Supreme, whether regarded as maker or ruler, will be the kind and degree of the terror. To this terror need belong no exalted ideas of God; those fear him most who most imagine him like their own evil selves, only beyond them in power, easily able to work his arbitrary will with them. That they hold him but a little higher than themselves, tends nowise to unity with him: who so far apart as those on the same level of hate and distrust? Power without love, dependence where is no righteousness, wake a worship without devotion, a loathliness of servile flattery. Neither, where the notion of God is better, but the conscience is troubled, will his goodness do much to exclude apprehension. The same consciousness of evil and of offence which gave rise to the bloody sacrifice, is still at work in the minds of most who call themselves Christians. Naturally the first emotion of man towards the being he calls God, but of whom he knows so little, is fear.
Where it is possible that fear should exist, it is well it should exist, cause continual uneasiness, and be cast out by nothing less than love. In him who does not know God, and must be anything but satisfied with himself, fear towards God is as reasonable as it is natural, and serves powerfully towards the development of his true humanity. Neither the savage, nor the self-sufficient sage, is rightly human.

===Chinese===

> “我一看见他，就仆倒在他脚前，像死了一样。他用右手按着我，说：不要惧怕；我是首先的、末后的、那存活的。”

充满惧怕的不单是宗教的最初开端。爱一日不完全，就有一日折磨的余地。唯有那充满心的爱——唯有爱能充满任何心——能赶出惧怕，不给它留立足之地。我们在宗教开端中所发现的，将按不同程度持续，直到那宗教、就是那爱、得以完全。
那未知却知其存在的东西，总会多少可畏。当它被知道无限大于我们、且对我们有主张有要求时，这些把握得越模糊，焦虑的余地就越大；而良心不清时，这焦虑尽可升至恐怖。专注于至上者观念的心思——无论把他看作造者还是治者——其性质如何，恐怖的种类与程度就如何。这恐怖无需配得上崇高的神观；最怕他的，恰是那些最把他想象得像他们自己邪恶自我、只是能力在他们之上、能轻易对他们行任意旨意的人。他们把他持得只比自己高一点，这无助于与他的合一：谁比那处在同一恨与不信层次上的人相距更远呢？没有爱的能力、没有义（righteousness）的依赖，唤醒的是没有虔诚的敬拜、一种奴性谄媚的令人作呕。同样，神观较好而良心不安的人那里，他的良善也排除不了多少恐惧。那曾引发血祭的同一个邪恶与过犯的意识，仍在大多数自称基督徒的心里作工。人对那他称之为神、却又知之甚少的存有，其最初的情感自然是惧怕。
凡惧怕可能存在的地方，惧怕存在是好的，叫人持续不安，且唯有爱能把它赶出。在那不认识神、又绝不该对自己满足的人身上，对神的惧怕既自然又合理，且有力地促进他真实人性的发展。野蛮人与自足的贤人，都不是正当的人。

===Original===

It matters nothing whether we regard the one or the other as degenerate or as undeveloped﻿—neither I say is human; the humanity is there, but has to be born in each, and for this birth everything natural must do its part; fear is natural, and has a part to perform nothing but itself could perform in the birth of the true humanity. Until love, which is the truth towards God, is able to cast out fear, it is well that fear should hold; it is a bond, however poor, between that which is and that which creates﻿—a bond that must be broken, but a bond that can be broken only by the tightening of an infinitely closer bond. Verily, God must be terrible to those that are far from him; for they fear he will do, yea, he is doing with them what they do not, cannot desire, and can ill endure. Such as many men are, such as all without God would become, they must prefer a devil, because of his supreme selfishness, to a God who will die for his creatures, and insists upon giving himself to them, insists upon their being unselfish and blessed like himself. That which is the power and worth of life they must be, or die; and the vague consciousness of this makes them afraid. They love their poor existence as it is; God loves it as it must be﻿—and they fear him.
The false notions of men of low, undeveloped nature both with regard to what is good and what the Power requires of them, are such that they cannot but fear, and devotion is lost in the sacrifices of ingratiation: God takes them where they are, accepts whatever they honestly offer, and so helps them to outgrow themselves, preparing them to offer the true offering, and to know him whom they ignorantly worship. He will not abolish their fear except with the truth of his own being. Till they apprehend that, and in order that they may come to apprehend it, he receives their sacrifices of blood, the invention of their sore need, only influencing for the time the modes of them. He will destroy the lie that is not all a lie only by the truth which is all true. Although he loves them utterly, he does not tell them there is nothing in him to make them afraid. That would be to drive them from him forever. While they are such as they are, there is much in him that cannot but affright them; they ought, they do well to fear him. It is, while they remain what they are, the only true relation between them.

===Chinese===

我们把哪一个看作堕落或未发展，都无关紧要——我说，两者都不是人性的；人性在那里，却必须在各人里面出生；为这出生，一切天然之物必须尽其一份；惧怕是天然的，在真实人性的出生中有唯它能尽的一份。直到那作为向神之真理的爱能赶出惧怕，惧怕持守着是好的；它是一条纽带，尽管贫乏，连着那存有的与那创造的——一条必须断裂的纽带，但只能借一条无限更近之纽带系紧而断裂。真的，神对远离他的人必是可怕的；因为他们怕他要作、是的、正在对他们作的，是他们所不愿、不能愿、也难以忍受的。照许多人现在的样子、照一切没有神的人将要成为的样子，他们必宁要一个魔鬼——因他的极端自私——而不要一位肯为受造者死、坚持把自己给他们、坚持要他们像他自己那样无私而蒙福的神。他们要么是那生命的能力与价值、要么就死；对这点的模糊意识使他们害怕。他们爱他们那现状的可怜存在；神爱它那必成为的样子——于是他们怕他。
低级未发展天性的人，关于什么是善、以及那大能者要求他们什么，其错误观念使他们不能不怕，虔诚消融在讨好的祭物里：神就着他们的本相接纳他们，悦纳他们诚心献上的无论什么，从而帮助他们长过自己，预备他们献上真的祭、认识他们无知中所拜的那位。他不废除他们的惧怕，除非用他自己存有的真理。直到他们领会它、也为了使他们得以领会它，他收纳他们的血祭——他们剧痛需要的发明——只暂时影响其方式。他只肯用那全然为真的真理，毁掉那并非全为假的谎。他虽全然爱他们，却不告诉他们他里面没有可叫他们害怕的。那将永远赶走他们。他们既仍是这样的，他里面就有许多必叫他们惊惧的；他们应当、也确实该怕他。在他们仍是本相期间，这是他们之间唯一真实的关系。

===Original===

To remove that fear from their hearts, save by letting them know his love with its purifying fire, a love which for ages, it may be, they cannot know, would be to give them up utterly to the power of evil. Persuade men that fear is a vile thing, that it is an insult to God, that he will none of it﻿—while yet they are in love with their own will, and slaves to every movement of passionate impulse, and what will the consequence be? That they will insult God as a discarded idol, a superstition, a falsehood, as a thing under whose evil influence they have too long groaned, a thing to be cast out and spit upon. After that how much will they learn of him? Nor would it be long ere the old fear would return﻿—with this difference, perhaps, that instead of trembling before a live energy, they would tremble before powers which formerly they regarded as inanimate, and have now endowed with souls after the imagination of their fears. Then would spiritual chaos with all its monsters be come again. God being what he is, a God who loves righteousness; a God who, rather than do an unfair thing, would lay down his Godhead, and assert himself in ceasing to be; a God who, that his creature might not die of ignorance, died as much as a God could die, and that is divinely more than man can die, to give him himself; such a God, I say, may well look fearful from afar to the creature who recognizes in himself no imperative good; who fears only suffering, and has no aspiration﻿—only wretched ambition!

===Chinese===

若不从他们心中除去那惧怕——除非借让他们认识他那带着炼净之火的爱，一种他们或许多年都不能认识的爱——就等于把他们完全交给恶的权势。劝人说惧怕是可鄙之物、是对神的侮辱、他完全不要它——而他们却仍恋慕自己的意志、仍作一切激情冲动的奴仆——后果将如何？他们必侮辱神，把他当作废弃的偶像、迷信、虚谎，当作一件他们曾在其恶影响下呻吟太久、当被抛出唾弃的东西。此后他们还能从他学到多少？而旧惧怕不久必回——所差者，或许只是：从前是在活的能量前发抖，如今是在他们从前视为无生命、如今按他们恐惧的想象赋了灵魂的力量前发抖。那时属灵的混沌同它一切的怪物必要回来。神既是他那样的神——一位爱义的神；一位宁肯放下神格、借不再是而确立自己、也不肯行一件不公之事的神；一位为叫他的受造者不死于无知、尽一位神所能死地死了——那在属神意义上远多于人之所能死——好把自己给他的神；我说，这样一位神，在那自己里面认不出任何当行之善、只怕受苦、毫无升腾——只有悲惨野心——的受造者从远处看，尽可以是可怕的。

===Original===

But in proportion as such a creature comes nearer, grows towards him in and for whose likeness he was begun; in proportion, that is, as the eternal right begins to disclose itself to him; in proportion as he becomes capable of the idea that his kind belongs to him as he could never belong to himself; approaches the capacity of seeing and understanding that his individuality can be perfected only in the love of his neighbour, and that his being can find its end only in oneness with the source from which it came; in proportion, I do not say as he sees these things, but as he nears the possibility of seeing them, will his terror at the God of his life abate; though far indeed from surmising the bliss that awaits him, he is drawing more nigh to the goal of his nature, the central secret joy of sonship to a God who loves righteousness and hates iniquity, does nothing he would not permit in his creature, demands nothing of his creature he would not do himself.
The fire of God, which is his essential being, his love, his creative power, is a fire unlike its earthly symbol in this, that it is only at a distance it burns﻿—that the farther from him, it burns the worse, and that when we turn and begin to approach him, the burning begins to change to comfort, which comfort will grow to such bliss that the heart at length cries out with a gladness no other gladness can reach, “Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee!” The glory of being, the essence of life and its joy, shining upon the corrupt and deathly, must needs, like the sun, consume the dead, and send corruption down to the dust; that which it burns in the soul is not of the soul, yea, is at utter variance with it; yet so close to the soul is the foul fungous growth sprung from and subsisting upon it, that the burning of it is felt through every spiritual nerve: when the evil parasites are consumed away, that is when the man yields his self and all that self’s low world, and returns to his lord and God, then that which, before, he was aware of only as burning, he will feel as love, comfort, strength﻿—an eternal, ever-growing life in him. For now he lives, and life cannot hurt life; it can only hurt death, which needs and ought to be destroyed.

===Chinese===

但随着这样的受造者就近前来，长向他——他正是为着他的像才被起始的——随着永恒的正当开始向他显明；随着他逐渐能够领会：他的类属于神、过于他永远可能属于自己；逐渐接近看见并明白：他的个体性唯有在爱邻舍中得以完全，他的存有唯有在与那它所自出的源头为一中寻得归宿——我不说随着他看见这些事，而说随着他临近看见它们的可能，他对生命之神的恐怖必消退；虽然他远未料到等候他的福乐，他正在临近他本性的目标——作那爱义恨恶之神儿子的中心秘密喜乐——这神不行他不许受造者行的任何事，不要求受造者任何他自己不肯行的事。
神的火——就是他的本质存有、他的爱、他创造的大能——是一团与其属地象征不同的火：它只在远处烧——离他越远，烧得越烈；当我们回转、开始就近他，焚烧就开始化为安慰，这安慰要长成那样的福乐，以致心至终带着别的喜乐不能及的欢乐呼喊：“在天上我有谁呢？在地上我也没有所爱慕的！”存有的荣耀、生命及其喜乐的本质，照在腐坏与死亡之上，就必像太阳一样烧灭死的、打发腐坏下到尘土；它在魂里烧掉的东西不属于魂，是的，与魂全然相左；然而那从魂里长出、靠魂养活的污秽菌体离魂如此之近，以致它的焚烧透过每一条属灵的神经被感觉到：当那些恶的寄生体被烧尽——就是当那人交出他的自我、及那自我全部的低俗世界、归回他的主他的神——那时他从前只觉为焚烧的，要感觉为爱、安慰、力量——一种在他里面永恒、常长的新生命。因为他如今活着，而生命不能伤害生命；它只能伤害死亡——那需要且应当被毁灭的。

===Original===

God is life essential, eternal, and death cannot live in his sight; for death is corruption, and has no existence in itself, living only in the decay of the things of life. If then any child of the father finds that he is afraid before him, that the thought of God is a discomfort to him, or even a terror, let him make haste﻿—let him not linger to put on any garment, but rush at once in his nakedness, a true child, for shelter from his own evil and God’s terror, into the salvation of the Father’s arms, the home whence he was sent that he might learn that it was home. What father being evil would it not win to see the child with whom he was vexed running to his embrace? how much more will not the Father of our spirits, who seeks nothing but his children themselves, receive him with open arms!
Self, accepted as the law of self, is the one demon-enemy of life; God is the only Saviour from it, and from all that is not God, for God is life, and all that is not God is death. Life is the destruction of death, of all that kills, of all that is of death’s kind.
When John saw the glory of the Son of Man, he fell at his feet as one dead. In what way John saw him, whether in what we vaguely call a vision, or in as human a way as when he leaned back on his bosom and looked up in his face, I do not now care to ask: it would take all glorious shapes of humanity to reveal Jesus, and he knew the right way to show himself to John. It seems to me that such words as were spoken can have come from the mouth of no mere vision, can have been allowed to enter no merely tranced ear, that the mouth of the very Lord himself spoke them, and that none but the living present Jesus could have spoken or may be supposed to speak them; while plainly John received and felt them as a message he had to give again. There are also, strangely as the whole may affect us, various points in his description of the Lord’s appearance which commend themselves even to our ignorance by their grandeur and fitness. Why then was John overcome with terror?

===Chinese===

神是本质的、永恒的生命，死亡在他眼前不能存活；因为死是朽坏，自身并无存在，只活在生命之物的衰败里。所以，父的孩子中若有谁发现在他面前害怕、对神的思想是不安、甚至是恐怖的，就让他赶快——让他不要耽延穿什么衣裳，就照本相赤露着、像一个真孩子，为躲避自己的恶与神的可畏，直奔入父之臂膀的救恩、那差他出来好叫他学会那是家的家。哪位邪恶的父亲见那惹他气恼的孩子跑进他的怀抱，会不赢得过来？何况我们灵之父，他除了他孩子们自己一无所求，岂不更要张开双臂接待他！
自我被接受为自我的律，是生命独一的鬼魔仇敌；神是唯一的救主，救我们脱离它、脱离一切不是神的，因为神是生命，一切不是神的都是死。生命是死的毁灭——毁灭一切杀生的、一切属死之类的。
约翰看见人子的荣耀时，就仆倒在他脚前像死了一样。约翰以什么方式看见他——是照我们模糊称之为异象的方式，还是像他那时靠在他胸膛上、仰望他脸那样属人的方式——我如今不想问：启示耶稣需要人性一切荣耀的形状，他知道向约翰显出自己的正当方式。在我看，那样的话只能从不止是幻象的口中说出、不能容进入只是出神之耳，是主自己亲口的说话，唯有活着的现在的耶稣能说、才可被设想在说；而显然约翰是把它们当作他要再传的信息领受并感受的。他的描述中还有几点——无论整体在我们看去多么奇特——以其宏伟与合宜、连向我们的无知自荐。那么约翰为什么被恐怖胜过？

===Original===

We recall the fact that something akin to terror overwhelmed the minds of the three disciples who saw his glory on the mount; but since then John had leaned on the bosom of his Lord, had followed him to the judgment seat and had not denied his name, had borne witness to his resurrection and suffered for his sake﻿—and was now “in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus:” why, I say, was he, why should he be afraid? No glory even of God *should* breed terror; when a child of God is afraid, it is a sign that the word *Father* is not yet freely fashioned by the child’s spiritual mouth. The glory can breed terror only in him who is capable of being terrified by it; while he is such it is well the terror should be bred and maintained, until the man seek refuge from it in the only place where it is not﻿—in the bosom of the glory.
There is one point not distinguishable in the Greek: whether is meant, “one like unto *the* Son of Man,” or, “one like unto *a* son of Man:” the authorized version has the former, the revised prefers the latter. I incline to the former, and think that John saw him like the man he had known so well, and that it was the too much glory, dimming his vision, that made him unsure, not any perceived unlikeness mingling with the likeness. Nothing blinds so much as light, and their very glory might well render him unable to distinguish plainly the familiar features of *The* Son of Man.
But the appearance of The Son of Man was not intended to breed terror in the son of man to whom he came. Why then was John afraid? why did the servant of the Lord fall at his feet as one dead? Joy to us that he did, for the words that follow﻿—surely no phantasmic outcome of uncertain vision or blinding terror! They bear best sign of their source: however given to his ears, they must be from the heart of our great Brother, the one Man, Christ Jesus, divinely human!
It was still and only the imperfection of the disciple, unfinished in faith, so unfinished in everything a man needs, that was the cause of his terror. This is surely implied in the words the Lord said to him when he fell! The thing that made John afraid, he speaks of as the thing that ought to have taken from him all fear.

===Chinese===

我们想起一个事实：在山上看见他荣耀的三位门徒，心里也被近于恐怖的东西压倒；但自那以后，约翰曾靠在他主的胸膛上，曾跟从他被带到审判（the judgment）座前而没有否认他的名，曾为他的复活作见证、为他受苦——如今“在名叫拔摩的海岛上，为神的道并为给耶稣作的见证”：为什么，我说，他会害怕？他为什么该害怕？连神的荣耀也*不该*滋生恐怖；神的孩子害怕时，那是*父*一词还没有被孩子属灵的口自由说出的记号。荣耀只能在那能被它恐吓的人里面滋生恐怖；他既是这样的，恐怖滋生并维持着是好的，直到那人从它寻求庇护——在唯一没有它的地方——在那荣耀的怀中。
希腊文里有一点无法区分：所指的是“像*那*人子的一位”，还是“像*一个*人子的一位”：钦定本取前者，修订本倾向后者。我倾向前者，想约翰看见他像他所熟识的那个人，是那过多的荣耀昏花了他的视觉使他不能确定，不是有什么察觉到的不似混杂在似中。没有什么比光更叫人瞎，那荣耀本身就足以使他认不出*那*人子熟识的面貌。
但那人的显现，本无意在它所临到的人身上滋生恐怖。那么约翰为什么害怕？主的仆人为什么仆倒在他脚前像死了一样？他倒了，是我们的喜乐，因为随后的话——确实不是不确定异象或致瞎恐怖的幻影产物！它们带着其来源的最好凭据：无论怎样临到他耳中，必是出于我们大兄、那独一之人基督耶稣、属神人性的心！
那仍是且只是门徒的不完全——信心（faith）未成、人所需要的一切都未成——才是他恐怖的原因。这确实含在主见他倒下时对他说的话里！使约翰害怕的那件事，他正说成那本该从他除去一切惧怕的事。

===Original===

For the glory that he saw, the head and hair pouring from it such a radiance of light that they were white as white wool﻿—snow-white, as his garments on mount Hermon; in the midst of the radiance his eyes like a flame of fire, and his countenance as the sun shineth in his strength; the darker glow of the feet, yet as of fine brass burning in a furnace﻿—as if they, in memory of the twilight of his humiliation, touching the earth took a humbler glory than his head high in the empyrean of undisturbed perfection; the girdle under his breast, golden between the snow and the brass;﻿—what were they all but the effulgence of his glory who was himself the effulgence of the Father’s, the poor expression of the unutterable verity which was itself the reason why John ought not to be afraid?﻿—“He laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last, and the living one.”
Endless must be our terror, until we come heart to heart with the fire-core of the universe, the first and the last and the living one!
But oh, the joy to be told, by Power himself, the first and the last, the living one﻿—told what we can indeed then see *must* be true, but which we are so slow to believe﻿—that the cure for trembling is the presence of Power; that fear cannot stand before Strength; that the visible God is the destruction of death; that the one and only safety in the universe, is the perfect nearness of the Living One! God is being; death is nowhere! What a thing to be taught by the very mouth of him who knows! He told his servant Paul that strength is made perfect in weakness; here he instructs his servant John that the thing to be afraid of is weakness, not strength. All appearances of strength, such as might rightly move terror, are but false appearances; the true Strong is the *One*, even as the true Good is the *One*. The Living One has the power of life; the Evil One but the power of death﻿—whose very nature is a self-necessity for being destroyed.
But the glory of the mildest show of the Living One is such, that even the dearest of his apostles, the best of the children of men, is cowed at the sight.

===Chinese===

因为他所见的荣耀——头与发从中倾出那样强的光、白如白羊毛——雪白，如他在黑门山上的衣裳；光焰之中他的眼如火焰，面貌如烈日放光；脚是较暗的光辉，却如炉中烧亮的精铜——仿佛它们因记念他自卑的暮色、因触着地、就取了比他那高在无扰完全之最高天的头更卑微的荣耀；胸间的带子，金色介于雪与铜之间；——这一切若不是那自身就是父之光辉者的光辉之外溢、若不是那不可言之实在的贫乏表达——而那实在本身就是约翰不该害怕的理由——还能是什么？——“他用右手按着我，对我说：不要惧怕；我是首先的、末后的、那存活的。”
直到我们与宇宙的火核、那首先的末后的存活的、心贴着心，我们的恐怖必无尽！
但哦，那被大能者本身、那首先的末后的存活的亲口告知——告知我们那时确能看见*必*为真、却如此迟信的事——的喜乐：颤抖之药是大能的同在；惧怕在力量面前站立不住；看得见的神是死的毁灭；宇宙中唯一的安全，是那存活者的完全临近！神是存有；死无处可寻！由那知道者的亲口受教，是何等的事！他告诉他的仆人保罗：能力在软弱中得以完全；在这里他教导他的仆人约翰：当怕的是软弱，不是力量。力量的一切外观——凡能正当地动恐怖的——都只是虚假的外观；真刚强的是*那一位*，正如真良善的是那一位。那存活的有着生命的大能；那恶者只有死的大能——死的本性正需要被毁灭。
但那存活者最温和显示的荣耀也如此之大，连他最亲爱的使徒、人子中最好的一个，一见也颓然。

===Original===

He has not yet learned that glory itself is a part of his inheritance, yea is of the natural condition of his being; that there is nothing in the man made in the image of God alien from the most glorious of heavenly shows: he has not learned this yet, and falls as dead before it﻿—when lo, the voice of him that was and is and is forevermore, telling him not to be afraid﻿—for the very reason, the one only reason, that he is the first and the last, the living one! For what shall be the joy, the peace, the completion of him that lives, but closest contact with his Life?﻿—a contact close as ere he issued from that Life, only in infinitely higher kind, inasmuch as it is now willed on *both* sides. He who has had a beginning, needs the indwelling power of that beginning to make his being complete﻿—not merely complete to his consciousness, but complete in itself﻿—justified, rounded, ended where it began﻿—with an “endless ending.” Then is it complete even as God’s is complete, for it is one with the self-existent, blossoming in the air of that world wherein it is rooted, wherein it lives and grows. Far indeed from trembling because he on whose bosom he had leaned when the light of his love was all but shut in now stands with the glory of that love streaming forth, John Boanerges ought to have felt the more joyful and safe as the strength of the living one was more manifested. It was never because Jesus was clothed in the weakness of the flesh that he was fit to be trusted, but because he was strong with a strength able to take the weakness of the flesh for the garment wherein it could best work its work: that strength was now shining out with its own light, so lately pent within the revealing veil. Had John been as close in spirit to the Son of Man as he had been in bodily presence, he would have indeed fallen at his feet, but not as one dead﻿—as one too full of joy to stand before the life that was feeding his; he would have fallen, but not to lie there senseless with awe the most holy; he would have fallen to embrace and kiss the feet of him who had now a second time, as with a resurrection from above, arisen before him, in yet heavenlier plenitude of glory.
It is the man of evil, the man of self-seeking design, not he who would fain do right, not he who, even in his worst time, would at once submit to the word of the Master, who is reasonably afraid of power.

===Chinese===

他还没有学会：荣耀本身就是他产业的一部分，是的，是他存有的天然光景之一；照神形象受造的人里面，没有与天上最荣耀显示相异的东西：他还没有学会这个，就死了一样倒下——看哪，那昔在今在以后永在者的声音，告诉他不要怕——恰恰因为那唯一的理由：他是首先的、末后的、存活的！因为活着之人的喜乐、平安、成全，除了与他生命最紧的相触，还能是什么？——紧如他未从那生命出来之前，只是高无限等的类，因为它如今是*双方*意愿的。凡有过起始的，都需要那起始的内住大能使他的存有完全——不只是对他的意识完全，而是本身完全——得着辩护、得以圆满、结束在它开始之处——带着一个“无尽的结束”。那时它就完全如神的完全，因为它与那自有者为一，在那它所生根、所活所长之世界的空气中开花。约翰雷子既曾靠在那胸怀上——那时他爱之光几乎全然关在里面——如今那爱之荣耀倾流而出，他实在远不该发抖，倒该因那存活者的大能愈加彰显而愈加喜乐平安。耶稣从来不是因为他穿上肉体的软弱才配受信托，而是因为他刚强——那刚强能拿肉体的软弱作它最好作工的衣裳：那刚强如今正以自己的光照出，不久前还收在启示的幔内。约翰若在灵里像当年在身体上那样亲近人子，他仍会倒在他脚前——但不像死了的——像喜乐得在那喂养他之生命面前站立不住的；他会倒下，但不是躺在那里被至圣之敬畏压得失去知觉；他会倒下去拥抱并亲吻那如今第二次、仿佛从上头复活、以更属天的荣耀丰满在他面前升起来的那位的脚。
那心怀恶计、自私自谋的人——不是那切愿行义的、不是那即使在最坏的时候也肯立刻顺服夫子之话的人——才合理地害怕能力。

===Original===

When God is no longer the ruler of the world, and there is a stronger than he; when there is might inherent in evil, and making-energy in that whose nature is destruction; then will be the time to stand in dread of power. But even then the bad man would have no security against the chance of crossing some scheme of the lawless moment, where disintegration is the sole unity of plan, and being ground up and destroyed for some no-idea of the Power of darkness. And then would be the time for the good﻿—no, not to tremble, but to resolve with the Lord of light to endure all, to let every billow of evil dash and break upon him, nor do the smallest ill, tell the whitest lie for God﻿—knowing that any territory so gained could belong to no kingdom of heaven, could be but a province of the kingdom of darkness. If there were two powers, the one of evil, the other of good, as men have not unnaturally in ignorance imagined, his sense of duty would reveal the being born of the good power, while he born of the evil could have no choice but be evil. But Good only can create; and if Evil were ever so much the stronger, the duty of men would remain the same﻿—to hold by the Living One, and defy Power to its worst﻿—like Prometheus on his rock, defying Jove, and forever dying﻿—thus forever foiling the Evil. For Evil can destroy only itself and its own; it could destroy no enemy﻿—could at worst but cause a succession of deaths, from each of which the defiant soul would rise to loftier defiance, to more victorious endurance﻿—until at length it laughed Evil in the face, and the demon-god shrunk withered before it. In those then who believe that good is the one power, and that evil exists only because for a time it subserves, cannot help subserving the good, what place can there be for fear? The strong and the good are one; and if our hope coincides with that of God, if it is rooted in his will, what should we do but rejoice in the effulgent glory of the First and the Last?
The First and the Last is the enclosing defence of the castle of our being; the Master is before and behind; he began, he will see that it be endless. He garrisons the place; he is the living, the live-making one.
The reason then for not fearing before God is, that he is all-glorious, all-perfect. Our being needs the all-glorious, all-perfect God.

===Chinese===

当神不再是世界的统治者、而有比他更强的；当恶里面有内在的大能、在那本性为毁灭者里面有造作的能量；那时才是惧怕能力的时候。但即使到那时，坏人也没有保障，防不住偶然撞上那无法无天之时刻的某个图谋——那里解体是唯一的计划统一——而被那黑暗之大能的某个无意义磨碎毁掉。而那时是好人——不，不是发抖、而是与光之主同心决意忍受一切的时候：让邪恶的每一道巨浪冲他、在他身上破碎，也不为神行最小的恶、说最白的谎——知道那样得来的任何疆土不能属任何天国、只能是黑暗之国的一省。若真有两大权能，一恶一善——如人在无知中并非不自然地想象过的——则义务感会显明人是善的权能所生，而那恶权能所生的别无选择、只能为恶。但唯有善能创造；而恶即使再强，人的义务仍然一样——忠于那存活的，向大能挑战到底——像磐石上的普罗米修斯（Prometheus），蔑视朱庇特，永远死去——如此永远挫败那恶。因为恶只能毁它自己和属它的；它毁不了仇敌——至多造成一连串的死，每一次死，那不屈的灵魂都要起来作更高的不屈、更得胜的忍受——直到末了它当面嘲笑恶，那鬼魔之神在它面前枯萎。那么在那些信善是独一大能、信恶之存在只因它一时服役于善、不能不服役于善的人里面，还能有什么惧怕的余地？刚强的与良善的是一；我们的盼望若与神的盼望相合、若扎根在他的旨意里，除了在那首先者末后者的光辉荣耀中喜乐，我们还该作什么？
那首先的末后的是我们存有之堡的环围防御；主在前在后；他开始了，他必看顾它无尽。他驻防此地；他是活着的、赐活的那位。
所以在神面前不惧怕的理由是：他是全荣耀、全完全的。我们的存有需要那全荣耀、全完全的神。
