To deny oneself then, is to act no more from the standing-ground of self; to allow no private communication, no passing influence between the self and the will; not to let the right hand know what the left hand doeth. No grasping or seeking, no hungering of the individual, shall give motion to the will; no desire to be conscious of worthiness shall order the life; no ambition whatever shall be a motive of action; no wish to surpass another be allowed a moment’s respite from death; no longing after the praise of men influence a single throb of the heart. To deny the self is to shrink from no dispraise or condemnation or contempt of the community, or circle, or country, which is against the mind of the Living one; for no love or entreaty of father or mother, wife or child, friend or lover, to turn aside from following him, but forsake them all as any ruling or ordering power in our lives; we must do nothing to please them that would not first be pleasing to him. Right deeds, and not the judgment thereupon; true words, and not what reception they may have, shall be our care. Not merely shall we not love money, or trust in it, or seek it as the business of life, but, whether we have it or have it not, we must never think of it as a windfall from the tree of event or the cloud of circumstance, but as the gift of God. We must draw our life, by the uplooking, acknowledging will, every moment fresh from the living one, the causing life, not glory in the mere consciousness of health and being. It is God feeds us, warms us, quenches our thirst.

===Chinese===

它不可作自己的律；基督必须作它的律。时候将到，那时它要被内住的神——那位是它更深的、最深的自己者——如此据有、如此扩大、如此理想化，以致不再需要任何强制的对它的否认；它已被最终地否认、拒绝、遣回它顺服的本位；它已学会感恩地领受、一无所求；不再绕着自己的中心打转、不再想供奉自己的好处。神对他自己的永恒否认——在那为我们、在肉身中天天背起他十架者身上启示出来的——将在那人里面得着发展；他永恒的喜乐将在神里面——并在他同伴们里面，在他们面前，他要把自己那喜乐的自己抛下，作他们行走的地毯、安歇的脚凳、攀登的阶梯。
那么，舍己，就是不再从自我的立足点行动；不容自我与意志之间有任何私下的交通、任何过往的影响；不让右手知道左手所作的。任何的攫取或寻求、任何的个体饥饿，都不可给意志以动力；任何求配得之意识的欲望都不可调度生活；任何野心都不可作行动的动机；任何想胜过别人的愿望，不可容它有一刻豁免于死；任何对人称的切慕不可影响心的每一次跳动。舍己，就是面对那与存活者之心相违的社群、圈子或国家的非难、定罪或轻蔑，毫不退缩；不为父母、妻儿、朋友或恋人的任何爱或恳求，转离对他的跟从，而把他们全然撇下、不作我们生活中任何统治或调度的力量；凡不先讨他喜悦的事，我们一件也不可为讨他们喜悦而行。当在意的，是正当的行为，而不是对它的评判；是真话，而不是它们可能受到的接待，而不是它们可能有怎样的被接受。我们不可仅不爱金钱、不信靠它、不以它为人生的正业，而且，无论有它没有它，都永不可把它想作从事件之树或环境之云落下的一阵横财，而要当作神的恩赐。我们必须靠那仰望的、承认的意志，每一刻从那存活者、那赋予生命者，重新汲取我们的生命，而不在单单的健康与存有的意识里自夸。是神喂养我们、温暖我们、解我们的渴。

===Original===

The will of God must be to us all in all; to our whole nature the life of the Father must be the joy of the child; we must know our very understanding his﻿—that we live and feed on him every hour in the closest, veriest way: to know these things in the depth of our knowing, is to deny ourselves, and take God instead. To try after them is to begin the denial, to follow him who never sought his own. So must we deny all anxieties and fears. When young we must not mind what the world calls failure; as we grow old, we must not be vexed that we cannot remember, must not regret that we cannot do, must not be miserable because we grow weak or ill: we must not mind anything. We have to do with God who can, not with ourselves where we cannot; we have to do with the Will, with the Eternal Life of the Father of our spirits, and not with the being which we could not make, and which is his care. He is our care; we are his; our care is to will his will; his care, to give us all things. This is to deny ourselves. “Self, I have not to consult you, but him whose idea is the soul of you, and of which as yet you are all unworthy. I have to do, not with you, but with the source of you, by whom it is that any moment you exist﻿—the Causing of you, not the caused you. You may be my consciousness, but you are not my being. If you were, what a poor, miserable, dingy, weak wretch I should be! but my life is hid with Christ in God, whence it came, and whither it is returning﻿—with you certainly, but as an obedient servant, not a master. Submit, or I will cast you from me, and pray to have another consciousness given me. For God is more to me than my consciousness of myself. He is my life; you are only so much of it as my poor half-made being can grasp﻿—as much of it as I can now know at once. Because I have fooled and spoiled you, treated you as if you were indeed my own self, you have dwindled yourself and have lessened me, till I am ashamed of myself. If I were to mind what you say, I should soon be sick of you; even now I am ever and anon disgusted with your paltry, mean face, which I meet at every turn. No! let me have the company of the Perfect One, not of you! of my elder brother, the Living One! I will not make a friend of the mere shadow of my own being! Goodbye, Self! I deny you, and will do my best every day to leave you behind me.”

===Chinese===

神的旨意于我们必须是在一切之中作一切；对我们全人，父的生命必须作孩子的喜乐；我们必须知道我们的悟性也是他的——我们每小时都以致切、至真的方式活在他身上、靠他喂养：在我们知道的深处知道这些事，就是舍己、以神代之。追求它们，就是开始那否认、开始跟从那位从不寻求自己的人。这样，我们必须否认一切的焦虑与惧怕。年轻时，我们不可在意世界所谓的失败；年老时，我们不可因不能记忆而烦恼、不可因不能作为而懊悔、不可因衰弱或疾病而悲苦：我们什么都不当在意。我们打交道的是那能的神，不是那不能的我们自己；我们打交道的是旨意、是我们灵之父的永恒生命，不是那我们自己造不出、又属他看顾的存有。他是我们的挂念；我们是他的；我们的挂念是意愿他的旨意；他的挂念，是把万物赐给我们。这就是舍己。“自我啊，我无须与你商量，只须与他——他的观念是你的灵魂、而至今你全不配它——商量。我打交道的不是你，而是你的源头，你每一刻的存在都靠他——是那造成你的，不是你这被造的。你可以作我的意识，但你不是我的存有。你若是，我将是个何等可怜、悲惨、昏暗、软弱的家伙！但我的生命与基督一同藏在神里面，从那里来，也归回那里去——当然带着你，但作为一个顺服的仆人，不是主人。降服吧，否则我要把你从我抛开，求他另赐我一个意识。因为神于我，多于我对自己的意识。他是我的生命；你不过是那生命的一部分，我这一半造成的可怜存有所能把握的——我此刻所能一下子知道的那么多。因为我愚弄了你、惯坏了你、待你仿佛真是我自己的自己，你就萎缩了你自己、也削减了我，直到我以自己为耻。我若理会你所说的话，我很快就会厌弃你；即便此刻，我也时时厌恶你那鄙陋、卑劣的脸——每个转弯都碰见的脸。不！让我与那完全者相伴，不与你！与我的长兄、那存活者相伴！我不愿与自己存有的影子作朋友！再会吧，自我！我否认你，并且每天尽力把你留在身后。”

===Original===

And in this regard we must not fail to see, or seeing ever forget, that, when Jesus tells us we must follow him, we must come to him, we must believe in him, he speaks first and always as *the Son* of the Father﻿—and that in the active sense, as the obedient God, not merely as one who claims the sonship for the ground of being and so of further claim. He is the Son of the Father as the Son who obeys the Father, as the Son who came expressly and only to do the will of the Father, as the messenger whose delight it is to do the will of him that sent him. At the moment he says “Follow me,” he is following the Father; his face is set homeward. He would have us follow him because he is bent on the will of the Blessed. It is nothing even thus to think of him, except thus we *believe* in him﻿—that is, so do. To believe in him is to do as he does, to follow him where he goes. We must believe in him *practically*﻿—altogether practically, as he believed in his Father; not as one concerning whom we have to hold something, but as one whom we have to follow out of the body of this death into life eternal. It is not to follow him to take him in any way theoretically, to hold this or that theory about why he died, or wherein lay his atonement: such things can be revealed only to those who follow him in his active being and the principle of his life﻿—who do as he did, live as he lived. There is no other following. He is all for the Father; we must be all for the Father too, else are we not following him. To follow him is to be learning of him, to think his thoughts, to use his judgments, to see things as he saw them, to feel things as he felt them, to be hearted, souled, minded, as he was﻿—that so also we may be of the same mind with his Father. This it is to deny self and go after him; nothing less, even if it be working miracles and casting out devils, is to be his disciple. Busy from morning to night doing great things for him on any other road, we should but earn the reception, “I never knew you.” When he says, “Take my yoke upon you,” he does not mean a yoke which he would lay upon our shoulders; it is his own yoke he tells us to take, and to learn of him﻿—it is the yoke he is himself carrying, the yoke his perfect Father had given him to carry. The will of the Father is the yoke he would have us take, and bear also with him.

===Chinese===

在这事上，我们不可看不见——或看见了就忘记——当耶稣告诉我们必须跟从他、必须到他那里、必须信他时，他首先、且始终是作为父的*子*说话——且是主动意义上的：作为顺服的神，不只是作为一位把儿子名分当作存有根据、从而当作进一步主张之根据者。他是父的子，作为顺服父的子、作为特意且唯独来行父旨意的子、作为以行差他来者旨意为乐的信使。当他说“跟从我”的那一刻，他正在跟从父；他的脸定意向家。他要我们跟从他，因为他一心于那蒙福者的旨意。连这样想他也算不得什么，除非我们如此*信*他——就是说，如此行。信他，就是照他所作的去作、跟从他到哪里。我们必须*实行地*信他——全然实行地，像他信他的父那样；不是作为一位我们对之必须持守什么的人，而是作为一位我们必须从这取死的身体里跟从出来、进入永生的人。照理论的方式接受他——持守这套那套关于他为何死、或他的赎罪（atonement）何在的理论——不是跟从他：这样的事只能向那些在他活泼的存有与生命的原则中跟从他的人——照他行的行、照他活的活——启示。没有别的跟从。他一切都为父；我们也必须一切都为父，否则就不是跟从他。跟从他，就是向他学、想他的思想、用他的判断、照他看事物那样看事物、照他感受那样感受——以他的心为心、以他的魂为魂、以他的意念为意念——好叫我们也与他的父同一心意。这才是舍己而去跟从他；少于这个——哪怕行神迹赶鬼——也不配作他的门徒。若在别的路上从早到晚忙着为他作大事，我们只会赚得那句回答：“我从来不认识你们。”当他说“你们当负我的轭”时，他不是指一副他要放在我们肩上的轭；他叫我们取的、学的是*他自己*的轭——是他自己正扛着的轭、他那完全的父给他扛的轭。父的旨意就是他要我们取的轭，且要与他一同扛。

===Original===

It is of this yoke that he says, “It is easy,” of this burden, “It is light.” He is not saying, “The yoke I lay upon you is easy, the burden light”; what he says is, “The yoke I carry is easy, the burden on my shoulders is light.” With the garden of Gethsemane before him, with the hour and the power of darkness waiting for him, he declares his yoke easy, his burden light. There is no magnifying of himself. *He first* denies himself, and takes up his cross﻿—then tells us to do the same. The Father magnifies the Son, not the Son himself; the Son magnifies the Father.
We must be jealous for God against ourselves, and look well to the cunning and deceitful Self﻿—ever cunning and deceitful until it is informed of God﻿—until it is thoroughly and utterly denied, and God is to it also All-in-all﻿—till we have left it quite empty of our will and our regard, and God has come into it, and made it﻿—not indeed an adytum, but a pylon for himself. Until then, its very denials, its very turnings from things dear to it for the sake of Christ, will tend to foster its self-regard, and generate in it a yet deeper self-worship. While it is not denied, only thwarted, we may through satisfaction with conquered difficulty and supposed victory, minister yet more to its self-gratulation. The Self, when it finds it cannot have honour because of its gifts, because of the love lavished upon it, because of its conquests, and the “golden opinions bought from all sorts of people,” will please itself with the thought of its abnegations, of its unselfishness, of its devotion to God, of its forsakings for his sake. It may not *call* itself, but it will soon *feel* itself a saint, a superior creature, looking down upon the foolish world and its ways, walking on high “above the smoke and stir of this dim spot”;﻿—all the time dreaming a dream of utter folly, worshipping itself with the more concentration that it has yielded the approbation of the world, and dismissed the regard of others: even they are no longer necessary to its assurance of its own worths and merits! In a thousand ways will Self delude itself, in a thousand ways befool its own slavish being. Christ sought not his own, sought not anything but the will of his Father: we have to grow diamond-clear, true as the white light of the morning. Hopeless task!﻿—were it not that he offers to come himself, and dwell in us.

===Chinese===

他说“容易”的，正是这轭；说“轻省”的，正是这担子。他不是在说“我放在你们身上的轭是容易的、担子是轻省的”；他说的是“我所扛的轭是容易的、我肩上的担子是轻省的”。面对着客西马尼园，面对着那等候他的时辰与黑暗的权势，他仍宣告他的轭容易、他的担子轻省。这里没有自我夸大。*他先*舍己、先背起他的十架——然后才叫我们照样行。父高举子，不是子高举自己；子高举父。
我们必须为神而戒备自己，谨防那诡诈欺人的自我——它一直诡诈欺人，直到被神浸透——直到被彻底而全然地否认、神对它也成为在一切之中作一切——直到我们已把我们的意志与顾念从它里面完全倒空、神已进来占据了它、使它——实在说不是至圣所、而是他自己的殿前塔。在那之前，它那些否认、那些为基督的缘故从它所亲爱之物转开，都只会助长它的自我顾念、在它里面生出更深的自我崇拜。当它未被否认、只是被违逆时，我们或会因征服了艰难、因想象的胜利而满足，反倒更喂养它的自得。那自我，当它发现自己不能因才干得尊荣、不能因倾浇于它的爱、不能因它的征服和“从各色人等买来的金色舆论”得尊荣时，就要以它的克己、它的无私、它对神的奉献、它为主的撇弃自娱。它或许不*称*自己、却很快会*觉*自己是一位圣徒、一个高等的受造者，俯看那愚昧的世界和它的道路，行在高处、“在这暗淡尘嚣之上”；——其实一直在作一场全然愚妄的梦，且因为它已交出了世界的赞许、遣散了他人的顾念，就以更集中的程度拜自己：连那些对它确信自身价值与功德都不再需要了！自我会以千种方式自欺，以千种方式愚弄它那奴性的存有。基督不寻求自己的，不寻求任何东西、唯独父的旨意：我们必须长成金刚石般透明、真实如清晨的白光。无望的工作！——若非他应许要亲自来、住在我们里面。

===Original===

I have wondered whether the word of the Lord, “take up his cross,” was a phrase in use at the time: when he used it first he had not yet told them that he would himself be crucified. I can hardly believe this form of execution such a common thing that the figure of bearing the cross had come into ordinary speech. As the Lord’s idea was new to men, so I think was the image in which he embodied it. I grant it *might*, being such a hateful thing in the eyes of the Jews, have come to represent the worst misery of a human being; but would they be ready to use as a figure a fact which so sorely manifested their slavery? I hardly think it. Certainly it had not come to represent the thing he was now teaching, that self-abnegation which he had but newly brought to light﻿—nay, hardly to the light yet﻿—only the twilight; and nothing less, it seems to me, can have suggested the terrible symbol!
But we must note that, although the idea of the denial of self is an entire and absolute one, yet the thing has to be done *daily*: we must keep on denying. It is a deeper and harder thing than any sole effort of most herculean will may finally effect. For indeed the will itself is not pure, is not free, until the Self is absolutely denied. It takes long for the water of life that flows from the well within us, to permeate every outlying portion of our spiritual frame, subduing everything to itself, making it all of the one kind, until at last, reaching the outermost folds of our personality, it casts out disease, our bodies by indwelling righteousness are redeemed, and the creation delivered from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God. Every day till then we have to take up our cross; every hour to see that we are carrying it. A birthright may be lost for a mess of pottage, and what Satan calls a trifle must be a thing of eternal significance.
Is there not many a Christian who, having begun to deny himself, yet spends much strength in the vain and evil endeavour to accommodate matters between Christ and the dear Self﻿—seeking to save that which so he must certainly lose﻿—in how different a way from that in which the Master would have him lose it!

===Chinese===

我曾疑惑，主那句“背起他的十架”，是不是当时通行的俗语：因为他初次使用它时，还没有告诉他们他自己将被钉十架。我很难相信这种行刑方式常见到“背十架”的形象已进入日常言语。正如主的观念对人来说是新的，我想那体现这观念的意象也是新的。我承认它*或许*——作为犹太人眼中如此可憎之物——已可代表一个人最坏的惨境；但他们会乐意用一件如此刺痛地显明他们奴役的事实作比喻吗？我不以为然。它当然还不曾代表他此刻所教导的东西——那他刚刚带进光中的舍己——不，还谈不上光、只是暮色；而在我看来，没有什么低于这个能暗示出那可畏的象征！
但我们必须注意：虽然舍己的观念是整全而绝对的，这事却必须*天天*去作：我们必须不断否认。这比任何海克力斯式意志的一次性努力所能最终成就的都更深更难。因为实在说，意志本身还未纯净、还未自由，直到自我被绝对否认。那从我们里面之井涌出的生命之水，需要长时间才渗透我们属灵身体的每一个边远部分，把一切都降服于它、使它全成一类，直到最后到达我们人格最外的褶层、逐出疾病、我们的身体因内住的义（righteousness）得赎、受造之物脱离败坏的辖制、进入神儿女自由的荣耀。在那日之前，我们天天必须背起我们的十架；每小时必须查看我们正扛着它。一碗红豆汤可以卖掉长子名分，而撒但所谓的小事必是含有永远意义的事。
岂不是有许多基督徒，既已开始舍己，却仍花许多力气、在基督与亲爱的自我之间徒然而邪恶地调和——寻求照这样救那他必失去的——与主要他失去它的方式何等不同！

===Original===

It is one thing to have the loved self devoured of hell in hate and horror and disappointment; another to yield it to conscious possession by the living God himself, who will raise it then first and only to its true individuality, freedom, and life. With its cause within it, then, indeed, it shall be saved!﻿—how then should it but live! Here is the promise to those who will leave all and follow him: “Whosoever shall lose his life, for my sake, the same shall save it,”﻿—in St. Matthew, “find it.” What speech of men or angels will serve to shadow the dimly glorious hope! To lose ourselves in the salvation of God’s heart! to be no longer any care to ourselves, but know God taking divinest care of us, his own! to be and feel just a resting-place for the divine love﻿—a branch of the tree of life for the dove to alight upon and fold its wings! to be an open air of love, a thoroughfare for the thoughts of God and all holy creatures! to know one’s self by the reflex action of endless brotherly presence﻿—yearning after nothing from any, but ever pouring out love by the natural motion of the spirit! to revel in the hundredfold of everything good we may have had to leave for his sake﻿—above all, in the unsought love of those who love us as we love them﻿—circling us round, bathing us in bliss﻿—never reached after, ever received, ever welcomed, altogether and divinely precious! to know that God and we mean the same thing, that we are in the secret, the child’s secret of existence, that we are pleasing in the eyes and to the heart of the Father! to live nestling at his knee, climbing to his bosom, blessed in the mere and simple being which is one with God, and is the outgoing of his will, justifying the being by the very facts of the being, by its awareness of itself as bliss!﻿—what a self is this to receive again from him for that we left, forsook, refused! We left it paltry, low, mean; he took up the poor cinder of a consciousness, carried it back to the workshop of his spirit, made it a true thing, radiant, clear, fit for eternal companying and indwelling, and restored it to our having and holding forever!
All high things can be spoken only in figures; these figures, having to do with matters too high for them, cannot *fit* intellectually; they can be interpreted truly, understood aright, only by such as have the spiritual fact in themselves.

===Chinese===

让蒙爱的自我在恨恶、惊骇与失望中被地狱（hell）吞灭是一回事；把它交给永活神自己有意识的占有——他要那时才、且唯有那时把它升到它真实的个体性、自由与生命——是另一回事。它的因由既在它里面，那时它实在必得救！——那时它怎能不活！这是对那些愿撇下一切跟从他之人的应许：“凡为我丧掉生命的，必救了生命”——在圣马太书里作“得着生命”。什么人的或天使的言语，能荫庇这朦胧而荣耀的盼望！在神心之救恩里失丧我们自己！不再作自己的任何挂虑，而知道神以最属神的看顾看顾我们、他自己的！只作并只觉自己是属神之爱的一个安歇之所——生命之树的一枝、供鸽子降落收翅！作一股敞开的爱之空气、神与一切圣洁受造者思想的一条通道！借那无尽弟兄同在的反作用认识自己——不向任何人索取什么，却凭灵的自然运行不断倾出爱！为我们为主的缘故可能不得不撇下的一切善物、得着百倍而欢腾——尤其在那不求而得之爱里，那些我们怎样爱他们、他们也怎样爱我们的人——环绕我们、浸我们于福乐——从不追求、却不断领受、不断被欢迎、全然而属神地宝贵！知道神与我们同指一意、知道我们在那秘密里——存在的孩子之秘密里、知道我们在父的眼与心里蒙喜悦！活在他的膝旁偎依、攀上他的胸怀、在那与神为一、为他旨意之流出的单纯存有里蒙福——借那存有的事实本身、借它作为福乐的自我意识、成全那存有！——这是怎样的一个自我，代替我们所撇下、所离弃、所拒绝的、从他那里重新领受！我们撇下它时，它鄙陋、低微、卑劣；他拾起那可怜的意识炭渣，带回他灵的工场，把它作成一件真东西、放射的、明澈的、配得上永恒的相伴与内住，并归还给我们永远拥有持守！
一切高的事只能用比喻说；这些比喻既关乎对它们过高的事，就不能在智性上*相合*；唯有那在自己里面具有那属灵事实的人，才能真实地解释、正确地理解它们。

===Original===

When we speak of a man and his soul, we imply a self and a self, reacting on each other: we cannot divide ourselves so; the figure suits but imperfectly. It was never the design of the Lord to explain things to our understanding﻿—nor would that in the least have helped our necessity; what we require is a means, a word, whereby to think with ourselves of high things: that is what a true figure, for a figure may be true while far from perfect, will always be to us. But the imperfection of his figures cannot lie in excess. Be sure that, in dealing with any truth, its symbol, however high, must come short of the glorious meaning itself holds. It is the low stupidity of an unspiritual nature that would interpret the Lord’s meaning as less than his symbols. The true soul sees, or will come to see, that his words, his figures always represent more than they are able to present; for, as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are the heavenly things higher than the earthly signs of them, let the signs be good as ever sign may be. There is no joy belonging to human nature, as God made it, that shall not be enhanced a hundredfold to the man who gives up himself﻿—though, in so doing, he may seem to be yielding the very essence of life. To yield self is to give up grasping at things in their second causes, as men call them, but which are merely God’s means, and to receive them direct from their source﻿—to take them seeing whence they come, and not as if they came from nowhere, because no one appears presenting them. The careless soul receives the Father’s gifts as if it were a way things had of dropping into his hand. He thus grants himself a slave, dependent on chance and his own blundering endeavour﻿—yet is he ever complaining, as if someone were accountable for the checks which meet him at every turn. For the good that comes to him, he gives no thanks﻿—who is there to thank? at the disappointments that befall him he grumbles﻿—there must be someone to blame! He does not think to what Power it could be of any consequence, nay, what power would not be worse than squandered, to sustain him after his own fashion, in his paltry, low-aimed existence! How could a God pour out his being to uphold the merest waste of his creatures? No world could ever be built or sustained on such an idea.

===Chinese===

当我们说到一个人和他的灵魂时，我们默认了一个自我与一个自我、彼此互动；我们不能这样分割自己；这比喻只有不完全的合适。主从来无意把事物解释给我们的悟性——那也全然帮不了我们的必需；我们需要的是一个凭借、一个词语，好与我们自己思想高的事：这正是真实的比喻——因为比喻尽可以真实而远非完全——将永远于我们的。但他比喻的不完全不可能在于过量。可以确信，在处理任何真理时，它的象征无论多高，必短于那荣耀的意义本身。把主的意思解说得少于他的象征，是属灵不入之天性的低劣愚钝。真实的灵魂看见、或将看见：他的话、他的比喻总是代表多于它们所能呈现的；因为正如天怎样高过地，天上的事也怎样高过它们地上的记号，任凭那些记号好到记号所能的极处。凡属人性——如神所造的——的喜乐，没有一样不给那交出自己的人增多百倍——尽管他这样作时，看似交出了生命的本质。交出自我，就是放弃抓取事物的第二因——如人们所称——它们不过是神的手段，而从它们的源头直接领受它们——看见它们从何处来而取，不当作从无处来、因为没有人显现在那里递送。那漫不经心的灵魂领受父的恩赐，仿佛那是事物掉进他手里的一种方式。他就这样自封为奴，靠机遇和他自己跌撞的努力——却总在抱怨，仿佛有谁当为他每个转弯所遇的挫折负责。临到他的善，他不感谢——有谁可感谢呢？遭遇失望，他嘟囔——总有谁可怪罪！他不想一想，他的那种存续方式、他那鄙陋、低目标的生存，对什么大能会有任何价值——不，什么大能支撑它不是浪费更坏！一位神怎能倾倒他的存有、去支撑他受造物中最纯粹的浪费？没有一个世界能照这样的观念被建造或维系。

===Original===

It is the children who shall inherit the earth; such as will not be children, cannot possess. The hour is coming when all that art, all that science, all that nature, all that animal nature, in ennobling subjugation to the higher even as man is subject to the Father, can afford, shall be the possession, to the endless delight, of the sons and daughters of God: to him to whom he is all in all, God is able to give these things; to another he cannot give them, for he is unable to receive them who is outside the truth of them. Assuredly we are not to love God for the sake of what he can give us; nay, it is impossible to love him save because he is our God, and altogether good and beautiful; but neither may we forget what the Lord does not forget, that, in the end, when the truth is victorious, God will answer his creature in the joy of his heart. For what is joy but the harmony of the spirit! The good Father made his children to be joyful; only, ere they can enter into his joy, they must be like himself, ready to sacrifice joy to truth. No promise of such joy is an appeal to selfishness. Every reward held out by Christ is a pure thing; nor can it enter the soul save as a death to selfishness. The heaven of Christ is a loving of all, a forgetting of self, a dwelling of each in all, and all in each. Even in our nurseries, a joyful child is rarely selfish, generally righteous. It is not selfish to be joyful. What power could prevent him who sees the face of God from being joyful?﻿—that bliss is his which lies behind all other bliss, without which no other bliss could ripen or last. The one bliss of the universe is the presence of God﻿—which is simply God being to the man, and felt by the man as being, that which in his own nature he is﻿—the indwelling power of his life. God must be to his creature what he is in himself, for it is by his essential being alone, that by which he is, that he can create. His presence is the unintermittent call and response of the creative to the created, of the father to the child. Where can be the selfishness in being so made happy? It may be deep selfishness to refuse to be happy. Is there selfishness in the Lord’s seeing of the travail of his soul and being satisfied? Selfishness consists in taking the bliss from another; to find one’s bliss in the bliss of another is not selfishness.

===Chinese===

承受大地的必是孩子们；凡不肯作孩子的，就不能拥有。那时刻要来：到时一切艺术、一切科学、一切自然、一切动物天性——在对高者的升华的降服中，正如人对父的降服——所能供献的，都必成为神儿女的产业、成为他们无尽的喜乐：对那以他为万有中之万有的人，神能把这些东西给他；给另一个人他不能给，因为在那些事物的真实之外的人无法领受它们。诚然，我们不可为神能给我们什么而爱他；不，除非因为他是我们的神、全然良善美丽，就不可能爱他；但我们也不可忘记主所不忘记的：末了，当真理得胜时，神必以他心中的喜乐回答他的受造者。因为喜乐是什么？不过是灵的和谐！那良善的父造他的儿女，是要他们喜乐；只是，他们能进入他的喜乐之前，必须像他自己，预备好为真理牺牲喜乐。这样喜乐的应许，没有一样是向自私的诉求。基督所持出的每一个赏赐都是纯净之物；且唯有作为向自私的一场死，它才能进入灵魂。基督的天堂是爱众人、忘自己、各人住在众人里面、众人在各人里面。连在我们的育儿室里，喜乐的孩子也少有自私、多半正当。喜乐不是自私。凡看见神面的，有什么能拦阻他喜乐呢？——那福乐是躺在一切别的福乐之后、没有它任何别的福乐都不能成熟或长存的。宇宙的独一福乐是神的同在——就是神对那人成为、且被那人觉为神在他自己本性中所是的——他生命内住的大能。神对他的受造者必是他在自己里面所是，因为唯有借他的本质存有、借他借以存在的那个，他才能创造。他的同在是创造者对受造者、父对孩子那不间断的呼召与回应。这样被造而喜乐，自私在哪里？拒绝喜乐倒可能是深层的自私。主看见他魂的劳苦、便心满意足，这里有自私吗？自私在于从别人夺去福乐；在别人的福乐里找到自己的福乐，不是自私。

===Original===

Joy is not selfishness; and the greater the joy thus reaped, the farther is that joy removed from selfishness. The one bliss, next to the love of God, is the love of our neighbour. If any say, “You love because it makes you blessed,” I deny it: “We are blessed, I say, because we love.” No one could attain to the bliss of loving his neighbour who was selfish and sought that bliss from love of himself. Love is unselfishness. In the main we love because we cannot help it. There is no merit in it: how should there be in any love?﻿—but neither is it selfish. There are many who confound righteousness with merit, and think there is nothing righteous where there is nothing meritorious. “If it makes you happy to love,” they say, “where is your merit? It is only selfishness!” There is no merit, I reply, yet the love that is born in us is our salvation from selfishness. It is of the very essence of righteousness. Because a thing is joyful, it does not follow that I do it for the joy of it; yet when the joy is in others, the joy is pure. That *certain* joys should be joys, is the very denial of selfishness. The man would be a demoniacally selfish man, whom love itself did not make joyful. It is selfish to enjoy in content beholding others lack; even in the highest spiritual bliss, to sit careless of others would be selfishness, and the higher the bliss, the worse the selfishness; but surely that bliss is right altogether of which a great part consists in labour that others may share it. Such, I will not doubt﻿—the labour to bring others in to share with us, will be a great part of our heavenly content and gladness. The making, the redeeming Father will find plenty of like work for his children to do. Dull are those, little at least can they have of Christian imagination, who think that where all are good, things must be dull. It is because there is so little good yet in them, that they know so little of the power or beauty of merest life divine. Let such make haste to be true. Interest will there be and variety enough, not without pain, in the ministration of help to those yet wearily toiling up the heights of truth﻿—perhaps yet unwilling to part with miserable self, which cherishing they are not yet worth being, or capable of having.
Some of the things a man may have to forsake in following Christ, he has not to forsake because of what they are in themselves.

===Chinese===

喜乐不是自私；并且这样收获的喜乐越大，它离自私越远。次于爱神之独一福乐的，是爱我们的邻舍。谁若说“你们爱，因为爱使你们有福”，我否认：“我们有福，我说，是因为我们爱。”没有一个自私而求福于自爱的人，能达到爱邻舍之福。爱就是无私。大体上我们爱，因为我们不能不爱。其中没有功德：任何爱里怎会有？——但它也不是自私。许多人把义（righteousness）与功德混为一谈，以为没有功德的地方就没有义。“爱若使你快乐，”他们说，“你的功德在哪里？那不过是自私！”没有功德，我回答；但那生在我们里面的爱，是我们脱离自私的救恩。它正是义的本质。一件事是喜乐的，不能推出我为它的喜乐而行它；但当喜乐在别人身上时，那喜乐是纯净的。*某些*喜乐之为喜乐，正是对自私的否认。一个连爱本身都不能使他喜乐的人，会是鬼魔般自私的人。以别人的匮乏为背景而自得地享受，是自私；连在最高的属灵福乐里，坐着不顾别人，也是自私，且福乐越高、自私越坏；但那福乐必是全然正当的——它的一大部分就在于劳碌使别人得以分享它。这样的劳碌——带别人进来与我们同享——将是我们天上满足与喜乐的一大部分，我不怀疑。那位创造、救赎的父，必为他儿女找到大量类似的工作。那些以为哪里的人都好、事情就必沉闷的人，是迟钝的——至少他们身上的基督徒想象力少得很。正因为他们里面的善还这样少，他们才对纯粹属神生命的大能与美知道得这样少。让这样的人赶紧成为真实。在那里，扶助那些还在疲惫地攀登真理之高坡——或许还不肯放开那悲惨的自我，抱着它就还不配存在、也无能拥有——的人，其中自有足够的兴味与多样，也不无痛苦。
一个人跟从基督所可能必须撇下的某些东西，他之必须撇下，不是因为它们本身如何。

===Original===

Neither nature, art, science, nor fit society, is of those things a man will lose in forsaking himself: they are God’s, and have no part in the world of evil, the false judgments, low wishes, and unrealities generally, that make up the conscious life of the self which has to be denied: such will never be restored to the man. But in forsaking himself to do what God requires of him﻿—his true work in the world, that is, a man may find he has to leave some of God’s things﻿—not to repudiate them, but for the time to forsake them, because they draw his mind from the absolute necessities of the true life in himself or in others. He may have to deny himself in leaving them﻿—not as bad things, but as things for which there is not room until those of paramount claim have been so heeded, that these will no longer impede but further them. Then he who knows God, will find that knowledge open the door of his understanding to all things else. He will become able to behold them from within, instead of having to search wearily into them from without. This gave to king David more understanding than had all his teachers. Then will the things he has had to leave, be restored to him a hundred fold. So will it be in the forsaking of friends. To forsake them for Christ, is not to forsake them as evil. It is not to cease to love them, “for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” it is﻿—not to allow their love to cast even a shadow between us and our Master; to be content to lose their approval, their intercourse, even their affection, where the Master says one thing and they another. It is to learn to love them in a far higher, deeper, tenderer, truer way than before﻿—a way which keeps all that was genuine in the former way, and loses all that was false. We shall love *their* selves, and disregard our own.
I do not forget the word of the Lord about “hating father and mother”: I have a glimpse of the meaning of it, but dare not attempt explaining it now. It is all against the self﻿—not against the father and mother.

===Chinese===

自然、艺术、科学、相宜的交往，都不属于人撇下自己时将失去的那些东西：它们是神的，在那恶世界——那构成必须被否认之自我之意识生活的虚假判断、低俗愿望与种种不实——里没有份：那样的东西永不会被归还给人。但人在撇下自己去行神所要求于他的——他在世上真实的工作——时，或会发现他不得不离开某些神的东西——不是弃绝它们，而是暂时撇下它们，因为它们把他的心思从他自己或别人里面真实生命的绝对必需上引开。他或须在撇下它们上舍己——不是当它们是坏东西，而是当它们尚无余地、直到那些有至上主张的事被这样听从了、以致它们不再拦阻、反而促进它们。那时，那认识神的人，将发现那认识为他悟性向别的一切事物开门。他将变得能从里面观看它们，而不必再从外面疲惫地探究它们。这给大卫王的理解，多过他一切的师傅。那时他不得不撇下的东西，必百倍归还他。撇下朋友也是如此。为基督撇下他们，不是把他们当邪恶撇下。不是不再爱他们——“不爱他所看见的弟兄，怎能爱没有看见的神呢？”——而是：不容他们的爱在我们的主与我们之间投下哪怕一片影；当主说一样、他们说另一样时，甘心失去他们的赞同、他们的交往、甚至他们的感情。这是学着以比从前远高、深、温柔、真实的方式爱他们——那方式保有从前一切真实的、去掉一切虚假的。我们将爱*他们的*自己，而不顾我们自己的。
我没有忘记主关于“恨父母”的话：我窥见它的意思，但此刻不敢尝试解释。它全是敌对自我——不是敌对父亲母亲。

===Original===

There is another kind of forsaking that may fall to the lot of some, and which they may find very difficult: the forsaking of such notions of God and his Christ as they were taught in their youth﻿—which they held, nor could help holding, at such time as they began to believe﻿—of which they have begun to doubt the truth, but to cast which away seems like parting with every assurance of safety.
There are so-called doctrines long accepted of good people, which how any man can love God and hold, except indeed by fast closing of the spiritual eyes, I find it hard to understand. If a man care more for opinion than for life, it is not worth any other man’s while to persuade him to renounce the opinions he happens to entertain; he would but put other opinions in the same place of honour﻿—a place which can *belong* to no opinion whatever: it matters nothing what such a man may or may not believe, for he is not a true man. By holding with a school he supposes to be right, he but bolsters himself up with the worst of all unbelief﻿—opinion calling itself faith﻿—unbelief calling itself religion. But for him who is in earnest about the will of God, it is of endless consequence that he should think rightly of God. He cannot come close to him, cannot truly know his will, while his notion of him is in any point that of a false god. The thing shows itself absurd. If such a man seem to himself to be giving up even his former assurance of salvation, in yielding such ideas of God as are unworthy of God, he must none the less, if he will be true, if he would enter into life, take up that cross also. He will come to see that he must follow *no* doctrine, be it true as word of man could state it, but the living Truth, the Master himself.
Good souls many will one day be horrified at the things they now believe of God. If they have not thought about them, but given themselves to obedience, they may not have done them much harm as yet; but they can make little progress in the knowledge of God, while, if but passively, holding evil things true of him. If, on the other hand, they do think about them, and find in them no obstruction, they must indeed be far from anything to be called a true knowledge of God.

===Chinese===

还有另一种撇下，或会落在某些人身上、且他们或会觉得很难：撇下他们幼年所受教导的、关于神和他的基督的那些观念——那些他们起初相信时持守着、也不能不持守的观念——他们已开始怀疑其真实，但要抛掉它们，仿佛就得与一切安全的把握分手。
有那么一些所谓教义，早为好人接受，人怎能一面爱神一面持守它们——除非真的紧紧闭上属灵的眼——我难以明白。一个人若看重意见过于生命，不值得任何人费力气劝他放弃他碰巧怀有的意见；他只会把别的意见放在同一个尊位上——一个根本不*属于*任何意见的位置：这样的人信什么不信什么，无关紧要，因为他不是一个真实的人。他投靠一个自以为对的学派，不过是拿最坏的不信——自称信心（faith）的意见、自称宗教的不信——撑住自己。但对那认真于神旨意的人，他对神的思想正当与否，有无尽的关系。他对神的观念在任何一点上是个假神的观念，他就不能就近他、不能真认识他的旨意。这事显出它自己的荒谬。这样的人若觉得自己在放弃那些配不上神的神观时，连从前得救的把握也在放弃，他若要真实、要进入生命，也必须背起那个十架。他将看见：他必须跟从的不是任何教义——哪怕真得如人的话所能陈述——而是那活的真理、夫子他自己。
许多善良的灵魂，有一日要为他们如今对神所信的东西惊骇。他们若不曾思想它们、只把自己交给顺服（obedience），它们或许还没有给他们多大害处；但他们若哪怕只是被动地持守着关于神的恶事为真，就难在认识神上有多少进步。另一方面，他们若真思想它们、且在其中不见阻碍，他们就必离任何可称为对神之真认识的东西很远。

===Original===

But there are those who find them a terrible obstruction, and yet imagine, or at least fear them true: such must take courage to forsake the false in *any* shape, to deny their old selves in the most seemingly sacred of prejudices, and follow Jesus, not as he is presented in the tradition of the elders, but as he is presented by himself, his apostles, and the spirit of truth. There are “traditions of men” after Christ as well as before him, and far worse, as “making of none effect” higher and better things; and we have to look to it, *how we have learned Christ*.

===Chinese===

但也有那些发现它们是可怕阻碍、却还想象、或至少惧怕它们为真的人：这样的人必须鼓起勇气，在*任何*形状上撇弃那虚假的，在那些看似最神圣的偏见里否认他们的旧我，跟从耶稣——不是照古人的传统所呈现的他，而是照他自己、他的使徒、和真理之灵所呈现的他。基督之后有“人的传统”，正如他之前有，而且更坏，因为它们“废掉”更高更好的事；我们必须留心*我们是怎样学了基督*。

### The Truth in Jesus / 在耶稣里的真理
===Original===

> “But ye did not so learn Christ; if so be that ye heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus: that ye put away, as concerning your former manner of life, the old man, which waxeth corrupt after the lusts of deceit.”6

===Chinese===

> “但你们学了基督，却不是这样。如果你们听过他的道，领了他的教，学了他的真理——正如真理在耶稣里——就要脱去你们从前行为上的旧人，这旧人是因私欲的迷惑渐渐变坏的。”6

===Original===

How have we learned Christ? It ought to be a startling thought, that we may have learned him wrong. That must be far worse than not to have learned him at all: his place is occupied by a false Christ, hard to exorcize! The point is, whether we have learned Christ as he taught himself, or as men have taught him who thought they understood, but did not understand him. Do we think we know him﻿—with notions fleshly, after low, mean human fancies and explanations, or do we indeed know him﻿—after the spirit, in our measure as God knows him? The Christian religion, throughout its history, has been open to more corrupt misrepresentation than ever the Jewish could be, for as it is higher and wider, so must it yield larger scope to corruption:﻿—have we learned Christ in false statements and corrupted lessons about him, or have we learned *himself*? Nay, true or false, is only our brain full of things concerning him, or does he dwell himself in our hearts, a learnt, and ever being learnt lesson, the power of our life?
I have been led to what I am about to say, by a certain utterance of one in the front rank of those who assert that we can know nothing of the “Infinite and Eternal energy from which all things proceed”; and the utterance is this:﻿—
“The visiting on Adam’s descendants through hundreds of generations dreadful penalties for a small transgression which they did not commit; the damning of all men who do not avail themselves of an alleged mode of obtaining forgiveness, which most men have never heard of; and the effecting a reconciliation by sacrificing a son who was perfectly innocent, to satisfy the assumed necessity for a propitiatory victim; are modes of action which, ascribed to a human ruler, would call forth expressions of abhorrence; and the ascription of them to the Ultimate Cause of things, even not felt to be full of difficulties, must become impossible.”
I do not quote the passage with the design of opposing either clause of its statement, for I entirely agree with it: almost it feels an absurdity to say so. Neither do I propose addressing a word to the writer of it, or to any who hold with him. The passage bears out what I have often said﻿—that I never yet heard a word from one of that way of thinking, which even touched anything I hold. One of my earliest recollections is of beginning to be at strife with the false system here assailed.

===Chinese===

我们是怎样学了基督的？这该是个惊人的念头：我们可能学错了基督。那必定比完全没有学过他坏得多：他的位置被一个假基督占据了，难以驱逐！问题在于：我们是照他自己的教导学了基督，还是照那些自以为明白、却不明白他的人的教导学了他？我们是以为自己认识他——凭着属肉体的观念、照低劣属人的想象与解释——还是真认识他——照圣灵、照我们各人的度量如神认识他那样？基督宗教在其全部历史中，比犹太教更容易受败坏的歪曲，因为它越高越广，就给败坏留出越大的余地：——我们是在关于他的虚假陈述与败坏的功课里学了基督，还是学了*他自己*？不，且不论真假：是我们脑子里装满了关于他的事物，还是他自己住在我们心里，作一门已学、且永远在学的课、作我们生命的大能？
我被引到我要说的话，是因一位居于前列者的一个言论——那些主张我们对“万物所自出的无限永恒的能量”一无所知者中的一位；那言论是：——
“把可怕的刑罚加在亚当的后裔身上、贯数百代、为他们所未犯的一点小过犯；定一切不利用某种传闻的蒙赦之道——而大多数人从未听说过它——之人的罪；借牺牲一位全然无辜的儿子、来满足对挽回祭之必需的假定、而达成和好：这些行动方式，若归之于一位人间的统治者，必招来憎恶之辞；把它们归于万物的终极原因，即使不觉得满有难处，也必成为不可能。”
我引这段话，无意反驳其中任何一条陈述，因为我完全同意它：说同意几乎都显得多余。我也无意对写这话的人、或与他同见的人说什么。这段话印证了我常说的一句——我从那种思路的人那里，从未听到一句触到我所持任何东西的话。我最早的记忆之一，就是开始与这里被攻击的那个虚假体系相争。

===Original===

Such paganism I scorn as heartily in the name of Christ, as I scorn it in the name of righteousness. Rather than believe a single point involving its spirit, even with the assurance thereby of such salvation as the system offers, I would join the ranks of those who “know nothing,” and set myself with hopeless heart to what I am now trying with an infinite hope in the help of the pure originating One﻿—to get rid of my miserable mean self, comforted only by the chance that death would either leave me without thought more, or reveal something of the Ultimate Cause which it would not be an insult to him, or a dishonour to his creature, to hold concerning him. Even such a chance alone might enable one to live.
I will not now enquire how it comes that the writer of the passage quoted seems to put forward these so-called beliefs as representing Christianity, or even the creed of those who call themselves Christians, seeing so many, and some of them of higher rank in literature than himself, believing in Christ with true hearts, believe not one of such things as he has set down, but hold them in at least as great abhorrence as he: his answer would probably be, that, even had he been aware of such being the fact, what he had to deal with was the forming and ruling notions of religious society;﻿—and that such are the things held by the bulk of both educated and uneducated calling themselves Christians, however many of them may vainly think by an explanatory clause here and there to turn away the opprobrium of their falsehood, while they remain virtually the same﻿—that such are the things so held, I am, alas! unable to deny. It helps nothing, I repeat, that many, thinking little on the matter, use quasi mitigated forms to express their tenets, and imagine that so they indicate a different class of ideas: it would require but a brief examination to be convinced that they are not merely analogous﻿—they are ultimately identical.

===Chinese===

这样的异教之物，我奉基督之名的鄙弃，与奉义（righteousness）之名的鄙弃同样衷心。与其信其中牵涉其精神的一点——哪怕因此得着那体系所许的这样救恩——我宁肯加入那些“一无所知”者的行列，怀着无望的心去作我如今在纯净本原者的帮助下、怀着无限盼望所努力作的——脱去我悲惨鄙陋的自我，只以一个机会自慰：死亡要么使我不再有思想，要么启示一些关于终极原因的、持之为他不致是侮辱、于他的受造者不致是羞辱的东西。连这样一个机会本身，也足以使人活下去。
我现在不想追问：引文作者为何似乎把这些所谓信仰当作基督教、甚至当作自称基督徒者的信条，既然有那么多人——有些文学地位还高于他——以真心信基督、却不信他列下的任何一条、且至少同他一样憎恶它们；他的回答大概是：即便他知道事实如此，他要对付的是宗教社会里成形并占统治的观念；——而那些东西正是受过教育与未受教育的自称基督徒的大众所持的，无论其中多少人妄以为靠这里那里一条解释性的但书，就能挡开其虚假的骂名，而实质照旧——它们既是这样被持守着，唉！我无法否认。我重复：许多人在这事上想得少、用准缓和的形式表达他们的信条、并以为这样就指明了一类不同的观念，这毫无助益；只需简短的省察就会确信：它们不只是类似——它们根本相同。

===Original===

But had I to do with the writer, I should ask how it comes that, refusing these dogmas as abominable, and in themselves plainly false, yet knowing that they are attributed to men whose teaching has done more to civilize the world than that of any men besides﻿—how it comes that, seeing such teaching as this could not have done so, he has not taken such pains of enquiry as must surely have satisfied a man of his faculty that such was not their teaching; that it was indeed so different, and so good, that even the forced companionship of such horrible lies as those he has recounted, has been unable to destroy its regenerative power. I suppose he will allow that there was a man named Jesus, who died for the truth he taught: can he believe he died for such alleged truth as that? Would it not be well, I would ask him, to enquire what he did really teach, according to the primary sources of our knowledge of him? If he answered that the question was uninteresting to him, I should have no more to say; nor did I now start to speak of him save with the object of making my position plain to those to whom I would speak﻿—those, namely, who call themselves Christians.
If of them I should ask, “How comes it that such opinions are held concerning the Holy One, whose ways you take upon you to set forth?” I should be met by most with the answer, “Those are the things he tells us himself in his word; we have learned them from the Scriptures”; by many with explanations which seem to them so to explain the things that they are no longer to be reprobated; and by others with the remark that better ideas, though largely held, had not yet had time to show themselves as the belief of the thinkers of the nation. Of those whose presentation of Christian doctrine is represented in the quotation above, there are two classes﻿—such as are content it should be so, and such to whom those things are grievous, but who do not see how to get rid of them. To the latter it may be some little comfort to have one who has studied the New Testament for many years and loves it beyond the power of speech to express, declare to them his conviction that there is not an atom of such teaching in the whole lovely, divine utterance; that such things are all and altogether the invention of men﻿—honest invention, in part at least, I grant, but yet not true.

===Chinese===

但若让我对付这位作者，我要问：既拒绝这些可憎的、本身显然虚假的教条，又知道它们被归于那些其教导使世界开化之功大于任何旁人的人——怎么不见：这样的教导既然不可能成就那事，他就该费心查究、而那查究必足以使一位有他才具的人确信那不是他们的教导；那教导实在如此不同、如此良善，连他所历数那些可怕谎言的被迫相伴，也毁不掉它重生的大能？我想他会容许曾有一个人名叫耶稣、为他所传的真理而死：他能信他是为这样传闻的“真理”而死吗？我岂不该问他：照我们认识他的首要来源，查一查他到底教导了什么，岂不好？他若回答这问题于他无关趣，我就无话可说；我如今也不是为他起头说话，只是要向我要对其说话的人——就是那些自称基督徒的人——把我的立场摆明。
若我问他们：“关于那位圣者——他的道路你们既承当陈明——怎会有这样的意见被持守？”多数人会答：“那些是他在他的道里亲自告诉我们的；我们从圣经学了它们”；许多人会给在他们看来足以解释这些事、使它们不再可斥的解释；另一些人会说：更好的观念虽被广持，还没有时间显明为这民族思想者的信仰。在上述引文所代表之基督教义的人中，有两类——一类满足于事情如此，一类觉得那些事可痛、却看不出怎样摆脱。对后者，有一点小小的安慰也许可以给：一个人研读新约多年、爱它过于言语所能表达，向他们宣告他的确信：在那全部可爱、属神的言语中，没有一丝一毫这样的教导；这些事全然彻底是人的发明——诚实的发明，至少部分是，我承认，但终究不是真的。

===Original===

Thank God, we are nowise bound to accept any man’s explanation of God’s ways and God’s doings, however good the man may be, if it do not commend itself to our conscience. The man’s conscience may be a better conscience than ours, and his judgment clearer; nothing the more can we accept while we cannot see good: to do so would be to sin.
But it is by no means my object to set forth what I believe or do not believe; a time may come for that; my design is now very different indeed. I desire to address those who call themselves Christians, and expostulate with them thus:﻿—
Whatever be your *opinions* on the greatest of all subjects, is it well that the impression with regard to Christianity made upon your generation, should be that of your opinions, and not of something beyond opinion? Is Christianity capable of being represented by opinion, even the best? If it were, how many of us are such as God would choose to represent his thoughts and intents by our opinions concerning them? Who is there of his friends whom any thoughtful man would depute to represent his thoughts to his fellows? If you answer, “The opinions I hold and by which I represent Christianity, are those of the Bible,” I reply, that none can understand, still less represent, the opinions of another, but such as are of the same mind with him﻿—certainly none who mistake his whole scope and intent so far as in supposing *opinion* to be the object of any writer in the Bible. Is Christianity a system of articles of belief, let them be correct as language can give them? Never. So far am I from believing it, that I would rather have a man holding, as numbers of you do, what seem to me the most obnoxious untruths, opinions the most irreverent and gross, if at the same time he *lived* in the faith of the Son of God, that is, trusted in God as the Son of God trusted in him, than I would have a man with every one of whose formulas of belief I utterly coincided, but who knew nothing of a daily life and walk with God. The one, holding doctrines of devils, is yet a child of God; the other, holding the doctrines of Christ and his Apostles, is of the world, yea, of the devil.
“How! a man hold the doctrine of devils, and yet be of God?”
Yes; for to hold a thing with the intellect, is not to believe it.

===Chinese===

感谢神，无论那人多好，若他对神的道路与作为的解释不能荐于我们的良心，我们丝毫没有义务接受。那人的良心可以比我们的好、他的判断可以更清明；在我们还看不见其善时，我们一点也不能接受：接受就是罪。
但我绝非要陈明我信什么或不信什么；时候或许会来；我现在的用意实在大不相同。我要对那些自称基督徒的人说话，这样劝他们：——
无论你在这至大主题上的*意见*如何，你们这一代所得关于基督教的印象，竟是你们的意见、而不是某种超出意见的东西——这好吗？基督教能由意见来代表吗、哪怕最好的意见？若能，我们中间有几人是神会拣选来借其关于他思想意图的意见代表他思想意图的？谁的友人中，有哪一位会被任何有思想的人派去代表他的思想给同伴？你若回答：“我所持、并借以代表基督教的意见，是圣经的意见，”我回答：唯与那人同一心思的人，才能明白、更遑论代表他的意见——凡把他整个范围与意图错认到以为*意见*是圣经任何作者之目的的人，当然更不能。基督教是一套信条系统吗、哪怕那些信条正确得如语言所能给的？绝不是。我离信这个远到宁愿一个人持着——如你们许多人那样——在我看来最可憎的不实、最不敬最粗鄙的意见，只要他同时*活*在神儿子的信心里、就是说、照神儿子信靠神那样信靠神；而不愿一个人与我信条的每一条完全一致、却对天天与神同行的生活一无所知。前者持着鬼魔的教义，却是神的孩子；后者持着基督与他使徒的教义，却属世界，是的、属鬼魔。
“怎么！一个人持鬼魔的教义，却属于神？”
是；因为以悟性持有一件事，不等于信它。

===Original===

A man’s real belief is that which he lives by; and that which the man I mean lives by, is the love of God, and obedience to his law, so far as he has recognized it. Those hideous doctrines are outside of him; he *thinks* they are inside, but no matter; they are not true, and they cannot really be inside any good man. They are sadly against him; for he cannot love to dwell upon any of those supposed characteristics of his God; he acts and lives nevertheless in a measure like the true God. What a man believes, is the thing he does. This man would shrink with loathing from actions such as he thinks God justified in doing; like God, he loves and helps and saves. Will the living God let such a man’s opinions damn him? No more than he will let the correct opinions of another, who lives for himself, save him. The best salvation even the latter could give would be but damnation. What I come to and insist upon is, that, supposing your theories right, and containing all that is to be believed, yet those theories are not what makes you Christians, if Christians indeed you are. On the contrary, they are, with not a few of you, just what keeps you from being Christians. For when you say that, to be saved, a man must hold this or that, then are you leaving the living God and his will, and putting trust in some notion about him or his will. To make my meaning clearer﻿—some of you say we must trust in the finished work of Christ; or again, our faith must be in the merits of Christ﻿—in the atonement he has made﻿—in the blood he has shed: all these statements are a simple repudiation of the living Lord, *in whom* we are told to believe, who, by his presence with and in us, and our obedience to him, lifts us out of darkness into light, leads us from the kingdom of Satan into the glorious liberty of the sons of God. No manner or amount of belief *about him* is the faith of the New Testament. With such teaching I have had a lifelong acquaintance, and declare it most miserably false. But I do not now mean to dispute against it; except the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Christ Jesus make a man sick of his opinions, he may hold them to doomsday for me; for no opinion, I repeat, is Christianity, and no preaching of any plan of salvation is the preaching of the glorious gospel of the living God.

===Chinese===

一个人真实的信，是他借以活着的；而我所说的这人借以活着的，是对神的爱、对他律法的顺服（obedience）、照他已认出的程度。那些丑陋的教义在他外面；他*以为*它们在里面，但不要紧；它们不是真的，就不能真在任何好人里面。它们可悲地不利于他；因为他不能乐于默想任何他神的那些假设特性；他仍然在一定程度上照真神那样行动生活。人所信的，是他所行的。这人会怀着憎恶从他认为神行来为义的这类行动前退缩；像神那样，他爱、帮助、拯救。永活的神会让这人的意见定他的罪吗？断不会，正如他不会让另一个为自己活的人的正确意见救他。连后者所能给的最好的救恩，也不过是定罪。我来到并坚持的是：假定你们的理论对、含有一切当信的，那些理论仍不是使你们成为基督徒的东西——若你们真是基督徒的话。相反，在你们不少人身上，它们恰是拦阻你们成为基督徒的东西。因为当你们说：要得救，人必须持守这持守那——那时你们就是撇下永活的神与他的旨意，把信靠放在关于他或他旨意的某个观念上。说得更明白些——你们有人说我们必须信靠基督已完成的工作；或者说我们的信心必须放在基督的功劳里——在他所作成的赎罪（atonement）里——在他流的血里：这一切说法都是对永活主的简单弃绝，我们受命要信的乃是*在他里面*——他借着他与我们同在、在我们里面的临在、并我们对他的顺服，把我们从黑暗中举起进入光、领我们出撒但的国、进入神儿女荣耀的自由。任何*关于他*的信法，无论方式或数量，都不是新约的信心（faith）。这样的教导我终生熟识，并宣告它虚假得可悲。但我现在无意与它争辩；除非基督耶稣面上神荣耀之光的知识叫一个人厌烦他的意见，他尽可以为我持守它们到末日；因为没有任何意见，我重复，是基督教；传讲任何救恩计划，都不是传讲永活神荣耀的福音。

===Original===

Even if your plan, your theories, were absolutely true, the holding of them with sincerity, the trusting in this or that about Christ, or in anything he did or could do, the trusting in anything but himself, his own living self, is a delusion. Many will grant this heartily, and yet the moment you come to talk with them, you find they insist that to believe in Christ is to believe in the atonement, meaning by that only and altogether their special theory about the atonement; and when you say we must believe in the atoning Christ, and cannot possibly believe in any theory concerning the atonement, they go away and denounce you, saying, “He does not believe in the atonement!” If I explain the atonement otherwise than they explain it, they assert that I deny the atonement; nor count it of any consequence that I say I believe in the atoner with my whole heart, and soul, and strength, and mind. This they call “contending for the truth!” Because I refuse an explanation which is not in the New Testament, though they believe it is, because they can think of no other, one which seems to me as false in logic as detestable in morals, not to say that there is no spirituality in it whatever, therefore I am not a Christian! What wonder men such as I have quoted refuse the Christianity they suppose such “believers” to represent! I do not say that with this sad folly may not mingle a potent faith in the Lord himself; but I do say that the importance they place on theory is even more sadly obstructive to true faith than such theories themselves: while the mind is occupied in enquiring,
“Do I believe or feel this thing right?”﻿—the true question is forgotten: “Have I left all to follow him?” To the man who gives himself to the living Lord, every belief will necessarily come right; the Lord himself will see that his disciple believe aright concerning him. If a man cannot trust him for this, what claim can he make to faith in him? It is because he has little or no faith, that he is left clinging to preposterous and dishonouring ideas, the traditions of men concerning his Father, and neither his teaching nor that of his apostles. The living Christ is to them but a shadow; the all but obliterated Christ of their theories no soul can thoroughly believe in: the disciple of such a Christ rests on his work, or his merits, or his atonement!

===Chinese===

即使你们的计划、你们的理论绝对为真，以诚心持守它们、信靠关于基督的这样那样、或他所行、或他能行的任何事——信靠他自己、他那活着的自己以外的任何事——仍是迷妄。许多人会衷心容许这一点；可你一同他们交谈，就发现他们坚持：信基督就是信赎罪，所指的又单单彻底是他们关于赎罪的那套特殊理论；而你说我们必须信那位赎罪的基督、不可能信任何关于赎罪的理论时，他们就离开、宣布说：“他不信赎罪！”我若照不同于他们的方式解释赎罪，他们就断言我否认赎罪；我说我尽心尽性尽力尽意信靠那位赎罪者，他们也不以为意。他们称之为“为真理争辩”！因为我拒绝一个新约里没有的解释——他们以为有，因为他们想不出别的——一个在我看来逻辑上虚假、道德上可憎、更不必说其中毫无属灵之物的解释，我就不是基督徒了！难怪我所引的那些人，拒绝他们以为这类“信徒”所代表的基督教！我不是说这种可悲的愚妄里不能掺着对主自己有力的信心；但我确说：他们放在理论上的重要性，比那些理论本身还更可悲地阻碍真信心：当心思忙于追问“我信不信这事？我觉得它对不对？”——真问题被忘了：“我可曾撇下一切跟从他？”对那把自己交给永活主的人，一切信仰必自然归正；主自己必看顾他的门徒对他信得正当。人若不能把这事信托他，还能对他有什么信心的主张？正因为他信心很少或没有，他才被撇下去紧抓那些荒谬辱人的观念——关于他父的人的传统，而不是他的教导、也不是他使徒的。永活的基督对他们只是影子；他们理论里那几乎被抹掉的基督，没有灵魂能彻底信：这样一位基督的门徒，靠的是他的工作、或他的功劳、或他的赎罪！

===Original===

What I insist upon is, that a man’s faith shall be in the living, loving, ruling, helping Christ, devoted to us as much as ever he was, and with all the powers of the Godhead for the salvation of his brethren. It is not faith that he did this, that his work wrought that﻿—it is faith in the man who did and is doing everything for us that will save him: without this he cannot work to heal spiritually, any more than he would heal physically, when he was present to the eyes of men. Do you ask, “What is faith in him?” I answer, The leaving of your way, your objects, yourself, and the taking of his and him; the leaving of your trust in men, in money, in opinion, in character, in atonement itself, *and doing as he tells you*. I can find no words strong enough to serve for the weight of this necessity﻿—this obedience. It is the one terrible heresy of the church, that it has always been presenting something else than obedience as faith in Christ. The work of Christ is not the Working Christ, any more than the clothing of Christ is the body of Christ. If the woman who touched the hem of his garment had trusted in the garment and not in him who wore it, would she have been healed? And the reason that so many who believe *about* Christ rather than in him, get the comfort they do, is that, touching thus the mere hem of his garment, they cannot help believing a little in the live man inside the garment. It is not wonderful that such believers should so often be miserable; they lay themselves down to sleep with nothing but the skirt of his robe in their hand﻿—a robe too, I say, that never was his, only by them is supposed his﻿—when they might sleep in peace with the living Lord in their hearts. Instead of so knowing Christ that they have him in them saving them, they lie wasting themselves in soul-sickening self-examination as to whether they are believers, whether they are really trusting in the atonement, whether they are truly sorry for their sins﻿—the way to madness of the brain, and despair of the heart.

===Chinese===

我所坚持的是：人的信心要在那位活的、爱的、治理的、帮助的基督里——他从前怎样倾心于我们、如今仍怎样，且带着神格全部的大能、为救他的弟兄。不是信他作了这个、他的工成了那个——是信那位已为我们作成、且正在作成一切的那人，才能救他：没有这个，他不能医治人的灵，正如他当年在人的眼前时、不凭信心不能医治人的身体。你问：“怎样算是信他？”我回答：撇下你的道路、你的目标、你自己，取他的道路、取他自己；撇下你对人、对金钱、对舆论、对名望、乃至对赎罪本身的信靠，*并照他所告诉你的去行*。我找不到够重的字眼来承载这必需的分量——这顺服（obedience）。教会那一个可怕的大异端，就是它一直把顺服以外的某种东西当作对基督的信心呈献。基督的工作不是那位作工的基督，正如基督的衣裳不是基督的身体。那摸他衣裳繸子的妇人，若信靠的是衣裳、而非穿它的那位，她会得医治吗？而那么多*关于*基督而信、而非信基督的人之所以得着他们所得的安慰，是因为：摸着的既是衣裳的边，就不能不多少信一点衣裳里面那活的人。这样的信徒常常痛苦，不足为奇；他们躺下睡觉，手里只有他袍子的衣角——那袍子，我说，从来不是他的、只是他们以为是——而他们本可以心里有永活的主、安然入睡。他们不这样认识基督、把他接在得救的位置上，反而躺着把自己耗损在令人心病的自我省察里：我是信徒吗？我真信靠赎罪吗？我真为罪难过吗？——那是通往脑的疯狂与心的绝望之路。

===Original===

Some even ponder the imponderable﻿—whether they are of the elect, whether they have an interest in the blood shed for sin, whether theirs is a saving faith﻿—when all the time the man who died for them is waiting to begin to save them from every evil﻿—and first from this self which is consuming them with trouble about its salvation; he will set them free, and take them home to the bosom of the Father﻿—if only they will mind what he says to them﻿—which is the beginning, middle, and end of faith. If, instead of searching into the mysteries of corruption in their own charnel-houses, they would but awake and arise from the dead, and come out into the light which Christ is waiting to give them, he would begin at once to fill them with the fullness of God.
“But I do not know how to awake and arise!”
I will tell you:﻿—Get up, and do something the master tells you; so make yourself his disciple at once. Instead of asking yourself whether you believe or not, ask yourself whether you have this day done one thing because he said, Do it, or once abstained because he said, Do not do it. It is simply absurd to say you believe, or even want to believe in him, if you do not anything he tells you. If you can think of nothing he ever said as having had an atom of influence on your doing or not doing, you have too good ground to consider yourself no disciple of his. Do not, I pray you, worse than waste your time in trying to convince yourself that you are his disciple notwithstanding﻿—that for this reason or that you still have cause to think you believe in him. What though you should succeed in persuading yourself to absolute certainty that you are his disciple, if, after all, he say to you, “Why did you not do the things I told you? Depart from me; I do not know you!” Instead of trying to persuade yourself, if the thing be true you can make it truer; if it be not true, you can begin at once to make it true, to *be* a disciple of the Living One﻿—by obeying him in the first thing you can think of in which you are not obeying him. We must learn to obey him in everything, and so must begin somewhere: let it be at once, and in the very next thing that lies at the door of our conscience! Oh fools and slow of heart, if you think of nothing but Christ, and do not set yourselves to do his words! you but build your houses on the sand.

===Chinese===

有人甚至推敲那不可推敲的——自己是否选民、在所流的血里有没有份、自己的信心是否得救的信心——而为他们死的那位，一直等着手要开始救他们脱离一切的恶——先脱离这为自身得救焦灼、正烧毁他们的自我；他要释放他们、带他们回父的怀里——只要他们肯听他对他们说的话——那是信心（faith）的始、中、终。他们若不是在掘自己藏骨堂里败坏的奥秘，而是醒来、从死里起来、出到基督等着要给他们的光里，他就要立刻开始用神的丰满充满他们。
“可我不知道怎样醒、怎样起来！”
我告诉你：——起来，去作夫子告诉你的一件事；这样就立刻使自己成为他的门徒。不要问自己信不信，要问自己今天可曾因为他一句话作过一件事、或因为他一句话戒过一次。你若不作他告诉你的任何事，还说自己信他、甚至说想信他，简直荒谬。你若想不起他曾说过的一句话对你的行与止有过一原子的影响，你就有充分的根据算自己不是他的门徒。我求你，不要比浪费时间更坏地去努力说服自己说你仍是他的门徒——说为这为那你仍有理由以为你信他。就算你说服自己到了绝对确定自己是他的门徒，末了他若对你说：“你为什么不行我告诉你的事？离开我，我不认识你！”——那又如何？与其努力说服自己，不如这样：这事若是真的，你能使它更真；若不是真的，你能立刻开始使它成真——*作*那位存活者的门徒——借着在你想到的头一件你不曾顺服他的事上顺服他。我们必须学着在凡事上顺服他，所以总得从某处开始：就现在、就在我们良心门口的那下一件事上开始吧！哦愚昧而心迟钝的人哪，若你们只想基督、却不着手行他的话！你们不过是把房子盖在沙土上。

===Original===

What have such teachers not to answer for who have turned your regard away from the direct words of the Lord himself, which are spirit and life, to contemplate plans of salvation tortured out of the words of his apostles, even were those plans as true as they are false! There is but one plan of salvation, and that is to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ; that is, to take him for what he is﻿—our master, and his words as if he meant them, which assuredly he did. To do his words is to enter into vital relation with him, to obey him is the only way to be one with him. The relation between him and us is an absolute one; it can nohow begin to *live* but in obedience: it is obedience. There can be no truth, no reality, in any initiation of atonement with him, that is not obedience. What! have I the poorest notion of a God, and dare think of entering into relations with him, the very first of which is not that what he saith, I will do? The thing is eternally absurd, and comes of the father of lies. I know what he whispers to those to whom such teaching as this is distasteful: “It is the doctrine of works!” But one word of the Lord humbly heard and received will suffice to send all the demons of false theology into the abyss. He says the man that does not do the things he tells him, builds his house to fall in utter ruin. He instructs his messengers to go and baptize all nations, “teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.” Tell me it is faith he requires: do I not know it? and is not faith the highest act of which the human mind is capable? But faith in what? Faith in what he is, in what he says﻿—a faith which can have no existence except in obedience﻿—a faith which is obedience. To do what he wishes is to put forth faith in him. For this the teaching of men has substituted this or that belief *about* him, faith in this or that supposed design of his manifestation in the flesh. It was himself, and God in him that he manifested; but faith in him and his father thus manifested, they make altogether secondary to acceptance of the paltry contrivance of a juggling morality, which they attribute to God and his Christ, imagining it the atonement, and “the plan of salvation.” “Do you put faith in *him*,” I ask, “or in the doctrines and commandments of men?”

===Chinese===

那些使你们的注视离开主自己的直接话语——那本是灵、本是生命——转去注视从他使徒话语中拷问出的救恩计划的教师，要为这担多大的责任——哪怕那些计划真得如它们假！救恩的计划只有一个，就是信靠主耶稣基督；就是照他所是的接待他——我们的主人——并照他话语的本意对待他的话，而他的本意确实如此。行他的话，就是进入与他的生命关系；顺服他，是与他为一的唯一途径。他与我们之间的关系是绝对的关系；它唯在顺服中才开始*活*：它就是顺服。任何与他联合的起始，若非顺服，就没有真理、没有实际。什么！我怀有最贫乏的神观，竟敢想进入与他的关系，而那关系的头一条不是“他所说的、我就去行”？这事永恒地荒谬，出于那说谎之父。我知道他向那些不喜欢这教导的人耳语什么：“这是行为之功的教义！”但主的一句话被谦卑地听见领受，就足以把一切虚假神学的鬼赶入深渊。他说不行他所告诉之事的人，是把房子盖到全然倒塌。他吩咐他的使者去使万民作门徒，“教训他们遵守我所吩咐你们的一切。”你对我说：他要求的是信心。我岂不知道！信心（faith）岂非人心所能有的最高行动？但信什么？信他所是的、信他所说的——一种唯在顺服中才能存在的信心——一种就是顺服的信心。行他所愿的，就是向他发出信心。人的教导把这换成了关于他的这样那样信念、对他道成肉身这一或那一设想设计的信心。他所彰显的本是他自己、与在他里面的神；但他们把对他与他父的信心弄成完全次要的、置于对一套骗人道德之拙劣设计——他们把它归于神与他的基督、称之为赎罪（atonement）与“救恩计划”——的接受之下。“你是把信心放在*他*身上，”我问，“还是放在人的教义与诫命上？”

===Original===

If you say “In him,”﻿—“Is it then possible,” I return, “that you do not see that, above all things and all thoughts, you are bound to obey him?” Do you not mourn that you cannot trust in him as you would, that you find it too hard? Too hard it is for you, and too hard it will remain, while the things he tells you to do﻿—the things you can do﻿—even those you will not try! How should you be capable of trusting in the true one while you are nowise true to him? How are you to believe he will do his part by you, while you are not such as to do your part by him? How are you to believe while you are not faithful? How, I say, should you be capable of trusting in him? The very thing to make you able to trust in him, and so receive all things from him, you turn your back upon: obedience you decline, or at least neglect. You say you do not refuse to obey him? I care not whether you refuse or not, while you do not obey. Remember the parable: “I go, sir, and went not.” What have you done this day because it was the will of Christ? Have you dismissed, once dismissed, an anxious thought for the morrow? Have you ministered to any needy soul or body, and kept your right hand from knowing what your left hand did? Have you begun to leave all and follow him? Did you set yourself to judge righteous judgment? Are you being ware of covetousness? Have you forgiven your enemy? Are you seeking the kingdom of God and his righteousness before all other things? Are you hungering and thirsting after righteousness? Have you given to someone that asked of you? Tell me something that you have done, are doing, or are trying to do because he told you. If you do nothing that he says, it is no wonder that you cannot trust in him, and are therefore driven to seek refuge in the atonement, as if something he had done, and not he himself in his doing were the atonement. *That is not as you understand it?* What does it matter how you understand, or what you understand, so long as you are not of one mind with the Truth, so long as you and God are not “at one,” do not atone together? How should you understand? Knowing that you do not heed his word, why should I heed your explanation of it? You do not his will, and so you cannot understand him; you do not know him, that is why you cannot trust in him. You think your common sense enough to let you know what he means?

===Chinese===

你若说“在他身上”——“那么，”我回问，“你岂不见，在一切事物、一切思想之上，你有本分顺服他吗？”你不哀恸自己不能如愿地信靠他、觉得太难吗？对你确实难、也必一直难，只要他叫你作的事——你作得到的事——连那些你也不肯试！你对他毫无真实，怎能信靠那位真实者？你自己不作你对他该作的那份，怎能信他会作他对你的一份？你不忠信，怎能信？我说，你怎能信靠他？那使你能信靠他、从而从他领受万事的唯一之物，你却背向它：顺服，你拒绝、或至少疏忽。你说你不拒绝顺服他？你不顺服，你拒不拒绝，我不在乎。记住那比喻：“先生，我去。却不去。”今天你因为这是基督的旨意，作过什么？你可曾把一次卸下、就不再收回的对明天的焦虑卸下？可曾供应过哪个需用的灵魂或身体、且左手所作的不叫右手知道？可曾开始撇下一切跟从他？可曾立志行公义的审判（the judgment）？可曾在警醒贪心？可曾饶恕你的仇敌？可曾在一切之先寻求神的国和他的义？可曾饥渴慕义？可曾给过那向你求的人？告诉我一件你因他吩咐而作过、正作着、或正努力去作的事。你若不行他所说的任何事，难怪你不能信靠他，于是被逼到赎罪里避难——仿佛他所作成的某事、而非正在作工的他自己、是那赎罪。*那不是你所理解的吗？*只要你还不同心于真理、只要你和神还不“归一”、还没有同赎一，你怎样理解、理解什么，有什么要紧？你怎能明白？知道你不理他的话，我为什么理你对它的解释？你不行他的旨意，所以你不能明白他；你不认识他，这就是你不能信靠他的原因。你以为你的常识足以让你知道他的意思？

===Original===

Your common sense ought to be enough to know itself unequal to the task. It is the heart of the child that alone can understand the Father. Would you have me think you guilty of the sin against the Holy Ghost﻿—that you *understand* Jesus Christ and yet will not obey him? That were too dreadful. I believe you do not understand him. No man can do yet what he tells him aright﻿—but are you trying? Obedience is not perfection, but trying. You count him a hard master, and will not stir. Do you suppose he ever gave a commandment knowing it was of no use for it could not be done? He tells us a thing knowing that we must do it, or be lost; that not his Father himself could save us but by getting us at length to do everything he commands, for not otherwise can we know life, can we learn the holy secret of divine being. He knows that you can try, and that in your trying and failing he will be able to help you, until at length you shall do the will of God even as he does it himself. He takes the will in the imperfect deed, and makes the deed at last perfect. Correctest notions without obedience are worthless. The doing of the will of God is the way to oneness with God, which alone is salvation. Sitting at the gate of heaven, sitting on the footstool of the throne itself, yea, clasping the knees of the Father, you could not be at peace, except in their every vital movement, in every their smallest point of consciousness, your heart, your soul, your mind, your brain, your body, were one with the living God. If you had one brooding thought that was not a joy in him, you would not be at peace; if you had one desire you could not leave absolutely to his will you would not be at peace; you would not be saved, therefore could not feel saved. God, all and in all, ours to the fulfilling of our very being, is the religion of the perfect, son-hearted Lord Christ.
Well do I know it is faith that saves us﻿—but not faith in any work of God﻿—it is faith in God himself.

===Chinese===

你的常识本该足以知道自己不堪此任。唯有孩子的心能明白父。你岂要我以为你犯了干犯圣灵的罪——说你*明白*耶稣基督却不肯顺服他？那太可怕了。我相信你不明白他。人还不能全然照他所告诉的作——但你在试吗？顺服不是完全，而是努力。你算他作忍心的主人，就不肯动。你想他曾给出一条明知无用、因为作不到的诫命吗？他告诉我们一件事，知道我们必须行它、否则就失丧；知道连他的父也不能救我们、除非最终使我们行他一切所吩咐的，因为不这样我们就不能认识生命、不能学会属神存有的圣洁秘密。他知道你能试，且在你的试与败中他能帮助你，直到末了你行神的旨意、正如他自己行它。他悦纳不完全之工里的意愿，至终使那工完全。没有顺服的最正确观念也毫无价值。行神的旨意是与神为一的路，那是唯一的救恩。坐在天门边、坐在宝座的脚凳上、是的、抱着父的膝，你也不能安息——除非你的心、你的魂、你的意、你的脑、你的身体，在它们每一个关键的运行、每一个最小的意识点上，都与永活的神为一。你若有一个不是以他为乐的郁思，你就不安息；你若有一个不能绝对交给他旨意的愿望，你就不安息；你就没有得救，因此也觉不出得救。神——在万有中、作万有的万有、我们的、直到我们存有本身的成全——这是那位完全的、以子为心的主基督的宗教。
我深知道救我们的是信心——但不是对神任何工作的信心——是对神自己的信心。

===Original===

If I did not believe God as good as the tenderest human heart, the fairest, the purest, the most unselfish human heart could imagine him, yea, an infinitude better, higher than we as the heavens are higher than the earth﻿—believe it, not as a proposition, or even as a thing I was convinced of, but with the responsive condition and being of my whole nature; if I did not feel every fibre of heart and brain and body safe with him because he is the Father who made me that I am﻿—I would not be saved, for this faith is salvation; it is God and the man one. God and man together, the vital energy flowing unchecked from the creator into his creature﻿—that is the salvation of the creature. But the poorest faith in the living God, the God revealed in Christ Jesus, if it be vital, true, that is obedient, is the beginning of the way to know him, and to know him is eternal life. If you mean by faith anything of a different kind, that faith will not save you. A faith, for instance, that God does not forgive me because he loves me, but because he loves Jesus Christ, cannot save me, because it is a falsehood against God: if the thing were true, such a gospel would be the preaching of a God that was not love, therefore in whom was no salvation, a God to know whom could not be eternal life. Such a faith would damn, not save a man; for it would bind him to a God who was anything but perfect. Such assertions going by the name of Christianity, are nothing but the poor remnants of paganism; and it is only with that part of our nature not yet Christian that we are able to believe them﻿—so far indeed as it is possible a lie should be believed. We must forsake all our fears and distrusts for Christ. We must receive his teaching heartily, nor let the interpretation of it attributed to his apostles make us turn aside from it. I say interpretation attributed to them; for what they teach is never against what Christ taught, though very often the exposition of it is﻿—and that from no fault in the apostles, but from the grievous fault of those who would understand, and even explain, rather than obey.

===Chinese===

我若不信神好到如最温柔的人心、最纯洁、最无私的人心所能想象的——是的、好到无限，高过我们如天之高过地——并且不是作为命题、甚至不是作为我被说服的事、而是以我全人回应的状态与存有去信；我若不觉得我心的每一纤维、脑、身体在他里面都稳妥、因为他是造我如今所是的父——我就不得救，因为这信心就是救恩；它是神与人的一。神与人同在，创造者的生命之能不受拦阻地流入他的受造者——那是受造者的救恩。但对永活的神——在基督耶稣里启示的神——最贫弱的信心，只要是活的、真的、就是说顺服的，就是认识他的路的开端，而认识他就是永生。你若把信心理解为别的种类，那信心救不了你。譬如一种信心，说神赦免我不是因为他爱我，而是因为他爱耶稣基督——它救不了我，因为它是针对神的虚谎：那事若为真，那样的福音传的就是一位不是爱的神、因此在他里面没有救恩、认识他不能是永生的神。那样的信心定人的罪、不救人；因为它把他绑在一位绝非完全的神身上。这类冒基督教之名的断言，不过是异教的可怜残余；我们只能以本性中尚未基督化的那部分信它们——就谎言竟能被信而言。我们必须为基督撇下一切的惧怕与不信托。我们必须衷心领受他的教导，也不可让归于他使徒的解释使我们转离它。我说归于他们的解释；因为他们所教导的从不与基督所教的相违，虽然对它的讲解常常相违——那不是使徒的错，是那些要明白、甚至要讲解、却不肯顺服之人的重错。

===Original===

We may be sure of this, that no man will be condemned for any sin that is past; that, if he be condemned, it will be because he would not come to the light when the light came to him; because he would not cease to do evil and learn to do well; because he hid his unbelief in the garment of a false faith, and would not obey; because he imputed to himself a righteousness that was not his; because he preferred imagining himself a worthy person, to confessing himself everywhere in the wrong, and repenting. We may be sure also of this, that, if a man becomes the disciple of Christ, he will not leave him in ignorance as to what he has to believe; he shall know the truth of everything it is needful for him to understand. If we do what he tells us, his light will go up in our hearts. Till then we could not understand even if he explained to us. If you cannot trust him to let you know what is right, but think you must hold this or that before you can come to him, then I justify your doubts in what you call your worst times, but which I suspect are your best times in which you come nearest to the truth﻿—those, namely, in which you fear you have no faith.
So long as a man will not set himself to obey the word spoken, the word written, the word printed, the word read, of the Lord Christ, I would not take the trouble to convince him concerning the most obnoxious doctrines that they were false as hell. It is those who would fain believe, but who by such doctrines are hindered, whom I would help. Disputation about things but hides the living Christ who alone can teach the truth, who is the truth, and the knowledge of whom is life; I write for the sake of those whom the false teaching that claims before all to be true has driven away from God﻿—as well it might, for the God so taught is not a God worthy to be believed in. A stick, or a stone, or a devil, is all that some of our brethren of mankind have to believe in: he who believes in a God not altogether unselfish and good, a God who does not do all he can for his creatures, belongs to the same class; his is not the God who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and the fountains of water﻿—not the God revealed in Christ.

===Chinese===

我们可以确信这一点：没有人会为任何已过的罪被定罪；人若被定罪，必是因为光临到他时他不肯就光；因为他不肯止住作恶、学习行善；因为他把不信藏在一件假信心的衣裳里、不肯顺服；因为他把不是自己的义归给自己；因为他宁想象自己是配得的人、而不肯处处认己为错并悔改。我们也可以确信：人若作了基督的门徒，基督不会撇下他、任他对当信的一无所知；凡他有必要明白的，他必知其真理。我们行他所告诉的，他的光必在我们心里升起。在那之前，即使他向我们解释，我们也不能明白。你若不能信托他叫你知道什么是正的、反倒以为必须先持这持那才能到他那里，那么我认你在你所谓最坏的时刻——我猜想其实是你们最接近真理的最好时刻——的那些怀疑为正当：就是你怕自己没有信心的那些时刻。
一个人既不肯着手顺服主基督所说的话、所写的话、所印的话、所读的话，哪怕最可憎的教义假如地狱（hell），我也不愿费力气说服他它们是假的。我要帮助的，是那些切愿相信、却被这些教义拦阻的人。对事物的争辩只是遮蔽了那位独一能教真理的永活基督——他就是真理，认识他就是生命；我写作，是为那些被那自称在一切之上为真的假教导驱离神的人——这也难怪，因为那样教出来的神，不是一位配得相信的神。一根杖、一块石头、或一个鬼魔，就是我们人类某些弟兄所有的可信之物：凡信一位非全然无私良善、非为其受造者作他所能作一切之神的，就属同一类；他的神不是那造天地海和众水泉源的神——不是在基督里启示的神。

===Original===

If a man see in God any darkness at all, and especially if he defend that darkness, attempting to justify it as one who respects the person of God, I cannot but think his blindness must have followed his mockery of “Lord! Lord!” Surely, if he had been strenuously obeying Jesus, he would ere now have received the truth that God is light, and in him is no darkness﻿—a truth which is not acknowledged by calling the darkness attributed to him light, and the candle of the Lord in the soul of man darkness. It is one thing to believe that God can do nothing wrong, quite another to call whatever presumption may attribute to him right.
The whole secret of progress is the doing of the thing we know. There is no other way of progress in the spiritual life; no other way of progress in the understanding of that life: only as we do, can we know.
Is there then anything you will not leave for Christ? You cannot know him﻿—and yet he is the Truth, the one thing alone that can be known! Do you not care to be imperfect? would you rather keep this or that, with imperfection, than part with it to be perfect? You cannot know Christ, for the very principle of his life was the simple absolute relation of realities; his one idea was to be a perfect child to his Father. He who will not part with all for Christ, is not worthy of him, and cannot know him; and the Lord is true, and cannot acknowledge him: how could he receive to his house, as one of his kind, a man who prefers something to his Father; a man who is not for God; a man who will strike a bargain with God, and say, “I will give up so much, if thou wilt spare me”! To yield all to him who has only made us and given us everything, yea his very self by life and by death, such a man counts too much. His conduct says, “I never asked thee to do so much for me, and I cannot make the return thou demandest.” The man will have to be left to himself. He must find what it is to be without God! Those who know God, or have but begun to catch a far-off glimmer of his gloriousness, of what he is, regard life as insupportable save God be the All in all, the first and the last.
To let their light shine, not to force on them their interpretations of God’s designs, is the duty of Christians towards their fellows.

===Chinese===

人若在神里看见任何一点黑暗，尤其若他为那黑暗辩护、像一个看神情面者那样想称它为义，我不能不想他的瞎瞎在他对“主啊、主啊”的戏弄之后。的确，他若一直在奋力顺服耶稣，如今必已领受那真理：神就是光、在他里面毫无黑暗——这真理不是靠把他名下的黑暗称为光、把主在人灵里的烛称为黑暗来承认的。相信神不能行错是一回事；把僭妄可能归于他的一切称为义，是另一回事。
长进的全部秘诀，是行我们所知道的事。属灵生命没有别的长进之路；对那生命的理解也没有别的长进之路：唯有行，才能知。
那么，有什么你不肯为基督撇下吗？你就不能认识他——而他本是真理、独一能被认识之物！你不介意不完全吗？你宁带着不完全保留这个那个，也不肯为完全而舍弃它吗？你不能认识基督，因为他生命的原理正是诸实际之间单纯绝对的关系；他唯一的念头，是对他父作一个完全的孩子。不肯为基督撇下一切的人，不配他，也不能认识他；而主是真实的，不能承认他：他怎能接进他的家、作他同类的一位，一个在某事上过于爱父的人；一个不向着神的人；一个要同神讲价、说“你若肯放过我，我就舍这么多”的人！对那位只是造了他、又给了他万物、是的、以生死给了他自己非常之身的那位全然降服——这样的人嫌太多。他的行为说：“我从未求你为我作这么多，我也还不出你所要求的。”这人必被撇给他自己。他必发现没有神是什么滋味！凡认识神的、或刚开始捕捉到他的荣耀——他的所是——之远光的，都看生命为不可承受，除非神是在一切之中作一切、是首先的、末后的。
让他们的光照耀，而不是把他们自己对神设计的解释强加于人，是基督徒对同伴的本分。

===Original===

If you who set yourselves to explain the theory of Christianity, had set yourselves instead to do the will of the Master, the one object for which the Gospel was preached to you, how different would now be the condition of that portion of the world with which you come into contact! Had you given yourselves to the understanding of his word that you might do it, and not to the quarrying from it of material wherewith to buttress your systems, in many a heart by this time would the name of the Lord be loved where now it remains unknown. The word of life would then by you have been held out indeed. Men, undeterred by your explanations of Christianity, for you would not be forcing them on their acceptance, and attracted by your behaviour, would be saying to each other, as Moses said to himself when he saw the bush that burned with fire and was not consumed, “I will now turn aside and see this great sight!” they would be drawing nigh to behold how these Christians loved one another, and how just and fair they were to everyone that had to do with them! to note that their goods were the best, their weight surest, their prices most *reasonable*, their word most certain! that in their families was neither jealousy nor emulation! that mammon was not there worshipped! that in their homes selfishness was neither the hidden nor the openly ruling principle; that their children were as diligently taught to share, as some are to save, or to lay out only upon self﻿—their mothers more anxious lest a child should hoard than lest he should squander; that in no house of theirs was religion one thing, and the daily life another; that the ecclesiastic did not think first of his church, nor the peer of his privileges.
What do I hear you say?﻿—“*How then shall the world go on?*” The Lord’s world will go on, and that without you; the devil’s world will go on, and that with you. The objection is but another and overwhelming proof of your unbelief. Either you do not believe the word the Lord spake﻿—that, if we seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, all things needful will be added to us; or what he undertakes does not satisfy you; it is not enough; you want more; you prefer the offers of Mammon. You are nowise anxious to be saved from the too-much that is a snare; you want what you call a fortune﻿—the freedom of the world.

===Chinese===

你们这些立志解释基督教理论的人，若当年立志去行夫子的旨意——福音传给你们正为此唯一目的——今日与你们相接触的那部分世界，光景将何等不同！你们若当年为行他的话而求明白它，而不是为支撑你们体系而从其中采石，到如今多少颗心里必已爱主的名，而那里如今还是空白。生命的道那时才真被你们递出。人不被你们对基督教的解释吓退——因为你们不会强要他们接受——又被你们的行为吸引，必彼此说，如摩西（Moses）见火烧荆棘而不毁时对自己说的：“我要过去看这大异象！”他们要近前来，看这些基督徒怎样彼此相爱、怎样公平待一切与她们有往来的人！要留意：他们的货最好、他们的秤最准、他们的价钱最公道、他们的话最可信！他们的家中没有嫉妒争竞！玛门不在那里受拜！他们家里，自私既不是暗中的、也不是公开的统治原则；他们的孩子受教导殷勤与人分享，像有些人家教储蓄、或只为自己花用——作母亲的更怕孩子囤积、过于怕孩子挥霍；他们没有一家是宗教一件事、日常生活另一件事；教士不先想他的教会，贵人不先想他的特权。
我听见你说什么？——“*那世界还怎么运转？*”主的世界会运转，用不着你；鬼魔的世界也会运转，用得着你。这反对只是你们不信的又一个压倒证明。你们要么不信主所说的话——先求神的国和他的义，一切所需都必加给你们；要么他的承担不能满足你；不够；你要更多；你宁要玛门的出价。你们毫不急于从那网罗式的“过多”中被救出；你们要你们所谓的财富——世界的自由。

===Original===

You would not live under such restrictions as the Lord might choose to lay upon you if he saw that something might be made of you precious in his sight! You would inherit the earth, and not by meekness; you would have the life of this world sweet, come of the life eternal, the life that God shares with you, what may: so much as that comes to, you would gladly leave God to look after, if only you might be sure of not sharing with the rich man when you die. But you find that, unable to trust him for this world, neither can you trust him for the world to come. Refusing to obey him in your life, how can you trust him for your life? Hence the various substitutes you seek for faith in him: you would hold him to his word, bind him by his promises, appeal to the atonement, to the satisfaction made to his justice, as you call it﻿—while you will take no trouble to fulfil the absolutely reasonable and necessary condition, yea, morally and spiritually imperative condition﻿—condition and means in one﻿—on which he offers, and through which alone he can offer you deliverance from the burden of life into the strength and glory of life﻿—that you shall be true, and to him obedient children. You say “Christ has satisfied the law,” but you will not satisfy him! He says, “Come unto me,” and you will not rise and go to him. You say, “Lord I believe; help mine unbelief,” but when he says, “Leave everything behind you, and be as I am towards God, and you shall have peace and rest,” you turn away, muttering about *figurative language*. If you had been true, had been living *the* life, had been Christians indeed, you would, however little, have drawn the world after you. In your churches you would be receiving truest nourishment, yea strength to live﻿—thinking far less of serving God on the Sunday, and far more of serving your neighbour in the week.

===Chinese===

主若见你能被造成他眼中宝贵之物、而加给你限制，你也不肯活在这样的限制下！你们要承受大地，却不要凭温柔；你们要这世界的生命甘甜——至于永生、神与你分享的生命，随它怎样：能得多少算多少，你们甘愿留给神照管，只要你们能确知死时不与那财主同分。但你们发现：既不能为这世界信托他，也不能为来世信托他。在生命里拒绝顺服他，又怎能为他生命信托他？于是你们寻求种种信心的代替品：你们要他守住他的话、被他的应许约束、诉诸赎罪、诉诸对他公义——如你们所说——的满足，而你们却不肯费一点力气履行那绝对合理而必需的条件、那道德与属灵上势在必行的条件——条件与途径合一——他借此、也唯独借此，能把你们从生命的重担救入生命的力量与荣耀——那就是你们当作真实的、向他顺服的孩子。你们说“基督满足了律法”，你们却不满足他！他说“到我这里来”，你们却不起来去到他那里。你们说“主啊我信，扶持我的不信”，而当他说“撇下你背后的一切、照我那样向神而活，你就必得平安安息”，你们却转开去，嘟囔着*比喻性的语言*。你们若当年真实、活的真是*那*生命、真是基督徒，哪怕再少，也必已把世界拖在你们后面。你们的教会里，你们本可领受最真实的滋养、是的、活的力量——少想主日在事奉神，多想在礼拜中间事奉你们的邻舍。

===Original===
