The sociable vile, the masterful rich, the deceitful trader, the ambitious poor, whom you have attracted to your communities with the offer of a salvation other than deliverance from sin, would not be lording it over them and dragging them down; they would be the cleaner and the stronger for their absence; while the publicans and the sinners would have been drawn instead, and turned into true men and women; and the Israelite indeed, who is yet more repelled by your general worldliness than by your misrepresentations of God, showing him selfish like yourselves who is the purity of the creation﻿—the Israelite in whom is no guile would have hastened to the company of the loving men and true, eager to learn what it was that made them so good, so happy, so unselfish, so free of care, so ready to die, so willing to live, so hopeful, so helpful, so careless to possess, so undeferential to possession. Finding you to hold, from the traditional force of false teaching, such things as you do, he would have said, “No! such beliefs can never account for such mighty results!” You would have answered, “Search the Scriptures and see.” He would have searched, and found﻿—not indeed the things you imagine there, but things infinitely better and higher, things that indeed account for the result he wondered at; he would have found such truth as he who has found will hold forever as the only gladness of his being. There you would have had your reward for being true Christians in spite of the evil doctrines you had been taught and teaching: you would have been taught in return the truth of the matter by him whom your true Christianity had enticed to itself, and sent to the fountainhead free of the prejudices that disabled your judgment. Thus delivered from the false notions which could not fail to have stunted your growth hitherto, how rapid would it not have become!
If any of you tell me my doctrine is presumptuous, that it is contrary to what is taught in the New Testament, and what the best of men have always believed, I will not therefore proceed to defend even my beliefs, the principles on which I try to live﻿—how much less my opinions! I appeal to you instead, whether or not I have spoken the truth concerning our paramount obligation to do the word of Christ. If you answer that I have not, I have nothing more to say; there is no other ground on which we can meet.

===Chinese===

那些好交际的卑污者、专横的富人、欺诈的商人、野心勃勃的穷人——你们用一个非脱离罪恶的救恩之许诺、把他们吸引进你们的群体——本不会辖制他们、拖垮他们；他们会因这些人的缺席而更洁净更强壮；而被吸引来的本该是税吏和罪人，被改变成真的男人女人；而那真以色列人——他被你们普遍的世俗、多于被你们对神的歪曲——你们把他说成像你们自己一样自私、而他本是受造之洁——排斥——那心中没有诡诈的真以色列人，本会急急到这群有爱与真实之人的中间，热切要知道是什么使他们这样良善、这样快乐、这样无私、这样无忧、这样乐于死、这样乐于活、这样有盼望、这样肯助人、这样不惦占有、这样不向占有屈膝。他发现你们因假教导的传统之力、持着你们所持的，就会说：“不！这样的信仰绝解释不了这样大能的结果！”你们会回答：“查查圣经看。”他会去查，并发现——不是你们想象在其中的那些东西，而是无限更好更高的东西、真能解释他所惊叹之结果的东西；他会发现那样的真理——凡寻见的必永远持守为存有唯一之乐。那时你们就得了回报——尽管受教又施教那些恶教义、仍作了真基督徒的回报：你们要反过来、被你们引来的那位——他的真基督徒性吸引了他、又使他脱离了瘫痪你们判断的偏见、直抵源头——在那事上受教。既这样脱离了那必已阻碍你们成长的假观念，你们的成长将何等迅速！
你们中若有人对我说：我的教义是擅专的、违背新约所教导、也违背历代最好的人所信的，我不因此就着手辩护哪怕我的信仰、我努力借以活着的那些原则——更遑论我的意见！我只诉诸你们：关于我们首要的本分是行基督的话，我说的是不是真理。你们若说不是，我就无话可说；我们没有别的可以相见的地面。

===Original===

But if you allow that it is a prime, even if you do not allow it *the* prime duty, then what I insist upon is, that you should do it, so and not otherwise recommending the knowledge of him. I do not attempt to change your opinions; if they are wrong, the obedience alone on which I insist can enable you to set them right; I only pray you to obey, and assert that thus only can you fit yourselves for understanding the mind of Christ. I say none but he who does right, can think right; you cannot *know* Christ to be right until you do as he does, as he tells you to do; neither can you set him forth, until you know him as he means himself to be known, that is, as he is. If you are serving and trusting in Mammon, how can you know the living God who, the source of life, is alone to be trusted in! If you do not admit that it is the duty of a man to do the word of Christ, or if, admitting the duty, you yet do not care to perform it, why should I care to convince you that my doctrine is right? What is it to any true man what you think of his doctrine? What does it matter what you think of any doctrine? If I could convince your judgment, your hearts remaining as they are, I should but add to your condemnation. The true heart must see at once, that, however wrong I may or may not be in other things, at least I am right in this, that Jesus must be obeyed, and at once obeyed, in the things he did say: it will not long imagine to obey him in things he did not say. If a man do what is unpleasing to Christ, believing it his will, he shall yet gain thereby, for it gives the Lord a hold of him, which he will use; but before he can reach liberty, he must be delivered from that falsehood. For him who does not choose to see that Christ must be obeyed, he must be left to the teaching of the Father, who brings all that hear and learn of him to Christ, that they may learn what he is who has taught them and brought them. He will leave no man to his own way, however much he may prefer it. The Lord did not die to provide a man with the wretched heaven he may invent for himself, or accept invented for him by others; he died to give him life, and bring him to the heaven of the Father’s peace; the children must share in the essential bliss of the Father and the Son.

===Chinese===

但你们若容许这是首要本分之一——即使不认它是*那*首要的——那么我所坚持的，是你们当去行它，以这方式、而不是别的方式推荐对他的认识。我不试图改变你们的意见；它们若错了，唯有我坚持的顺服能使你们归正它们；我只求你们顺服，并断言唯有这样你们才能预备自己明白基督的心意。我说，唯有行正的人能思正；你们不能*知道*基督为正，直到你们照他行的行、照他告诉的作；你们也不能把他陈明出来，直到你们照他要人认识他的方式、就是说、照他所是的认识他。你们若正事奉并信靠玛门，怎能认识那位生命的源头、独一当信靠的永活神！你们若不承认行基督的话是人的本分，或承认了本分却无心去行，我为什么要在意说服你们我的教义是对的？你们怎样想他的教义，于任何真实的人有什么要紧？你们怎样想任何教义，有什么要紧？我若能说服你们的判断、你们的心却照旧，我只是加增你们的定罪。真实的心必立刻看见：无论我在别的事上错或不错，至少这点上我是对的——耶稣必须被顺服，并且立刻被顺服，在他确实说过的事上：它不会长久想象去顺服他没说过的事。人行了基督所不喜悦的事、却信那是他的旨意，他仍必由此得益，因为那给主一个可用的把握，主必使用它；但要达到自由，他必先脱离那虚假。至于那不肯看见基督必须被顺服的人，只能把他留给父的教导——父把一切听见并学于他的人带到基督那里，使他们认识那位教导了他们、带领了他们的是谁。他不留任何一个人在自己的路上，无论那人多喜欢那路。主死，不是要给人一个他为自己发明、或接受别人替他发明的可怜天堂；他死，是要给他生命、带他进父之平安的天堂；孩子们必须有分于父与子的本质福乐。

===Original===

This is and has been the Father’s work from the beginning﻿—to bring us into the home of his heart, where he shares the glories of life with the Living One, in whom was born life to light men back to the original life. This is our destiny; and however a man may refuse, he will find it hard to fight with God﻿—useless to kick against the goads of his love. For the Father is goading him, or will goad him, if needful, into life by unrest and trouble; hellfire will have its turn if less will not do: can any need it more than such as will neither enter the kingdom of heaven themselves, nor suffer them to enter it that would? The old race of the Pharisees is by no means extinct; they were St. Paul’s great trouble, and are yet to be found in every religious community under the sun.
The one only thing truly to reconcile all differences is, to walk in the light. So St. Paul teaches us in his epistle to the Philippians, the third chapter and sixteenth verse. After setting forth the loftiest idea of human endeavour in declaring the summit of his own aspiration, he says﻿—not, “This must be your endeavour also, or you cannot be saved”; but, “If in anything ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you. Nevertheless whereto we have already attained, let us walk by that same.” Observe what widest conceivable scope is given by the apostle to honest opinion, even in things of grandest import!﻿—the one only essential point with him is, that whereto we have attained, what we have seen to be true, *we walk by that*. In such walking, and in such walking only, love will grow, truth will grow; the soul, then first in its genuine element and true relation towards God, will see into reality that was before but a blank to it; and he who has promised to teach, will teach abundantly. Faster and faster will the glory of the Lord dawn upon the hearts and minds of his people so walking﻿—then his people indeed; fast and far will the knowledge of him spread, for truth of action, both preceding and following truth of word, will prepare the way before him.

===Chinese===

这是、也一直是从起初父的工——把我们带进他心的家，在那里他与那存活者分享生命的荣耀，生命在他里面出生、要把人照亮、领回原初的生命。这是我们的定命；无论人怎样拒绝，他必发现与神相争何等艰难——抗拒他爱的刺棍是无用的。因为父正以不安与烦恼刺他、或必要时要刺他入生命；若更轻的不够，地狱之火必轮到它：还有谁比那些自己不进天国、又不许要进的人进去的更需要它呢？法利赛人的旧族绝未绝种；他们是圣保罗的大患，如今在日下每一个宗教团体里都找得到。
唯一真能调和一切分歧的，是行在光中。圣保罗在致腓立比人书（3:16）里这样教导我们。在陈明人类奋斗的最高观念、宣告他自己志向的极顶之后，他说的不是“这也必须是你们的志向，否则不能得救”；而是“然而我们到了什么地步，就当照着什么地步行。”看使徒给诚实的意见留了何等无可再宽的余地，甚至在至大的事上！——他唯一必要的一点是：到了什么地步、看见了什么是真的，*就当照着行*。在这样的行走中、也唯独在其中，爱要生长，真理要生长；灵魂那时第一次处于它真实的元素、对神真实的关系中，要看进它从前只是空白的实际；那位应许教导的，必丰盛教导。主荣耀的光必照着这样行走之百姓——那时才真是他的百姓——的心思意念、越来越快地破晓；对他的认识必传得又快又远，因为行动的真理、先行又随后于言语的真理，必在他面前预备道路。

===Original===

The man walking in that whereto he has attained, will be able to think aright; the man who does not think right, is unable because he has not been walking right; only when he begins to do the thing he knows, does he begin to be able to think aright; then God comes to him in a new and higher way, and works along with the spirit he has created. The soul, without its heaven above its head, without its life-breath around it, without its love-treasure in its heart, without its origin one with it and bound up in it, without its true self and originating life, cannot think to any real purpose﻿—nor ever would to all eternity. When man joins with God, then is all impotence and discord cast out. Until then, there can be but jar; God is in contest with the gates of hell that open in the man, and can but hold his own; when the man joins him, then is Satan foiled. For then first nature receives her necessity: no such necessity has she as this law of all laws﻿—that God and man are one. Until they begin to be one in the reality as in the divine idea, in the flower as in the root, in the finishing as in the issuing creation, nothing can go right with the man, and God can have no rest from his labour in him. As the greatest orbs in heaven are drawn by the least, God himself must be held in divine disquiet until every one of his family be brought home to his heart, to be one with him in a unity too absolute, profound, far-reaching, fine, and intense, to be understood by any but the God from whom it comes, yet to be guessed at by the soul from the unspeakableness of its delight when at length it is with the *only* that can be its own, the one that it can possess, the one that can possess it. For God is the heritage of the soul in the ownness of origin; man is the offspring of his making will, of his life; God himself is his birthplace; God is the self that makes the soul able to say *I too, I myself*. This absolute unspeakable bliss of the creature is that for which the Son died, for which the Father suffered with him. Then only is life itself; then only is it right, is it one; then only is it as designed and necessitated by the eternal life-outgiving Life.
Whereto then we have attained let us walk by that same!

===Chinese===

照所达到的而行走的人，才能思想正当；思想不正当的人不能，是因为他没有行得正当；唯有开始行所知道的，才开始能思想正当；那时神以一条新的更高的路临到他、与他所造的灵同工。灵魂没有它头顶的天、没有环绕它的生命之息、没有它心中的爱之宝、没有与它为一、缠结于它的本源、没有它真实的自己与赋予生命的生命，就不能思想出任何真实的果效——直到永永远远也不能。人与神联合，那时一切的无能与不谐才被逐出。在那之前，只能有刺耳的杂音；神与那在人里面敞开的地狱之门相争、只能守住自己的阵地；当人与他联合，撒但才被挫败。因为那时自然才第一次领受它的必需：她没有比这律中之律更大的必需——神与人是一。直到他们开始在实际上、如在属神观念中那样为一，在花中如在根中，在完成的创造中如在发出的创造中，没有一件事能对人转正，神在他里面的劳碌也不得安息。正如天上最大的天体被最小的牵引，神自己必持在属神的不宁中，直到他家的每一个都被带回他心、与他为一——那合一太绝对、太深、太远、太精微、太炽烈，除它所从出的神外无人能懂，然而灵魂可以从它至终与那*独一*能属于它的、独一它能拥有的、独一能拥有它的同在时那说不出的喜乐中去猜度。因为神是灵魂在本源之自有里的产业；人是他创造意志、他的生命的后裔；神自己是他的生地；神是那使灵魂能说*我也在，我自己*的自己。受造者这绝对而说不出的福乐，正是子为之死、父与他同受苦的那一切。唯有那时才有生命本身；唯有那时它才正、才是一；唯有那时它才如那永远倾出生命之生命所设计与命定的那样。
那么，我们到了什么地步，就当照着什么地步行！

### The Creation in Christ / 在基督里的创造
===Original===

> All things were made by him, and without him was not anything made that was made. In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

===Chinese===

> 万物是借着他造的；凡被造的，没有一样不是借着他造的。生命在他里头，这生命就是人的光。

===Original===

It seems to me that any lover of the gospel given to thinking, and especially one accustomed to the effort of uttering thought, can hardly have failed to feel dissatisfaction, more or less definite, with the close of the third verse, as here presented to English readers. It seems to me in its feebleness, unlike, and rhetorically unworthy of the rest. That it is no worse than pleonastic, that is, redundant, therefore only unnecessary, can be no satisfaction to the man who would find perfection, if he may, in the words of him who was nearer the Lord than any other. The phrase “that was made” seems, from its uselessness, weak even to foolishness after what precedes: “All things were made by him, and without him was not anything made *that was made*.”
My hope was therefore great when I saw, in reading the Greek, that the shifting of a period would rid me of the pleonasm. If thereupon any precious result of meaning should follow, the change would not merely be justifiable﻿—seeing that points are of no authority with anyone accustomed to the vagaries of scribes, editors, and printers﻿—but one for which to give thanks to God. And I found the change did unfold such a truth as showed the rhetoric itself in accordance with the highest thought of the apostle. So glad was I, that it added little to my satisfaction to find the change supported by the best manuscripts and versions. It could add none to learn that the passage had been, in respect of the two readings, a cause of much disputation: the ground of argument on the side of the common reading, seemed to me worse than worthless.
Let us then look at the passage as I think it ought to be translated, and after that, seek the meaning for the sake of which it was written. It is a meaning indeed by no means dependent for its revelation on this passage, belonging as it does to the very truth as it is in Jesus; but it is therein magnificently expressed by the apostle, and differently from anywhere else﻿—that is, if I am right in the interpretation which suggested itself the moment I saw the probable rhetorical relation of the words.
“All things were made through him, and without him was made not one thing. That which was made in him was life, and the life was the light of men.”
Note the antithesis of the “through” and the “in.”

===Chinese===

在我看来，凡爱好福音而又惯于思考的人，尤其是惯于费力将思想诉诸言语的人，几乎不可能不感到某种或隐或显的不满——对着这节经文的结尾，照它在此呈现给英语读者的样子。在我看来，以它的软弱，既与其余部分不相称，在修辞上也配不上其余部分。它顶多算是冗赘，也就是叠床架屋，因而只是多余——这个事实，对于想在那位比任何人都更亲近主之人的言语中寻找完全（倘若可以寻见）的人，不可能是满足。那短语「*那被造的*」（that was made），就其无用而言，接在前文之后，软弱得近乎愚蠢：「万物都是借着他造的，凡被造之物，没有一样不是借着他造的*那被造之物*」。

因此，当我阅读希腊文时发现，只要把句号挪动一下，就能摆脱这冗赘，我的希望便大增。倘若由此能得出什么宝贵的含义，那么这一改动就不仅是可以成立的——因为在见过抄经士、编者与印刷工种种无常之举的人看来，标点本无权威——更是值得感谢神（God）的一项改动。而我发现，这改动果真展开了一样真理，显明这段话的修辞本身，正与使徒最高的思想相合。我如此欣喜，以致后来发现这改动得到最佳抄本与译本的支持，也只给我添了很少的满足；至于得知这段经文就这两种读法曾引起诸多争论，更是一分也添不上：持通行读法一方所持的论据，在我看来比无用还要糟。

那么，让我们来看这段经文——照我认为它当有的译法——然后再来寻求那使徒为之写下它的含义。这含义的启示，确实绝不依赖这一段经文，因为它本属「在耶稣里的真理」本身；但使徒在此把它表达得宏伟壮丽，且与任何别处都不同——这就是说，如果我一看见这些字句之间大概的修辞关系时便自行浮现的那个解释不错的话。

「万物都是借着他造的；离开了他，被造的没有一样。那在他里面受造的，乃是生命，这生命就是人的光。」

请注意「借着」（through）与「在……里面」（in）的对举。

===Original===

In this grand assertion seems to me to lie, more than shadowed, the germ of creation and redemption﻿—of all the divine in its relation to all the human.
In attempting to set forth what I find in it, I write with no desire to provoke controversy, which I loathe, but with some hope of presenting to the minds of such as have become capable of seeing it, the glory of the truth of the Father and the Son, as uttered by this first of seers, after the grandest fashion of his insight. I am as indifferent to a reputation for orthodoxy as I despise the championship of novelty. To the untrue, the truth itself must seem unsound, for the light that is in them is darkness.
I believe, then, that Jesus Christ is the eternal son of the eternal father; that from the first of firstness Jesus is the son, because God is the father﻿—a statement imperfect and unfit because an attempt of human thought to represent that which it cannot grasp, yet which it so believes that it must try to utter it even in speech that cannot be right. I believe therefore that the Father is the greater, that if the Father had not been, the Son could not have been. I will not apply logic to the thesis, nor would I state it now but for the sake of what is to follow. The true heart will remember the inadequacy of our speech, and our thought also, to the things that lie near the unknown roots of our existence. In saying what I do, I only say what Paul implies when he speaks of the Lord giving up the kingdom to his father, that God may be all in all. I worship the Son as the human God, the divine, the only Man, deriving his being and power from the Father, equal with him as a son is the equal at once and the subject of his father﻿—but *making himself the equal of his father in what is most precious in Godhead, namely, Love*﻿—which is, indeed, the essence of that statement of the evangelist with which I have now to do﻿—a higher thing than the making of the worlds and the things in them, which he did by the power of the Father, not by a self-existent power in himself, whence the apostle, to whom the Lord must have said things he did not say to the rest, or who was better able to receive what he said to all, says, “All things were made” not *by*, but “*through* him.”
We must not wonder things away into nonentity, but try to present them to ourselves after what fashion we are able﻿—our shadows of the heavenly.

===Chinese===

在我看来，在这一庄严的宣告里，所藏的远不止是投影，而是创造与救赎的胚芽——是一切属神之事与一切属人之事的关系的胚芽。

在试图阐明我在这宣告中所见之时，我写作并非想要挑起争辩——那是我厌恶的——而是抱着一点希望，想把这父与子之真理的荣耀，照这位第一先见者以其最宏大洞察的表达，呈现在那些已经能够看见的人心里。我对正统名声的无所谓，一如我对求新之冠冕的鄙弃。对不真的人，真理本身必显得不可靠，因为他们里头的光原是黑暗。

这样，我信耶稣基督是永恒之父（the Father）的永恒之子；信从元初之先，耶稣就是子，因为神是父——这陈述既不完全、也不合宜，因为那是人的思想在试图表述它所把握不了的东西；然而人既如此相信，便纵然言语必不能说得恰当，也仍要设法把它说出来。因此我信父是更大的，若没有父，子便不能存在。我不愿对这论题施用逻辑；若不是为下文的缘故，我现在也不愿陈述它。真实的心会记得，我们的言语、连同我们的思想，对那些贴近我们存在之未知根部的事物，是何等不济。我所说的，不过是保罗说到主将国交与父、叫神在万物之上、为万物之主时所暗示的。我拜子，拜他为人中之神、为神圣者、为那唯一的人——他的存在与权能都源于父；他与父平等，正如儿子同时既是父亲的平等者、又是父亲的属下——但他是*在神格中最宝贵的那件事上，就是爱，使自己与父平等*——这实在就是我现在要谈的福音书作者那句宣告的本旨——是比创造诸世界和其中万物更高的事；那些世界是父的能力造的，不是靠他自己里面自存的能力；因此那位使徒——主必定对他讲过些未对其余人讲的事，或者他比众人更能领受主对众人所讲的话——说，「万物」不是「*由*」（by）他、而是「*借着他*」（through）造的。

我们必不可因着惊叹把事物惊成虚无，而要尽力照我们所能的方式，把它们呈现在自己面前——作为属天之物的影儿。

===Original===

For our very beings and understandings and consciousnesses, though but shadows in regard to any perfection either of outline or operation, are yet shadows of his being, his understanding, his consciousness, and he has cast those shadows; they are no more causally our own than his power of creation is ours. In our shadow-speech then, and following with my shadow-understanding as best I can the words of the evangelist, I say, The Father, in bringing out of the unseen the things that are seen, made essential use of the Son, so that all that exists was created “through” him. What the difference between the part in creation of the Father and the part of the Son may be, who can understand?﻿—but perhaps we may one day come to see into it a little; for I dare hope that, through our willed sonship, we shall come far nearer ourselves to creating. The word “creation” applied to the loftiest success of human genius, seems to me a mockery of humanity, itself in process of creation.
Let us read the text again: “All things were made *through* him, and without him was made not one thing. That which was made *in* him was life.” You begin to see it? The power by which he created the worlds was given him by his father; he had in himself a greater power than that by which he made the worlds. There was something made, not *through* but *in* him; something brought into being by himself. Here he creates in his grand way, in himself, as did the Father. “That which was made *in* him was *life*.”
What does this mean? What is the “life” the apostle intends? Many forms of life have come to being through the Son, but those were results, not forms of the life that was brought to existence *in* him. He could not have been employed by the Father in creating, save in virtue of the life that was *in* him.
As to what the life of God is to himself, we can only know that we cannot know it﻿—even that not being absolute ignorance, for no one can see that, from its very nature, he cannot understand a thing without therein approaching that thing in a most genuine manner. As to what the life of God is in relation to us, we know that it is the causing life of everything that we call life﻿—of everything that is; and in knowing this, we know something of that life, by the very forms of its force.

===Chinese===

因为我们这些存在、这些领悟、这些意识，虽然在轮廓或作用上都谈不上任何完全，却仍是他的存在、他的领悟、他的意识的影儿，而且是他所投下的影儿；论到因果，它们并非属于我们自己，正如他的创造大能不属于我们一样。因此，用我们这影儿的言语，以我这影儿的领悟尽力跟随福音书作者的话，我说：父在将看得见之物从看不见之中带出来时，本质地使用了子，以致凡存在的，都是「借着他」造的。父在创造里的分与子在创造里的分，其间的分别是什么，谁能明白呢？——但也许有一天我们能稍稍看进去一点；因为我敢于盼望，借着我们甘愿的儿子名分，我们自己也将大大接近于创造。「创造」一词若用在人类天才最高的成就上，在我看来是对人类的一种嘲弄，因为人类自己正在受造的过程之中。

让我们再读这经文：「万物都是*借着他*造的；离开了他，被造的没有一样。那*在他里面*受造的，乃是生命。」你开始看见了吗？他用以创造诸世界的能力，是他父赐给他的；在他自己里面，他还有一样比创造诸世界更大的能力。有一样东西被造出来，不是*借着他*、而是*在他里面*；有一样东西，是他自己使之进入存在的。在这里，他以他那宏伟的方式创造，在他自己里面创造，正如父那样。「那*在他里面*受造的，乃是*生命*。」

这是什么意思呢？使徒所说的「生命」是什么？许多生命的形式都是借着子进入存在的，但那些是结果，不是那在他「里面」被带来存在之生命的诸形式。他若不是凭着他「里面」的生命，父就不能用他来创造。

至于神的生命对他自己是什么，我们只能知道：我们无法知道——连这也并非绝对的无知，因为从其本性而言，没有人能看见这一点：人理解不了一件事物，却不同时在其中以最真实的方式接近那事物。至于神的生命相对于我们是什么，我们知道它是我们所称为生命之一切——一切存在之物——的发生之因的生命；知道了这一点，我们便凭它力量之诸形式，对那生命知道了一点。

===Original===

But the one interminable mystery, for I presume the two make but one mystery﻿—a mystery that must be a mystery to us forever, not because God will not explain it, but because God himself could not make us understand it﻿—is first, how he can be self-existent, and next, how he can make other beings exist: self-existence and creation no man will ever understand. Again, regarding the matter from the side of the creature﻿—the cause of his being is antecedent to that being; he can therefore have no knowledge of his own creation; neither could he understand that which he can do nothing like. If we could make ourselves, we should understand our creation, but to do that we must be God. And of all ideas this﻿—that, with the self-dissatisfied, painfully circumscribed consciousness I possess, I could in any way have caused myself, is the most dismal and hopeless. Nevertheless, if I be a child of God, I must be *like* him, like him even in the matter of this creative energy. There must be something in me that corresponds in its childish way to the eternal might in him. But I am forestalling. The question now is: What was that life, the thing made “in” the Son﻿—made by him inside himself, not outside him﻿—made not “through” but “in him”﻿—the life that was his own, as God’s is his own?
It was, I answer, that act in him that corresponded in him, as the son, to the self-existence of his father. Now what is the deepest in God? His power? No, for power could not make him what we mean when we say “God.” Evil could, of course, never create one atom; but let us understand very plainly, that a being whose essence was only power would be such a negation of the divine that no righteous worship could be offered him: his service must be fear, and fear only. Such a being, even were he righteous in judgment, yet could not be God. The God himself whom we love could not be righteous were he not something deeper and better still than we generally mean by the word﻿—but, alas, how little can language say without seeming to say something wrong! In one word, God is Love. Love is the deepest depth, the essence of his nature, at the root of all his being. It is not merely that he could not be God, if he had made no creatures to whom to be God; but love is the heart and hand of his creation; it is his right to create, and his power to create as well.

===Chinese===

但那无穷尽的奥秘——我想这两者其实只是一个奥秘——一个对我们必永远是奥秘的奥秘，不是因为神不肯解释它，而是因为神自己也无法使我们明白它——第一是他怎能自有自存，第二是他怎能叫别的存在者存在：自存与创造，是无人永远能明白的。再从受造者这一面看这事——他存在的原因先于他的存在；因此他对于自己的受造不可能有认识；他也不能理解一件他自己毫无办法作出类似之事的事。我们若能造自己，就必明白自己的受造；但要那样，我们就必须是神。而在一切观念之中，这一个——即带着我现在这自我不满、痛苦受拘限的意识的我，居然能在什么意义上造成了我自己——是最阴郁、最无望的。然而，我若是神的儿女，我就必须*像*他，甚至在这创造大能的事上也像他。我里面必得有什么东西，以它孩子气的方式，与他里面那永恒的大能相应。但这话我说早了。现在的问题是：那生命、那在子「里面」造出来的东西——由他在他自己里面造的，不是在他外面造的——不是「借着他」、而是「在他里面」造的——那属于他自己的生命，正如神的生命属于神自己——究竟是什么？

我回答说，那是他里面的一举，是他作为子，在他里面与父之自存相应的一举。那么，神里面最深的是什么？是他的权能吗？不，因为权能不能使他成为我们说「神」时所意指的那一位。恶当然永远造不出一个原子；但让我们清清楚楚地明白：一位其本质唯有权能的存在者，乃是对神性的否定，以致无人能献给他义（righteousness）的敬拜：对他的事奉只能是惧怕，唯独惧怕。这样的一位，即使在审判上公义，也仍是神不成。我们所爱的这位神自己，若不是比我们通常用这词所指的更深更好的什么，就不可能是义的——可是，唉，言语一开口，就仿佛要说错，它能说的何其少！总之一句话：神是爱。爱是最深的深度，是他性情的本质，在他一切存在的根部。这不仅是说，他若没有造出受造者来作他们的神，就不能是神；爱更是他创造的心与手；爱是他创造的权利，也是他创造的大能。

===Original===

The love that foresees creation is itself the power to create. Neither could he be righteous﻿—that is, fair to his creatures﻿—but that his love created them. His perfection is his love. All his divine rights rest upon his love. Ah, he is not the great monarch! The simplest peasant loving his cow, is more divine than any monarch whose monarchy is his glory. If God would not punish sin, or if he did it for anything but love, he would not be the father of Jesus Christ, the God who works as Jesus wrought. What then, I say once more, is in Christ correspondent to the creative power of God? It must be something that comes also of love; and in the Son the love must be to the already existent. Because of that eternal love which has no beginning, the Father must have the Son. God could not love, could not be love, without making things to love: Jesus has God to love; the love of the Son is responsive to the love of the Father. The response to self-existent love is self-abnegating love. The refusal of himself is that in Jesus which corresponds to the creation of God. His love takes action, creates, in self-abjuration, in the death of self as motive; in the drowning of self in the life of God, where it lives only as love. What is life in a child? Is it not perfect response to his parents? thorough oneness with them? A child at strife with his parents, one in whom their will is not his, is no child; as a child he is dead, and his death is manifest in rigidity and contortion. His spiritual order is on the way to chaos. Disintegration has begun. Death is at work in him. See the same child yielding to the will that is righteously above his own; see the life begin to flow from the heart through the members; see the relaxing limbs; see the light rise like a fountain in his eyes, and flash from his face! Life has again its lordship!
The life of Christ is this﻿—negatively, that he does nothing, cares for nothing for his own sake; positively, that he cares with his whole soul for the will, the pleasure of his father. Because his father is his father, therefore he will be his child. The truth in Jesus is his relation to his father; the righteousness of Jesus is his fulfilment of that relation.

===Chinese===

那预见了创造的爱，本身就是创造的权能。他也不可能为义——就是说，对他的受造者公平——除非是他的爱造了他们。他的完全就是他的爱。他一切神圣的权利都立在他的爱上。啊，他不是那位大君主！一个爱着他的母牛的最简朴的农夫，也比任何以君权为荣耀的君主更神圣。神若不肯刑罚罪，或者他刑罚罪不是单单出于爱，他就不是耶稣基督的父，不是那位照耶稣作工的样子作工的神。那么，我再说一次：基督里面有什么与神的创造大能相应？那必是同样出于爱的东西；而在子里，这爱必是向着那已经存在者的。因着那没有起头的永恒之爱，父就必有子。神若不造出可爱之物，就不能爱，就不能是爱：耶稣有神可爱；子的爱回应父的爱。对自存之爱的回应，是舍己之爱。对自我的拒绝，正是耶稣里面那与神的创造相应的东西。他的爱采取行动、进行创造，是在自我弃绝之中，在把自我当作动机治死之中，在把自我淹没于神的生命里——在那里，自我只作为爱而活。孩子里面的生命是什么？岂不是对父母完全的回应？岂不是与父母彻底的合一？与父母相争的孩子、那在其中父母的旨意不是他旨意的孩子，就不是孩子；作为孩子他是死的，他的死显在僵硬与扭曲里。他属灵的秩序正走向混乱。崩解已经开始。死亡在他里面作工。看这同一个孩子，顺服于那义地高过他自己的旨意；看生命开始从心流过四肢；看绷紧的肢体松弛下来；看光像泉水一样在他眼里升起，从他脸上闪耀！生命又恢复了它的主权！

基督的生命乃是这个——消极地说，他不为自己的缘故做任何事、挂心任何事；积极地说，他以全魂挂心父的旨意、父的喜悦。因为他的父是他的父，所以他甘愿作他的孩子。耶稣里面的真理，就是他与父的关系；耶稣的义，就是他对那关系的成全。

===Original===

Meeting this relation, loving his father with his whole being, he is not merely alive as born of God; but, giving himself with perfect will to God, choosing to die to himself and live to God, he therein creates in himself a new and higher life; and, standing upon himself, has gained the power to awake life, the divine shadow of his own, in the hearts of us his brothers and sisters, who have come from the same birth-home as himself, namely, the heart of his God and our God, his father and our father, but who, without our elder brother to do it first, would never have chosen that self-abjuration which is life, never have become alive like him. To will, not from self, but with the Eternal, is to live.
This choice of his own being, in the full knowledge of what he did; this active willing to be the Son of the Father, perfect in obedience﻿—is that in Jesus which responds and corresponds to the self-existence of God. Jesus rose at once to the height of his being, set himself down on the throne of his nature, in the act of subjecting himself to the will of the Father as his only good, the only *reason* of his existence. When he died on the cross, he did that, in the wild weather of his outlying provinces in the torture of the body of his revelation, which he had done at home in glory and gladness. From the infinite beginning﻿—for here I can speak only by contradictions﻿—he completed and held fast the eternal circle of his existence in saying, “Thy will, not mine, be done!” He made himself what he is by *deathing* himself into the will of the eternal Father, through which will he was the eternal Son﻿—thus plunging into the fountain of his own life, the everlasting Fatherhood, and taking the Godhead of the Son. This is the life that was made “in” Jesus: “That which was made in him was life.” This life, self-willed in Jesus, is the one thing that makes such life﻿—the eternal life, the true life, possible﻿—nay, imperative, essential, to every man, woman, and child, whom the Father has sent into the outer, that he may go back into the inner world, his heart. As the self-existent life of the Father has given us being, so the willed devotion of Jesus is his power to give us eternal life like his own﻿—to enable us to do the same.

===Chinese===

他迎向这关系，以他全部的存在爱他的父，就不仅是作为神所生的而活着；他更以完全的意志把自己献给神，选择向己死、向神活，便在其中于自己里面创造出一种新的、更高的生命；并且，他立于自己之上，赢得了唤醒生命的大能——他自己那生命之神圣的影儿——在我们这些他弟兄姐妹的心里唤醒它；我们与他出自同一个出生之家，就是他的神、我们的神，他的父、我们的父的心；但若没有我们的长兄先行去行，我们永远不会拣选那作为生命的自我弃绝，永远不会像他那样活起来。立志，不出于自我，而是与那永恒者同愿，就是活着。

他对自己存在的这一拣选，是在对他所行之完全的知悉中作出的；这主动的立志要做父的儿子、在顺服（obedience）上完全——这就是耶稣里面那回应并相应于神之自存的东西。耶稣一跃升到他存在的高处，登上他本性的宝座，就在那使自己顺服于父的旨意、以之为他唯一的美善、他存在唯一*理由*的举动之中。当他死在十字架上时，他在他那遥远行省的风雨里、在他启示之身体的剧痛中，行了他在家中、在荣耀与喜乐里早已行过的事。从无穷的起初——因为在这里我只能借着矛盾来说话——他在说「愿你的旨意成全，不要照我的！」时，就完成并守住了他存在的永恒之环。他借着把自己*死入*永恒之父的旨意，造成了他的所是；正是借着那旨意，他为永恒之子——如此，他纵身跃入他自己生命的泉源，那永存的父性，取得了子的神格。这就是那在耶稣「里面」被造的生命：「那在他里面受造的，乃是生命。」这生命，在耶稣里是自我立志而成的，正是唯独它使这样的生命——永生、真生命——对每一个父所差到外面来的男人、女人、孩子成为可能，不，成为必需、成为根本，好叫他可以回到那内在的世界，他的心。正如父那自存的生命给了我们存在，耶稣那甘愿的奉献，就是他赐给我们他那样式永生的大能——叫我们能够照样去行。

===Original===

There is no life for any man, other than the same kind that Jesus has; his disciple must live by the same absolute devotion of his will to the Father’s; then is his life one with the life of the Father.
Because we are come out of the divine nature, which chooses to be divine, we must *choose* to be divine, to be of God, to be one with God, loving and living as he loves and lives, and so be partakers of the divine nature, or we perish. Man cannot originate this life; it must be shown him, and he must choose it. God is the father of Jesus and of us﻿—of every possibility of our being; but while God is the father of his children, Jesus is the father of their sonship; for in him is made the life which is sonship to the Father﻿—the recognition, namely, in fact and life, that the Father has his claim upon his sons and daughters. We are not and cannot become true sons without our will willing his will, our doing following his making. It was the will of Jesus to be the thing God willed and meant him, that made him the true son of God. He was not the son of God because he could not help it, but because he willed to be in himself the son that he was in the divine idea. So with us: we must *be* the sons we are. We are not made to be what we cannot help being; sons and daughters are not after such fashion! We are sons and daughters in God’s claim; we must be sons and daughters in our will. And we can be sons and daughters, saved into the original necessity and bliss of our being, only by choosing God for the father he is, and doing his will﻿—yielding ourselves true sons to the absolute Father. Therein lies human bliss﻿—only and essential. The working out of this our salvation must be pain, and the handing of it down to them that are below must ever be in pain; but the eternal form of the will of God in and for us, is intensity of bliss.
“And the life was the light of men.”
The life of which I have now spoken became light to men in the appearing of him in whom it came into being. The life became light that men might see it, and themselves live by choosing that life also, by choosing so to live, such to be.
There is always something deeper than anything said﻿—something of which all human, all divine words, figures, pictures, motion-forms, are but the outer laminar spheres through which the central reality shines more or less plainly.

===Chinese===

任何人所能有的生命，除了与耶稣所有的同一种类外，别无其他；他的门徒必须以同样绝对的奉献——把自己的意志献给父的意志——来活；这样，他的生命就与父的生命合为一。

因为我们出于那神圣本性——那拣选要成为神圣的神圣本性——我们就必须*拣选*成为神圣，成为属神的，与神合一，像他爱与活那样去爱、去活，从而有分于神圣的本性，不然我们便灭亡。人不能发起这生命；这生命必须显给他看，而他必须拣选它。神是耶稣的父，也是我们的父——是我们一切存在可能性的父；但神虽是他儿女的父，耶稣却是他们儿子名分之父；因为在他里面造出了那向父作儿子的生命——就是以事实、以生命承认父对他的儿女们拥有他的权利。若没有我们的意志志愿他的旨意、我们的行为跟从他的作为，我们就不是、也不能成为真正的儿子。耶稣立志要做神所愿、所意要他做的那个，这才使他成为神真正的儿子。他之为神子，不是因为无可奈何，而是因为他志愿在自己里面成为他在神圣观念中所是的那个子。我们也如此：我们必须*成为*我们所是的儿子。我们不是被造来作我们不得不作的东西；儿子女儿不是照那种样子作成的！在神的权利里，我们是儿子是女儿；在我们的意志里，我们也必须是儿子是女儿。而我们唯有拣选神、认他照他的本相作我们的父，并行他的旨意——把自己交出来，作那位绝对之父的真儿子——才能作儿子作女儿，得救进入我们存在本初的必然与福气。人的福气就在于此——唯独于此、本质地于此。这救恩在我们身上的作成必是痛苦，把它传递给在下面的人，也必永远在痛苦中进行；但神的旨意（the will of God）在我们里面、为我们所取的永恒形式，却是浓烈的喜乐。

「这生命就是人的光。」

我刚才所说的那生命，是在它所成于其人之内的那位的显现中，成为人的光。生命成为光，是要叫人看见它，并借着同样拣选那生命、拣选那样活、那样存在，而自己得以活。

凡是说出来的，总还有比它更深的东西——一切属人的、属神的言词、比喻、图画、动态的形式，都不过是外层的鳞状球壳，中央的那真实，只是或明或暗地透过它们照耀而已。

===Original===

Light itself is but the poor outside form of a deeper, better thing, namely, life. The life is Christ. The light too is Christ, but only the body of Christ. The life is Christ himself. The light is what we *see* and shall see in him; the life is what we may *be* in him. The life “is a light by abundant clarity invisible”; it is the unspeakable unknown; it must become light such as men can see before men can know it. Therefore the obedient human God appeared as the obedient divine man, doing the works of his father﻿—the things, that is, which his father did﻿—doing them humbly before unfriendly brethren. The Son of the Father must take his own form in the substance of flesh, that he may be seen of men, and so become the light of men﻿—not that men may have light, but that men may have life;﻿—that, seeing what they could not originate, they may, through the life that is in them, begin to hunger after the life of which they are capable, and which is essential to their being;﻿—that the life in them may long for him who is their life, and thirst for its own perfection, even as root and stem may thirst for the flower for whose sake, and through whose presence in them, they exist. That the child of God may become the son of God by beholding *the* Son, the life revealed in light; that the radiant heart of the Son of God may be the sunlight to his fellows; that the idea may be drawn out by the presence and drawing of the Ideal﻿—that Ideal, the perfect Son of the Father, was sent to his brethren.
Let us not forget that the devotion of the Son could never have been but for the devotion of the Father, who never seeks his own glory one atom more than does the Son; who is devoted to the Son, and to all his sons and daughters, with a devotion perfect and eternal, with fathomless unselfishness. The whole being and doing of Jesus on earth is the same as his being and doing from all eternity, that whereby he is the blessed son-God of the father-God; it is the shining out of that life that men might see it. It is a being like God, a doing of the will of God, a working of the works of God, therefore an unveiling of the Father in the Son, that men may know him. It is the prayer of the Son to the rest of the sons to come back to the Father, to be reconciled to the Father, to behave to the Father as he does.

===Chinese===

光本身，不过是一件更深更好之物——即生命——那贫弱的外在形式。生命就是基督。光也是基督，却只是基督的身体。生命是基督自己。光是我们在他身上所*看见*、也将要看见的；生命是我们在他里面所可能*成为*的。这生命「是一团光，因其过度的澄明而不可见」；它是那说不出的未知；它必须先成为人能看见的光，人才能认识它。所以，那位顺服的人中之神，显为顺服的神中之人，行他父的作为——就是他父所行的那些事——在不友善的弟兄面前谦卑地行。父的子必须在肉身的实体中取他自己的形像，好叫人看见他，从而成为人的光——不是要人得光，而是要人得生命；——叫人看见他们自己所不能发起的，便能借着在他们里面的生命，开始饥渴慕求那他们所能及、且为他们存在所必需的生命；——叫他们里面的生命渴慕那位就是他们生命的主，渴慕它自己的完全，正如根与茎渴慕那花——为了那花，也借着那花在它们里面的同在，它们才存在。为叫神的儿女可以借着注视*那位*子——在光中显明的生命——而成为神的儿子；为叫神儿子的那颗发光的心，可以作他同胞的日光；为叫观念可以因那理想的同在与吸引而被引出来——那理想、父的完全之子，就被差到他的弟兄们这里来了。

我们不要忘记，子的奉献若非因着父的奉献，就永远不能存在：父寻求自己的荣耀，一分一毫也不比子多；父以完全而永恒的奉献、以无底的忘我，献身子，也献身于他一切的儿女。耶稣在地上全部的存在与作为，与他从永远就有的存在与作为是同一回事，就是那使他成为父神之蒙福子神的所在；那是那生命的照耀，好叫人看见。那是一种像神的存在，一种行神旨意的行，一种作神之工的作，因此是父在子里的揭开，好叫人认识他。那是子对其余众子的祷告（prayer），召他们回到父那里去，与父和好，像他那样对待父。

===Original===

He seems to me to say: “I know your father, for he is my father; I know him because I have been with him from eternity. You do not know him; I have come to you to tell you that as I am, such is he; that he is just like me, only greater and better. He only is the true, original good; I am true because I seek nothing but his will. He only is all in all; I am not all in all, but he is my father, and I am the son in whom his heart of love is satisfied. Come home with me, and sit with me on the throne of my obedience. Together we will do his will, and be glad with him, for his will is the only good. You may do with me as you please; I will not defend myself. Because I speak true, my witness is unswerving; I stand to it, come what may. If I held my face to my testimony only till danger came close, and then prayed the Father for twelve legions of angels to deliver me, that would be to say the Father would do anything for his children until it began to hurt him. I bear witness that my father is such as I. In the face of death I assert it, and dare death to disprove it. Kill me; do what you will and can against me; my father is true, and I am true in saying that he is true. Danger or hurt cannot turn me aside from this my witness. Death can only kill my body; he cannot make me his captive. Father, thy will be done! The pain will pass; it will be but for a time! Gladly will I suffer that men may know that I live, and that thou art my life. Be with me, father, that it may not be more than I can bear.”
Friends, if you think anything less than this could redeem the world, or make blessed any child that God has created, you know neither the Son nor the Father.
The bond of the universe, the chain that holds it together, the one active unity, the harmony of things, the negation of difference, the reconciliation of all forms, all shows, all wandering desires, all returning loves; the fact at the root of every vision, revealing that “love is the only good in the world,” and selfishness the one thing hateful, in the city of the living God unutterable, is the devotion of the Son to the Father. It is the life of the universe. It is not the fact that God created all things, that makes the universe a whole; but that he through whom he created them loves him perfectly, is eternally content in his father, is satisfied to be because his father is with him.

===Chinese===

在我听来，他仿佛是说：「我认识你们的父，因为他就是我的父；我认识他，因为我从永远就与他同在。你们不认识他；我到你们这里来，是要告诉你们：我怎样，他就是怎样；他就像我，只是更大、更好。唯有他是那真实、本源的美善；我是真实的，因为我只寻求他的旨意。唯有他是万有中的万有；我不是万有中的万有，但他是我的父，而我是那使他的爱心得着满足的儿子。跟我回家来，与我同坐在我顺服的宝座上。我们要一同行他的旨意，与他一同欢喜，因为他的旨意是唯一的善。你们要怎样待我，就怎样待我；我不为自己辩护。因为我说的是真话，我的见证就不动摇；无论怎样，我都站定在这里。倘若我持守我的见证只到危险临近，然后就求父差遣十二营天使来救我，那就等于说，父为他的儿女做任何事，都得等到他自己开始受痛为止。我见证我的父就是像我这样的人。在死亡面前我断言这一点，并敢叫死亡来反驳。杀我吧；随你们的意思、随你们的能力对付我；我的父是真实的，我说他真实，这话也是真实的。危险或伤害都不能使我偏离这见证。死亡只能杀我的身体；它不能把我掳作它的俘虏。父啊，愿你的旨意成全！这痛苦必要过去；它不过是一时！我甘愿受苦，使人知道我活着，知道你是我的生命。父啊，与我同在，免得它过于我所能受的。」

朋友们，你们若以为比这更少的任何东西就能救赎世界，或能叫神所造的任何一个孩子有福，你们就既不认识子，也不认识父。

宇宙的结、维系它的链、那独一活跃的合一、万物的和谐、差异的否定、一切形式、一切景象、一切流荡的欲愿、一切归回之爱的和好；那在每一个异象根部的事实，显明「爱是世上唯一的善」，而自私是唯一可恨之物——在那无法言说的永生神之城——就是子对父的奉献。它是宇宙的生命。使宇宙成为一体的，不是神创造了万物这事实；而是那位神借以创造万物者完全地爱他、永远在他的父里面满足、因他的父与他同在而甘于存在这事实。

===Original===

It is not the fact that God is all in all, that unites the universe; it is the love of the Son to the Father. For of no onehood comes unity; there can be no oneness where there is only one. For the very beginnings of unity there must be two. Without Christ, therefore, there could be no universe. The reconciliation wrought by Jesus is not the primary source of unity, of safety to the world; that reconciliation was the necessary working out of the eternal antecedent fact, the fact making itself potent upon the rest of the family﻿—that God and Christ are one, are father and son, the Father loving the Son as only the Father can love, the Son loving the Father as only the Son can love. The prayer of the Lord for unity between men and the Father and himself, springs from the eternal need of love. The more I regard it, the more I am lost in the wonder and glory of the thing. But for the Father and the Son, no two would care a jot the one for the other. It might be the right way for creatures to love because of mere existence, but what two creatures would ever have originated the loving? I cannot for a moment believe it would have been I. Even had I come into being as now with an inclination to love, selfishness would soon have overborne it. But if the Father loves the Son, if the very music that makes the harmony of life lies, not in the theory of love in the heart of the Father, but in the fact of it, in the burning love in the hearts of Father and Son, then glory be to the Father and to the Son, and to the spirit of both, the fatherhood of the Father meeting and blending with the sonhood of the Son, and drawing us up into the glory of their joy, to share in the thoughts of love that pass between them, in their thoughts of delight and rest in each other, in their thoughts of joy in all the little ones. The life of Jesus is the light of men, revealing to them the Father.
But light is not enough; light is for the sake of life. We too must have life in ourselves. We too must, like the Life himself, live. We can live in no way but that in which Jesus lived, in which life was made in him. That way is, to give up our life. This is the one supreme action of life possible to us for the making of life in ourselves. Christ did it of himself, and so became light to us, that we might be able to do it in ourselves, after him, and through his originating act.

===Chinese===

使宇宙合一的，不是神在万有中作万有这事实；而是子对父的爱。因为从「独一之一者」生不出合一；在只有一位的地方，不可能有合一。为着合一最起初的开端，必须先有二。因此，若没有基督，就不可能有宇宙。耶稣所成就的和好，并不是合一、并不是世界之安全的最初源头；那和好乃是那永恒在先之事实的必然后效，是那事实在其余家人身上发动的大能——那事实就是：神与基督为一，是父与子，父爱子，如唯有父能爱；子爱父，如唯有子能爱。主为人与父并他自己之间的合一所献的祷告，源于爱那永恒的需要。我越注视这事，越迷失在它的奇妙与荣耀里。若没有父与子，没有哪两位会彼此挂念丝毫。受造之物因单单存在而彼此相爱，也许是正当的路；但哪两个受造之物会发起那相爱呢？我一刻也不能相信那会是我。即使我像如今这样带着爱的倾向进入存在，自私也很快会将它压倒。但父若爱子，若那构成生命和谐的音乐，不在于父心中爱的理论，而在于爱的实际，在于父与子心中炽燃的爱，那么，愿荣耀归于父、归于子，也归于他俩的灵——父的父性与子的子性相遇相融，把我们提升进他们喜乐的荣耀里，有分于他们之间往来的爱念，有分于他们彼此里面喜乐与安息的思念，有分于他们在一切小者身上的欢喜。耶稣的生命就是人的光，将父显明给他们。

但光还不够；光是为着生命的缘故。我们自己里面也必须有生命。我们也必须像那位生命本身一样活。我们唯有照耶稣活着的方式、照生命在他里面被造的方式，才能活。那方式就是：舍去我们的生命。这是我们能行的一件至高的生命之举，用以在自己里面作成生命。基督自己这样行了，就如此成为我们的光，使我们能够在他之后、借着他那创始的举动，在自己里面也这样行。

===Original===

We must do it ourselves, I say. The help that he has given and gives, the light and the spirit-working of the Lord, the spirit, in our hearts, is all in order that we may, as we must, do it ourselves. Till then we are not alive; life is not made in us. The whole strife and labour and agony of the Son with every man, is to get him to die as he died. All preaching that aims not at this, is a building with wood and hay and stubble. If I say not with whole heart, “My father, do with me as thou wilt, only help me against myself and for thee”; if I cannot say, “I am thy child, the inheritor of thy spirit, thy being, a part of thyself, glorious in thee, but grown poor in me: let me be thy dog, thy horse, thy anything thou willest; let me be thine in any shape the love that is my Father may please to have me; let me be thine in any way, and my own or another’s in no way but thine”;﻿—if we cannot, fully as this, give ourselves to the Father, then we have not yet laid hold upon that for which Christ has laid hold upon us. The faith that a man may, nay, must put in God, reaches above earth and sky, stretches beyond the farthest outlying star of the creatable universe. The question is not at present, however, of removing mountains, a thing that will one day be simple to us, but of waking and rising from the dead now.
When a man truly and perfectly says with Jesus, and as Jesus said it, “Thy will be done,” he closes the everlasting life-circle; the life of the Father and the Son flows through him; he is a part of the divine organism. Then is the prayer of the Lord in him fulfilled: “I in them and thou in me, that they made be made perfect in one.” The Christ in us, is the spirit of the perfect child toward the perfect father. The Christ in us is our own true nature made blossom in us by the Lord, whose life is the light of men that it may become the life of men; for our true nature is childhood to the Father.
Friends, those of you who know, or suspect, that these things are true, let us arise and live﻿—arise even in the darkest moments of spiritual stupidity, when hope itself sees nothing to hope for. Let us not trouble ourselves about the cause of our earthliness, except we know it to be some unrighteousness in us, but go at once to the Life. Never, never let us accept as consolation the poor suggestion, that the cause of our deadness is physical.

===Chinese===

我说，我们必须自己去行。他已给又正给的援助、主的光与主的灵的运行、那在我们心里的灵，全都是为了叫我们能——正如我们必须——自己去行。在那之前，我们还没有活；生命还没有在我们里面作成。子与每一个人全部的争战、劳苦与剧痛，就是要叫他像子那样死。一切不以这个为目标的讲道，都是用木、草、禾秸在上面建造。我若不能以全心说：「我的父啊，愿你随意待我，只要帮助我敌对我自己、为着你」；我若不能说：「我是你的孩子，是你的灵、你的存在的后嗣，是你自己的一部分，在你里面荣耀，在我里面却沦为贫穷：让我作你的狗、你的马、你所愿意的任何东西；让那为我父的爱随意以什么形像拥有我；让我在任何方式里属你，而除了属你，不在任何方式里属我自己、也不属别人」；——我们若不能像这样完全地把自己交给父，那我们就还没有抓住基督耶稣所以要抓住我们的那目标。人对神所能、而且必须怀的信心（faith），高过天地，直伸过那可造之宇宙最远的边星。然而，现在的问题还不是移山——那件事有一天对我们必是再简单不过——而是现在就从死里醒来、起来。

当一个人真实而完全地与耶稣同说、且照耶稣说它的方式说「愿你的旨意成全」时，他就闭合了那永远的生命之环；父与子的生命流经他；他是那神圣机体的一部分。那时，主的祷告就在他身上得成全：「我在他们里面，你在我里面，使他们完完全全地合而为一」。在我们里面的基督，是完全的孩子向着完全的父的灵。在我们里面的基督，是我们的真本性借主在我们里面开出的花；主的生命是人的光，为要成为人的生命；因为我们的真本性，就是向父作孩子。

朋友们，你们中间凡知道、或疑心这些事是真的的，让我们起来活吧——哪怕在属灵的麻木（spiritual stupidity）最黑暗的时刻、当盼望自己也看不见有什么可盼望时，也要起来。不要为我们属地之气的原因烦扰，除非我们知道那是我们里面的某种不义；要直去就那生命。千万不要、千万不要接受那可怜的暗示作安慰，说我们死沉的原因是身体性的。

===Original===

Can it be comfort to know that this body of ours, because of the death in it, is too much for the spirit﻿—which ought not merely to triumph over it, but to inspire it with subjection and obedience? Let us comfort ourselves in the thought of the Father and the Son. So long as there dwells harmony, so long as the Son loves the Father with all the love the Father can welcome, all is well with the little ones. God is all right﻿—why should we mind standing in the dark for a minute outside his window? Of course we miss the “inness,” but there is a bliss of its own in waiting. What if the rain be falling, and the wind blowing; what if we stand alone, or, more painful still, have some dear one beside us, sharing our “outness”; what even if the window be not shining, because of the curtains of good inscrutable drawn across it; let us think to ourselves, or say to our friend, “God is; Jesus is not dead; nothing can be going wrong, however it may look so to hearts unfinished in childness.” Let us say to the Lord, “Jesus, art thou loving the Father in there? Then we out here will do his will, patiently waiting till he open the door. We shall not mind the wind or the rain much. Perhaps thou art saying to the Father, ‘Thy little ones need some wind and rain: their buds are hard; the flowers do not come out. I cannot get them made blessed without a little more winter-weather.’ Then perhaps the Father will say, ‘Comfort them, my son Jesus, with the memory of thy patience when thou wast missing me. Comfort them that thou wast sure of me when everything about thee seemed so unlike me, so unlike the place thou hadst left.’ ” In a word, let us be at peace, because peace is at the heart of things﻿—peace and utter satisfaction between the Father and the Son﻿—in which peace they call us to share; in which peace they promise that at length, when they have their good way with us, we shall share.
Before us, then, lies a bliss unspeakable, a bliss beyond the thought or invention of man, to every child who will fall in with the perfect imagination of the Father. His imagination is one with his creative will. The thing that God imagines, that thing exists. When the created falls in with the will of him who “loved him into being,” then all is well; thenceforward the mighty creation goes on in him upon higher and yet higher levels, in more and yet more divine airs.

===Chinese===

知道我们的这身体因着它里头的死亡，竟压过了那灵——那灵本不该仅仅胜过它，更当把顺服与听命灌输给它——这能算安慰吗？让我们在父与子的思想里得安慰。只要和谐长存，只要子以父所能欢迎的全部的爱爱父，小者们就一切都好。神一切都好——在他的窗外黑地里站上一会儿，我们又何必放在心上呢？我们当然想念那「在内」；但等候自有属于等候的福气。雨正落着、风正刮着，何妨；我们独自站着，或更痛苦些，有亲爱的人在身旁分担我们的「在外」，又何妨；纵然窗子因有美善莫测的帘幕拉在上面而不放光，又何妨；让我们心里这样想，或对朋友这样说：「神存在；耶稣没有死；没有什么能真正坏下去，无论它在孩子气未成全的心里看来多么像要坏下去。」让我们对主说：「耶稣，你在里面爱着父吗？那我们在外面的，就必行他的旨意，耐心等候，直到他开门。风和雨，我们就不大介意了。也许你正对父说：『你的小者们需要一点风雨：他们的花苞发硬；花开不出来。不再多一点冬天的天气，我无法叫他们得着福气。』那么也许父会说：『我儿耶稣，用你想念我时那忍耐的记忆安慰他们。用这个安慰他们：当围绕你的一切都如此不像我、如此不像你所离开的那地方时，你仍确信着我。』」总而言之，让我们平安，因为在万事的心中乃是平安——父与子之间全然的平安与满足——在这平安里，他们召我们去有分；在这平安里，他们应许：末了，当他们在我们身上遂了他们的美意时，我们必有分。

这样，在我们面前躺着说不出的福气，一样远超人的思想与发明的福气，等着每一个愿随父那完全之想象的儿女。他的想象与他的创造意志为一。神所想象的那东西，就存在。当受造者随从那位「把他爱进存在」者的旨意时，一切都好了；从此，那宏伟的创造就在他里面继续进行，在更高又更高的层面上，在越来越神圣的气息里。

===Original===

Thy will, O God, be done! Nought else is other than loss, than decay, than corruption. There is no life but that born of the life that the Word made in himself by doing thy will, which life is the light of men. Through that light is born the life of men﻿—the same life in them that came first into being in Jesus. As he laid down his life, so must men lay down their lives, that as he liveth they may live also. That which was made in him was life, and the life is the light of men; and yet his own, to whom he was sent, *did not believe him*.

===Chinese===

神啊，愿你的旨意成全！除它之外，一切都是损失、是衰朽、是败坏。除了那生命——道（the Word）在自己里面借着行你的旨意而造出的生命——之外，再无生命；这生命就是人的光。人的生命是借着那光生的——在他们里面的，与那首先在耶稣里面进入存在的，是同一个生命。他怎样舍去他的生命，人也必须这样舍去他们的生命，好叫他们像他活着那样，也得以活着。那在他里面受造的是生命，这生命就是人的光；然而他自己的、就是他被差到他们那里去的那些人，却*不信他*。

### The Knowing of the Son / 认识子
===Original===

> Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you; for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.

===Chinese===

> 你们从来没有听见他的声音，也没有看见他的形像。你们并没有他的道存在心里，因为他所差来的，你们不信。

===Original===

We shall know one day just how near we come in the New Testament to the very words of the Lord. That we have them with a difference, I cannot doubt. For one thing, I do not believe he spoke in Greek. He was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and would speak their natural language, not that which, at best, they knew in secondary fashion. That the thoughts of God would come out of the heart of Jesus in anything but the mother-tongue of the simple men to whom he spoke, I cannot think. He may perhaps have spoken to the Jews of Jerusalem in Greek, for they were less simple; but at present I do not see ground to believe he did.
Again, are we bound to believe that John Boanerges, who indeed best, and in some things alone, understood him, was able, after such a lapse of years, to give us in his gospel, supposing the Lord to have spoken to his disciples in Greek, the *very* words in which he uttered the simplest profundities ever heard in the human world? I do not say he was not able; I say﻿—Are we bound to believe he was able? When the disciples became, by the divine presence in their hearts, capable of understanding the Lord, they remembered things he had said which they had forgotten; possibly the very words in which he said them returned to their memories; but must we believe the evangelists always precisely recorded his words? The little differences between their records is answer enough. The gospel of John is the outcome of years and years of remembering, recalling, and pondering the words of the Master, one thing understood recalling another. We cannot tell of how much the memory, in best condition﻿—that is, with God in the man﻿—may not be capable; but I do not believe that John would have always given us the very words of the Lord, even if, as I do not think he did, he had spoken them in Greek. God has not cared that we should anywhere have assurance of his very words; and that not merely, perhaps, because of the tendency in his children to word-worship, false logic, and corruption of the truth, but because he would not have them oppressed by words, seeing that words, being human, therefore but partially capable, could not absolutely contain or express what the Lord meant, and that even he must depend for being understood upon the spirit of his disciple.

===Chinese===

有一天我们终会知道，新约里的话与主亲口所说的究竟相差多近。至于我们所得到的话是有所不同的，这一点我不能怀疑。其一，我不相信他用希腊话讲论。他奉差遣到以色列家迷失的羊（the lost sheep）那里去，必说他们本乡的语言，而不会说那种他们至多只有二手认识的语言。神的诸般思想从耶稣心里发出时，竟不用那些单纯之人的母语——我不能这样想。对耶路撒冷的犹太人，他或可用希腊话讲论，因为他们不那么单纯；但目前我看不出有什么根据相信他这样做了。
再者，设若主确曾用希腊话对门徒讲论，我们是否有义务相信，那位实在最了解主、在某些事上更是唯独他才了解主的半尼其约翰，在多年之后，能在他的福音书里把那些话一字不差（very）地给我们——他所说出的、人类世界从未听过的最单纯而深邃的话？我不是说他不能；我是说——我们是否有义务相信他能？当门徒因神在他们心里的临在而能够明白主时，他们记起了自己曾忘却的主所说的话；那些话本来的字句也可能回到他们记忆里；但我们是否必须相信福音书作者们总是精确记录了他的话？他们记录之间的小差异，就是足够的回答。约翰福音乃是年复一年记着、回想、思量主的话的成果，明白了一件事，又勾起另一件。处在最佳状态的记忆——也就是有神内住的人的记忆——其能力大到什么地步，我们无法断言；但我不相信约翰总会把主的字句原原本本给我们，即便主真曾用希腊话说出——其实我不认为如此。神并没有打算让我们在任何地方对他的确切字句有绝对的把握；这或许不仅因为他的儿女有拜字句、假逻辑、败坏真理的倾向，更因为他不愿他们被字句压伤——要知道，字句既是属人的，能力便有限，断不能绝对包容或表达主的意思；就连主自己，要被人明白，也须倚赖门徒的灵。

===Original===

Seeing it could not give life, the letter should not be throned with power to kill; it should be but the handmaid to open the door of the truth to the mind that was *of* the truth.
“Then you believe in an individual inspiration to anyone who chooses to lay claim to it!”
Yes﻿—to everyone who claims it from God; not to everyone who claims from men the recognition of his possessing it. He who has a thing, does not need to have it recognized. If I did not believe in a special inspiration to every man who asks for the holy spirit, the good thing of God, I should have to throw aside the whole tale as an imposture; for the Lord has, according to that tale, promised such inspiration to those who ask it. If an objector has not this spirit, is not inspired with the truth, he knows nothing of the words that are spirit and life; and his objection is less worth heeding than that of a savage to the assertion of a chemist. His assent equally is but the blowing of an idle horn.
“But how is one to tell whether it be in truth the spirit of God that is speaking in a man?”
You are not called upon to tell. The question for you is whether you have the spirit of Christ yourself. The question is for you to put to yourself, the question is for you to answer to yourself: Am I alive with the life of Christ? Is his spirit dwelling in me? Everyone who desires to follow the Master has the spirit of the Master, and will receive more, that he may follow closer, nearer, in his very footsteps. He is not called upon to prove to this or that or any man that he has the light of Jesus; he has to let his light shine. It does not follow that his work is to teach others, or that he is able to speak large truths in true forms. When the strength or the joy or the pity of the truth urges him, let him speak it out and not be afraid﻿—content to be condemned for it; comforted that if he mistake, the Lord himself will condemn him, and save him “as by fire.” The condemnation of his fellow men will not hurt him, nor a whit the more that it be spoken in the name of Christ. If he speak true, the Lord will say “I sent him.” For all truth is of him; no man can see a true thing to be true but by the Lord, the spirit.
“How am I to know that a thing is true?”
By *doing* what you know to be true, and calling nothing true until you see it to be true; by shutting your mouth until the truth opens it.

===Chinese===

字句既不能赐人生命，就不该被高抬上宝座、得着杀戮的权柄；它只该作一个婢女，为那属（of）真理的心思打开真理的门。
「那么你是相信，谁愿意自称有个人默示，谁就有默示了！」
是的——对每一个向神求这默示的人是如此；对每一个只是向人求承认、说自己拥有它的人则不然。真正拥有一样东西的人，不需要别人承认他拥有。我若不信每一个求圣灵——神的美物——的人都能得着特别的默示，我就只得把整卷记载当作骗局抛开；因为按那记载，主已应许凡求这默示的必得着。反对者若没有这灵，未受真理的默示，他对那些是灵是生命的话便一无所知；他的反对还比不上一个野蛮人反对化学家的论断来得值得理会。他的赞同同样不过是空吹号角。
「可是，人如何分辨那在人里面说话的，究竟是不是神的灵呢？」
你没有受召去分辨。你的问题是：你自己有没有基督的灵。这问题该由你问自己，该由你自己回答：我身上活着的是基督的生命吗？他的灵住在我里面吗？凡渴望跟从主的，就有主的灵，还要领受更多，好叫他跟得更紧、更近，行在主的脚踪里。他不必向这个人、那个人或任何人证明自己有耶稣的光；他只要让他的光照耀。这并不必然意味着他的工作是教导人，也不意味着他能用恰当的形式讲论宏大的真理。当真理的力量、喜乐或怜悯催促他时，就让他说出来，不要惧怕——甘心为之被定罪；并得安慰，因为他若有错，主自己必责备他，又「如同从火中经过」一样地救他。世人的定罪伤害不了他，哪怕那定罪是奉基督的名发出的，也分毫不能多伤他。他若说的是真的，主必说：「是我差他去的。」因为一切真理都出于他；人若非借着主——就是那灵——就不能看见真实之事为真。
「我怎么知道一件事是真的？」
借着行（doing）你所知道为真的事，在你看见一件事为真之前不称之为真；借着闭住你的口，直到真理开启它。

===Original===

Are you meant to be silent? Then woe to you if you speak.
“But if I do not take the words attributed to him by the evangelists, for the certain, absolute, very words of the Master, how am I to know that they represent his truth?”
By seeing in them what corresponds to the plainest truth he speaks, and commends itself to the power that is working in you to make of you a true man; by their appeal to your power of judging what is true; by their rousing of your conscience. If they do not seem to you true, either they are not the words of the Master, or you are not true enough to understand them. Be certain of this, that, if any words that are his do not show their truth to you, you have not received his message in them; they are not yet to you the word of God, for they are not in you spirit and life. They may be the nearest to the truth that words can come; they may have served to bring many into contact with the heart of God; but for you they remain as yet sealed. If yours be a true heart, it will revere them because of the probability that they are words with the meaning of the Master behind them; to you they are the rock in the desert before Moses spoke to it. If you wait, your ignorance will not hurt you; if you presume to reason from them, you are a blind man disputing of that you never saw. To reason from a thing not understood, is to walk straight into the mire. To dare to reason of truth from words that do not show to us that they are true, is the presumption of Pharisaical hypocrisy. Only they who are not true, are capable of doing it. Humble mistake will not hurt us: the truth is there, and the Lord will see that we come to know it. We may think we know it when we have scarce a glimpse of it; but the error of a true heart will not be allowed to ruin it. Certainly that heart would not have mistaken the truth except for the untruth yet remaining in it; but he who casts out devils will cast out that devil.
In the saying before us, I see enough to enable me to believe that its words embody the mind of Christ. If I could not say this, I should say, “The apostle has here put on record a saying of Christ’s; I have not yet been able to recognise the mind of Christ in it; therefore I conclude that I cannot have understood it, for to understand what is true is to know it true.”

===Chinese===

你本该缄默吗？那么你说话就有祸了。
「可若我不把福音书作者归于他的话当作主的确定的、绝对的、一字不差的话，我又怎么知道它们代表他的真理呢？」
借着在其中看见与他说过的最浅明的真理相合的东西，并看见它们与那正在你里面动工、要使你成为真实之人的能力相契；借着它们诉诸你判断真伪的能力；借着它们唤醒你的良心。它们若在你看来不真，那么或是它们不是主的话，或是你不够真，还不能明白它们。你要确知这一点：若任何属他的话没有向你显明其真，你就还没有在其中领受他的信息；对你而言它们还不是神的道，因为它们在你里面还不是灵，还不是生命。它们也许已是字句所能最接近真理的地步；也许已使许多人接触到神的心；但对你，它们仍是封着的。你的心若真实，就会因它们背后多半藏着主的意义而敬重它们；对你，它们如今还是旷野中那块摩西（Moses）未曾吩咐以前的磐石。你若等候，你的无知便伤害不了你；你若妄自据之推理，便是瞎子争论自己从未见过的事物。从未明白之事推演道理，就是径直走进泥沼。竟敢从并未向我们显明为真的字句推论真理，是法利赛式伪善的僭妄。唯有不真的人做得出这种事。谦卑的错失伤害不了我们：真理就在那里，主必使我们终能认识它。我们也许才瞥见一眼就以为认识了它；但真实之心的错谬，不会被容许毁掉它。那颗心若不是因为里面还残留的不真，本不会错认真理；而那位赶鬼的，也必赶出这一个鬼。
在我们面前的这句话里，我所看见的已足够使我相信，其中字句负载着基督的心意。我若说不出这话，就该说：「使徒在这里记下了基督的一句话；我还没能在其中认出基督的心意；所以我断定我必是没有明白它，因为明白真实之事，就是知道它为真。」

===Original===

I have yet seen no words credibly reported as the words of Jesus, concerning which I dared to say, “His mind is not therein, therefore the words are not his.” The mind of man can receive any word only in proportion as it is the word of Christ, and in proportion as he is one with Christ. To him who does verily receive his word, it is a power, not of argument, but of life. The words of the Lord are not for the logic that deals with words as if they were things; but for the spiritual logic that reasons from divine thought to divine thought, dealing with spiritual facts.
No thought, human or divine, can be conveyed from man to man save through the symbolism of the creation. The heavens and the earth are around us that it may be possible for us to speak of the unseen by the seen; for the outermost husk of creation has correspondence with the deepest things of the Creator. He is not a God that hideth himself, but a God who made that he might reveal; he is consistent and one throughout. There are things with which an enemy hath meddled; but there are more things with which no enemy could meddle, and by which we may speak of God. They may not have revealed him to us, but at least when he is revealed, they show themselves so much of his nature, that we at once use them as spiritual tokens in the commerce of the spirit, to help convey to other minds what we may have seen of the unseen. Belonging to this sort of mediation are the words of the Lord I would now look into.
“And the Father himself which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.”
If Jesus said these words, he meant more, not less, than lies on their surface. They cannot be mere assertion of what everybody knew; neither can their repetition of similar negations be tautological. They were not intended to inform the Jews of a fact they would not have dreamed of denying. Who among them would say he had ever heard God’s voice, or seen his shape? John himself says “No man hath seen God at any time.” What is the tone of the passage? It is reproach. Then he reproaches them that they had not seen God, when no man hath seen God at any time, and Paul says no man can see him! Is there here any paradox?

===Chinese===

至今我还没有见过哪一段可靠地传为耶稣之言的话，是我敢说「其中没有他的心意，所以这话不是他的」。人的心只能按那话是基督的话的程度、按他与基督合一的程度来领受任何一句话。对那真正领受他之道的人，那道是一种能力——不是论证的能力，而是生命的能力。主的话不是为那种把字句当作实物来处理的逻辑预备的，而是为那属灵的逻辑预备的——它从神圣的思想推想到神圣的思想，处理属灵的事实。
任何思想，无论是人的还是神的，都不能不借着受造之物的象征从一人传给另一人。天地环绕我们，为的是我们可以借着可见的讲说那不可见的；因为受造之物最外层的皮壳，也与创造者最深处的东西相应。他不是一位自隐的神，而是一位为要启示而创造的神；他前后一贯，始终如一。有些事物曾被仇敌染指；但更多的事物是仇敌无从染指的，我们可以借着它们讲说神。它们也许不曾向我们启示他；但至少当他被启示出来时，它们显出自己与他性情的那么多相通之处，以致我们立刻用它们作属灵交往中的属灵记号，帮助我们把自己所见的那不可见的传给别人。我现在要查考的主的话，正属于这类居间之物。
「差我来的父（the Father）也为我作过见证。你们从来没有听见他的声音，也没有看见他的形像。你们并没有他的道存在心里，因为他所差来的，你们不信。」
耶稣若说过这些话，他所指的必比字面更多，而不是更少。它们不可能只是陈述人人皆知之事；其中相似否定句的重复也不可能是重复废话。它们不是要告诉犹太人一件他们做梦也不会否认的事实。他们中间谁会说自己是听过神的声音、见过他的形像的呢？约翰自己就说「从来没有人看见过神」。这段话的语气是什么？是责备。那么他责备他们没有见过神——可是从来没有人看见过神，保罗又说没有人能看见他！这里有悖论吗？

===Original===

There cannot be the sophism: “No man hath seen God; ye are to blame that ye have not seen God; therefore all men are to blame that they have not seen God!” If we read, “No man hath seen God, but some men ought to have seen him,” we do not reap such hope for the race as will give the aspect of a revelation to the assurance that not one of those capable of seeing him has ever seen him!
The one utterance is of John; the other of his master: if there is any contradiction between them, of course the words of John must be thrown away. But there can hardly be contradiction, since he who says the one thing, is recorder of the other as said by his master, him to whom he belonged, whose disciple he was, whom he loved as never man loved man before.
The word “see” is used in one sense in the one statement, and in another sense in the other. In the one it means “see with the eyes”; in the other, “with the soul.” The one statement is made of all men; the other is made to certain of the Jews of Jerusalem concerning themselves. It is true that no man hath seen God, and true that some men ought to have seen him. No man hath seen him with his bodily eyes; these Jews ought to have seen him with their spiritual eyes.
No man has ever seen God in any outward, visible, close-fitting form of his own: he is revealed in no shape save that of his son. But multitudes of men have with their mind’s, or rather their heart’s eye, seen more or less of God; and perhaps every man might have and ought to have seen something of him. We cannot follow God into his infinitesimal intensities of spiritual operation, any more than into the atomic life-potencies that lie deep beyond the eye of the microscope: God may be working in the heart of a savage, in a way that no wisdom of his wisest, humblest child can see, or imagine that it sees. Many who have never beheld the face of God, may yet have caught a glimpse of the hem of his garment; many who have never seen his shape, may yet have seen the vastness of his shadow; thousands who have never felt the warmth of its folds, have yet been startled by

> No face: only the sight

Of a sweepy garment vast and white.

===Chinese===

不可能有这样的诡辩：「没有人看见过神；你们没有见过神，是你们的罪；所以一切人没有见过神，都是一切人的罪！」我们若读作「没有人看见过神，但有些人本该看见他」，那么对「凡有见神之能的，竟无一人曾见过他」这断言，我们便得不着那样的盼望——能叫这断言显出启示气象的盼望。
一句话出于约翰，另一句出于他的主：两者若有矛盾，当然该丢弃的是约翰的话。但几乎不可能有矛盾，因为说其中一句的，正是另一句的记录者——把它记为主所说的，那主是他所属的、他是其门徒的、他爱之如世人从未爱过人的。
「看见」一词在两句话中意义不同。一处指「用眼睛看」；另一处指「用灵魂看」。一句话论到一切人；另一句是对耶路撒冷的某些犹太人、论到他们自己说的。从来没有人看见过神，这是真的；有些人本该看见他，也是真的。没有人用肉眼见过他；这些犹太人本该用属灵的眼睛看见他。
从来没有人见过神以任何属于他自己的外在、可见、贴切的形式：除了他儿子的形像，他不以任何形状启示自己。但无数人曾以心智之眼——毋宁说心灵之眼——或多或少看见过神；或许每一个人都可能、也应该见过他的某些方面。我们不能跟随神进入他属灵运作那极微的深处，正如不能进入显微镜视野之外深处的原子生命潜能：神也许正在一个野蛮人心里动工，其方式连他最智慧、最谦卑的儿女的智慧也看不见，或自以为看见。许多人从未见过神的面，却或许警见过他衣裳的繸子；许多人从未见过他的形状，却或许见过他那影子之浩大；成千上万从未感受过那衣褶温暖的人，却曾被这景象惊动：

Some have dreamed his hand laid upon them, who never knew themselves gathered to his bosom. The reproach in the words of the Lord is the reproach of men who ought to have had an experience they had not had. Let us look a little nearer at his words.
“Ye have not heard his voice at any time,” might mean, “Ye have never listened to his voice,” or “Ye have never obeyed his voice” but the following phrase, “nor seen his shape,” keeps us rather to the primary sense of the word “hear”: “The sound of his voice is unknown to you”; “You have never heard his voice so as to know it for his.” “You have not seen his shape”;﻿—“You do not know what he is like.” Plainly he implies, “You ought to know his voice; you ought to know what he is like.” “You have not his word abiding in you”;﻿—“The word that is in you from the beginning, the word of God in your conscience, you have not kept with you, it is not dwelling in you; by yourselves accepted as the witness of Moses, the scripture in which you think you have eternal life does not abide with you, is not at home in you. It comes to you and goes from you. You hear, heed not, and forget. You do not dwell with it, and brood upon it, and obey it. It finds no acquaintance in you. You are not of its kind. You are not of those to whom the word of God comes. Their ears are ready to hear; they hunger after the word of the Father.”
On what does the Lord found this his accusation of them? What is the sign in them of their ignorance of God?﻿—“For whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.”
“How so?” the Jews might answer. “Have we not asked from thee a sign from heaven, and hast thou not pointblank refused it?”
The argument of the Lord was indeed of small weight with, and of little use to, those to whom it most applied, for the more it applied, the more incapable were they of seeing that it did apply; but it would be of great force upon some that stood listening, their minds more or less open to the truth, and their hearts drawn to the man before them. His argument was this: “If ye had ever heard the Father’s voice; if ye had ever known his call; if you had ever imagined him, or a God anything like him; if you had cared for his will so that his word was at home in your hearts, you would have known me when you saw me﻿—known that I must come from him, that I must be his messenger, and would have listened to me.

主的论证，对于那些最适用的人，分量实在微小、用处实在有限；因为越是适用于他们，他们越看不见它适用；但对站在旁边听的另一些人——他们的心思多少向真理敞开，他们的心被面前这位吸引——这论证必大有力量。他的论证是这样的：「你们若曾听过父的声音；若曾认识他的呼召；若曾想象过他、或任何与他略略相似的神；若曾顾念他的旨意，以致他的道在你们心里安了家，你们看见我的时候就必认得我——知道我必是从他那里来的，必是他的使者，也必听我。

The least acquaintance with God, such as any true heart must have, would have made you recognize that I came from the God of whom you knew that something. You would have been capable of knowing me by the light of his word abiding in you; by the shape you had beheld however vaguely; by the likeness of my face and my voice to those of my father. You would have seen my father in me; you would have known me by the little you knew of him. The family-feeling would have been awake in you, the holy instinct of the same spirit, making you know your elder brother. That you do not know me now, as I stand here speaking to you, is that you do not know your own father, even my father; that throughout your lives you have refused to do his will, and so have not heard his voice; that you have shut your eyes from seeing him, and have thought of him only as a partisan of your ambitions. If you had loved my father, you would have known his son.” And I think he might have said, “If even you had loved your neighbour, you would have known me, neighbour to the deepest and best in you.” If the Lord were to appear this day in England as once in Palestine, he would not come in the halo of the painters, or with that wintry shine of effeminate beauty, of sweet weakness, in which it is their helpless custom to represent him. Neither would he probably come as carpenter, or mason, or gardener. He would come in such form and condition as might bear to the present England, Scotland, and Ireland, a relation like that which the form and condition he then came in, bore to the motley Judea, Samaria, and Galilee. If he came thus, in form altogether unlooked for, who would they be that recognized and received him? The idea involves no absurdity. He is not far from us at any moment﻿—if the old story be indeed more than the best and strongest of the fables that possess the world. He might at any moment appear: who, I ask, would be the first to receive him? Now, as then, it would of course be the childlike in heart, the truest, the least selfish. They would not be the highest in the estimation of any church, for the childlike are not yet the many. It might not even be those that knew most about the former visit of the Master, that had pondered every word of the Greek Testament. The first to cry, “It is the Lord!” would be neither “good churchman” nor “good dissenter.”

主若今日在英国显现，像当年在巴勒斯坦那样，他必不会带着画家们画出的光环来，也不会带着那种女性之美的冷辉、甜弱的柔光来——那是画家们无能为力地惯于描绘他的样子。他多半也不会以木匠、石匠或园丁的样子来。他会以这样的形状和境况来到，使它对今日的英格兰、苏格兰和爱尔兰，正如他当年所取的形状和境况对那五方杂处的犹太、撒马利亚和加利利一样。他若这样来临，形状全然出人意表，那些认出他、接待他的，会是谁呢？这想法并无荒谬之处。他无时无刻不离我们不远——倘若那古老的故事确实不只是占据着世界的最好、最有力量的传说。他随时可能显现：我问，谁会最先接待他？如今一如当年，当然会是那些心里像小孩子的人、最真实的人、最不自私的人。他们不会是任何教会评价中最高的那些人，因为像小孩子的还不是多数。甚至未必是那些对主上一次降临知道得最多、把希腊文新约的每个字都揣摩过的人。最先喊出「是主！」的，既不会是「好国教徒」，也不会是「好非国教徒」。

It would be no one with so little of the mind of Christ as to imagine him caring about stupid outside matters. It would not be the man that holds by the mooring-ring of the letter, fast in the quay of what he calls theology, and from his rotting deck abuses the presumption of those that go down to the sea in ships﻿—lets the wind of the spirit blow where it listeth, but never blow him out among its wonders in the deep. It would not be he who, obeying a command, does not care to see reason in the command; not he who, from very barrenness of soul, cannot receive the meaning and will of the Master, and so fails to fulfil the letter of his word, making it of none effect. It would certainly, if any, be those who were likest the Master﻿—those, namely, that did the will of their father and his father, that built their house on the rock by hearing and doing his sayings. But are there any enough like him to know him at once by the sound of his voice, by the look of his face? There are multitudes who would at once be taken by a false Christ fashioned after their fancy, and would at once reject the Lord as a poor impostor. One thing is certain: they who first recognized him would be those that most loved righteousness and hated iniquity.
But I would not forget that there are many in whom foolish forms cover a live heart, warm toward everything human and divine; for the worst-fitting and ugliest robe may hide the loveliest form. Every covering is not a clothing. The grass clothes the fields; the glory surpassing Solomon’s clothes the grass; but the traditions of the worthiest elders will not clothe any soul﻿—how much less the traditions of the unworthy! Its true clothing must grow out of the live soul itself. Some naked souls need but the sight of truth to rush to it, as Dante says, like a wild beast to his den; others, heavily clad in the garments the scribes have left behind them, and fearful of rending that which is fit only to be trodden underfoot, right cautiously approach the truth, go round and round it like a shy horse that fears a hidden enemy. But let each be true after the fashion possible to him, and he shall have the Master’s praise.

===Original===

We may see from this passage how the apostle Paul received the Lord, and how he understands his life to be the light of men, and so their life also.
Of all writers I know, Paul seems to me the most plainly, the most determinedly practical in his writing. What has been called his mysticism is at one time the exercise of a power of seeing, as by spiritual refraction, truths that had not, perhaps have not yet, risen above the human horizon; at another, the result of a wide-eyed habit of noting the analogies and correspondences between the concentric regions of creation; it is the working of a poetic imagination divinely alive, whose part is to foresee and welcome approaching truth; to discover the same principle in things that look unlike; to embody things discovered, in forms and symbols heretofore unused, and so present to other minds the deeper truths to which those forms and symbols owe their being.
I find in Paul’s writing the same artistic fault, with the same resulting difficulty, that I find in Shakespeare’s﻿—a fault that, in each case, springs from the admirable fact that the man is much more than the artist﻿—the fault of trying to say too much at once, of pouring out stintless the plethora of a soul swelling with life and its thought, through the too narrow neck of human utterance. Thence it comes that we are at times bewildered between two or more meanings, equally good in themselves, but perplexing as to the right deduction, as to the line of the thinker’s reasoning. The uncertainty, however, lies always in the intellectual region, never in the practical. What Paul cares about is plain enough to the true heart, however far from plain to the man whose desire to understand goes ahead of his obedience, who starts with the notion that Paul’s design was to teach a system, to explain instead of help to see God, a God that can be revealed only to childlike insight, never to keenest intellect. The energy of the apostle, like that of his master, went forth to rouse men to seek the kingdom of God over them, his righteousness in them; to dismiss the lust of possession and passing pleasure; to look upon the glory of the God and Father, and turn to him from all that he hates; to recognize the brotherhood of men, and the hideousness of what is unfair, unloving, and self-exalting.

===Chinese===

从这段经文我们可以看出，使徒保罗是怎样领受主的，以及他怎样理解主的生命就是人的光、因而也是人的生命。

在我认识的一切作者中，保罗在我看来是最直截了当、最坚定务实的一个。他那被人称作神秘主义的东西，有时是一种看见之能的运用——如同借着属灵的折射，看见那些尚未、也许至今仍未升上人类地平线的真理；有时则是那睁大眼睛留意创造之层层同心区域之间的类比与对应的习惯的结果；那是一种神圣地活着的诗性想象力的运作，它的职分是预见并迎接正临近的真理，是在看似不同的事物中发现同一个原理，是把所发现的装进前所未用的形式与象征里，从而把那些形式与象征所由来的更深真理，呈现在别人心里。

我在保罗的写作中发现的那个艺术上的毛病、以及随之而来的难处，与我在莎士比亚（Shakespeare）那里发现的一样——这毛病，在两人身上，都源自一个可敬佩的事实：这人远远不止是艺术家——那毛病是想一口气说太多，是把一个因生命及其思想而胀满的心灵的过剩，不知节制地倾倒出来，倒过人这条过窄的话语瓶颈。由此，我们有时会在两种或更多的含义之间无所适从；那些含义各自都好，却叫人难以断定该作怎样的推论、难以摸清思想者的思路。然而，这不确定总在智性一面，从不在实行一面。保罗所关心的，对真实的心而言够明白的了；但对那种想明白的欲望跑在顺服（obedience）前头的人——那种以为保罗的目的是要传授一套体系、是要解释神（God）而不是帮助人看见神的人——却远不明朗；这神只能向孩子式的洞察显明，从不向最锐利的智性显明。这位使徒的精力，像他主的精力一样，是用来唤醒人去寻求神的国（the kingdom）在他们之上、神的义（righteousness）在他们之内；去抛弃占有欲和转眼即逝的享乐；去仰望神就是父的荣光，从他一切所恨的事上转回向他；去认出人的弟兄之谊，认出不公、无爱、自高之事的丑恶。
