His design was not to teach any plan of salvation other than obedience to the Lord of Life. He knew nothing of the so-called Christian systems that change the glory of the perfect God into the likeness of the low intellects and dull consciences of men﻿—a worse corruption than the representing of him in human shape. What kind of soul is it that would not choose the Apollo of light, the high-walking Hyperion, to the notion of the dull, self-cherishing monarch, the law-dispensing magistrate, or the cruel martinet, generated in the pagan arrogance of Rome, and accepted by the world in the church as the portrait of its God! Jesus Christ is the *only* likeness of the living Father.
Let us see then what Paul teaches us in this passage about the life which is the light of men. It is his form of bringing to bear upon men the truth announced by John.
When Moses came out from speaking with God, his face was radiant; its shining was a wonder to the people, and a power upon them. But the radiance began at once to diminish and die away, as was natural, for it was not indigenous in Moses. Therefore Moses put a veil upon his face that they might not see it fade. As to whether this was right or wise, opinion may differ: it is not my business to discuss the question. When he went again into the tabernacle, he took off his veil, talked with God with open face, and again put on the veil when he came out. Paul says that the veil which obscured the face of Moses lies now upon the hearts of the Jews, so that they cannot understand him, but that when they turn to the Lord, go into the tabernacle with Moses, the veil shall be taken away, and they shall see God. Then will they understand that the glory is indeed faded upon the face of Moses, but by reason of the glory that excelleth, the glory of Jesus that overshines it. Here, after all, I can hardly help asking﻿—Would not Moses have done better to let them see that the glory of their leader was altogether dependent on the glory within the veil, whither they were not worthy to enter? Did that veil hide Moses’s face only? Did he not, however unintentionally, lay it on their hearts? Did it not cling there, and help to hide God from them, so that they could not perceive that the greater than Moses was come, and stormed at the idea that the glory of their prophet must yield?

===Chinese===

他的目的不是要传授任何别的救恩方案，除了对生命之主的顺服。他对那些所谓基督教体系一无所知——那些体系把完全之神的荣耀，变作人低微的智性与迟钝的良心的样式——那比用人的形像来表现他更是败坏。什么样的灵魂，会不选光明的阿波罗、那高视阔步的许佩里翁，反倒取那沉闷而自我眷顾的君主、那分派律法的执法官、或那残忍的酷吏呢——那形像是在罗马的异教傲慢中生出来的，又被教会里的世界当作它神的肖像领受下来！耶稣基督是永活之父（the Father）*唯一*的形像。

那么，让我们看看保罗在这段经文里，关于那作为人之光的生命，教导了我们什么。这是他以自己的方式，把约翰所宣告的真理施行到人身上。

当摩西（Moses）与神说完话出来，他的脸发光；那光辉对百姓是奇事，也是临到他们身上的能力。但那光辉立刻就开始消退、衰残，这也自然，因为它并非摩西里面生来就有的。于是摩西用帕子蒙上脸，免得他们看见它消退。至于这做得对不对、明智不明智，见仁见智：这不是我要讨论的问题。他再进会幕时，就揭去帕子，敞着脸与神说话；出来时又蒙上帕子。保罗说，那蒙蔽摩西脸的帕子，如今蒙在犹太人的心上，使他们认不出他来；但当他们转向主、与摩西一同进入会幕时，那帕子就必除去，他们就必看见神。那时他们就必明白：摩西脸上的荣耀果真是褪去了，但那是为了那更大的荣耀——那盖过它的耶稣的荣耀。说到这里，我终究忍不住要问——摩西若让他们看见，他们领袖的荣耀全然系于帕子以内、他们不配进入之处的荣耀，岂不更好？那帕子只遮蔽了摩西的脸吗？他岂不是——虽出于无心——把它盖在了他们的心上？它岂不是贴在那里，帮着把神向他们隐藏，以致他们认不出那比摩西更大的已经来了，并且一听说他们先知的荣耀必须让位，就大大发怒？

===Original===

Might not the absence of that veil from his face have left them a little more able to realize that his glory was a glory that must pass, a glory whose glory was that it prepared the way for a glory that must extinguish it? Moses had put the veil forever from his face, but they clutched it to their hearts, and it blinded them﻿—admirable symbol of the wilful blindness of old Mosaist or modern Wesleyan, admitting no light that his Moses or his Wesley did not see, and thus losing what of the light he saw and reflected.
Paul says that the sight of the Lord will take that veil from their hearts. His light will burn it away. His presence gives liberty. Where he is, there is no more heaviness, no more bondage, no more wilderness or Mount Sinai. The Son makes free with sonship.
And now comes the passage whose import I desire to make more clear:
“But we all,” having this presence and this liberty, “with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image,” that of the Lord, “from glory to glory, even as of the Lord, the spirit.”
“We need no Moses, no earthly mediator, to come between us and the light, and bring out for us a little of the glory. We go into the presence of the Son revealing the Father﻿—into the presence of the Light of men. Our mediator is the Lord himself, the spirit of light, a mediator not sent by us to God to bring back his will, but come from God to bring us himself. We enter, like Moses, into the presence of the visible, radiant God﻿—only how much more visible, more radiant! As Moses stood with uncovered face receiving the glory of God full upon it, so with open, with uncovered face, full in the light of the glory of God, in the place of his presence, stand we﻿—you and I, Corinthians. It is no reflected light we see, but the glory of God shining *in*, shining out of, shining in and from the face of Christ, the glory of the Father, one with the Son. Israel saw but the fading reflection of the glory of God on the face of Moses; we see the glory itself in the face of Jesus.”
But in what follows, it seems to me that the revised version misses the meaning almost as much as the authorized, when, instead of “beholding as in a glass,” it gives “reflecting as a mirror.” The former is wrong; the latter is far from right. The idea, with the figure, is that of a poet, not a man of science.

===Chinese===

若他脸上没有那帕子，岂不会让他们多明白一点：他的荣耀原是必要过去的荣耀，那荣耀的荣耀，正在于它为那必盖灭它的荣耀开路？摩西已把那帕子从脸上永远挪去了，他们却把它死死抓在心上，它就叫他们瞎了眼——这是旧的摩西派或现代卫斯理派甘心瞎眼的绝妙象征：凡他的摩西或他的卫斯理没有看见的光，一概不认，结果连他自己所见所反照的那点光也失去了。

保罗说，见主一面，就必把那帕子从他们心上除掉。他的光必把它烧尽。他的同在带来自由。他在哪里，哪里就不再有沉重，不再有捆绑，不再有旷野或西奈山。儿子借着儿子名分使人自由。

现在来到那段我愿把它含义讲得更明白的经文：

「我们众人」——既有这同在、这自由——「敞着脸，如同在镜中观看主的荣耀，就变成同样的形像」，就是主的形像，「从荣耀到荣耀，如同出于主，就是那灵」。

「我们不再需要摩西，不需要任何地上的中保，站在我们与光之间，为我们带出一点荣耀来。我们进入那显明父之子的同在——进入人这光（the Light of men）的同在。我们的中保是主自己，就是那光之灵；这中保不是我们差到神那里去领回他旨意的，而是从神那里来、把他自己带给我们的。我们像摩西一样，进入那可见的、发光的神的同在——只是何等更加可见、更加发光！摩西敞着脸站着，让神的荣耀完完全全照在脸上；我们也这样敞着脸、不蒙脸，站在神荣耀的光中，站在他同在之处——我和你们，哥林多人啊。我们所看见的不是反照的光，而是神的荣耀在基督的脸*里面*照耀、从基督的脸照耀出来、在基督的脸里且从其中照耀——那脸就是父的荣耀，与子为一的。以色列所看见的，不过是神的荣耀在摩西脸上那正在消退的反照；我们看见的，是在耶稣脸上的荣耀本身。」

但在下文，我觉得修订译本几乎与钦定本一样失了原意：它不译作「如同在镜中观看」（beholding as in a glass），而译作「如镜子反照」（reflecting as a mirror）。前者是错的；后者也远不算对。这观念，连同这比喻，属于诗人，不属于科学家。

===Original===

The poet deals with the outer show of things, which outer show is infinitely deeper in its relation to truth, as well as more practically useful, than the analysis of the man of science. Paul never thought of the mirror as reflecting, as throwing back the rays of light from its surface; he thought of it as receiving, taking into itself, the things presented to it﻿—here, as filling its bosom with the glory it looks upon. When I see the face of my friend in a mirror, the mirror seems to hold it in itself, to surround the visage with its liquid embrace. The countenance is *there*﻿—down there in the depth of the mirror. True, it shines radiant out of it, but it is not the shining out of it that Paul has in his thought; it is the fact﻿—the *visual* fact, which, according to Wordsworth, the poet always seizes﻿—of the mirror holding in it the face.
That this is the way poet or prophet﻿—Paul was both﻿—would think of the thing, especially in the age of the apostle, I shall be able to make appear even more probable by directing your notice to the following passage from Dante﻿—whose time, though so much farther from that of the apostle than our time from Dante’s, was in many respects much liker Paul’s than ours.
The passage is this: —﻿*Dell’ Inferno*: Canto XXIII 25﻿–﻿27:

> E quei: “S’io fossi d’impiombato vetro,

L’immagine di fuor tua non trarrei

Più tosto a me, che quella dentro impetro.”

===Chinese===

诗人处理的是事物的外在显现；这外在显现，论其与真理的关系，比科学家的分析不知深了多少，在实用上也更有用处。保罗从未把镜子想成反照的、把光线从表面抛回去的东西；他把它想成领受的、把呈现在它面前的东西纳进自身的东西——在这里，就是用它所仰望的荣耀充满它的胸怀。当我在镜中看见朋友的脸，那镜子仿佛把它含在自己里面，用它的流质怀抱环住那面容。那面容就*在那里*——就在镜子的深处。不错，它是从镜子里发光照出来的；但保罗心里想的不是那照出来，而是这个事实——那*视觉的*事实（据华兹华斯说，诗人抓住的正是这个）——镜子把脸含在它里面。

诗人或先知——保罗两者都是——会这样想这件事，尤其在那使徒的时代；这一点，我可以请你们注意但丁（Dante）的下面一段，使它显得更加可信——但丁的时代，虽然离使徒的时代比我们的时代离但丁的时代远得多，在许多方面却比我们的时代更像保罗的时代。

这段话是这样的——«地狱篇»（Dell' Inferno）第二十三歌第25–27行：

> E quei: "S'io fossi d'impiombato vetro,

L'immagine di fuor tua non trarrei

Più tosto a me, che quella dentro impetro."

===Original===

Here Virgil, with reference to the power he had of reading the thoughts of his companion, says to Dante:
“If I were of leaded glass,”﻿—meaning, “If I were glass covered at the back with lead, so that I was a mirror,”﻿—“I should not draw thy outward image to me more readily than I gain thy inner one”;﻿—meaning, “than now I know your thoughts.”
It seems, then, to me, that the true simple word to represent the Greek, and the most literal as well by which to translate it, is the verb “mirror”﻿—when the sentence, so far, would run thus: “But we all, with unveiled face, mirroring the glory of the Lord﻿—.”
I must now go on to unfold the idea at work in the heart of the apostle. For the mere correctness of a translation is nothing, except it bring us something deeper, or at least some fresher insight: with him who cares for the words apart from what the writer meant them to convey, I have nothing to do: he must cease to “pass for a man” and begin to be a man indeed, on the way to be a live soul, before I can desire his intercourse. The prophet-apostle seems to me, then, to say, “We all, with clear vision of the Lord, mirroring in our hearts his glory, even as a mirror would take into itself his face, are thereby changed into his likeness, his glory working our glory, by the present power, in our inmost being, of the Lord, the spirit.” Our mirroring of Christ, then, is one with the presence of his spirit in us. The idea, you see, is not the reflection, the radiating of the light of Christ on others, though that were a figure lawful enough; but the taking into, and having in us, him working to the changing of us.
That the thing signified transcends the sign, outreaches the figure, is no discovery; the thing figured always belongs to a higher stratum, to which the simile serves but as a ladder; when the climber has reached it, “he then unto the ladder turns his back.” It is but according to the law of symbol, that the thing symbolized by the mirror should have properties far beyond those of leaded glass or polished metal, seeing it is a live soul understanding that which it takes into its deeps﻿—holding it, and conscious of what it holds. It mirrors by its will to hold in its mirror.

===Chinese===

这里，维吉尔针对自己能读出同伴心思的能力，对但丁说：

「若我是镀铅的玻璃」——意思是说，「若我是背面镀了铅的玻璃，成了一面镜子」——「我便不会把你外面的形像拉向我，比我现在得着你里面的形像更快」；——意思是说，「比我现在知道你的心思更快」。

这样看来，在我看来，那真而简的、能代表这希腊文的词，也是最贴近的字面译法，就是动词「如镜映照」——如此，这句话到此处便成了这样：「但我们众人，既然敞着脸，如镜映照主的荣耀——」。

现在我必须进而展开那在使徒心中运行的观念。因为译文的仅仅正确算不得什么，除非它带给我们更深的东西，或至少带来某个更新的看见：至于那种撇开作者要言语传达的意思、只关心字句的人，我与他无干：他必须不再「充作一个人」，开始真正作一个人，走在成为活灵魂的路上，我才会想与他交往。这样，这位先知使徒在我看来是说：「我们众人既清清楚楚看见主，就在心里如镜映照他的荣耀，正如镜子把他的脸纳进自身那样，便因此被改变成他的样式，他的荣耀在我们里面作成我们的荣耀——是借着主、就是那灵，此刻在我们最深处的大能。」这样，我们对基督的镜照，就与他灵在我们里面的同在合为一。你看，这观念不是反照、不是把基督的光辐射到别人身上——虽然那也是个够正当的比喻；而是把他接进来、有他在我们里面，让他在我们里面作那改变我们的工。

所表明的胜过那表明的记号、超过那比喻，这算不得什么发现；被比喻的东西总属于更高的地层，明喻不过是通到那里的一道梯子；登梯的人到了那里，「便向梯子转过背去」。照象征的定律，那由镜子象征的东西，其性质自然远远超过镀铅的玻璃或磨光的金属，因为它是一个活着的灵魂，懂得它纳入深处的东西——持守着它，并知道自己所持守的是什么。它镜照，是凭着把它持守在它镜中的意志。

===Original===

Unlike its symbol, it can hold not merely the outward visual resemblance, but the inward likeness of the person revealed by it; it is open to the influences of that which it embraces, and is capable of active cooperation with them: the mirror and the thing mirrored are of one origin and nature, and in closest relation to each other. Paul’s idea is, that when we take into our understanding, our heart, our conscience, our being, the glory of God, namely Jesus Christ as he shows himself to our eyes, our hearts, our consciences, he works upon us, and will keep working, till we are changed to the very likeness we have thus mirrored in us; for with his likeness he comes himself, and dwells in us. He will work until the same likeness is wrought out and perfected in us, the image, namely, of the humanity of God, in which image we were made at first, but which could never be developed in us except by the indwelling of the perfect likeness. By the power of Christ thus received and at home in us, we are changed﻿—the glory in him becoming glory in us, his glory changing us to glory.
But we must beware of receiving this or any symbol “after the flesh,” beware of interpreting it in any fashion that partakes of the character of the mere physical, psychical, or spirituo-mechanical. The symbol deals with things far beyond the deepest region whence symbols can be drawn. The indwelling of Jesus in the soul of man, who shall declare! But let us note this, that the dwelling of Jesus in us is the power of the spirit of God upon us; for “the Lord is that spirit,” and that Lord dwelling in us, we are changed “even as from the Lord the spirit.” When we think Christ, Christ comes; when we receive his image into our spiritual mirror, he enters with it. Our thought is not cut off from his. Our open receiving thought is his door to come in. When our hearts turn to him, that is opening the door to him, that is holding up our mirror to him; then he comes in, not by our thought only, not in our idea only, but he comes himself, and of his own will﻿—comes in as we could not take him, but as he can come and we receive him﻿—enabled to receive by his very coming the one welcome guest of the whole universe.

===Chinese===

与它的象征不同，它所能持守的不仅是外在的视像相似，更是那被显明者内在的样式；它向它所怀抱之物的感化敞开，并能与之主动地配合：镜与所镜照之物同出一源、同有一性，彼此处于最亲近的关系中。保罗的观念是：当我们把神的荣耀——就是耶稣基督，照他向我们眼睛、我们心、我们良心所显明的自己——接进我们的领悟、我们的心、我们的良心、我们的存在里，他就在我们身上作工，并且要一直作下去，直到我们被改变成我们这样镜照在心的那同一个样式；因为随着他的样式，他自己也来，住在我们里面。他要一直作工，直到同样的样式在我们里面被作成、被成全——就是神之人性的形像；我们起初就是照着那形像造的，但那形像若非借着那完全样式的内住，就永不能在我们里面发展出来。借着这样领受、又安家在我们里面的基督的大能，我们就被改变——他里面的荣耀成为我们里面的荣耀，他的荣耀把我们改变成荣耀。

但我们必须提防「按肉体」领受这个或任何象征，提防以任何带纯属物理、心理、或属灵机械性质的方式去解释它。象征所对付的，远在一切能引出象征的最深区域之外。耶稣在人灵魂里的内住，谁能述说呢！但让我们注意这一点：耶稣住在我们里面，就是神的灵在我们身上的能力；因为「主就是那灵」，而那主既住在我们里面，我们就「如同从主——就是那灵——被改变」。当我们思想基督，基督就来；当我们把他的形像接进我们属灵的镜子里，他就随着它进来。我们的思想与他的思想并不隔绝。我们敞开领受的思想，就是他进来的门。当我们的心转向他，那就是向他开门，那就是把我们的镜子举向他；于是他进来了——不只是借着我们的思想，不只是存在于我们的观念里，而是他自己来，凭他自己的意思来——照我们所不能领受的方式进来，却照他能来、我们能接待的方式进来——借着他的来临，使我们能以接待那全宇宙唯一受欢迎的宾客。

===Original===

Thus the Lord, the spirit, becomes the soul of our souls, becomes spiritually what he always was creatively; and as our spirit informs, gives shape to our bodies, in like manner his soul informs, gives shape to our souls. In this there is nothing unnatural, nothing at conflict with our being. It is but that the deeper soul that willed and wills our souls, rises up, the infinite Life, into the Self we call *I* and *me*, but which lives immediately from him, and is his very own property and nature﻿—unspeakably more his than ours: this deeper creative soul, working on and with his creation upon higher levels, makes the “I” and “me” more and more his, and himself more and more ours; until at length the glory of our existence flashes upon us, we face full to the sun that enlightens what it sent forth, and know ourselves alive with an infinite life, even the life of the Father; know that our existence is not the moonlight of a mere consciousness of being, but the sun-glory of a life justified by having become one with its origin, thinking and feeling with the primal Sun of life, from whom it was dropped away that it might know and bethink itself, and return to circle forever in exultant harmony around him. Then indeed we *are*; then indeed we have life; the life of Jesus has, through light, become life in us; the glory of God in the face of Jesus, mirrored in our hearts, has made us alive; we are one with God forever and ever.
What less than such a splendour of hope would be worthy the revelation of Jesus? Filled with the soul of their Father, men shall inherit the glory of their Father; filled with themselves, they cast him out, and rot. The company of the Lord, soul to soul, is that which saves with life, his life of God-devotion, the souls of his brethren. No other saving can save them. They must receive the Son, and through the Son the Father. What it cost the Son to get so near to us that we could say “Come in,” is the story of his life. He stands at the door and knocks, and when we open to him he comes in, and dwells with us, and we are transformed to the same image of truth and purity and heavenly childhood. Where power dwells, there is no force; where the spirit-Lord is, there is liberty.

===Chinese===

这样，主——那灵——就成了我们灵魂的灵魂；在属灵一面，他成了他在创造一面从来所是的那样；正如我们的灵赋予我们身体以形、以状，照样他的灵魂赋予我们的灵魂以形、以状。这里头没有任何不自然之处，没有任何与我们的存在相冲突之处。这不过是说：那曾愿意、并且仍愿意我们灵魂的更深灵魂，就是那无穷的生命，升上来，进入那我们称之为*我*与*自我*的自我——这自我本是直接从他而活，本是他自己的产业与性情——无可言喻地更是他的，而不是我们的：这更深的创造性灵魂，在更高的层面上作工于他的创造、也与他的创造同工，使那「我」与「自我」越来越多地成为他的，也使他自己越来越多地成为我们的；直到末了，我们存在的荣耀向我们闪耀，我们正面朝向那照亮他所放出之物的太阳，知道自己因一个无穷的生命——就是父的生命——而活着；知道我们的存在不是单单意识到存在的那种月光，而是一个生命的日头荣耀——那生命因与它的本源合一而得称为义，与生命的元阳同思同感；我们原是从那元阳脱落下来的，好叫我们能认识自己、省察自己，并回到他那里，永远在他周围欢然和谐地环绕。那时我们才真*是*；那时我们才真有生命；耶稣的生命已经借着光，成为我们里面的生命；那在耶稣脸上之神（God）的荣耀，镜照在我们心里，已经使我们活了；我们与神合一，直到永永远远。

比这更小的盼望的辉煌，哪一点配得上耶稣的启示呢？人既被他们父的灵魂充满，就必承受他们父的荣耀；若被自己充满，就把他赶出去，并且腐烂。与主同在、灵魂对灵魂的相交，才是那以生命、以他那向神奉献的生命，救他弟兄灵魂的救法。别的拯救救不了他们。他们必须领受子，并借着子领受父。子要挨近我们近到一个地步，使我们能说「请进来」，这代价是什么，那就是他一生的故事。他站在门外叩门；我们给他开门，他就进来到我们这里住，我们也就被改变成同样的形像——真理、纯洁与属天孩童的形像。大能所在之处，没有强逼；灵之主所在之处，就有自由。

===Original===

The Lord Jesus, by free, potent communion with their inmost being, will change his obedient brethren till in every thought and impulse they are good like him, unselfish, neighbourly, brotherly like him, loving the Father perfectly like him, ready to die for the truth like him, caring like him for nothing in the universe but the will of God, which is love, harmony, liberty, beauty, and joy.
I do not know if we may call this having life in ourselves; but it is the waking up, the perfecting in us of the divine life inherited from our Father in heaven, who made us in his own image, whose nature remains in us, and makes it the deepest reproach to a man that he has neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. He who would thus live must, as a mirror draws into its bosom an outward glory, receive into his “heart of heart” the inward glory of Jesus Christ, *the Truth*.

===Chinese===

主耶稣要借着他与他们最深处之存有自由而大能的相交，改变他那些顺服的弟兄，直到他们在每一个心思和冲动上，都像他那样良善，像他那样无私、亲邻、为弟兄，像他那样完全爱父，像他那样甘愿为真理死，像他那样，在这宇宙中除了神的旨意（the will of God）——就是爱、和谐、自由、美与喜乐——之外一无所求。

我不知道我们可否称这为我们自己里面有生命；但这是那从我们在天上的父承受来的神圣生命的苏醒、是我们里面这生命的成全——他用他自己的形像造我们，他的性情仍留在我们里面，而这就使一件事成为一个人最深的羞辱：他从未听见过他的声音，也从未见过他的形状。那要这样活的人，必须像镜子把外面的荣耀纳入胸怀那样，把耶稣基督——*那真理*——的内里荣耀，接进他的「心之心」里。

### The Truth / 真理
===Original===

> I am the truth.

When the man of the five senses talks of “truth,” he regards it but as a predicate of something historical or scientific proved a fact; or, if he allows that, for aught he knows, there may be higher truth, yet, as he cannot obtain proof of it from without, he acts as if under no conceivable obligation to seek any other satisfaction concerning it. Whatever appeal be made to the highest region of his nature, such a one behaves as if it were the part of a wise man to pay it no heed, because it does not come within the scope of the lower powers of that nature. According to the word of *the* man, however, truth means more than fact, more than relation of facts or persons, more than loftiest abstraction of metaphysical entity﻿—means being and life, will and action; for he says, “*I am the truth.*”
I desire to help those whom I may to understand more of what is meant by “the truth,” not for the sake of definition, or logical discrimination, but that, when they hear the word from the mouth of the Lord, the right idea may rise in their minds; that the word may neither be to them a void sound, nor call up either a vague or false notion of what he meant by it. If he says, “I am the truth,” it must, to say the least, be well to know what he means by the word with whose idea he identifies himself. And at once we may premise that he can mean nothing merely intellectual, such as may be set forth and left there; he means something vital, so vital that the whole of its necessary relations are subject to it, so vital that it includes everything else which, in any lower plane, may go or have gone by the same name. Let us endeavour to arrive at his meaning by a gently ascending stair.
A thing being so, the word that says it is so, is the truth. But the fact may be of no value in itself, and our knowledge of it of no value either. Of most facts it may be said that the truth concerning them is of no consequence. For instance, it cannot be in itself important whether on a certain morning I took one side of the street or the other. It may be of importance to someone to know which I took, but in itself it is of none. It would therefore be felt unfit if I said, “It is a *truth* that I walked on the sunny side.” The correct word would be a “fact,” not a truth.

===Chinese===

> 我就是真理。

那活在五官中的人说到「真理」时，只把它当作某个已被证明为事实的历史或科学之物的谓语；或者，他即便容许说，就他所知也许还有更高的真理，却因不能从外界得到证明，就表现得仿佛丝毫没有寻求的义务似的。无论有什么诉诸他本性最高境界的呼吁，这样的人总是表现得仿佛智者本分就是对它置之不理，因为它不属他本性中较低能力的范围。然而，照着那人（the man）的话，真理的意思却多于事实，多于事实或人物的关系，多于形而上实体最高远的抽象——它意味着存在与生命、意志与行动；因为他说：「我（I）就是真理。」
我愿意帮助我所能帮助的人，更多明白「真理」一词的意思——不为定义，不为逻辑的分辨，而是要叫他们从主口中听见这话时，心里升起正确的观念；使这话对他们既不是空洞的声音，也不唤起对他本意的模糊或错误的观念。他既说「我就是真理」，那么至少，弄清楚他用这个他所认同的观念之词是什么意思，总是好的。而且我们可以立刻预设：他所指的绝不可能是仅属理智的东西，那种可以陈述完就掠在一边的东西；他指的是某种有生命的东西，其生命力强到它的一切必然关系都从属于它，强到它包含着一切在较低层面上以这名相称或曾以这名相称的东西。让我们循着一道缓缓上升的阶梯，努力抵达他的意思。
一件事既是这样，说出它如此的话，就是真理。但那事实本身可能毫无价值，我们对它的认识也毫无价值。对大多数事实，都可以说关于它们的真理无关紧要。例如，某个早晨我走了街的这边还是那边，这本身不可能重要。某人也许需要知道我走的哪边，但事情本身无关紧要。所以若我说「我走在向阳的一边是一个真理（truth）」，就会显得不称；恰当的词是「事实」，不是真理。

===Original===

If the question arose whether a statement concerning the thing were correct, we should still be in the region of fact or no fact; but when we come to ask whether the statement was true or false, then we are concerned with the matter as the assertion of a human being, and ascend to another plane of things. It may be of no consequence which side I was upon, or it may be of consequence to someone to know which, but it is of vital importance to the witness and to any who love him, whether or not he believes the statement he makes﻿—whether the man himself is true or false. Concerning the thing it can be but a question of “fact”; it remains a question of fact even whether the man has or has not spoken the truth; but concerning the man it is a question of truth: he is either a pure soul, so far as this thing witnesses, or a false soul, capable and guilty of a lie. In this relation it is of no consequence whether the man spoke the fact or not; if he meant to speak the fact, he remains a true man.
Here I would anticipate so far as to say that there are “truths” as well as “facts,” and lies against truths as well as against facts. When the Pharisees said “Corban,” they lied against the truth that a man must honour his father and mother.
Let us go up now from the region of facts that seem casual, to those facts that are invariable, by us unchangeable, which therefore involve what we call “law.” It will be seen at once that the *fact* here is of more dignity, and the truth or falsehood of a statement in this region of more consequence in itself. It is a small matter whether the water in my jug was frozen on such a morning; but it is a fact of great importance that at thirty-two degrees of Fahrenheit water always freezes. We rise a step here in the nature of the facts concerned: are we come therefore into the region of truths? Is it a truth that water freezes at thirty-two degrees? I think not. There is no principle, open to us, involved in the changeless fact. The principle that lies at the root of it in the mind of God must be a truth, but to the human mind the fact is as yet only a fact. The word truth ought to be kept for higher things.

===Chinese===

若问题在于关于此事的一个陈述是否准确，我们仍处在「有此事实或无此事实」的地带；但当我们进而问那陈述是真实还是虚假时，我们就是把它作为一个人的断言来处理，升入了事物的另一层面。我走在哪一边也许无关紧要，或者某人知道我走在哪一边或有关系；但对作证的人、对爱他的任何人来说，他是否相信自己所作的陈述——这人自己是真实的还是虚假的——却是性命攸关。关于那事，只能是「事实」的问题；连这人有没有说真话，也仍是事实问题；但关于这人，却是真理的问题：就此事作证而言，他或是一个纯洁的灵魂，或是一个虚假的灵魂——能撒谎、也犯过谎。在这一层关系里，他所说的是否属实无关紧要；他若有意说出事实，他仍是一个真实的人。
在这里我想提前说一句：既有「事实」，也有「真理」；既有违背事实的谎言，也有违背真理的谎言。法利赛人说「各耳板」时，他们撒谎违背了人当孝敬父母的真理。
现在让我们从看似偶然的事实，上升到那些不变的事实——我们所不能更改的事实，它们因此涉及我们所谓的「法则」。立刻可以看出，这里的「事实」更有尊严，在这一地带，一个陈述的真假其本身也更重要。某天早晨我壶里的水结了冰，这是小事；但在华氏三十二度水总是结冰，这却是重大的事实。我们在这里就所涉事实的性质升高了一级：我们是否因此进入了真理的地带？水在三十二度结冰是一个真理吗？我想不是。这不变的事实里没有向我们敞开的原则。在神心意中位于其根底的原则必是一个真理，但对人的心思来说，那事实至今只是事实。「真理」一词应当留给更高的事物。

===Original===

There are those that think such facts the highest that can be known; they put therefore the highest word they know to the highest thing they know, and call the facts of nature truths; but to me it seems that, however high you come in your generalization, however wide you make your law﻿—including, for instance, all solidity under the law of freezing﻿—you have not risen higher than the statement that such and such is an invariable fact. Call it a law if you will﻿—a law of nature if you choose﻿—that it always is so, but not a truth. It cannot be to us a truth until we descry the reason of its existence, its relation to mind and intent, yea to self-existence. Tell us why it *must* be so, and you state a truth. When we come to see that a law is such, because it is the embodiment of a certain eternal thought, beheld by us in it, a fact of the being of God, the facts of which alone are truths, then indeed it will be to us, not a law merely, but an embodied truth. A law of God’s nature is a way he would have us think of him; it is a necessary truth of all being. When a law of Nature makes us see this; when we say, I understand that law; I see why it ought to be; it is just like God; then it rises, not to the dignity of a truth in itself, but to the truth of its own nature﻿—namely, a revelation of character, nature, and will in God. It is a picture of something in God, a word that tells a fact about God, and is therefore far nearer being called a truth than anything below it. As a simple illustration: What notion should we have of the unchanging and unchangeable, without the solidity of matter? If, such as we are, we had nothing solid about us, where would be our thinking about God and truth and law?
But there is a region perhaps not so high as this from the scientific point of view, where yet the word truth may begin to be rightly applied. I believe that every fact in nature is a revelation of God, is there such as it is because God is such as he is; and I suspect that all its facts impress us so that we learn God unconsciously. True, we cannot think of any one fact thus, except as we find the soul of it﻿—its fact of God; but from the moment when first we come into contact with the world, it is to us a revelation of God, his things seen, by which we come to know the things unseen.

===Chinese===

有人以为这样的事实便是可知之物的最高者；于是把他们所知的最高之词放在他们所知的最高之物上，称自然的事实为真理；但在我看，无论你的概括升得多高，无论你把法则拓得多宽——例如把一切凝固性都归在结冰的法则之下——你并没有升高到「如此这般乃是一个不变的事实」这一陈述之上。你尽可称之为法则——若你愿意，称之为自然法则——说它总是如此，但不要称之为真理。直到我们望见它存在的理由，它与心意和意图的关系，乃至与自有永有的关系，它才能成为我们的真理。告诉我们它为什么必（must）然如此，你就陈述了一个真理。当我们渐渐看见，一条法则之所以如此，是因为它是某个永恒思想的体现——我们在其中得见它，它是神存在的一个事实，惟有神的事实才是真理——那时它对我们才确实不只是法则，而是体现出来的真理。神本性的一条法则，是他愿意我们借以思想他的一种方式；它是一切存在的一个必然真理。当一条自然法则使我们看见这一点；当我们说，我明白那法则了；我看见它为什么应当如此；这正是神的作风——那时它就升高了，不是升到本身成为真理的尊严，而是升到它自己本性的真理——就是神里面性格、本性与旨意的启示。它是神里面某件事物的图画，是述说神之事实的一句话，因此比它以下的一切更配称为真理。举个简单的例：若没有物质的可固性，我们对那不变与不能变者会有什么观念呢？像我们这样的存在，若四围没有一样坚固的东西，我们关于神、真理与法则的思想从何而来？
但有一个地带，从科学的观点看也许不及这里高，在那里「真理」一词却已经开始可以恰当地使用。我相信自然中的每一个事实都是神的启示，它之所以在那里、之所以如此，是因为神就是这样；我疑心它的一切事实如此深地印在我们身上，以致我们不知不觉地认识了神。诚然，除非我们找到某一事实的灵魂——它属神的那事实，我们不能这样思想它；但从我们初次与世界接触的那一刻起，世界对我们就是神的启示，是那可见的他的事物，我们借以认识那不可见的。

===Original===

How should we imagine what we may of God, without the firmament over our heads, a visible sphere, yet a formless infinitude! What idea could we have of God without the sky? The truth of the sky is what it makes us feel of the God that sent it out to our eyes. If you say the sky could not but be so and such, I grant it﻿—with God at the root of it. There is nothing for us to conceive in its stead﻿—therefore indeed it must be so. In its discovered laws, light seems to me to be such because God is such. Its so-called laws are the waving of his garments, waving so because he is thinking and loving and walking inside them.
We are here in a region far above that commonly claimed for science, open only to the heart of the child and the childlike man and woman﻿—a region in which the poet is among his own things, and to which he has often to go to fetch them. For things as they are, not as science deals with them, are the revelation of God to his children. I would not be misunderstood: there is no fact of science not yet incorporated in a law, no law of science that has got beyond the hypothetic and tentative, that has not in it the will of God, and therefore may not reveal God; but neither fact nor law is there for the sake of fact or law; each is but a mean to an end; in the perfected end we find the intent, and there God﻿—not in the laws themselves, save as his means. For that same reason, human science cannot discover God; for human science is but the backward undoing of the tapestry-web of God’s science, works with its back to him, and is always leaving him﻿—his intent, that is, his perfected work﻿—behind it, always going farther and farther away from the point where his work culminates in revelation. Doubtless it thus makes some small intellectual approach to him, but at best it can come only to his back; science will never find the face of God; while those who would reach his heart, those who, like Dante, are returning thither where they are, will find also the spring-head of his science. Analysis is well, as death is well; analysis is death, not life. It discovers a little of the way God walks to his ends, but in so doing it forgets and leaves the end itself behind. I do not say the man of science does so, but the very process of his work is such a leaving of God’s ends behind.

===Chinese===

若没有我们头顶的穹苍——一个可见的球体，又是无形的无限——我们怎能想象我们对神所能想象的一切！没有天空，我们对神能有什么观念？天空的真理，是它使我们感受到的那位把它送到我们眼前的神。你若说天空不能不是这样那样，我承认——以神为其根本。我们没有别的东西可以设想来顶替它——所以它确实必当如此。在它被发现的法则里，光在我看来之所以如此，是因为神就是如此。它那些所谓法则，是他衣裳的飘动；它那样飘动，因为他正在里面思想、爱、行走。
我们在此进入了一个地带，远高于通常归于科学的那地带，只向孩子与孩子般之男女的心敞开——在那地带里，诗人是处在属于自己的事物中间，他常常必须到那里去取它们。因为事物之本然的样子——不是科学所处理的样子——才是神给他儿女的启示。我不愿被误解：没有一个尚未纳入法则的科学事实，没有一条超出假设与试探阶段的科学法则，其中不含有神的旨意（the will of God），因此也都可能启示神；但无论事实还是法则，都不是为事实或法则本身而存在；各者不过是达至目的的手段；在成全的目的里，我们找到意图，也就找到神——不在法则本身之中，除非作为他的手段。正因如此，人的科学不能发现神；因为人的科学不过是把神之科学的织锦从背面拆开，背对着他工作，总是把他——把他的意图，也就是他成全了的工作——留在身后，离他那工作在启示中登峰造极之点越走越远。无疑，它这样对神作了一点小小的理智上的接近，但至多只能摸到他的背；科学永不会找到神的脸；而那些要达到他心的人，那些像但丁（Dante）那样正从自己所在之处回返的人，却也要找着他科学的泉源。分析是好的，正如死是好的；分析是死，不是生命。它发现一点神走向他目的的路，但在这样做时，它忘记并把那目的本身丢在了身后。我不是说科学家本人如此，而是他工作的过程本身就是这样一种把神的目的留在身后的过程。

===Original===

It is a following back of his footsteps, too often without appreciation of the result for which the feet took those steps. To rise from the perfected work is the swifter and loftier ascent. If the man could find out why God worked so, then he would be discovering God; but even then he would not be discovering the best and the deepest of God; for his means cannot be so great as his ends. I must make myself clearer.
Ask a man of mere science, what is the truth of a flower: he will pull it to pieces, show you its parts, explain how they operate, how they minister each to the life of the flower; he will tell you what changes are wrought in it by scientific cultivation; where it lives originally, where it can live; the effects upon it of another climate; what part the insects bear in its varieties﻿—and doubtless many more facts about it. Ask the poet what is the truth of the flower, and he will answer: “Why, the flower itself, the perfect flower, and what it cannot help saying to him who has ears to hear it.” The truth of the flower is, not the facts about it, be they correct as ideal science itself, but the shining, glowing, gladdening, patient thing throned on its stalk﻿—the compeller of smile and tear from child and prophet. The man of science laughs at this, because he is only a man of science, and does not know what it means; but the poet and the child care as little for his laughter as the birds of God, as Dante calls the angels, for his treatise on aerostation. The children of God must always be mocked by the children of the world, whether in the church or out of it﻿—children with sharp ears and eyes, but dull hearts. Those that hold love the only good in the world, understand and smile at the world’s children, and can do very well without anything they have got to tell them. In the higher state to which their love is leading them, they will speedily outstrip the men of science, for they have that which is at the root of science, that for the revealing of which God’s science exists. What shall it profit a man to know all things, and lose the bliss, the consciousness of well-being, which alone can give value to his knowledge?
God’s science in the flower exists for the existence of the flower in its relation to his children.

===Chinese===

那是循着他脚印往回走，往往并不领会那双脚当初为着什么结果才迈出那些步。从成全了的工作上升，才是更迅疾、更高远的升腾。人若能查出神为何这样工作，他就是在发现神；但即便那样，他发现的还不是神最好、最深的部分；因为他的手段不可能像他的目的那样伟大。我必须把自己说得更清楚些。
问一个纯粹的科学家，一朵花的真理是什么：他会把它撕成碎片，给你看它的各部分，解释它们如何运作、如何各自伺候花的生命；他会告诉你科学的栽培使它起了什么变化；它原生长在何处、能生长在何处；另一种气候对它的影响；昆虫在其变种中扮演什么角色——无疑还有关于它的许多别的事实。问诗人一朵花的真理是什么，他会回答：「嗐，就是花本身，那完全的花，就是它忍不住要对那有耳可听的人说的话。」花的真理不是关于它的事实——哪怕那些事实精确如理想的科学本身——而是那闪耀着、焕发着、令人喜乐、坚忍不拔、端坐在花茎之上的东西——是它迫使孩子和先知露出微笑、流出眼泪。科学家嘲笑这个，因为他只是个科学家，不懂这话什么意思；但诗人和孩子对他的嘲笑毫不在意，正如神的飞鸟——但丁这样称呼天使——毫不在意他论气行的论文。神的儿女总要被世界的儿女嘲笑，无论在教会之内还是之外——那些儿女耳目锐利，心却迟钝。那些持定爱为世上唯一之善的人，了解世界的儿女，对他们一笑置之，他们要告诉自己的一切，没有也照样很好。在他们那爱正引领他们进入的更高境况里，他们要迅速超过科学家们，因为他们拥有那在科学根底的东西，拥有那神之科学为之存在、要加以启示的东西。人若赚得万事的知识，却丢了那唯独能给知识以价值的福祉——安康的自觉——有什么益处呢？
神在花里面的科学之所以存在，是为着花在与他儿女关系中的存在。

===Original===

If we understand, if we are at one with, if we love the flower, we have that for which the science is there, that which alone can equip us for true search into the means and ways by which the divine idea of the flower was wrought out to be presented to us. The idea of God *is* the flower; his idea is not the botany of the flower. Its botany is but a thing of ways and means﻿—of canvas and colour and brush in relation to the picture in the painter’s brain. The mere intellect can never find out that which owes its being to the heart supreme. The relation of the intellect to that which is born of the heart is an unreal except it be a humble one. The idea of God, I repeat, is the flower. He thought it; invented its means; sent it, a gift of himself, to the eyes and hearts of his children. When we see how they are loved by the ignorant and degraded, we may well believe the flowers have a place in the history of the world, as written for the archives of heaven, which we are yet a long way from understanding, and which science could not, to all eternity, understand, or enable to understand. Watch that child! He has found one of his silent and motionless brothers, with God’s clothing upon it, God’s thought in its face. In what a smile breaks out the divine understanding between them! Watch his mother when he takes it home to her﻿—no nearer understanding it than he! It is no old association that brings those tears to her eyes, powerful in that way as are flowers, and things far inferior to flowers; it is God’s thought, unrecognized as such, holding communion with her. She weeps with a delight inexplicable. It is only a daisy! only a primrose! only a pheasant-eye-narcissus! only a lily of the field! only a snowdrop! only a sweet-pea! only a brave yellow crocus! But here to her is no mere fact; here is no law of nature; here is a truth of nature, the truth of a flower﻿—a perfect thought from the heart of God﻿—a truth of God!﻿—not an intellectual truth, but a divine fact, a dim revelation, a movement of the creative soul! Who but a father could think the flowers for his little ones? We are nigh the region now in which the Lord’s word is at home﻿—“I am the truth.”
I will take an illustrative instance altogether to my mind and special purpose. What, I ask, is the truth of water? Is it that it is formed of hydrogen and oxygen?

===Chinese===

我们若明白这花、与花合一、爱这花，我们就拥有了那科学为之存在的东西，唯有它能装备我们，真正查究那花之神圣观念是借着什么手段与途径作成、呈现在我们面前的。神的观念就是（is）花；他的观念不是花的植物学。花的植物学不过是手段与途径之事——正如画布、颜料与画笔之于画家脑中的画。单凭理智，永远找不出那亏欠其存在于至高之心的事物。理智与那出于心之所生之物的关系，若非谦卑的关系，便是不真的关系。我再说一遍，神的观念就是花。他思想了它；发明了它的种种手段；把它作为他自己的礼物，送到他儿女的眼与心里。看见无知与堕落之人怎样爱花，我们就大可相信，花在那为天上档案而写的世界史中占有一席之地——那历史我们远未明白，而科学到永永远远也不能明白，也不能叫人明白。看那孩子！他找到了自己一个静默不动的兄弟，身上穿着神的衣裳，脸上带着神的思想。两人之间那神圣的默契，在怎样的微笑里绽开！再看他把花带回家交给母亲时——他对花的理解并不比孩子多！使她眼含泪水的，不是旧的联想——花在这种力量上固然强大，远逊于花的东西也一样——而是神的思想，虽未被认出是神的思想，却在与她交通。她带着无从解释的喜悦流泪。不过是一朵雏菊！不过是一朵报春花！不过是一朵红口水仙！不过是野地里的一朵百合！不过是一朵雪滴花！不过是一朵香豌豆花！不过是一朵勇敢的黄番红花！但在这里，对她而言不再只是事实；这里没有自然法则；这里有一个自然的真理，一朵花的真理——一个从神心里出来的完全思想——一个属于神的真理！——不是理智的真理，而是属神的事实，一个隐约的启示，那创造之魂的一次悸动！除了父亲，谁能为他小小的孩子们想出这些花来？我们如今已临近主的话安家之地——「我就是真理」。
我要举一个完全合我心思、合我特殊目的的例证。我问，水的真理是什么？是它由氢和氧构成吗？

===Original===

﻿—That the chemist has now another mode of stating the *fact* of water, will not affect my illustration. His new mode will probably be one day yet more antiquated than mine is now.﻿—Is it for the sake of the fact that hydrogen and oxygen combined form water, that the precious thing exists? Is oxygen-and-hydrogen the divine idea of water? Or has God put the two together only that man might separate and find them out? He allows his child to pull his toys to pieces; but were they made that he might pull them to pieces? He were a child not to be envied for whom his inglorious father would make toys to such an end! A school-examiner might see therein the best use of a toy, but not a father! Find for us what in the constitution of the two gases makes them fit and capable to be thus honoured in forming the lovely thing, and you will give us a revelation about more than water, namely about the God who made oxygen and hydrogen. There is no water in oxygen, no water in hydrogen: it comes bubbling fresh from the imagination of the living God, rushing from under the great white throne of the glacier. The very thought of it makes one gasp with an elemental joy no metaphysician can analyse. The water itself, that dances, and sings, and slakes the wonderful thirst﻿—symbol and picture of that draught for which the woman of Samaria made her prayer to Jesus﻿—this lovely thing itself, whose very wetness is a delight to every inch of the human body in its embrace﻿—this live thing which, if I might, I would have running through my room, yea, babbling along my table﻿—this water is its own self its own truth, and is therein a truth of God. Let him who would know the love of the maker, become sorely athirst, and drink of the brook by the way﻿—then lift up his heart﻿—not at that moment to the maker of oxygen and hydrogen, but to the inventor and mediator of thirst and water, that man might foresee a little of what his soul may find in God. If he become not then as a hart panting for the water-brooks, let him go back to his science and its husks: they will at last make him thirsty as the victim in the dust-tower of the Persian. As well may a man think to describe the joy of drinking by giving thirst and water for its analysis, as imagine he has revealed anything about water by resolving it into its scientific elements.

===Chinese===

——化学家如今表述水之「事实」的方式已另有新法，这不影响我的例证。他的新法有一天多半会比我现在说法更旧。——这珍贵之物之所以存在，是为了氢氧化合成水这个事实吗？氢和氧就是水的神圣观念吗？还是神把两者放在一起，只为让人去分解、去发现它们？他容许他的孩子把玩具拆散；但玩具造出来，就是为了让他拆散的吗？若父亲造玩具就是为了这个目的，那父亲不体面，孩子也不足羡！学校的督学也许在其中看出玩具最好的用处，父亲却不会！你若为我们找出，这两种气体的构造里有什么使它们配得、也能够这样受尊荣去形成那可爱之物，你就给了我们一个关于不止于水的启示——是关于那位造了氢和氧之神的启示。氧里没有水，氢里也没有水：水是从永活神的想象里新新冒泡涌出的，从冰川那巨大的白色宝座底下奔流而出。单单想到它，就使人因一种元素般的喜乐而屏息，那是没有形而上学家能分析的。这水本身，那舞蹈着、歌唱着、解那奇妙之渴的——那撒玛利亚妇人向耶稣所求之饮的象征与图画——这可爱之物本身，它的湿润使拥抱它的每一寸人体都感欢愉——这活物，我若能够，愿它流过我的房间，是的，沿我的桌子潺潺低语——这水，它自己就是它自己的真理，并因此在其中是神的一个真理。谁要认识造物者的爱，就让他渴得难受，就着路旁的溪水喝——然后举起他的心——那一刻不是举向氢和氧的制造者，而是举向那发明并安排了渴与水的中介者，使人得以预尝他的灵魂在神里面将要找着什么。他若那时不像鹿切慕溪水，就让他回到他的科学和它的糠靴那里去：它们至终要使他像波斯尘塔里的祭牲那样渴。人想借着给出渴与水作分析来描写饮水的喜乐，与想借着把水解析成科学元素就以为自己揭示了关于水的什么，是同样的荒唐。

===Original===

Let a man go to the hillside and let the brook sing to him till he loves it, and he will find himself far nearer the fountain of truth than the triumphal car of the chemist will ever lead the shouting crew of his half-comprehending followers. He will draw from the brook the water of joyous tears, “and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.”
The truth *of a thing*, then, is the blossom of it, the thing it is made for, the topmost stone set on with rejoicing; truth in a man’s imagination is the power to recognize this truth of a thing; and wherever, in anything that God has made, in the glory of it, be it sky or flower or human face, we see the glory of God, there a true imagination is beholding a truth of God. And now we must advance to a yet higher plane.
We have seen that the moment whatever goes by the name of truth comes into connection with man; the moment that, instead of merely mirroring itself in his intellect as a thing outside of him, it comes into contact with him as a being of action; the moment the knowledge of it affects or ought to affect his sense of duty, it becomes a thing of far nobler import; the question of truth enters upon a higher phase, looks out of a loftier window. A fact which in itself is of no value, becomes at once a matter of life and death﻿—moral life and death, when a man has the choice, the imperative choice of being true or false concerning it. When the truth, the heart, the summit, the crown of a thing, is perceived by a man, he approaches the fountain of truth whence the thing came, and perceiving God by understanding what is, becomes more of a man, more of the being he was meant to be. In virtue of this truth perceived, he has relations with the universe undeveloped in him till then. But far higher will the doing of the least, the most insignificant duty raise him. He begins thereby to be a true man. A man may delight in the vision and glory of a truth, and not himself be true. The man whose vision is weak, but who, as far as he sees, and desirous to see farther, does the thing he sees, is a true man. If a man knows what is, and says it is not, his knowing does not make him less than a liar. The man who recognizes the truth of any human relation, and neglects the duty involved, is not a true man.

===Chinese===

让人到山坡去，让溪水向他歌唱，直到他爱上它，他就会发现自己远比化学家那凯旋之车所引领的一群似懂非懂、呼喊喧嚷的追随者更接近真理的泉源。他要从溪里汲取喜乐之泪的水，「敬拜那创造天、地、海和众水泉源的」。
那么，一事物的真理（truth of a thing）就是它的花朵，是它为之而被造的那件事，是欢欢喜喜安放上去的顶石；人想象中的真理，就是认出这事物之真理的能力；无论何处，在神所造的任何事物里，在它的荣耀中——无论是天空、花朵还是人的脸——我们看见了神的荣耀，那里就有一个真实的想象在注视神的一个真理。现在我们必须进到一个更高的层面。
我们已经看见：无论什么以真理为名之物，一旦与人发生关联；一旦不再只是作为他身外之物映在他的理智里，而是作为行动的存在与他相接触；一旦对它的认识影响、或应当影响他的义务感，它就成了意义远为高贵之物；真理的问题进入更高的阶段，从更高的窗口望出。本身毫无价值的事实，当人在其上有选择——那不可回避的选择：作真实的人还是虚假的人——就立刻成了生死攸关之事——道德的生死攸关。当一件事物的真理、它的心、它的顶点、它的冠冕被一个人看见，他就接近了那事物所从而出的真理泉源，并因明白现状而认识神，就更是一个人，更是他受造所当是的存在。因着所看见的这真理，他有了此前在他里面尚未展开的与宇宙的关系。但行那最小、最不起眼的义务，却要把他升得远比这更高。他由此开始成为一个真实的人。人可以陶醉于一个真理的异象与荣耀，自己却不真实。那视力弱小的人，只要他照所看见的去行，并渴望看得更远，行他所看见的事，就是一个真实的人。人若知道事情如此，却说不是，他的知道并不能使他不成为说谎的。人若承认某个人间关系的真理，却忽略其中包含的义务，他就不是真实的人。

===Original===

The man who knows the laws of nature, and does not heed them, the more he teaches them to others, the less is he a true man. But he may obey them all and be the falsest of men, because of far higher and closer duties which he neglects. The man who takes good care of himself and none of his brother and sister, is false. A man may be a poet, aware of the highest truth of a thing, of that beauty which is the final cause of its existence; he may draw thence a notion of the creative loveliness that thought it out; he may be a man who would not tell a lie, or steal, or slander﻿—and yet he may not be a true man, inasmuch as the essentials of manhood are not his aim: having nowise come to the flower of his own being, nowise, in his higher degree, attained the truth of *a thing*﻿—namely, that for which he exists, the creational notion of him﻿—neither is he striving after the same. There are relations closer than those of the facts around him, plainer than those that seem to bring the maker nigh to him, which he is failing to see, or seeing fails to acknowledge, or acknowledging fails to fulfil. Man is man only in the doing of the truth, perfect man only in the doing of the highest truth, which is the fulfilling of his relations to his origin. But he has relations with his fellow man, closer infinitely than with any of the things around him, and to many a man far plainer than his relations with God. Now the nearer is plainer that he may step on it, and rise to the higher, till then the less plain. These relations make a large part of his being, are essential to his very existence, and spring from the very facts of the origination of his being. They are the relation of thought to thought, of being to being, of duty to duty. The very nature of a man depends upon or is one with these relations. They are *truths*, and the man is a true man as he fulfils them. Fulfilling them perfectly, he is himself a *truth*, a living truth. As regarded merely by the intellect, these relations are facts of man’s nature; but that they are of man’s nature makes them truths, and the fulfilments of them are duties.

===Chinese===

那认识自然法则却不理会它们的人，越是把它们教给别人，就越不是真实的人。但他可能全都顺从了它们，却是众人中最虚假的，因为他忽略了远更高、更亲近的义务。那只顾自己好、全然不顾弟兄姊妹的人，是虚假的。人可以是诗人，知晓一件事物最高的真理，知晓那作为其存在之终极因的美；他可以由此得出一点关于那把它想出来的创造之可爱的观念；他可以是一个不肯撒谎、不肯偷窃、不肯诽谤的人——然而他可能仍不是真实的人，因为人之为人的本质不是他的目标：他既丝毫没有到自己存在的花朵，丝毫没有在更高的程度上达到一事物的真理——就是他为之存在的那件事，他受造的观念——他也没有追求它。有些关系比他四围事实的关系更亲近，比那些似乎把造他者带到他近旁的关系更明显，他却未能看见，或看见而不肯承认，或承认而不去履行。人惟独在行真理时才是人，惟独在行最高真理时才是完全人，而行最高真理，就是成全他与本源的关系。但他与同胞的关系，比与四围任何事物的关系亲近无限倍，而且对许多人来说，远比他与神的关系更明显。近的所以更明显，是为叫他可以踏在其上，升到更高处——在那之前，更高的总欠明显。这些关系构成他存在的一大部分，对他生存本身不可或缺，且发端于他存在之起源的那些事实本身。它们是思想对思想、存在对存在、义务对义务的关系。人的本性正依赖于此、或说与此合一。它们是真理（truths），人履行它们到什么地步，就是什么地步的真实之人。完全履行它们，他自己就成了一真理——一个活的真理。仅就理智看来，这些关系是人本性的事实；但它们既属于人的本性，它们就是真理，对它们的履行就是义务。

===Original===

He is so constituted as to understand them at first more than he can love them, with the resulting advantage of having thereby the opportunity of choosing them purely because they are true; so doing he chooses to love them, and is enabled to love them in the doing, which alone can truly reveal them to him, and make the loving of them possible. Then they cease to show themselves in the form of duties, and appear as they more truly are, absolute truths, essential realities, eternal delights. The man is a true man who chooses duty; he is a perfect man who at length never thinks of duty, who forgets the name of it. The duty of Jesus was the doing in lower forms than the perfect that which he loved perfectly, and did perfectly in the highest forms also. Thus he fulfilled all righteousness. One who went to the truth by mere impulse, would be a holy animal, not a true man. Relations, truths, duties, are shown to the man away beyond him, that he may choose them, and be a child of God, choosing righteousness like him. Hence the whole sad victorious human tale, and the glory to be revealed!
The moral philosopher who regards duties only as facts of his system; nay, even the man who rewards them as truths, essential realities of his humanity, but goes no farther, is essentially a liar, a man of untruth. He is a man indeed, but not a true man. He is a man in possibility, but not a real man yet. The recognition of these things is the imperative obligation to fulfil them. Not fulfilling these relations, the man is undoing the right of his own existence, destroying his *raison d’être*, making of himself a monster, a live reason why he should not live, for nothing on those terms could ever have begun to be. His presence is a claim upon his creator for destruction.
The facts of human relation, then, are truths indeed, and of awfullest import. “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer; and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him!” The man who lives a hunter after pleasure, not a labourer in the fields of duty, who thinks of himself as if he were alone on the earth, is in himself a lie. Instead of being the man he looks, the man he was made to be, he lives as the beasts seem to live﻿—with this difference, I trust, that they are rising, while he, so far as lies in himself, is sinking.

===Chinese===

他的构造使起初对它们懂得比爱得多，由此带来的好处是：他因此有机会纯粹因它们真而选择它们；这样行，他就选择去爱它们，并在行中得着爱它们的能力——惟有这行能真正把它们启示给他，使爱它们成为可能。那时它们就不再以义务的面目显出，而是照它们更真实的本相显出：绝对的真理、本质的真实、永恒的喜乐。选择义务的人是真实的人；那至终不再想到义务、忘了义务之名的人，是完全人。耶稣的义务，是以低于完全的形式去做他那完全所爱的、且在最高形式里也完全成就了的事。这样，他成全了诸般的义（righteousness）。单凭冲动走向真理的，将是圣洁的动物，不是真实的人。关系、真理、义务被显明给那人，远超他自身之外，好叫他能选择它们，像神那样选择义，作神的儿女。由此才有这整部悲怆而得胜的人间故事，以及那将要显明的荣耀！
那只把义务当作其体系之事实的伦理学家——不，甚至那把义务尊为其人性之真理、本质真实、却到此为止的人——本质上是个说谎的，一个不真之人。他诚然是人，却不是真实的人。他是可能性中的人，还不是真实在的人。认出这些事，就是履行它们的绝对命令。不履行这些关系，人就在拆毁自己生存的权利，摧毁他存在的理由（raison d'être），把自己造成一个怪物，一个活生生的不该活着的理由，因为按那些条件存在的，根本无物能开始存在。他的存在本身，就是向他的创造者提出的毁灭之诉求。
所以人间关系的事实确是真理，而且是可畏至极的真理。「凡恨他弟兄的，就是杀人的；你们晓得凡杀人的，没有永生存在他里面！」那活着只作快乐的猎户、不作义务之田里劳力、把自己想成世上孤身一人的人，本身就是谎言。他本该是他看起来的那种人、他受造所当是的人，却活得像野兽所看起来的那样——所不同者，我相信，是野兽正在上升，而他，就他自己所能作的而言，正在下沉。

===Original===

But he cannot be allowed to sink beyond God’s reach; hence all the holy﻿—that is, healing﻿—miseries that come upon him, of which he complains as so hard and unfair: they are for the compelling of the truth he will not yield﻿—a painful suasion to be himself, to be a truth.
But suppose, for the sake of my progressive unfolding, that a man did everything required of him﻿—fulfilled all the relations to his fellows of which I have been speaking, was toward them at least, a true man; he would yet feel, doubtless would feel it the more, that something was lacking to him﻿—lacking to his necessary well-being. Like a live flower, he would feel that he had not yet blossomed, and could not tell what the blossom ought to be. In this direction the words of the Lord point, when he says to the youth, “If thou wouldst be perfect.” The man whom I suppose, would feel that his existence was not yet justified to itself, that the truth of his being and nature was not yet revealed to his consciousness. He would remain unsatisfied; and the cause would be that there was in him a relation, and that the deepest, closest, and strongest, which had not yet come into live fact, which had not yet become a truth in him, toward which he was not true, whereby his being remained untrue, he was not himself, was not ripened into the divine idea, which alone can content itself. A child with a child’s heart who does not even know that he has a father, yet misses him﻿—with his whole nature, even if not with his consciousness. This relation has not yet so far begun to be fulfilled in him, as that the coming blossom should send before it patience and hope enough to enable him to live by faith without sight. When the flower begins to come, the human plant begins to rejoice in the glory of God not yet revealed, the inheritance of the saints in light; with uplifted stem and forward-leaning bud expects the hour when the lily of God’s field shall know itself alive, with God himself for its heart and its atmosphere; the hour when God and the man shall be one, and all that God cares for shall be the man’s. But again I forget my progression.
The highest truth to the intellect, the abstract truth, is the relation in which man stands to the source of his being﻿—his will to the will whence it became a will, his love to the love that kindled his power to love, his intellect to the intellect that lighted his.

===Chinese===

但不容他沉到神够不着的地方；因此有一切临到他的圣洁的——就是医治的——苦难，他抱怨它们又硬又不公平：它们是要逼出他不肯交出的真理——一种痛苦的劝服，要他作他自己，作一个真理。
但为了我渐进的铺陈，且假设一个人行了一切所求于他的——成全了我所说与他同胞的一切关系，至少对他们而言是个真实的人；他仍会觉得——无疑会觉得更深——自己缺了什么，缺了他生存之必需。像一朵活的花，他会觉得自己尚未开花，又说不出那花该是什么。主对那青年说「你若愿意作完全人」，他的话正指向这个方向。我所设想的这人，会觉得自己的存在尚未向自己证明自己，觉得他生命与性情的真理尚未向他的意识显明。他仍不得满足；原因是：他里面有一个关系——那最深、最近、最强的关系——尚未成为活的事实，尚未在他里面成为真理，他对它还不真实，因此他的存在仍不真实，他还不是他自己，还没有成熟到那神圣的观念里去——惟有那观念能使自己满足。一个有孩童之心的孩子，甚至不知道自己有父亲，却想念他——以他整个的天性，即便不以他的意识。这关系在他里面尚未开始成全到这样的地步，使那将临的花先遣来足够的忍耐与盼望，叫他能够凭着信心（faith）不凭眼见地活着。当花开始来到，这人形的植物就开始在那尚未显明之神荣耀里喜乐——就是众圣徒在光明中的基业（the inheritance）；它挺起茎、前倾着花苞，盼望那时刻：神田野间的百合知道自己活着，以神自己为它的心和它的氛围；那时辰：神与人合而为一，神所顾念的一切都归于那人。可是我又忘了我的层递。
对理智而言最高的真理、抽象的真理，是人对他存在之源所站的关系——他的意志对那使它成为意志的意志，他的爱对那点燃他爱的能力之爱，他的理智对那点亮他的理智。

If a man deal with these things only as things to be dealt with, as objects of thought, as ideas to be analysed and arranged in their due order and right relation, he treats them as facts and not as truths, and is no better, probably much the worse, for his converse with them, for he knows in a measure, and is false to all that is most worthy of his faithfulness.
But when the soul, or heart, or spirit, or what you please to call that which is the man himself and not his body, sooner or later becomes aware that he needs someone above him, whom to obey, in whom to rest, from whom to seek deliverance from what in himself is despicable, disappointing, unworthy even of his own interest; when he is aware of an opposition in him, which is not harmony; that, while he hates it, there is yet present with him, and seeming to be himself, what sometimes he calls “the old Adam,” sometimes “the flesh,” sometimes “his lower nature,” sometimes “his evil self”; and sometimes recognizes as simply that part of his being where God is not; then indeed is the man in the region of truth, and beginning to come true in himself. Nor will it be long ere he discover that there is no part in him with which he would be at strife, so God were there, so that it were true, what it ought to be﻿—in right relation to the whole; for, by whatever name called, the old Adam, or antecedent horse, or dog, or tiger, it would then fulfil its part holily, intruding upon nothing, subject utterly to the rule of the higher; horse or dog or tiger, it would be good horse, good dog, good tiger.

===Chinese===

人若只把这些东西当作待处理之物、思想的对象、待分析并按其当有次序与正当关系排列的观念，他就是把它们当事实而非真理对待，这样的交往于他无益——多半大大有害——因为他有所认识，却对那最配他忠信的一切不忠。
但那灵魂、心、或灵——或随你怎样称呼那作为人自己而非他身体的东西——迟早会察觉：他需要一位在他以上的，可以顺服，可以在里面安息，可以从他寻求拯救，脱离他自己里面那可鄙的、令人失望的、甚至连他自己都不屑一顾的东西；当他察觉自己里面有一种对立，那不是和谐；察觉他所恨的东西虽为他所恨，却仍与他同在、又仿佛是他自己——他有时称之为「老亚当」，有时称之为「肉体」，有时称之为「他较低的天性」，有时称之为「他邪恶的自我」；有时又只认出那不过是他存在中神不在的那部分；那时，这人确实处在真理的地带，开始在他自己里面成为真实。他不久就会发现：他里面没有任何一部分是他在神若临在其中时还愿与之争斗的——只要神在那里，只要它成了真的、成了它当是的、与全体有正当关系；因为不论叫什么名字——老亚当，或先在的马、狗、老虎——它那时都要圣洁地尽它的本分，不侵扰任何东西，全然服在较高的辖管之下；是马、是狗、是老虎，它都会是好马、好狗、好老虎。

===Original===

When the man bows down before a power that can account for him, a power to whom he is no mystery as he is to himself; a power that knows whence he came and whither he is going; who knows why he loves this and hates that, why and where he began to go wrong; who can set him right, longs indeed to set him right, making of him a creature to look up to himself without shadow of doubt, anxiety or fear, confident as a child whom his father is leading by the hand to the heights of happy-making truth, knowing that where he is wrong, the father is right and will set him right; when the man feels his whole being in the embrace of self-responsible paternity﻿—then the man is bursting into his flower; then the truth of his being, the eternal fact at the root of his new name, his real nature, his idea﻿—born in God at first, and responsive to the truth, the being of God, his origin﻿—begins to show itself; then his nature is almost in harmony with itself. For, obeying the will that is the cause of his being, the cause of that which demands of itself to be true, and that will being righteousness and love and truth, he begins to stand on the apex of his being, to know himself divine. He begins to feel himself free. The truth﻿—not as known to his intellect, but as revealed in his own sense of being true, known by his essential consciousness of his divine condition, without which his nature is neither his own nor God’s﻿—trueness has made him free. Not any abstract truth, not all abstract truth, not truth its very metaphysical self, held by purest insight into entity, can make any man free; but the truth done, the truth loved, the truth lived by the man; the truth *of* and not merely *in* the man himself; the honesty that makes the man himself a child of the honest God.
When a man is, with his whole nature, loving and willing the truth, he is then a live truth. But this he has not originated in himself. He has seen it and striven for it, but not originated it. The one originating, living, visible truth, embracing all truths in all relations, is Jesus Christ. He is true; he is the live Truth. His truth, chosen and willed by him, the ripeness of his being, the flower of his sonship which is his nature, the crown of his one topmost perfect relation acknowledged and gloried in, is his absolute obedience to his father. The obedient Jesus is Jesus the Truth.

===Chinese===

当这人俯伏在一位能说明他的大能者面前——这位大能者看他不像他自己看自己那样是个谜；知道他从哪里来、往哪里去；知道他为何爱这个恨那个、为何以及从哪里开始走错；能纠正他，也实在渴望纠正他，把他造成一个能仰望他而无一丝疑虑、焦虑或惧怕的受造物，像孩子那样笃定——他父亲正牵着他的手，领他上那使人幸福的真理之高处，孩子知道，凡自己错了的地方，父亲是对的，必把他纠正过来；当这人感到自己的整个存在在那自我担当的父性的怀抱中——那时，这人就在绽出他的花朵；那时，他存在的真理——他那新名字根底那永恒的事实，他真实的性情，他的观念——起初生于神，又对真理、对神的存在、对他的本源有所回应——开始显出自己；那时他的性情几乎与自身和谐。因为，顺服那作为他存在之因的意志——那作为「要求自身成为真实者」之因的意志——而那意志乃是义与爱与真理，他就开始立在他存在的顶点，知道自己有神性。他开始感到自由。真理——不是作为他理智所知的，而是作为在他自己「真实存在」之感中启示出来的，凭他对自身属神境况的本质意识而知道的，没有这意识，他的性情既不属于自己也不属于神——是真实使他得了自由。不是任何抽象的真理，不是全部抽象的真理，不是那以其形而上本身、以对实体最纯粹洞见所持守的真理，能叫人自由；能叫人自由的，是行出来的真理、被爱的真理、被人活出来的真理；是那出于（of）人、而不只住在（in）人里面的真理；是那使人自己成为诚实之神孩子的诚实。
当一个人以他整个天性爱真理、愿意真理，他那时就是一个活的真理。但这不是他自己创始的。他见过它、为它奋斗过，但没有创始它。那独一的创始的、活的、可见的真理，包含一切关系中的一切真理，就是耶稣基督。他是真实的；他是那活着的真理。他的真理——他所选择、所定意的那真理，他存在的成熟，他那作为本性的儿子名分之花，他那独一无二至上完全之关系的冠冕，被他承认且引以为荣——就是他对他父（the Father）的绝对顺服（obedience）。那顺服的耶稣，就是作为真理的耶稣。

He is true and the root of all truth and development of truth in men. Their very being, however far from the true human, is the undeveloped Christ in them, and his likeness to Christ is the truth of a man, even as the perfect meaning of a flower is the truth of a flower. Every man, according to the divine idea of him, must come to the truth of that idea; and under every form of Christ is the Christ. The truth of every man, I say, is the perfected Christ in him. As Christ is the blossom of humanity, so the blossom of every man is the Christ perfected in him. The vital force of humanity working in him is Christ; he is his root﻿—the generator and perfecter of his individuality. The stronger the pure will of the man to be true; the freer and more active his choice; the more definite his individuality, ever the more is the man and all that is his, Christ’s. Without him he could not have been; being, he could not have become capable of truth; capable of truth, he could never have loved it; loving and desiring it, he could not have attained to it. Nothing but the heart-presence, the humanest sympathy, and whatever deeper thing else may be betwixt the creating Truth and the responding soul, could make a man go on hoping, until at last he forget himself, and keep open house for God to come and go. He gives us the will wherewith to will, and the power to use it, and the help needed to supplement the power, whatever in any case the need may be; but we ourselves must will the truth, and for that the Lord is waiting, for the victory of God his father in the heart of his child. In this alone can he see of the travail of his soul, in this alone be satisfied. The work is his, but we must take our willing share. When the blossom breaks forth in us, the more it is ours the more it is his, for the highest creation of the Father, and that preeminently through the Son, is the being that can, like the Father and the Son, of his own self will what is right. The groaning and travailing, the blossom and the joy, are the Father’s and the Son’s and ours. The will, the power of willing, may be created, but the willing is begotten. Because God wills first, man wills also.

他是真实的，是人里面一切真理及真理发育之根。人的存在本身——无论离真实的人性多远——就是他们里面尚未发育的基督；人像基督，就是人的真理，正如一朵花完全的意义就是那花的真理。每一个人，照神对他所有的神圣观念，都必须达到那观念的真理；而基督的每一个形相底下，都是那基督。我说，每个人的真理，就是他里面被成全的基督。基督既是人性的花朵，每个人的花朵也就是在他里面被成全的基督。在他里面运行的人性生命力就是基督；基督是他的根——他个体性的生成者与成全者。人要真实的那纯净意志越强，他的选择越自由、越活跃，他的个体性越明确，则这人并他一切所有，就越是基督的。没有他，人根本不能存在；存在了，也无力成为能承载真理的；能承载真理了，也永不会爱它；爱它、渴慕它了，也达不到它。惟有那心的同在、那最属人的同情，以及那在创造之真理与回应之魂之间可能有的任何更深之物，能叫一个人一直盼望下去，直到末了忘记自己，为神的来去敞开着门户。他赐给我们借以意愿的意志、运用它的力量，并补足那力量所需的一切帮助——无论各人所需是什么；但我们自己必须意愿那真理，主正为此等候——为着神他父在他孩子心里的得胜。惟独在这事上，他能看见他灵魂的劳苦果效；惟独在这事上，他能满足。工作是他的，但我们必须甘愿有分。当那花在我们里面绽放时，它越是我们的，就越是他的；因为父（the Father）最高的创造——且特要借着子——乃是这样一种存在：它能像父与子那样，凭自己意愿那正当的。那叹息与劳苦、那花朵与喜乐，是父的、是子的、也是我们的。意志、那意愿的能力，可以是造的；但意愿本身是生的。因为神先意愿，人才意愿。

When my being is consciously and willedly in the hands of him who called it to live and think and suffer and be glad﻿—given back to him by a perfect obedience﻿—I thenceforward breathe the breath, share the life of God himself. Then I am free, in that I am true﻿—which means one with the Father. And freedom knows itself to be freedom. When a man is true, if he were in hell he could not be miserable. He is right with himself because right with him whence he came. To be right with God is to be right with the universe; one with the power, the love, the will of the mighty Father, the cherisher of joy, the lord of laughter, whose are all glories, all hopes, who loves everything, and hates nothing but selfishness, which he will not have in his kingdom.

### Freedom / 自由
===Original===

> The Truth shall make you free.﻿ ﻿… Whosoever committeth sin, is the servant of sin. And the servant abideth not in the house forever: but the Son abideth ever. If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

===Chinese===

> 真理必叫你们得以自由。……所有犯罪的就是罪的奴仆。奴仆不能永远住在家里，儿子是永远住在家里。所以天父的儿子若叫你们自由，你们就真自由了。

===Original===

As this passage stands, I have not been able to make sense of it. No man could be in the house of the Father in virtue of being the servant of sin; yet this man is in the house as a servant, and the house in which he serves is not the house of sin, but the house of the Father. The utterance is confused at best, and the reasoning faulty. He must be in the house of the Father on some other ground than sin. This, had no help come, would have been sufficient cause for leaving the passage alone, as one where, perhaps, the words of the Lord were misrepresented﻿—where, at least, perceiving more than one fundamental truth involved in the passage, I failed to follow the argument. I do not see that I could ever have suggested where the corruption, if any, lay. Most difficulties of similar nature have originated, like this, I can hardly doubt, with some scribe who, desiring to explain what he did not understand, wrote his worthless gloss on the margin: the next copier took the words for an omission that ought to be replaced in the body of the text, and inserting them, falsified the utterance, and greatly obscured its intention. What do we not owe to the critics who have searched the scriptures, and found what really was written! In the present case, Dr. Westcott’s notation gives us to understand that there is another with “a reasonable probability of being the true reading.” The difference is indeed small to the eye, but is great enough to give us fine gold instead of questionable ore. In an alternative of the kind, I must hope in what seems logical against what seems illogical; in what seems radiant against what seems trite.
What I take for the true reading then, I English thus: “Everyone committing sin is a slave. But the slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remaineth forever. If then the son shall make you free, you shall in reality be free.” The authorized version gives, “Whosoever committeth sin, is the servant of *sin*”; the revised version gives, “Everyone that committeth sin is the bondservant of *sin*”; both accepting the reading that has the words, “*of sin*.” The statement is certainly in itself true, but appears to me useless for the argument that follows.

===Chinese===

照这经文现在的样子，我一直没法读出个道理来。人不可能因作罪的奴仆就在父（the Father）的家里；然而这人却是以奴仆的身份在家里，而且他所服事的那个家，不是罪的家，而是父的家。这宣告顶多算是混乱，其推理也有毛病。他必是因别的什么根据而在父的家里。倘若没有帮助来临，这一点就足以叫人把这经文搁在一边，当作一处也许主的话被传错了的地方——至少是一处我从其中看出不止一个根本真理、却追不上其论证的地方。我看不出我原本能指出那讹误（若有的话）在哪里。同类性质的难处，多半像这样——我几乎不能怀疑——是起于某个抄写者：他想解释自己不懂的东西，便把那一文不值的注释写在页边；下一个抄写者把这些字当作一段本该补进正文的缺文，把它们插进去，就窜改了那宣告，大大弄昏了它的用意。我们对那些查考圣经、找出原本所写之字的批评家，亏欠何等多！在眼前这件事上，魏斯科特博士的标注使我们知道，还有另一个读法，「有相当的可能是真读法」。那差别在眼里确实很小，却大得足以给我们纯金，而不是可疑的矿石。在这样的二选一里，我必须盼望那看似合逻辑的，胜过那看似不合逻辑的；盼望那看似发光的，胜过那看似陈腐的。

这样，那我认为真的读法，译出来是这样：「凡犯罪的，就是奴仆。奴仆不能永远住在家里；儿子却永远住着。所以儿子若叫你们自由，你们就真的自由了。」钦定本作「凡犯罪的，就是*罪*的奴仆」；修订本作「凡犯罪的，就是*罪*的奴仆」；两者都接受了带「*罪*」字的那个读法。这话本身当然是真的，但在我看来，对下面的论证毫无用处。

===Original===

And I think it may have been what I take to be the true reading, that suggested to the apostle Paul what he says in the beginning of the fourth chapter of his Epistle to the Galatians﻿—words of spirit and life from which has been mistakenly drawn the doctrine of adoption, merest poison to the child-heart. The words of the Lord here are not that he who sins is the slave of sin, true utterly as that is; but that he is a slave, and the argument shows that he means a slave to God. The two are perfectly consistent. No amount of slavery to sin can keep a man from being as much the slave of God as God chooses in his mercy to make him. It is his sin makes him a slave instead of a child. His slavery to sin is his ruin; his slavery to God is his only hope. God indeed does not love slavery; he hates it; he will have children, not slaves; but he may keep a slave in his house a long time in the hope of waking up the poor slavish nature to aspire to the sonship which belongs to him, which is his birthright. But the slave is not to be in the house forever. The father is not bound to keep his son a slave because the foolish child prefers it.
Whoever will not do what God desires of him, is a slave whom God can compel to do it, however he may bear with him. He who, knowing this, or fearing punishment, obeys God, is still a slave, but a slave who comes within hearing of the voice of his master. There are, however, far higher than he, who yet are but slaves. Those to whom God is not all in all, are slaves. They may not commit great sins; they may be trying to do right; but so long as they *serve* God, as they call it, from duty, and do not know him as their father, the joy of their being, they are slaves﻿—good slaves, but slaves. If they did not try to do their duty, they would be bad slaves. They are by no means so slavish as those that serve from fear, but they are slaves; and because they are but slaves, they can fulfil no righteousness, can do no duty perfectly, but must ever be trying after it wearily and in pain, knowing well that if they stop trying, they are lost. They are slaves indeed, for they would be glad to be adopted by one who is their own father! Where then are the sons? I know none, I answer, who are yet utterly and entirely sons or daughters.

而且我想，可能正是我认为真的那个读法，给使徒保罗提示了他在《加拉太书》第四章开头所说的话——那些属灵属生命的言语，人却从其中错引出了「收养」的教义，那对孩子的真心是至毒的毒药。主在这里的话，不是说犯罪的是罪的奴仆——这话尽管全然真；而是说他是个奴仆，而论证显明，他指的乃是一个神（God）的奴仆。这两者完全相合。无论怎样为罪所奴役，都不能拦阻人照样作神的奴仆，到神照他的怜悯所愿意的程度。是他的罪使他作奴仆，而不是作孩子。他之为罪的奴仆是他的败亡；他之为神的奴仆是他唯一的盼望。神实在不爱奴役；他恨恶它；他要的是儿女，不是奴仆；但他也许会把一个奴仆在家里留很久，指望唤醒那可怜的奴性，使它渴慕那本属于他、是他生来权利的儿子名分。但奴仆不能永远在家里。父并没有义务因为那愚昧的孩子情愿，就把他的儿子一直当奴仆。

凡不愿行神所要他行的，就是一个神能强制去行的奴仆——无论神怎样宽容他。知道这一点而顺服（obedience）神的，或因怕刑罚而顺服神的，仍是个奴仆，只是个进入主人声音可闻之处的奴仆。然而还有远高过他的，也仍是奴仆。凡神之于他不是万有中的万有的，都是奴仆。他们可能不犯大罪；可能正在努力行善；但只要他们照自己的说法是本于责任地「事奉」神，而不认识神是他们的父、是他们存在的喜乐，他们就是奴仆——好奴仆，但仍是奴仆。他们若不努力尽本分，就是坏奴仆。他们远不像那些出于惧怕而事奉的那么奴性，但他们仍是奴仆；而正因为只是奴仆，他们就不能成全任何义（righteousness），不能完美地尽任何本分，只能疲惫而痛苦地一直追赶，心里清楚一旦停下努力，他们就完了。他们实在还是奴仆，因为他们竟甘愿被那本来就是他们自己父亲的一位「收养」！那么儿子们在哪里呢？我回答说，我还不知道有谁已经全然、彻底地作了儿子或女儿。

There may be such﻿—God knows; I have not known them; or, knowing them, have not been myself such as to be able to recognize them. But I do know some who are enough sons and daughters to be at war with the slave in them, who are not content to be slaves to their father. Nothing I have seen or known of sonship, comes near the glory of the thing; but there are thousands of sons and daughters, though their number be yet only a remnant, who are siding with the father of their spirits against themselves, against all that divides them from him from whom they have come, but out of whom they have never come, seeing that in him they live and move and have their being. Such are not slaves; they are true though not perfect children; they are fighting along with God against the evil separation; they are breaking at the middle wall of partition. Only the rings of their fetters are left, and they are struggling to take them off. They are children﻿—with more or less of the dying slave in them; they know it is there, and what it is, and hate the slavery in them, and try to slay it. The real slave is he who does not seek to be a child; who does not desire to end his slavery; who looks upon the claim of the child as presumption; who cleaves to the traditional authorized service of forms and ceremonies, and does not know the will of him who made the seven stars and Orion, much less cares to obey it; who never lifts up his heart to cry “Father, what wouldst thou have me to do?” Such are continually betraying their slavery by their complaints. “Do we not well to be angry?” they cry with Jonah; and, truly, being slaves, I do not know how they are to help it. When they are sons and daughters, they will no longer complain of the hardships, and miseries, and troubles of life; no longer grumble at their aches and pains, at the pinching of their poverty, at the hunger that assails them; no longer be indignant at their rejection by what is called Society. Those who believe in their own perfect father, can ill blame him for anything they do not like. Ah, friend, it may be you and I are slaves, but there *are* such sons and daughters as I speak of.
The slaves of sin rarely grumble at that slavery; it is their slavery to God they grumble at; of that alone they complain﻿—of the painful messengers he sends to deliver them from their slavery both to sin and to himself.

也许有这样的人——神知道；我不认识他们；或者虽认识他们，我自己却还不是那能认出他们的那种人。但我确实认识一些人，他们作儿女作得够真，足以与他们里面的奴仆交战，不甘于作他们父亲的奴仆。我所见过、所知道的一切儿子名分，没有一样及得上这事的荣耀；但有成千上万的儿女——虽然他们的数目如今还只是余数——正站在他们灵之父的一边，反对他们自己，反对一切使他们与那位他们所从出者隔绝的东西；但他们从未从他里面出来过，因为他们生活、动作、存留都在乎他。这样的人不是奴仆；他们是真实却未完全的孩子；他们正与神一同攻打那邪恶的隔绝；他们正在拆那隔断的墙。他们锁链的环子只剩下几圈，他们正挣扎着要把它褪下来。他们是孩子——里面还带着或多或少垂死的奴仆；他们知道它在，知道它是什么，恨恶他们里面的奴役，想要杀死它。真正的奴仆，是那不求作孩子的人；不渴望结束自己奴役的人；把孩子的权利看作僭妄的人；紧抓住那传统而钦定的形式与仪文之事奉、却不认识那造昴星和参星者的旨意、更谈不上在乎去顺服的人；从不曾举起心来喊「父啊，你要我做什么？」的人。这样的人不断以他们的抱怨暴露自己的奴籍。他们与约拿同喊：「我发怒以至于死，难道不合宜吗？」；说实话，既作了奴仆，我不知道他们如何能不这样。等到他们作了儿女，就再不会抱怨人生的艰苦、悲惨与烦难；再不会为他们的疼痛呻吟，为贫穷的拮据发怨言，为饥饿的来袭埋怨；再不会因所谓「社会」的排斥而愤愤。那些信自己有完全之父的人，很难为任何他们不喜欢的事责怪他。啊，朋友，也许你和我都是奴仆，但我所说的那样的儿女，*是*有的。

They must be sons or slaves. They cannot rid themselves of their owner. Whether they deny God, or mock him by acknowledging and not heeding him, or treat him as an arbitrary, formal monarch; whether, taking no trouble to find out what pleases him, they do dull things for his service he cares nothing about, or try to propitiate him by assuming with strenuous effort some yoke the Son never wore, and never called on them to wear, they are slaves, and not the less slaves that they are slaves to God; they are so thoroughly slaves, that they do not care to get out of their slavery by becoming sons and daughters, by finding the good of life where alone it can or could lie. Could a creator make a creature whose well-being should not depend on himself? And if he could, would the creature be the greater for that? Which, the creature he made more, or the creature he made less dependent on himself, would be the greater? The slave in heart would immediately, with Milton’s Satan, reply, that the farthest from him who made him must be the freest, thus acknowledging his very existence a slavery, and but two kinds in being﻿—a creator, and as many slaves as he pleases to make, whose refusal to obey is their unknown protest against their own essence. *Being* itself must, for what they call liberty, be repudiated! Creation itself, to go by their lines of life, is an injustice! God had no right to create beings less than himself; and as he could not create equal, he ought not to have created! But they do not complain of having been created; they complain of being required to do justice. They will not obey, but, his own handiwork, ravish from his work every advantage they can! They desire to be free with another kind of freedom than that with which God is free; unknowing, they seek a more complete slavery. There is, in truth, no mid way between absolute harmony with the Father and the condition of slaves﻿—submissive, or rebellious. If the latter, their very rebellion is by the strength of the Father in them. Of divine essence, they thrust their existence in the face of their essence, their own nature.
Yet is their very rebellion in some sense but the rising in them of his spirit against their false notion of him﻿—against the lies they hold concerning him.

他们要么作儿子，要么作奴仆。他们无法摆脱他们的主人。无论他们否认神，还是以承认而不理会来讥诮他，还是把他当作一位任性而徒有其表的君主；无论他们不肯费心去查明什么使他喜悦，只为他的服事做些他毫不在意的沉闷事，还是想靠苦行般担上一种儿子从未负过、也从未叫他们负的轭来讨好他——他们都是奴仆，而且因为是神的奴仆，就一点不少地是奴仆；他们奴性到这般地步，以致不肯借成为儿女走出他们的奴役，不肯在生命的好处唯一能存在的地方去寻找它。一个创造者能造出一个受造者，其福祉竟不系于他自己吗？倘若能，那受造者会因此更伟大吗？他所造的更依赖他的那个，与更不依赖他的那个，哪一个更伟大？心里的奴仆会立刻同弥尔顿（Milton）的撒但一样回答：离造他者最远的，必是最自由的——这就等于承认他自己的存在就是奴役，而存在里只有两种——一位创造者，和随他高兴造出的许多奴仆；这些奴仆的不顺服，乃是他们对自己本质的未知抗议。照他们所谓的自由，连*存在*本身都必须被丢弃！照他们生活的路线，创造本身就是一件不义！神无权创造低于自己的存在者；他既造不出相等的，就根本不该创造！但他们并不抱怨被造；他们抱怨的是被要求行公义。他们不肯顺服，却又是他手中的工作，倒要从他的工作里抢走一切能抢的好处！他们想以一种不同于神之自由的那种自由来自由；不知不觉，他们寻求的是更完全的奴役。事实上，在与父绝对和谐同心的状态和奴仆的状态之间——或顺从的奴仆，或反叛的奴仆——没有中间路。若是后者，他们那反叛所凭的力气，还是父在他们里面的力气。他们既出于神的本质，就把他们的存在，怼在他们自己的本质、他们自己的本性脸上。

然而就某种意义说，他们的反叛，不过是他的灵在他们里面起来，反对他们对他的错误观念——反对他们所持关于他的谎言。

They do not see that, if his work, namely, they themselves, are the chief joy to themselves, much more might the life that works them be a glory and joy to them the work﻿—inasmuch as it is nearer to them than they to themselves, causing them to be, and extends, without breach of relation, so infinitely above and beyond them. For nothing can come so close as that which creates; the nearest, strongest, dearest relation possible is between creator and created. Where this is denied, the schism is the widest; where it is acknowledged and fulfilled, the closeness is unspeakable. But ever remains what cannot be said, and I sink defeated. The very protest of the rebel against slavery, comes at once of the truth of God in him, which he cannot all cast from him, and of a slavery too low to love truth﻿—a meanness that will take all and acknowledge nothing, as if his very being was a disgrace to him. The liberty of the God that would have his creature free, is in contest with the slavery of the creature who would cut his own stem from his root that he might call it his own and love it; who rejoices in his own consciousness, instead of the life of that consciousness; who poises himself on the tottering wall of his own being, instead of the rock on which that being is built. Such a one regards his own dominion over himself﻿—the rule of the greater by the less, inasmuch as the conscious self is less than the self﻿—as a freedom infinitely greater than the range of the universe of God’s being. If he says, “At least I have it my own way!” I answer, You do not know what is your way and what is not. You know nothing of whence your impulses, your desires, your tendencies, your likings come. They may spring now from some chance, as of nerves diseased; now from some roar of a wandering bodiless devil; now from some infant hate in your heart; now from the greed or lawlessness of some ancestor you would be ashamed of if you knew him; or it may be now from some far-piercing chord of a heavenly orchestra: the moment it comes up into your consciousness, you call it your own way, and glory in it!

Two devils amusing themselves with a duet of inspiration, one at each ear, might soon make that lordly “me” you are so in love with, rejoice in the freedom of willing the opposite each alternate moment; and at length drive you mad at finding that you could not, will as you would, make choice of a way and its opposite simultaneously. The whole question rests and turns on the relation of creative and created, of which relation few seem to have the consciousness yet developed. To live without the eternal creative life is an impossibility; freedom from God can only mean an incapacity for seeing the facts of existence, an incapability of understanding the glory of the creature who makes common cause with his creator in his creation of him, who wills that the lovely will calling him into life and giving him choice, should finish making him, should draw him into the circle of the creative heart, to joy that he lives by no poor power of his own will, but is one with the causing life of his life, in closest breathing and willing, vital and claimant oneness with the life of all life. Such a creature knows the life of the infinite Father as the very flame of his life, and joys that nothing is done or will be done in the universe in which the Father will not make him all of a sharer that it is possible for perfect generosity to make him. If you say this is irreverent, I doubt if you have seen the God manifest in Jesus. But all will be well, for the little god of your poor content will starve your soul to misery, and the terror of the eternal death creeping upon you, will compel you to seek a perfect father. Oh, ye hidebound Christians, the Lord is not straitened, but ye are straitened in your narrow unwilling souls! Some of you need to be shamed before yourselves; some of you need the fire.
But one who reads may call out, in the agony and thirst of a child waking from a dream of endless seeking and no finding, “I am bound like Lazarus in his grave-clothes! what am I to do?” Here is the answer, drawn from this parable of our Lord; for the saying is much like a parable, teaching more than it utters, appealing to the conscience and heart, not to the understanding: “You are a slave; the slave has no hold on the house; only the sons and daughters have an abiding rest in the home of their father. God cannot have slaves about him always.

===Chinese===

两个魔鬼各据一耳、以一支二重奏自娱，可能很快就叫你所痴恋的那位威风的「我」，为那每隔一刻便翻转的意愿自由而欢欣；末了更叫你发疯——因为你发现，任你怎样意愿，也不能同时选定一条路又选定它的反面。整个问题都落系于、也转于创造者与受造者的关系上；对这关系，似乎少有人已发展出那份意识。没有那永恒的创造生命而活，是不可能的；脱离神的自由，只能意味着看不见存在的事实，意味着不能领悟受造者的荣耀——这受造者在自己受造的事上与自己的创造者同心同工，愿那唤他入生命、又赐他选择权的可爱旨意，来作完对他的制造，把他吸引进那创造之心的圈子里，叫他喜乐：他活着，不是靠自己意志那点可怜的能力，而是与他生命的致因生命合为一，与一切生命之生命有着最贴近的呼吸与意愿、活泼而有权柄的合一。这样的受造者认那无穷之父的生命，就是他自己生命的火焰，并且喜乐：宇宙中所成就、将成就的事，没有一件，父不照完全的慷慨所能作的，使他十足有分。你若说这是不敬，我怀疑你并未看见那在耶稣里显明的神。但一切终必安好，因为你那可怜的满足的小神，必要把你的灵魂饿到悲苦，那悄悄爬近你的永死之恐怖，必要催逼你去寻求一位完全的父。哦，你们这些被硬壳捆住的基督徒啊，主并不狭窄，是你们在自己狭窄而不情愿的灵魂里狭窄了！你们中间有人需要在你们自己面前蒙羞；有人需要那火。

但读者中也许有人喊出，像一个从无尽寻求却一无所得的梦中醒来的孩子，在干渴与剧痛中喊：「我像拉撒路那样被裹尸布捆着！我该怎么办？」这里有答案，是从我们主这个比喻里抽出来的；因为这句话很像一个比喻，教导的多于说出的，诉诸的是良心与心，不是悟性：「你是个奴仆；奴仆在家里没有立足之地；唯有儿女才在父亲的家里享有恒久的安息。神不能常有奴仆在身旁。

===Original===

You must give up your slavery, and be set free from it. That is what I am here for. If I make you free, you shall be free indeed; for I can make you free only by making you what you were meant to be, sons like myself. That is how alone the Son can work. But it is you who must become sons; you must will it, and I am here to help you.” It is as if he said, “You shall have the freedom of my father’s universe; for, free from yourselves, you will be free of his heart. Yourselves are your slavery. That is the darkness which you have loved rather than the light. You have given honour to yourselves, and not to the Father; you have sought honour from men, and not from the Father! Therefore, even in the house of your father, you have been but sojourning slaves. We in his family are all one; we have no party-spirit; we have no self-seeking: fall in with us, and you shall be free as we are free.”
If then the poor starved child cry﻿—“How, Lord?” the answer will depend on what he means by that “how.” If he means, “What plan wilt thou adopt? What is thy scheme for cutting my bonds and setting me free?” the answer may be a deepening of the darkness, a tightening of the bonds.
