To believe in a vicarious sacrifice, is to think to take refuge with the Son from the righteousness of the Father; to take refuge with his work instead of with the Son himself; to take refuge with a theory of that work instead of the work itself; to shelter behind a false quirk of law instead of nestling in the eternal heart of the unchangeable and righteous Father, who is merciful in that he renders to every man according to his work, and compels their obedience, nor admits judicial quibble or subterfuge. God will never let a man off with any fault. He must have him clean. He will excuse him to the very uttermost of truth, but not a hair’s-breadth beyond it; he is his true father, and will have his child true as his son Jesus Christ is true.

===Chinese===

那甘愿担当这刑罚的强大存在，尽可被视为当受敬拜；但他这样挫败的那位神，他那所谓的公义，又怎么说？你若说要求这受苦的是公义，不是神；我说，公义不能要求不义之事，而整个这件事是不义的。神绝对公义，人无法逃脱他的公义——那公义与他的怜悯原为一。这设计是个荒谬——一个奇形怪状的荒谬。把永活的神描绘成这类行径的同谋，就是用残忍与伪善的面具，遮蔽那惟有在耶稣脸上才能看见其荣耀的脸；就是把一通庸俗罗马法学的长篇攻讦，放进那有怜悯有恩典、万不以有罪为无罪的主神口中。与其对他相信这样的丑陋愚妄——他的名本足以叫认识他的人发出那切慕溪水之鹿的喘息；与其对他存这样的想法——这想法若在人身上，会使我不惜性命地躲避他——我宁愿说：「没有神；我们不吃不喝，死了吧！看哪，这不是我们的神！这不是我们所等候的那位！」但我已在耶稣基督的脸上见过他的面，在他的声音里听过他的声；我说，这是我们的神，就是那一位——因着他的所是，受造成为无限的喜乐。我不要文士和法利赛人的神——无论是犹太的还是基督教的、新教的、罗马的还是希腊的；我只要你的父，基督啊！他是我的神。你若说：「那是我们的神，不是你的！」我回答：「你们为你们的神画的像，是对基督之面容的一幅恶毒漫画。」
信一位代赎的祭，就是想从父的义逃到子那里避难；是投靠他的工作而不投靠子自己；是投靠那工作的一种理论而不投靠那工作本身；是躲在一套法律的奸计背后，而不安卧在那永不改变、公义之父的永恒心中——他正因照各人所行的报应各人而显为怜悯，他催逼人顺服，却不接受任何司法的遁词与巧辩。神决不放任人带任何过犯过去。他必要他洁净。他必体谅他到真理的极处，但一发也不越过；他是他真实的父，必叫他自己的孩子真实，如同他的儿子耶稣基督真实一样。

===Original===

He will impute to him nothing that he has not, will lose sight of no smallest good that he has; will quench no smoking flax, break no bruised reed, but send forth judgment unto victory. He is God beyond all that heart hungriest for love and righteousness could to eternity desire.
If you say the best of men have held the opinions I stigmatize, I answer, “Some of the best of men have indeed held these theories, and of men who have held them I have loved and honoured some heartily and humbly﻿—but because of what they *were*, not because of what they *thought*; and they were what they were in virtue of their obedient faith, not of their opinion. They were not better men because of holding these theories. In virtue of knowing God by obeying his son, they rose above the theories they had never looked in the face, and so had never recognized as evil. Many have arrived, in the natural progress of their sacred growth, at the point where they must abandon them. The man of whom I knew the most good gave them up gladly. Good to worshipfulness may be the man that holds them, and I hate them the more therefore; they are lies that, working under cover of the truth mingled with them, burrow as near the heart of the good man as they can go. Whoever, from whatever reason of blindness, may be the holder of a lie, the thing is a lie, and no falsehood must mingle with the justice we mete out to it. There is nothing for any lie but the pit of hell. Yet until the man sees the thing to be a lie, how shall he but hold it! Are there not mingled with it shadows of the best truth in the universe? So long as a man is able to love a lie, he is incapable of seeing it is a lie. He who is true, out and out, will know at once an untruth; and to that vision we must all come. I do not write for the sake of those who either make or heartily accept any lie. When they see the glory of God, they will see the eternal difference between the false and the true, and not till then. I write for those whom such teaching as theirs has folded in a cloud through which they cannot see the stars of heaven, so that some of them even doubt if there be any stars of heaven. For the holy ones who believed and taught these things in days gone by, all is well. Many of the holiest of them cast the lies from them long ere the present teachers of them were born.

===Chinese===

他不会把人所没有的归算给人，也不会看漏人所有的哪怕最小的善；压伤的芦苇他不折断，将残的灯火他不吹灭，等他施行公理，叫公理得胜。他这样的神，远超那对爱与义（righteousness）最饥渴的心到永恒所能渴望的一切。
你若说，持我这般痛斥之见解的也有最好的人，我回答：「确实，有些最好的人持过这些理论；持这些理论的人中，也有几位我是衷心而谦卑地爱过敬过的——却是因他们的所是（were），不是因他们的所想（thought）；他们之所以成为那样的人，是凭他们顺服的信心（faith），不是凭他们的意见。他们并不因持这些理论而成为更好的人。他们因顺服神的儿子而认识神，就超越了那些他们从未正视、因而从未认出其为恶的理论。许多人已在那神圣生长的自然进程中，到达了必须丢弃它们的那一点。我所认识的那最好的人，是欣然丢弃它们的。持这些理论的人可以好到近乎可敬；正因如此，我更恨这些理论；它们是谎言，藏身于与之混杂的真理的掩护下，竭力向善人的心掘进。无论谁、出于何种盲目，作了一个谎言的持有者，那东西终是谎言；我们对它施以公义时，不可掺和任何虚妄。任何谎言只有一个归宿——地狱（hell）的坑。然而，在那人看见这东西是谎言之前，他怎能不持有它！其中不是也掺着宇宙间最佳真理的影子吗？人一日还能爱一个谎言，就一日无能看见它是谎言。那彻底真实的人，一望便知虚假；我们都必来到那样的视力。我不是为那些制造或衷心接受任何谎言的人而写。他们看见神的荣耀时，就必看见真假之间永恒的分别——不到那时不能。我是为那些被他们这类教训裹进云层、以致看不见天上星辰的人而写；他们中有些人甚至怀疑是否真有天上的星辰。至于往昔相信并教导这些事的圣徒们，一切都好。他们中最圣洁的许多人，早在今日这些教师出生之前，就已把那些谎言抛开了。」

===Original===

Many who would never have invented them for themselves, yet receiving them with the seals affixed of so many good men, took them in their humility as recognized truths, instead of inventions of men; and, oppressed by authority, the authority of men far inferior to themselves, did not dare dispute them, but proceeded to order their lives by what truths they found in their company, and so had their reward, the reward of obedience, in being by that obedience brought to know God, which knowledge broke for them the net of a presumptuous self-styled orthodoxy. Every man who tries to obey the Master is my brother, whether he counts me such or not, and I revere him; but dare I give quarter to what I see to be a lie, because my brother believes it? The lie is not of God, whoever may hold it.
“Well, then,” will many say, “if you thus unceremoniously cast to the winds the doctrine of vicarious sacrifice, what theory do you propose to substitute in its stead?”
“In the name of the truth,” I answer, *None*. I will send out no theory of mine to rouse afresh little whirlwinds of dialogistic dust mixed with dirt and straws and holy words, hiding the Master in talk about him. If I have any such, I will not cast it on the road as I walk, but present it on a fair patine to him to whom I may think it well to show it. Only eyes opened by the sun of righteousness, and made single by obedience, can judge even the poor moony pearl of formulated thought. Say if you will that I fear to show my opinion. Is the man a coward who will not fling his child to the wolves? What faith in this kind I have, I will have to myself before God, till I see better reason for uttering it than I do now.
“Will you then take from me my faith, and help me to no other?”
Your faith! God forbid. Your theory is not your faith, nor anything like it. Your faith is your obedience; your theory I know not what. Yes, I will gladly leave you without any of what you call faith. Trust in God. Obey the word﻿—every word of the Master. That is faith; and so believing, your opinion will grow out of your true life, and be worthy of it. Peter says the Lord gives the spirit to them that obey him: the spirit of the Master, and that alone, can guide you to any theory that it will be of use to you to hold. A theory arrived at any other way is not worth the time spent on it.

===Chinese===

许多本不会自己发明这些理论的人，只因领受它们时盖着这么多好人的印信，就在谦卑中把它们当作公认的真理，而不是人的发明；又被权威——远不如他们自己之人的权威——所压制，不敢质疑，只管照他们在这些理论中所发现的真理来安排自己的生活，于是得着了他们的赏赐，顺服的赏赐：因那顺服被带到认识神的地步；这认识为他们打破了那妄自尊大、自立名目的正统之网。凡努力顺服主的，都是我的弟兄，无论他认不认我为弟兄，我都敬重他；但我岂敢因我弟兄信它，就对我看明是谎言的东西留情面呢？谎言不出于神，无论谁持有它。
「好吧，」许多人会说，「你既然这样毫不客气地把代赎献祭的教义抛到风中，你打算拿什么理论来顶替它呢？」
「奉真理的名，」我回答，什么也没有（None）。我不会把自己的任何理论抛出去，再搅起那些由争辩的尘土、烂草和圣言混成的小旋风，把主掩埋在关于他的谈论里。我若真有这类东西，也不肯边走边丢在路上，只肯端端正正摆在盘子里，给我认为值得一看的人看。惟有被义之日照亮、又因顺服而变得单纯的眼睛，才能评判哪怕那月亮般清冷的、被条理化之思想的小珠。你若愿意，就说我是不敢亮出我的见解吧。不肯把孩子丢给狼的人，是懦夫吗？我在这方面若有的一点信心，我愿只留给自己、留在神面前，直到我看见比现在更好的发表理由。
「那么你要夺去我的信心，又不帮我得着别的？」
你的信心！神不容。你的理论不是你的信心，也毫不像它。你的信心是你的顺服；你的理论，我不知道是什么。是的，我甘愿让你一点也没有你所称的那种信心。信靠神。顺服那道——主的每一句话。那才是信心；这样信着，你的意见必从你真实的生命中长出来，配得上那生命。彼得（Peter）说，主赐圣灵给顺从他的人：惟有主的灵能引导你得到任何值得持有的理论。以任何别的方式得出的理论，不值耗费在上面的时间。

===Original===

Jesus is the creating and saving lord of our intellects as well as of our more precious hearts; nothing that he does not think, is worth thinking; no man can think as he thinks, except he be pure like him; no man can be pure like him, except he go with him, and learn from him. To put off obeying him till we find a credible theory concerning him, is to set aside the potion we know it our duty to drink, for the study of the various schools of therapy. You know what Christ requires of you is right﻿—much of it at least you believe to be right, and your duty to do, whether he said it or not: *do it*. If you do not do what you know of the truth, I do not wonder that you seek it intellectually, for that kind of search may well be, as Milton represents it, a solace even to the fallen angels. But do not call anything that may be so gained, “The Truth.” How can you, not caring to *be* true, judge concerning him whose life was to do for very love the things you confess your duty, yet do them not? Obey the truth, I say, and let theory wait. Theory may spring from life, but never life from theory.
I will not then tell you what I think, but I will tell any man who cares to hear it what I believe. I will do it now. Of course what I say must partake thus much of the character of theory that I cannot prove it; I can only endeavour to order my life by it.
I believe in Jesus Christ, the eternal Son of God, my elder brother, my lord and master; I believe that he has a right to my absolute obedience whereinsoever I know or shall come to know his will; that to obey him is to ascend the pinnacle of my being; that not to obey him would be to deny him. I believe that he died that I might die like him﻿—die to any ruling power in me but the will of God﻿—live ready to be nailed to the cross as he was, if God will it. I believe that he is my Saviour from myself, and from all that has come of loving myself, from all that God does not love, and would not have me love﻿—all that is not worth loving; that he died that the justice, the mercy of God, might have its way with me, making me just as God is just, merciful as he is merciful, perfect as my father in heaven is perfect. I believe and pray that he will give me what punishment I need to set me right, or keep me from going wrong.

===Chinese===

耶稣是我们理智——正如我们更宝贵的心——的创造与拯救之主；他所不思想的，就不值得思想；人除非像他那样纯洁，就不能像他那样思想；人除非与他同行、从他学习，就不能像他那样纯洁。把顺服他推迟到我们找到一个关于他的可信理论，就是把我们明知当喝的药放到一边，去研究各家疗法的学问。你知道基督对你所求的是正当的——至少其中许多你信是正当的、是你的本分，无论是不是他说的：去行（do it）吧。你若不行你所知道的真理，我不怪你要在理智上寻求它，因为那种寻求，正如弥尔顿（Milton）所描绘的，连堕落的天使也可以从中得安慰。但不要把这样得来的任何东西称为「真理」。你既无心成为真实，怎能论断那位以行你所认为本分却不行之事为生命者呢？要顺服真理，我说，让理论等候。理论可以出于生命，生命永不能出于理论。
那么，我不告诉你我所想的，我要告诉愿意听的任何人我所信的。我现在就这样做。当然，我所说的难免带上一点理论的性质——我无法证明它；我只能努力照它安排我的生活。
我信耶稣基督，神的永子，我的长兄，我的主与夫子；我信，凡我知道或将知道他旨意之处，他都有权要我无条件的顺服；信顺服他就是登上我存在的绝顶；信不顺服他就是否认他。我信他死，是叫我能够像他那样死——向我心里除神的旨意（the will of God）以外的任何掌权者死——活着随时豫备像他那样被钉十字架，若神愿意。我信他是救我脱离我自己、脱离爱我自己所生的一切、脱离神所不爱、也不愿我爱的那一切——一切不值得爱的——的救主；我信他死，是要叫神的公义、神的怜悯在我身上通行无阻，使我公义如神公义，怜悯如他怜悯，完全如我在天上的父完全。我信并且祷告（pray），他必把我所需的刑罚赐给我，使我归正，或保守我不入歧途。

===Original===

I believe that he died to deliver me from all meanness, all pretence, all falseness, all unfairness, all poverty of spirit, all cowardice, all fear, all anxiety, all forms of self-love, all trust or hope in possession; to make me merry as a child, the child of our father in heaven, loving nothing but what is lovely, desiring nothing I should be ashamed to let the universe of God see me desire. I believe that God is just like Jesus, only greater yet, for Jesus said so. I believe that God is absolutely, grandly beautiful, even as the highest soul of man counts beauty, but infinitely beyond that soul’s highest idea﻿—with the beauty that creates beauty, not merely shows it, or itself exists beautiful. I believe that God has always done, is always doing his best for every man; that no man is miserable because God is forgetting him; that he is not a God to crouch before, but our father, to whom the child-heart cries exultant, “Do with me as thou wilt.”
I believe that there is nothing good for me or for any man but God, and more and more of God, and that alone through knowing Christ can we come nigh to him.
I believe that no man is ever condemned for any sin except one﻿—that he will not leave his sins and come out of them, and be the child of him who is his father.
I believe that justice and mercy are simply one and the same thing; without justice to the full there can be no mercy, and without mercy to the full there can be no justice; that such is the mercy of God that he will hold his children in the consuming fire of his distance until they pay the uttermost farthing, until they drop the purse of selfishness with all the dross that is in it, and rush home to the Father and the Son, and the many brethren﻿—rush inside the centre of the life-giving fire whose outer circles burn. I believe that no hell will be lacking which would help the just mercy of God to redeem his children.
I believe that to him who obeys, and thus opens the doors of his heart to receive the eternal gift, God gives the spirit of his son, the spirit of himself, to be in him, and lead him to the understanding of all truth; that the true disciple shall thus always know what he ought to do, though not necessarily what another ought to do; that the spirit of the father and the son enlightens by teaching righteousness.

===Chinese===

我信他死，是要救我脱离一切卑劣、一切虚饰、一切虚假、一切不公、一切灵里的贫乏、一切怯懦、一切惧怕、一切忧虑、一切形态的自爱、一切对占有的信靠与盼望；是要使我快活如孩子——我们天父的孩子——只爱那可爱的，不欲任何我羞于让神的宇宙看见我欲求的东西。
我信神正像耶稣，只是更大，因为耶稣这样说。我信神绝对地、宏伟地美——按人最高灵魂所计的美，却无限超越那灵魂最高的观念——他的美是创造美的美，不只是显出美、或自己存在为美的美。我信神向来行的、一直行的，都是为每个人尽他最好的；没有人因神忘了他而受苦；他不是叫人蜷伏其前的神，而是我们的父，孩子的心向他欢呼：「照你的意愿待我吧。」
我信，除了神、以及愈来愈多的神，没有什么于我或于任何人是好的；也信惟独借着认识基督，我们才能亲近他。
我信，人绝不为任何罪被定罪，除了一样——他不肯离弃他的罪、从罪里出来、作那本是他父亲者的孩子。
我信，公义与怜悯简直是一件事；没有完全的公义就没有怜悯，没有完全的怜悯就没有公义；我信神的怜悯就是这样：他必把他孩子守在他那距离的吞灭之火中，直到他们还清那极小的一文钱，直到他们丢下那装满渣滓的自私钱袋，奔回父与子并众弟兄那里——奔回那外圈燃烧、中心赐生命之火的中心。我信，凡有助于神那公正之怜悯救赎他儿女的地狱（hell），一个也不会缺少。
我信，人顺服，从而敞开心门领受那永恒的恩赐，神就把自己儿子的灵、他自己的灵赐给他，住在他里面，引导他明白一切真理；真门徒必因此总知道自己当行什么——虽然未必知道别人当行什么；父与子的灵以教导义来光照人。

===Original===

I believe that no teacher should strive to make men think as he thinks, but to lead them to the living Truth, to the Master himself, of whom alone they can learn anything, who will make them in themselves know what is true by the very seeing of it. I believe that the inspiration of the Almighty alone gives understanding. I believe that to be the disciple of Christ is the end of being; that to persuade men to be his disciples is the end of teaching.
“The sum of all this is that you do not believe in the atonement?”
I believe in Jesus Christ. Nowhere am I requested to believe *in* anything, or *in* any statement, but everywhere to believe in God and in Jesus Christ. In what you call “the atonement,” in what you mean by the word, what I have already written must make it plain enough I do not believe. God forbid I should, for it would be to believe a lie, and a lie which is to blame for much nonacceptance of the gospel in this and other lands. But, as the word was used by the best English writers at the time when the translation of the Bible was made﻿—with all my heart, and soul, and strength, and mind, I believe in the atonement, call it the “a‑tone‑ment,” or the “at‑one‑ment,” as you please. I believe that Jesus Christ *is* our atonement; that through him we are reconciled to, made one with God. There is not one word in the New Testament about reconciling God to us; it is we that have to be reconciled to God. I am not writing, neither desire to write, a treatise on the atonement, my business being to persuade men to be atoned to God; but I will go so far to meet my questioner as to say﻿—without the slightest expectation of satisfying him, or the least care whether I do so or not, for his *opinion* is of no value to me, though his truth is of endless value to me and to the universe﻿—that, even in the sense of the atonement being a making-up for the evil done by men toward God, I believe in the atonement. Did not the Lord cast himself into the eternal gulf of evil yawning between the children and the Father? Did he not bring the Father to us, let us look on our eternal Sire in the face of his true son, that we might have that in our hearts which alone could make us love him﻿—a true sight of him? Did he not insist on the one truth of the universe, the one saving truth, that God was just what he was?

===Chinese===

我信，没有教师该努力叫人照他那样思想，而该领人到那活的真理、到主自己面前——惟独从他，人才能学到什么；他要人亲自在看见中认识什么是真。我信，惟独全能者的默示赐人悟性。我信，作基督的门徒乃是存在的目的；劝人作他的门徒，乃是教导的目的。
「这一切归结起来就是：你不信赎罪？」
我信耶稣基督。没有任何地方要求我信任何东西、或信任何陈述；处处都是要求我信神、信耶稣基督。至于你们所称的「赎罪」，你们用这词所指的意思，我已写的必已清楚表明我不信。神不许我信，因为那是信一个谎言，一个该为福音在此地与别处遭拒负责的谎言。但按圣经翻译之时最好的英文作家使用这词的意思——我尽心、尽性、尽力、尽意地信赎罪；你随你怎么称呼它，「赎-tone-ment」或「at-one-ment（复和）」都好。我信耶稣基督就是（is）我们的赎罪；我们借着他与神和好、与神合一。新约里没有一个字说到使神与我们和好；是要我们与神和好。我不是在写、也不想写一篇论赎罪的论文；我的正业是劝人与神和好；但我愿就便答复我的提问者这样说——全不指望满足他，也毫不在意是否满足他，因为他的意见于我毫无价值，虽然他的真实于我于宇宙有永恒的价值——即便在赎罪是弥补人对神所行之恶这个意义上，我也信赎罪。
主岂不是把自己投身到那在儿女与父（the Father）之间张口的永恒恶之鸿沟里？他岂不是把父带到我们面前，让我们在他真儿子的脸上仰望我们永恒的父，使我们心里得着那惟一能使我们爱他的东西——对他的真实看见？他岂不是坚持宇宙那独一的真理、那独一的救恩真理——神就是他所是的？

===Original===

Did he not hold to that assertion to the last, in the face of contradiction and death? Did he not thus lay down his life persuading us to lay down ours at the feet of the Father? Has not his very life by which he died passed into those who have received him, and recreated theirs, so that now they live with the life which alone is life? Did he not foil and slay evil by letting all the waves and billows of its horrid sea break upon him, go over him, and die without rebound﻿—spend their rage, fall defeated, and cease? Verily, he made atonement! *We* sacrifice to God!﻿—it is God who has sacrificed his own son to us; there was no way else of getting the gift of himself into our hearts. Jesus sacrificed himself to his father and the children to bring them together﻿—all the love on the side of the Father and the Son, all the selfishness on the side of the children. If the joy that alone makes life worth living, the joy that God is such as Christ, be a true thing in my heart, how can I but believe in the atonement of Jesus Christ? I believe it heartily, as God means it.
Then again, as the power that brings about a making-up for any wrong done by man to man, I believe in the atonement. Who that believes in Jesus does not long to atone to his brother for the injury he has done him? What repentant child, feeling he has wronged his father, does not desire to make atonement? Who is the mover, the causer, the persuader, the creator of the repentance, of the passion that restores fourfold?﻿—Jesus, our propitiation, our atonement. He is the head and leader, the prince of the atonement. He could not do it without us, but he leads us up to the Father’s knee: he makes us make atonement. Learning Christ, we are not only sorry for what we have done wrong, we not only turn from it and hate it, but we become able to serve both God and man with an infinitely high and true service, a soul-service. We are able to offer our whole being to God to whom by deepest right it belongs. Have I injured anyone? With him to aid my justice, new risen with him from the dead, shall I not make good amends? Have I failed in love to my neighbour? Shall I not now love him with an infinitely better love than was possible to me before? That I will and can make atonement, thanks be to him who is my atonement, making me at one with God and my fellows!

===Chinese===

面对顶撞与死亡，他岂不是坚持那宣告到底？他岂不是这样舍了他的生命，劝我们把我们的生命也放在父的脚前？他那舍去生命的生命，岂不是已进入凡接待他的人里面，重造了他们的生命，使他们如今活着的，是那独一算得生命的生命？他岂不是任凭恶那可怖之海的一切波浪漫过他身上、无声地消逝——泄尽它们的狂怒、倒下、败亡、止息——以此挫败并杀死恶？他实在作成了赎罪！是我们（We）向神献祭吗！——是神把他自己的儿子献给了我们；舍此别无他法，能把他自己的恩赐送进我们心里。耶稣把自己献给他父和众儿女，为要使两者相聚——一切的爱在父与子这边，一切的自私在儿女这边。那独一使人生值得活的喜乐——神正如基督所是的喜乐——若在我心里是真实的，我怎能不信耶稣基督的赎罪？我全心信它，照神所赋予它的意思信它。
再者，作为那使人对人所行的任何错得着弥补的能力，我也信赎罪。信耶稣的人，谁不渴望向他亏负了的弟兄偿还？悔改的孩子自觉亏负了父亲，谁不渴望赎罪？那悔改的发动者、促成者、劝说者、创造者——那使人四倍偿还的心情的创造者——是谁？——耶稣，我们的挽回祭，我们的赎罪。他是赎罪的首领与引领者，是赎罪的君王。他离了我们不能作成，但他把我们领到父的膝前：他使我们去赎罪。学基督，我们不仅为所行的错忧伤，不仅转离它、恨它，更开始能以无限高尚而真实的事奉——一种灵魂的事奉——事奉神和人。我们能把自己整个的存在献给那凭至深之权拥有它的神。我伤害过谁吗？有他帮助我的公义、我又与他一同从死里复活，我岂不作出充分的补偿？我曾在爱上亏欠邻舍吗？我如今岂不要用比以前所能的无限更好的爱去爱他？我愿、且能赎罪——感谢那作我赎罪者、使我与神并与我同伴合一的那位！

===Original===

He is my life, my joy, my lord, my owner, the perfecter of my being by the perfection of his own. I dare not say with Paul that I am the slave of Christ; but my highest aspiration and desire is to be the slave of Christ.
“But you do not believe that the sufferings of Christ, as sufferings, justified the supreme ruler in doing anything which he would not have been at liberty to do but for those sufferings?”
I do not. I believe the notion as unworthy of man’s belief, as it is dishonouring to God. It has its origin doubtless in a salutary sense of sin; but sense of sin is not inspiration, though it may lie not far from the temple-door. It is indeed an opener of the eyes, but upon home-defilement, not upon heavenly truth; it is not the revealer of secrets. Also there is another factor in the theory, and that is unbelief﻿—incapacity to accept the freedom of God’s forgiveness; incapacity to believe that it is God’s chosen nature to forgive, that he is bound in his own divinely willed nature to forgive. No atonement is necessary to him but that men should leave their sins and come back to his heart. But men cannot believe in the forgiveness of God. Therefore they need, therefore he has given them a mediator. And yet they will not know him. They think of the father of souls as if he had abdicated his fatherhood for their sins, and assumed the judge. If he put off his fatherhood, which he cannot do, for it is an eternal fact, he puts off with it all relation to us. He cannot repudiate the essential and keep the resultant. Men cannot, or will not, or dare not see that nothing but his being our father gives him any right over us﻿—that nothing but that could give him a perfect right. They regard the father of their spirits as their governor! They yield the idea of the Ancient of Days, “the glad creator,” and put in its stead a miserable, puritanical martinet of a God, caring not for righteousness, but for his rights; not for the eternal purities, but the goody proprieties. The prophets of such a God take all the glow, all the hope, all the colour, all the worth, out of life on earth, and offer you instead what they call eternal bliss﻿—a pale, tearless hell. Of all things, turn from a mean, poverty stricken faith. But, if you ate straitened in your own mammon-worshipping soul, how shall you believe in a God any greater than can stand up in that prison-chamber?

===Chinese===

他是我的生命、我的喜乐、我的主、我的拥有者，是以他自己的完全成全我存在的那位。我不敢像保罗那样说我是基督的奴仆；但我最高的向往与渴望，是作基督的奴仆。
「可你不信基督的受苦——就其作为受苦而言——使那至高统治者有正当理由行他若非因那些受苦便无权行的事？」
我不信。我认为这观念既不配人信，也羞辱神。它无疑源于一种有益的罪感；但罪感不是默示，虽然它或许离圣殿的门不远。它确实开人的眼，却是开向自家的污秽，不是开向属天的真理；它不是奥秘的启示者。这理论里还有另一个因素，就是不信——无能接受神赦免的自由；不能相信赦免是神所拣选的本性，不能相信他受自己神圣意愿的本性所系，必须赦免。于他，除了一件事，别无赎罪的需要：人离开他们的罪，回到他心里。但人不能相信神的赦免。所以他们需要、所以他给了他们一位中保。可他们还是不肯认识他。他们想那万灵之父，仿佛他为他们的罪退位了父职，穿上了法官的袍子。他若脱下父职——他不能，因为那是永恒的事实——他就连同脱下与我们的一切关系。他不能弃绝本质而保留其结果。人不能、不肯、也不敢看见：惟独他作我们的父，才使他对我们有任何权利——惟独那才能给他完全的权利。他们竟把万灵之父当作他们的总督！他们交出了亘古常在者、「那喜乐的创造者」的观念，换上一位可鄙的、清教徒式的小军曹之神——他不在乎义，只在乎他的权利；不在乎永恒的纯洁，只在乎规规矩矩的善行。这样一位神的先知们，把地上生命的一切光焰、一切盼望、一切色彩、一切价值都抽走，换给你他们所谓的永福——一个苍白无泪的地狱。在一切事上，都要转离那卑劣穷酸的信心。但你若在自己那敬拜玛门的灵魂里被困住了，你怎能信一位大得能在这囚室中站起来的神呢？

I desire to wake no dispute, will myself dispute with no man, but for the sake of those whom certain *believers* trouble, I have spoken my mind. I love the one God seen in the face of Jesus Christ. From all copies of Jonathan Edwards’s portrait of God, however faded by time, however softened by the use of less glaring pigments, I turn with loathing. Not such a God is he concerning whom was the message John heard from Jesus, *that he is light, and in him is no darkness at all*.

===Chinese===

我不愿挑起争辩，自己也不与任何人争辩；但为着那些被某些信的人（believers）搅扰的人，我说出了我的心里话。我爱那位在耶稣基督脸上显明的独一的神。至于乔纳森·爱德华兹那幅神的画像的一切摹本——无论怎样被时间冲淡、怎样因用了不那么刺目的颜料而显得柔和——我都怀着厌恶转离。约翰从耶稣所听见的信息所论到的那位神，不是这样的神：神就是光，在他毫无黑暗。

### Light / 光

> This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

===Chinese===

> 神就是光，在他毫无黑暗。这是我们从主所听见、又报给你们的信息。

===Original===

We call the story of Jesus, told so differently, yet to my mind so consistently, by four narrators, “the gospel.” What makes this tale “the good news”? Is everything in the story of Christ’s life on earth good news? Is it good news that the one only good man was served by his fellow-men as Jesus was served﻿—cast out of the world in torture and shame? Is it good news that he came to his own, and his own received him not? What makes it fit, I repeat, to call the tale *good news*? If we asked this or that theologian, we should, in so far as he was a true man, and answered from his own heart and not from the tradition of the elders, understand what he saw in it that made it good news to him, though it might involve what would be anything but good news to some of us. The deliverance it might seem to this or that man to bring, might be founded on such notions of God as to not a few of us contain as little of good as of news. To share in the deliverance which some men find in what they call the gospel﻿—for all do not apply the word to the tale itself, but to certain deductions made from the epistles and their own consciousness of evil﻿—we should have to believe such things of God as would be the opposite of an evangel to us﻿—yea, a message from hell itself; we should have to imagine that whose possibility would be worse than any ill from which their “good news” might offer us deliverance: we must first believe in an unjust God, from whom we have to seek refuge. True, they call him just, but say he does that which seems to the best in me the essence of injustice. They will tell me I judge after the flesh: I answer, Is it then to the flesh the Lord appeals when he says, “Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?” Is he not the light that lighteth every man that cometh into the world? They tell me I was born in sin, and I know it to be true; they tell me also that I am judged with the same severity as if I had been born in righteousness, and that I know to be false. They make it a consequence of the purity and justice of God that he will judge us, born in evil, for which birth we were not accountable, by our sinfulness, instead of by our guilt.

===Chinese===

我们称那由四位叙述者讲述、讲法各不相同、在我看来却全然一致的故事为「福音」。是什么使这个故事成了「好消息」？基督在世生平的故事里，样样都是好消息吗？那唯一的好人被他的同胞这样对待——在酷刑与羞辱中被赶出世界——这是好消息吗？他到自己的地方来，自己的人倒不接待他，这是好消息吗？我再说一遍，是什么使这个故事配称作*好消息*？我们若问这位或那位神学家——只要他是真诚的人，是从自己心里、而不是从古人的遗传回答——我们就会明白他在其中看见了什么，使它成了对他的好消息，尽管其中可能包含着对我们某些人来说绝非好消息的东西。这个人或那个人以为福音所带来的拯救，可能建立在那样一些关于神的观念上——那些观念在我们不少人看来，好消息的成分与新闻的成分一样稀少。要分享一些人在他们所谓的福音里所找到的拯救——因为并不是人人都把这词用在故事本身上，而是用在从那些书信和他们自己的罪恶意识引出的某些推论上——我们就得相信关于神（God）的一些事，那些事对我们恰是福音的反面——不，是从地狱（hell）本身来的信息；我们就得去想象那样一件事，其可能性比他们的「好消息」也许能救我们脱离的任何灾祸更坏：我们必须先相信一位不义的神，好从他那里寻求庇护。不错，他们称他为义，却又说他作那在我里面最善的部分看来乃是不义之本质的事。他们会告诉我，我是凭肉体判断；我回答：那么主说「你们自己审量，什么是合理的」时，岂是向肉体呼吁？他岂不是那照亮一切生在世上之人的光？他们告诉我，我生在罪中，我知道那是真的；他们又告诉我，我受审判的严厉，与我若生在义（righteousness）中所受的一样，这一点我知道是假的。他们把神的纯洁与公正弄成一个后果：说他将按我们的罪性、而不是按我们的罪责来审判我们这些生在恶中的人——而那出生，我们并无责任。

===Original===

They tell me, or at least give me to understand, that every wrong thing I have done makes me subject to be treated as if I had done that thing with the free will of one who had in him no taint of evil﻿—when, perhaps, I did not at the time recognize the thing as evil, or recognized it only in the vaguest fashion. Is there any gospel in telling me that God is unjust, but that there is a way of deliverance from him? Show me my God unjust, and you wake in me a damnation from which no power can deliver me﻿—least of all God himself. It may be good news to such as are content to have a God capable of unrighteousness, if only he be on their side!
Who would not rejoice to hear from Matthew, or Mark, or Luke, what, in a few words, he meant by the word “gospel”﻿—or rather, what in the story of Jesus made him call it “good news”! Each would probably give a different answer to the question, all the answers consistent, and each a germ from which the others might be reasoned; but in the case of John, we have his answer to the question: he gives us in one sentence of two members, not indeed the gospel according to John, but the gospel according to Jesus Christ himself. He had often told the story of Jesus, the good news of what he was, and did, and said: what in it all did John look upon as the essence of the goodness of its news? In his gospel he gives us all “about” him, the message “concerning” him; now he tells us what in it makes it to himself and to us good news﻿—tells us the very goodness of the good news. It is not now his own message about Jesus, but the soul of that message﻿—that which makes it gospel﻿—the news Jesus brought concerning the Father, and gave to the disciples as his message for them to deliver to men. Throughout the story, Jesus, in all he does, and is, and says, is telling the news concerning his father, which he was sent to give to John and his companions, that they might hand it on to their brothers; but here, in so many words, John tells us what he himself has heard from The Word﻿—what in sum he has gathered from Jesus as the message he has to declare. He has received it in no systematic form; it is what a life, *the* life, what a man, *the* man, has taught him. The Word is the Lord; the Lord is the gospel. The good news is no fagot of sticks of a man’s gathering on the Sabbath.
Every man must read the Word for himself.

===Chinese===

他们告诉我，或者至少让我以为：我所作的每一件错事，都使我配受这样的对待，仿佛我作那事时，有着一个里面毫无邪恶污点的自由意志——而那时我也许根本不认为那事是恶的，或只是模模糊糊地认为。告诉我神不义、却有一条从他那里得救的路，这里头有什么福音？给我看一位不义的神，你就唤醒了我里面一个没有任何大能——神自己尤其不能——能救我脱离的定罪。对那些只要神站在他们一边、就甘心要一位能行不义之神的人来说，这也许是好消息！

谁不乐意听马太、或马可、或路加亲口用几句话说明，他所谓「福音」一词是什么意思——或者说，耶稣故事里的什么，使他称它为「好消息」呢！对这问题，各人的回答多半不同，而所有的回答彼此相合，每一个都是一粒胚芽，别个都可由此推演出来；至于约翰，我们手里就有他对这问题的回答：他用一句两个分句的话，给我们的不是照约翰所记的福音，而是照耶稣基督自己的福音。他常讲述耶稣的故事，讲述他所是、所行、所说的好消息：这一切之中，约翰把什么看作这消息之善的本质？在他的福音书里，他把关于他的一切告诉我们，那「论到」他的信息；如今他告诉我们，其中是什么使它对他、也对我们成为好消息——告诉我们那好消息的善之所在。如今不再是他自己关于耶稣的信息，而是那信息的灵魂——使它成为福音的那个——耶稣带来的关于父（the Father）的消息，是他交给门徒、叫他们传给人的。在整个故事里，耶稣在他的所行、所是、所说中，一直讲述着关于他父的消息，就是他奉差赐给约翰和他的同伴、叫他们传递给弟兄们的；但在这里，约翰用明明白白的话，告诉我们他自己从道（the Word）所听见的——他从耶稣所总括领受、必须宣告的信息是什么。他领受它时，它没有任何系统的形式；它是一个生命——*那*生命，一个人——*那*人——所教给他的。道就是主；主就是福音。这好消息不是一个人在安息日拾来的一捆柴。

每个人都必须自己读这道。

===Original===

One may read it in one shape, another in another: all will be right if it be indeed the Word they read, and they read it by the lamp of obedience. He who is willing to do the will of the Father shall know the truth of the teaching of Jesus. The spirit is “given to them that obey him.”
But let us hear how John reads the Word﻿—near what is John’s version of the gospel.
“This then is the message,” he says, “which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.” Ah, my heart, this is indeed the good news for thee! This is a gospel! If God be light, what more, what else can I seek than God, than God himself! Away with your doctrines! Away with your salvation from the “justice” of a God whom it is a horror to imagine! Away with your iron cages of false metaphysics! I am saved﻿—for God is light! My God, I come to thee. That thou shouldst be thyself is enough for time and eternity, for my soul and all its endless need. Whatever seems to me darkness, that I will not believe of my God. If I should mistake, and call that darkness which is light, will he not reveal the matter to me, setting it in the light that lighteth every man, showing me that I saw but the husk of the thing, not the kernel? Will he not break open the shell for me, and let the truth of it, his thought, stream out upon me? He will not let it hurt me to mistake the light for darkness, while I take not the darkness for light. The one comes from blindness of the intellect, the other from blindness of heart and will. I love the light, and will not believe at the word of any man, or upon the conviction of any man, that that which seems to me darkness is in God. Where would the good news be if John said, “God is light, but you cannot see his light; you cannot tell, you have no notion, what light is; what God means by light, is not what you mean by light; what God calls light may be horrible darkness to you, for you are of another nature from him!” Where, I say, would be the good news of that? It is true, the light of God may be so bright that we see nothing; but that is not darkness, it is infinite hope of light. It is true also that to the wicked “the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light”; but is that because the conscience of the wicked man judges of good and evil oppositely to the conscience of the good man?

===Chinese===

这个人可以读成这个样子，那个人读成那个样子：只要他们读的确实是道，又是在顺服（obedience）的灯下读的，就都是对的。凡愿意行父旨意的，必晓得耶稣教训的真实。那灵是「赐给顺从他之人的」。

但让我们听听约翰怎样读这道——约翰所领会的福音是什么说法。

「这就是我们从他所听见、又报给你们的信息，」他说，「就是神是光，在他毫无黑暗。」啊，我的心，这对你实在是好消息！这才是福音！神若就是光，除了神、除了神自己，我还能寻求什么、还寻求什么别的呢！你们的教义都去吧！你们那从一位想象起来令人恐怖之神的「公义」中得救的救法，也去吧！你们那些虚假形而上学的铁笼子，都去吧！我得救了——因为神是光！我的神啊，我到你这里来。你自己是光，这本身就足够填满时间与永恒、填满我的灵魂和我一切无尽的缺乏。凡在我看是黑暗的，我绝不相信它属于我的神。我若错了，把光称作黑暗，他岂不会向我显明这事，把它摆在那照亮一切人的光里，指给我看：我看见的不过是那东西的壳，不是核？他岂不会替我打开那壳，让它的真实、他的思想，倾流到我身上？只要我不把黑暗当光，他就不会叫我把光误当黑暗这件事伤害我。前者出于智性的失明，后者出于心与意志的失明。我爱光，无论谁的话、无论谁的信念，都不能叫我相信：那在我看来是黑暗的东西，在神里面。约翰若说「神是光，但你看不见他的光；你无法知道、无从想象光是什么；神所谓光，不是你所谓光；神称为光的，对你可能是可怕的黑暗，因为你与他性情不同」，那好消息又在哪里？我说，那好消息在哪里？不错，神的光可能亮得使我们什么也看不见；但那不是黑暗，那是光的无穷指望。不错，对恶人，「主的日子是黑暗，不是光」；但那是因为恶人的良心对善恶的判断，与善人的良心相反吗？

===Original===

When he says, “Evil, be thou my good,” he means by “evil” what God means by evil, and by “good” he means “pleasure.” He cannot make the meanings change places. To say that what our deepest conscience calls darkness may be light to God, is blasphemy; to say light in God and light in man are of differing kinds, is to speak against the spirit of light. God is light far beyond what we can see, but what we mean by light, God means by light; and what is light to God is light to us, or would be light to us if we saw it, and will be light to us when we do see it. God means us to be jubilant in the fact that he is light﻿—that he is what his children, made in his image, mean when they say “light”; that what in him is dark to them, is dark by excellent glory, by too much cause of jubilation; that, however dark it may be to their eyes, it is light even as they mean it, light for their eyes and souls and hearts to take in the moment they are enough of eyes, enough of souls, enough of hearts, to receive it in its very being. Living Light, thou wilt not have me believe anything dark of thee! thou wilt have me so sure of thee as to dare to say that is not of God which I see dark, see unlike the Master! If I am not honest enough, if the eye in me be not single enough to see thy light, thou wilt punish me, I thank thee, and purge my eyes from their darkness, that they may let the light in, and so I become an inheritor, with thy other children, of that light which is thy Godhead, and makes thy creatures need to worship thee. “In thy light we shall see light.”
All man will not, in our present imperfection, see the same light; but light is light notwithstanding, and what each does see, is his safety if he obeys it. In proportion as we have the image of Christ mirrored in us, we shall know what is and is not light. But never will anything prove to be light that is not of the same kind with that which we mean by light, with that in a thing which makes us call it light. The darkness yet left in us makes us sometimes doubt of a thing whether it be light or darkness; but when the eye is single, the whole body will be full of light.
To fear the light is to be untrue, or at least it comes of untruth. No being, for himself or for another, needs fear the light of God. Nothing can be in light inimical to our nature, which is of God, or to anything in us that is worthy.

===Chinese===

当他说「恶啊，你作我的善」时，他所谓「恶」，正是神所谓的恶；他所谓「善」，意思是「快乐」。他改变不了这两个意思的位置。说我们最深的良心所称的黑暗，在神也许是光，这是亵渎；说神里面的光与人里面的光种类不同，这是与光之灵作对。神是光，远超我们所能看见；但我们所谓光，神也就所谓光；在神是光的，在我们也是光——我们若看见它，就会是光；我们看见它时，就必是光。神要我们因他是光而欢腾——因他就是他的儿女——那按他形像造的儿女——说「光」时所意指的那位；那在他们看他里面显得暗的，是因极大的荣耀而暗，因欢呼的理由太多而暗；无论它在他们眼中多么暗，它正是他们所意指的那种光，等他们的眼睛、灵魂、心灵一足够成为眼睛、足够成为灵魂、足够成为心灵，能以承接它的本体时，它就是给他们眼睛、灵魂、心灵承接的光。永活的光啊，你必不要我相信你里面有任何黑暗！你必要我对你有把握，到一个地步，敢说我看为暗、看为不像主的，就不是出于神！我若不够诚实，我里面的眼睛不够单纯来看你的光，你必刑罚我——我感谢你——并洗去我眼中的黑暗，叫它们放进光来，这样我就与你别的儿女一同承受那光，就是你的神格、使你的受造者不能不敬拜你的那光。「在你的光中，我们必得见光。」

在我们如今的不完全里，不是人人都会看见同一个光；但光终究是光，各人所看见的，只要他顺从它，就是他的安全。基督的形像镜照在我们里面的程度越高，我们就越知道什么是光、什么不是光。但无论什么，若不是与我们所谓光——与那使我们对一件事物称它为光的那个东西——同类的，就永不会证明是光。我们里面还留下的黑暗，有时使我们怀疑一件事是光还是暗；但眼睛若单纯了，全身就必充满光。

怕光就是不真实，或至少是出于不真实。没有任何存在者——为他自己或为别人——需要怕神的光。光里面不可能有敌对我们本性——我们的本性出于神——或敌对我们里面任何配得之事的东西。

===Original===

All fear of the light, all dread lest there should be something dangerous in it, comes of the darkness still in those of us who do not love the truth with all our hearts; it will vanish as we are more and more interpenetrated with the light. In a word, there is no way of thought or action which we count admirable in man, in which God is not altogether adorable. There is no loveliness, nothing that makes man dear to his brother man, that is not in God, only it is infinitely better in God. He is God our saviour. Jesus is our saviour because God is our saviour. He is the God of comfort and consolation. He will soothe and satisfy his children better than any mother her infant. The only thing he will not give them is﻿—leave to stay in the dark. If a child cry, “I want the darkness,” and complain that he will not give it, yet he will not give it. He gives what his child needs﻿—often by refusing what he asks. If his child say, “I will not be good; I prefer to die; let me die!” his dealing with that child will be as if he said﻿—“No; I have the right to content you, not giving you your own will but mine, which is your one good. You shall not die; you shall live to thank me that I would not hear your prayer. You know what you ask, but not what you refuse.” There are good things God must delay giving until his child has a pocket to hold them﻿—till he gets his child to make that pocket. He must first make him fit to receive and to have. There is no part of our nature that shall not be satisfied﻿—and that not by lessening it, but by enlarging it to embrace an ever-enlarging enough.

===Chinese===

对光的一切惧怕、一切唯恐光里有什么危险的心情，都出于我们这些还未全心爱真理之人里面尚存的黑暗；随着光越来越多地渗透我们，它必要消失。总之一句话：凡是我们在人身上视为可敬的思想或行为方式，神在其中就全然可拜。没有一样可爱之处、没有一样使人对他弟兄显得宝贵的东西，不在神里面——只是在神里面，它是无限地更好。他是神我们的救主。耶稣是我们的救主，因为神是我们的救主。他是安慰与慰藉之神。他要安抚、满足他的儿女，胜过任何母亲安抚她的婴孩。只有一样东西他不给他们——留在黑暗里的许可。孩子若哭喊「我要黑暗」，抱怨他不给，他还是不给。他给孩子所需要的——常常是借着拒绝他所求的。他的孩子若说「我不要学好；我宁愿死；让我死吧！」他对待那孩子，就仿佛是说——「不；我有权叫你满足——不是给你你自己的意思，而是给你我的意思，那才是你唯一的善。你不可死；你要活着感谢我不肯应允你的祷告（prayer）。你知道你所求的是什么，却不知道你所拒绝的是什么。」有些好东西，神必须延迟再给，等他的孩子有一个口袋来装它们——等他使他的孩子作出那口袋。他必须先使他配得着、配拥有。我们的本性没有一部分将不得满足——而且不是借着削减它，而是借着扩大它，去拥抱一个不断扩大的足够。

===Original===

Come to God, then, my brother, my sister, with all thy desires and instincts, all thy lofty ideals, all thy longing for purity and unselfishness, all thy yearning to love and be true, all thy aspiration after self-forgetfulness and child-life in the breath of the Father; come to him with all thy weaknesses, all thy shames, all thy futilities; with all thy helplessness over thy own thoughts; with all thy failure, yea, with the sick sense of having missed the tide of true affairs; come to him with all thy doubts, fears, dishonesties, meannesses, paltrinesses, misjudgments, wearinesses, disappointments, and stalenesses: be sure he will take thee and all thy miserable brood, whether of draggle-winged angels, or covert-seeking snakes, into his care, the angels for life, the snakes for death, and thee for liberty in his limitless heart! For he is light, and in him is no darkness at all. If he were a king, a governor; if the name that described him were “The Almighty,” thou mightst well doubt whether there could be light enough in him for thee and thy darkness; but he is thy father, and more thy father than the word can mean in any lips but his who said, “my father and your father, my God and your God”; and such a father is light, an infinite, perfect light. If he were any less or any other than he is, and thou couldst yet go on growing, thou must at length come to the point where thou wouldst be dissatisfied with him; but he is light, and in him is no darkness at all. If anything seem to be in him that you cannot be content with, be sure that the ripening of thy love to thy fellows and to him, the source of thy being, will make thee at length know that anything else than just what he is would have been to thee an endless loss. Be not afraid to build upon the rock Christ, as if thy holy imagination might build too high and heavy for that rock, and it must give way and crumble beneath the weight of thy divine idea. Let no one persuade thee that there is in him a little darkness, because of something he has said which his creature interprets into darkness. The interpretation is the work of the enemy﻿—a handful of tares of darkness sown in the light. Neither let thy cowardly conscience receive any word as light because another calls it light, while it looks to thee dark. Say either the thing is not what it seems, or God never said or did it.

===Chinese===

那么，到神这里来吧，我的弟兄，我的姊妹，带着你一切的愿望与本能、一切崇高的理想、一切对纯洁与无私的渴慕、一切想要爱并想要真实的切望、一切在父的气息里对忘我与孩子生命的向往；带着你一切的软弱、一切的羞惭、一切的徒劳，带着你对自己心思的全然无助，带着你一切的失败——是的，带着那错过了真实事务之潮的病感；带着你一切的疑惑、惧怕、不诚、卑鄙、琐碎、误断、疲惫、失望与陈腐，到他这里来：要确信，他必把你和你那一窝可怜的东西——无论是拖着湿翅膀的天使，还是找隐蔽的蛇——都收进他的眷顾，天使为着生命，蛇为着死亡，而你，为着在他无限的心中得自由！因为他就是光，在他毫无黑暗。他若是一位君王、一位总督；若描写他的名字是「全能者」，你尽可以怀疑他里面是否有够你的黑暗用的光；但他是你的父，而且比这词在任何嘴唇上所能意指的更甚——除了在那说「我的父，也是你们的父；我的神，也是你们的神」者的嘴唇上；这样一位父就是光，无穷而完全的光。他若比他现在的所是更小一点、或别的什么，而你还能继续成长，你就必终于来到一个地步，对他不满；但他是光，在他毫无黑暗。他里面若有任何你不能满足的东西，要确信：你对你同伴、对你存在之本源的爱一旦成熟，就必使你至终知道，任何不是恰恰他所是的，对你都必是无尽的损失。不要怕在磐石基督上建造，仿佛你圣洁的想象会在这磐石上建得太高太重，它必在你这神圣观念的重压下崩塌。不要让任何人说服你，说他里面有一点点黑暗，因为他曾说过什么话，被他的受造者解成了黑暗。那解释是仇敌的工作——一把撒在光里的黑暗稗子。也不要让你那怯懦的良心，因为别人称之为光，就把任何一句话当作光领受下来，而它在你看来是暗的。你要说：要么这东西不是它看起来的那样，要么神从未说过、从未行过它。

===Original===

But, of all evils, to misinterpret what God does, and then say the thing as interpreted must be right because God does it, is of the devil. Do not try to believe anything that affects thee as darkness. Even if thou mistake and refuse something true thereby, thou wilt do less wrong to Christ by such a refusal than thou wouldst by accepting as his what thou canst see only as darkness. It is impossible thou art seeing a true, a real thing﻿—seeing it as it is, I mean﻿—if it looks to thee darkness. But let thy words be few, lest thou say with thy tongue what thou wilt afterward repent with thy heart. Above all things believe in the light, that it is what thou callest light, though the darkness in thee may give thee cause at a time to doubt whether thou art verily seeing the light.
“But there is another side to the matter: God is light indeed, but there *is* darkness; darkness is death, and men are in it.”
Yes; darkness is death, but not death to him that comes out of it.
It may sound paradoxical, but no man is condemned for anything he has done; he is condemned for continuing to do wrong. He is condemned for not coming out of the darkness, for not coming to the light, the living God, who sent the light, his son, into the world to guide him home. Let us hear what John says about the darkness.
For here also we have, I think, the word of the apostle himself: at the 13th verse he begins, I think, to speak in his own person. In the 19th verse he says, “And this is the condemnation,”﻿—not that men are sinners﻿—not that they have done that which, even at the moment, they were ashamed of﻿—not that they have committed murder, not that they have betrayed man or woman, not that they have ground the faces of the poor, making money by the groans of their fellows﻿—not for any hideous thing are they condemned, but that they will not leave such doings behind, and do them no more: “This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men” would not come out of the darkness to the light, but “loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Choosing evil, clinging to evil, loving the darkness because it suits with their deeds, therefore turning their backs on the inbreaking light, how can they but be condemned﻿—if God be true, if he be light, and darkness be alien to him!

===Chinese===

但是，在一切邪恶之中，曲解神的作为，然后说那被曲解的事必是对的、因为是神作的，这是出于魔鬼。不要努力去相信任何使你感受为黑暗的东西。即使你因此误拒了某样真实的东西，你这样拒绝给基督带来的错处，也比把你只能看作黑暗的东西当作他的来接受所带来的少。一件事若在你看来是黑暗，你就不可能看见一件真实的、真正的东西——我是说，照它的本相看见它。但你的话要少，免得你的舌头说了你日后要用心悔改的话。在一切事之上，要信这光——信它就是你称为光的那东西，尽管你里面的黑暗也许一时使你有理由怀疑，你是否真看见了光。

「但这事还有另一面：神确是光，但黑暗*是*存在的；黑暗就是死亡，而人正在其中。」

是的；黑暗是死亡，但对那从其中出来的人，不是死亡。

这话听来也许像悖论：没有一个人是因他已行过的事被定罪；他是因继续行恶被定罪。他被定罪，是因他不肯从黑暗里出来，不肯就了光——那永活的神——这里来；神已差那光、他的儿子，到世上来引导他回家。让我们听听约翰论到黑暗说了什么。

因为在这里，我想我们也有使徒自己的话：从第13节起，我想他是用自己的声音说话了。在第19节他说，「定他们的罪就是在此」——不是因他们是罪人——不是因他们作了那当时就使他们羞愧的事——不是因他们犯了凶杀，不是因他们出卖了男人或女人，不是因他们磨穷人的脸、靠同伴的呻吟赚钱——他们被定罪，不是为任何丑恶的事，而是因他们不肯撇下这些行为、不再去作：「光来到世间，世人却不肯从黑暗出来就光，倒爱黑暗，定他们的罪就是在此，因为他们的行为是恶的。」拣选恶、抓住恶、因黑暗合乎他们的行为而爱黑暗、因此背向那照进来的光——这样的人，怎能不被定罪呢——若神是真实的，若他是光，而黑暗于他是陌生之物！

===Original===

Whatever of honesty is in man, whatever of judgment is left in the world, must allow that their condemnation is in the very nature of things, that it must rest on them and abide.
But if one happens to utter some individual truth which another man has made into one of the cogs of his system, he is in danger of being supposed to accept all the toothed wheels and their relations in that system. I therefore go on to say that it does not follow, because light has come into the world, that it has fallen upon this or that man. He has his portion of the light that lighteth every man, but the revelation of God in Christ may not yet have reached him. A man might see and pass the Lord in a crowd, nor be to blame like the Jews of Jerusalem for not knowing him. A man like Nathanael might have started and stopped at the merest glimpse of him, but all growing men are not yet like him without guile. Everyone who has not yet come to the light is not necessarily keeping his face turned away from it. We dare not say that this or that man would not have come to the light had he seen it; we do not know that he will not come to the light the moment he does see it. God gives every man time. There is a light that lightens sage and savage, but the glory of God in the face of Jesus may not have shined on this sage or that savage. The condemnation is of those who, having seen Jesus, refuse to come to him, or pretend to come to him but do not the things he says. They have all sorts of excuses at hand; but as soon as a man begins to make excuse, the time has come when he might be doing that from which he excuses himself. How many are there not who, believing there is something somewhere with the claim of light upon them, go on and on to get more out of the darkness! This consciousness, all neglected by them, gives broad ground for the expostulation of the Lord﻿—“Ye will not come unto me that ye might have life!”
“All manner of sin and blasphemy,” the Lord said, “shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy against the spirit shall not be forgiven.” God speaks, as it were, in this manner: “I forgive you everything. Not a word more shall be said about your sins﻿—only come out of them; come out of the darkness of your exile; come into the light of your home, of your birthright, and do evil no more.

===Chinese===

人里面无论还剩多少诚实，世上无论还剩多少判断力，都必须承认：他们的定罪乃在事物的本性之中，必落在他们身上、存留。

但一个人若碰巧说出某一条单独的真理，而那真理已被另一个人做成了他体系里的一个齿轮，他就有被以为接受了那体系里全部齿轮及其啮合的危险。因此我接着说：光来到世间，并不等于光已照到这个人或那个人身上。他有他那一份照亮一切人的光，但神在基督里的启示也许还未到达他那里。一个人可能在人群中看见主、又走过去，而不像耶路撒冷的犹太人那样因不认识他而有罪。一个像拿但业（Nathanael）那样的人，也许会因最微弱的一瞥而震惊而停步；但一切正在成长的人，并非都像他那样没有诡诈。凡还未就光的，不一定都是把脸转离光的。我们不敢说，这个人或那个人若看见了光，也必不肯来；我们不知道，他一看见光，会不会立时就来。神给每个人时间。有一光，照亮哲人与野人；但神在耶稣脸上的荣耀，也许还未照到这个哲人或那个野人身上。被定罪的，是那些看见了耶稣却拒绝到他那里去的，或假装到他那里去、却不行他所说之事的人。他们手边有各式各样的借口；但一个人一开始找借口，他本可以去做那他借以推脱之事的时候就已经到了。有多少人不是这样——相信某处有个东西带着光对他们的主权要求，却继续又继续，要从黑暗里多捞一点！这被他们全然忽视的意识，给了主那责备广阔的根据——「你们不肯到我这里来得生命！」

「一切的罪和亵渎，」主说，「都可得赦免；惟独亵渎圣灵的，总不得赦免。」神仿佛是这样说话的：「我赦免你们的一切。你们的罪，一个字也不再提——只要从其中出来；从你们流亡的黑暗里出来；进到你们家中、你们生来权利的光里，不要再作恶。

===Original===

Lie no more; cheat no more; oppress no more; slander no more; envy no more; be neither greedy nor vain; love your neighbour as I love you; be my good child; trust in your father. I am light; come to me, and you shall see things as I see them, and hate the evil thing. I will make you love the thing which now you call good and love not. I forgive all the past.”
“I thank thee, Lord, for forgiving me, but I prefer staying in the darkness: forgive me that too.”
“No; that cannot be. The one thing that cannot be forgiven is the sin of choosing to be evil, of refusing deliverance. It is impossible to forgive that sin. It would be to take part in it. To side with wrong against right, with murder against life, cannot be forgiven. The thing that is past I pass, but he who goes on doing the same, annihilates this my forgiveness, makes it of no effect. Let a man have committed any sin whatever, I forgive him; but to choose to go on sinning﻿—how can I forgive that? It would be to nourish and cherish evil! It would be to let my creation go to ruin. Shall I keep you alive to do things hateful in the sight of all true men? If a man refuse to come out of his sin, he must suffer the vengeance of a love that would be no love if it left him there. Shall I allow my creature to be the thing my soul hates?”
There is no excuse for this refusal. If we were punished for every fault, there would be no end, no respite; we should have no quiet wherein to repent; but God passes by all he can. He passes by and forgets a thousand sins, yea, tens of thousands, forgiving them all﻿—only we must begin to be good, begin to do evil no more. He who refuses must be punished and punished﻿—punished through all the ages﻿—punished until he gives way, yields, and comes to the light, that his deeds may be seen by himself to be what they are, and be by himself reproved, and the Father at last have his child again. For the man who in this world resists to the full, there may be, perhaps, a whole age or era in the history of the universe during which his sin shall not be forgiven; but *never* can it be forgiven until he repents. How can they who will not repent be forgiven, save in the sense that God does and will do all he can to make them repent? Who knows but such sin may need for its cure the continuous punishment of an aeon?

不要再撒谎；不要再欺哄；不要再压榨；不要再毁谤；不要再嫉妒；不要贪婪，不要虚荣；要爱你的邻舍，像我爱你们那样；作我的好孩子；信靠你的父。我就是光；到我这里来，你们就必看见事物如同我看见它们的那样，恨恶那恶的东西。我要叫你们爱那你们如今称为善却不爱的东西。过往的一切，我都赦免。」

「主啊，我感谢你赦免我，但我宁愿留在黑暗里：这个也请你赦免。」

「不；那不能。唯一不能赦免的罪，就是拣选作恶、拒绝拯救的罪。赦免那罪是不可能的。赦免它，就是与它有分。站在错的一边敌对对的一边，站在凶杀的一边敌对生命，是不能得赦免的。已过的事我放过，但那继续行同样之事的人，就把我这赦免消灭了，使它归于无效。一个人无论犯过什么罪，我都赦免他；但拣选继续犯罪——这个我怎能赦免呢？赦免它，就是养育恶、珍爱恶！就是任凭我的创造走向毁灭。我岂可留你活着，去行一切真实之人眼中可憎的事呢？人若拒绝从他的罪里出来，他就必受一种爱的报应——那爱若留他在那里，就不再是爱。我岂可容许我的受造者，作我灵魂所恨的那种东西？」

这拒绝没有借口。我们若每件过犯都受刑罚，就永无止境、永无喘息；我们就再没有安然悔改的余地；但神放过一切他能放过的。他放过、忘记千样的罪，不，几万样，全部赦免——只要我们开始变好，开始不再作恶。那拒绝的人，必受刑罚又受刑罚——在整个世代里受刑罚——受刑罚直到他让步、屈服、来到光中，叫他的行为被他自己看见是它们本来的样子、被他自己责备，父也终久得回他的孩子。对那在今世顽抗到底的人，在宇宙的历史中也许有一整个世代或纪元，其间他的罪不得赦免；但直到他悔改，那罪*总*不能得赦免。那不肯悔改的人，除非在「神正在并必将作他所能作的一切叫他们悔改」这个意义上，怎能得赦免呢？谁知道呢——这样的罪，其医治或许需要一个永世之久的持续刑罚？

===Original===

There are three conceivable kinds of punishment﻿—first, that of mere retribution, which I take to be entirely and only human﻿—therefore, indeed, more properly inhuman, for that which is not divine is not essential to humanity, and is of evil, and an intrusion upon the human; second, that which works repentance; and third, that which refines and purifies, working for holiness. But the punishment that falls on whom the Lord loveth because they have repented, is a very different thing from the punishment that falls on those whom he loveth in deed but cannot forgive because they hold fast by their sins.
There are also various ways in which the word “forgive” can be used. A man might say to his son﻿—“My boy, I forgive you. You did not know what you were doing. I will say no more about it.” Or he might say﻿—“My boy, I forgive you; but I must punish you, for you have done the same thing several times, and I must make you remember.” Or, again, he might say﻿—“I am seriously angry with you. I cannot forgive you. I must punish you severely. The thing was too shameful! I cannot pass it by.” Or, once more, he might say﻿—“Except you alter your ways entirely, I shall have nothing more to do with you. You need not come to me. I will not take the responsibility of anything you do. So far from answering for you, I shall feel bound in honesty to warn my friends not to put confidence in you. Never, never, till I see a greater difference in you than I dare hope to see in this world, will I forgive you. I can no more regard you as one of the family. I would die to save you, but I cannot forgive you. There is nothing in you now on which to rest forgiveness. To say, I forgive you, would be to say, Do anything you like; I do not care what you do.” So God may forgive and punish; and he may punish and not forgive, that he may rescue. To forgive the sin against the holy spirit would be to damn the universe to the pit of lies, to render it impossible for the man so forgiven ever to be saved. He cannot forgive the man who will not come to the light because his deeds are evil. Against that man his fatherly heart is *moved with indignation*.

===Chinese===

可以设想有三类刑罚——第一，纯报应性的，我认为那全然只是属人的——因此，其实更恰当说是非人的，因为凡不属神的，就不属于人性的本质，乃是出于恶，是对人性的侵扰；第二，那作成悔改的；第三，那炼净与纯净、作成圣洁的。但那因他们已经悔改而临到主所爱之人身上的刑罚，与那临到他确实爱、却因他们紧抓住罪而不能赦免之人身上的刑罚，是大不相同的。

「赦免」一词也有几种用法。一个人可以对他的儿子说——「孩子，我饶恕你。你不知道自己在作什么。这事我不再说了。」他也可以说——「孩子，我饶恕你；但我必须刑罚你，因为同样的事你已经作过好几回，我必须叫你记住。」他又可以说——「我真地对你发怒。我不能饶恕你。我必须重重刑罚你。这事太可耻了！我不能放过它。」他还可以说——「除非你彻底改换你的行径，我与你再无干系。你不必到我这里来。你作任何事，我都不担责任。我非但不替你担保，还觉得诚然有义务警告我的朋友，不要信任你。直到我看见你身上有一个我不敢指望在今生看见的更大改变，我永不、永不饶恕你。我不能再把你当作家里的一员。我愿意舍命救你，但我不能饶恕你。你如今里面没有任何可供饶恕立足的东西。说我饶恕你，就等于说：你随便作什么都可以；你作什么我都不在乎。」神可以这样又赦免又刑罚；他也可以刑罚而不赦免，为的是拯救。赦免那对圣灵的罪，就是咒诅宇宙坠入谎言的坑，就是叫那被如此赦免的人永远不可能得救。他不能赦免那因行为是恶而不肯就光的人。对那个人，他作父的心是*动了义怒*。

### The Displeasure of Jesus / 耶稣的不悦
===Original===

> When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled.

Grimm, in his lexicon to the New Testament, after giving as the equivalent of the word *ἐμβριμάομαι* in pagan use, “I am moved with anger,” “I roar or growl,” “I snort at,” “I am vehemently angry or indignant with someone,” tells us that in Mark 1:43, and Matthew 9:30, it has a meaning different from that of the pagans, namely, “I command with severe admonishment.” That he has any authority for saying so, I do not imagine, and believe the statement a blunder. The Translators and Revisers, however, have in those passages used the word similarly, and in one place, the passage before us, where a true version is of yet more consequence, have taken another liberty and rendered the word “groaned.” The Revisers, at the same time, place in the margin what I cannot but believe its true meaning﻿—“was moved with indignation.”
Let us look at all the passages in which the word is used of the Lord, and so, if we may, learn something concerning him. The only place in the gospel where it is used of any but the Lord is Mark 14:5. Here both versions say of the disciples that they “murmured at” the waste of the ointment by one of the women who anointed the Lord. With regard to this rendering I need only remark that surely “murmured at” can hardly be strong enough, especially seeing “they had indignation among themselves” at the action.
It is indeed right and necessary to insist that many a word must differ in moral weight and colour as used of or by persons of different character. The anger of a good man is a very different thing from the anger of a bad man; the displeasure of Jesus must be a very different thing from the displeasure of a tyrant. But they are both anger, both displeasure, nevertheless. We have no right to change a root-meaning, and say in one case that a word means “he was indignant,” in another that it means “he straitly or strictly charged,” and in a third that it means “he groaned.” Surely not thus shall we arrive at the truth! If any statement is made, any word employed, that we feel unworthy of the Lord, let us refuse it; let us say, “I do not believe that”; or, “There must be something there that I cannot see into: I must wait; it cannot be what it looks to me, and be true of the Lord!”

===Chinese===

> 耶稣看见她哭，并看见与她同来的犹太人也哭，就心里悲叹，又甚忧愁。

格里姆在他那部新约词典里，先给出 *ἐμβριμάομαι* 一词在异教用法中的对应义——「我动了怒气」「我吼叫或咆哮」「我对……喷鼻息」「我对某人激烈地发怒或愤慨」——然后告诉我们，在马可福音1:43和马太福音9:30，它有一个不同于异教徒的意思，即「我带着严厉的告诫吩咐」。我不认为他这样说有什么根据，并且相信这陈述是一个错误。然而，译经者与修订者在那些经文里都同样用了那样的译法，而在另一处——就是摆在我们眼前的这段，一个真实译法更关系重大的地方——又取了另一重自由，把这个词译作「悲叹」。修订者同时把我不信不是其真义的——「动了义怒」——放在页边。

让我们看看所有用这个词说到主的经文，这样，倘若可以，我们就能学到一点关于他的事。福音书里唯一一处把这词用在主以外之人身上的，是马可福音14:5。在那里，两个译本都说，对于一位膏主之女人枉费香膏的事，门徒们「向她发怨言」。就这译法我只需指出：「向她发怨言」恐怕不够强，尤其看到他们「彼此动了怒气」。

坚持许多词在用于或出自不同品格之人时，必须在道德分量与色彩上不同，这确实是对的、也是必需的。好人的怒与坏人的怒是很不同的东西；耶稣的不悦必与暴君的不悦很不同。但它们两者都是怒，都是不悦。我们无权更改一个根义，说这处这词的意思是「他动了义怒」，那处是「他严严地嘱咐」，第三处是「他悲叹」。我们必不能因此达到真理！若有任何陈述、任何用词，我们觉得配不上主，就让我们拒绝它；让我们说：「我不信这个」；或说：「那里必有我看不透的东西：我必须等候；它不可能既是我看起来的样子，又是属于主的真实！」

===Original===

But to accept the word as used of the Lord, and say it means something quite different from what it means when used by the same writer of someone else, appears to me untruthful.
We shall take first the passage, Mark 1:43﻿—in the authorized version, “And he straitly charged him”; in the revised, “And he strictly charged him,” with “sternly” in the margin. Literally, as it seems to me, it reads, and ought to be read, “And being angry” or “displeased” or “vexed” “with him, he immediately dismissed him.” There is even some dissatisfaction implied, I think, in the word I have translated “dismissed.” The word in John 9:34, “they cast him out,” is the same, only a little intensified.
This adds something to the story, and raises the question, Why should Jesus have been angry? If we can find no reason for his anger, we must leave the thing as altogether obscure; for I do not know where to find another meaning for the word, except in the despair of a would-be interpreter.
Jesus had cured the leper﻿—not with his word only, which would have been enough for the mere cure, but was not enough without the touch of his hand﻿—the Sinaitic version says “his hands”﻿—to satisfy the heart of Jesus﻿—a touch defiling him, in the notion of the Jews, but how cleansing to the sense of the leper! The man, however, seems to have been unworthy of this delicacy of divine tenderness. The Lord, who could read his heart, saw that he made him no true response﻿—that there was not awaked in him the faith he desired to rouse: he had not drawn the soul of the man to his. The leper was jubilant in the removal of his pain and isolating uncleanness, in his deliverance from suffering and scorn; he was probably elated with the pride of having had a miracle wrought for *him*. In a word, he was so full of himself that he did not think truly of his deliverer.
The Lord, I say, saw this, or something of this kind, and was not satisfied. He had wanted to give the man something so much better than a pure skin, and had only roused in him an unseemly delight in his own cleanness﻿—*unseemly*, for it was such that he paid no heed to the Lord, but immediately disobeyed his positive command. The moral position the man took was that which displeased the Lord, made him angry. He saw in him positive and rampant self-will and disobedience, an impertinent assurance and self-satisfaction.

===Chinese===

但接受这个词用在主身上，又说它在此的意思与同一位作者用在别人身上时的意思大不相同，在我看来是不诚实的。

我们先看马可福音1:43——钦定本作「耶稣严严地嘱咐他」；修订本作「耶稣切切地嘱咐他」，页边注作「严厉地」。照我看，按字面它读作、也应当读作：「耶稣*恼怒*他」——或「不悦」他，或「对他动气」——「就立刻打发他走」。我想，连那个我译作「打发」的词里，也含着几分不满。约翰福音9:34「他们把他赶出去」用的正是这个词，只是稍加强化。

这给故事添了一点东西，也引出了问题：耶稣为什么会动怒？我们若找不出他动怒的理由，就只能把这事当作全然隐晦的；因为除了在自命解经者的绝望里，我不知道还能到哪里为这词另找一个意思。

耶稣治好了那长大麻风的——不只用他的话，单单一句话对治病本身原已足够，却不足以满足耶稣的心，还必须有他手的触摸——西乃抄本作「他的双手」——那触摸在犹太人的观念里叫他染了污秽，对麻风病人的感觉却是何等的洁净！然而这人似乎配不上这神圣温柔的体贴。那能读人心的主，看出他没有给他真实的回应——他里面没有唤醒他所要唤醒的信心：他没有把这人的灵魂吸引到自己的灵魂这里来。那麻风病人为他疼痛与隔绝之不洁的除去而欢腾，为他脱离苦难与轻蔑而欢腾；他多半还因居然有神迹为*他*行出来而傲然自得。总而言之，他满了自己，以致对他的拯救者没有真实的想念。

我说，主看出了这个，或这一类的事，并不满足。他本想给这人一样远比洁净皮肤更好的东西，却只在他里面激起了一种对自己的洁净不合宜的欢喜——*不合宜*，因为它叫他全不理会主，立刻违背了主明确的命令。这人所取的道德立场，就是那使主不悦、使他动怒的。主在他身上看见猖獗而公然的任性与悖逆，看见无礼的自恃与自满。

===Original===

Filled, not with pure delight, or the childlike merriment that might well burst forth, mingled with tears, at such deliverance; filled, not with gratitude, but gratification, the keener that he had been so long an object of loathing to his people; filled with arrogance because of the favour shown to him, of all men, by the great prophet, and swelling with boast of the same, he left the presence of the healer to thwart his will, and, commanded to tell no man, at once “began”﻿—the frothy, volatile, talking soul﻿—“to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was without in desert places.”
Let us next look at the account of the healing of the two blind men, given in the ninth chapter of Matthew’s gospel. In both the versions the same phrases are used in translation of the word in question, as in the story of the leper in Mark’s gospel﻿—“straitly,” “strictly,” “sternly charged them.” I read the passage thus: “And Jesus was displeased”﻿—or, perhaps, “much displeased”﻿—“with them, saying, See that no man know it.”
“But they went forth, and spread abroad his fame in all that land.” Surely here we have light on the cause of Jesus’ displeasure with the blind men! it was the same with them as with the leper: they showed themselves bent on their own way, and did not care for his. Doubtless they were, in part, all of them moved by the desire to spread abroad his fame; that may even have seemed to them the best acknowledgment they could render their deliverer. They never suspected that a great man might desire to avoid fame, laying no value upon it, knowing it for a foolish thing. They did not understand that a man desirous of helping his fellows might yet avoid a crowd as obstructive to his object. “What is a prophet without honour?” such virtually ask, nor understand the answer, “A man the more likely to prove a prophet.” These men would repay their healer with trumpeting, not obedience. By them he should have his right﻿—but as they not be judged fit! In his modesty he objected, but they would take care he should not go without his reward! Through them he should reap the praises of men! “Not tell!” they exclaim. “Indeed, we will tell!” They were too grateful not to rumour him, not grateful enough to obey him.
We cannot surely be amazed at their self-sufficiency.

===Chinese===

他里面充满的不是纯粹的喜乐——那样的拯救原可以叫孩子气的欢愉与泪水一同迸发——不是感谢，而是自得，而且因他久为自己百姓所厌弃而愈发尖锐；他因那位大先知在万人中独独恩待自己而狂傲，又为此涨满，就离开医治者的面前去挫败他的意思，受嘱不可告诉人，却随即「开始」——那轻浮善变、多话的灵魂——「宣传开来，把这件事传扬出去，以致耶稣不得再明明地进城，只好在外边旷野地方」。

其次让我们看马太福音第九章中医好两个瞎子的记载。两个译本在这词的翻译上，都与马可福音麻风病人的故事用了同样的短语——「严严地」「切切地」「严厉地嘱咐他们」。我这样读这段经文：「耶稣就*不悦*他们」——或作「大大不悦他们」——「说，你们要小心，不可叫人知道。」「但他们出去，竟把他的名声传遍了那地方。」无疑，这里我们就看见了耶稣对两个瞎子不悦的原因之光！他们的情形与那麻风病人一样：他们显出一心走自己的路，不理会他的路。无疑，他们——三人都是——也部分出于传扬他名声的愿望；这愿望在他们看，甚至可能是他们能给拯救者的最好报答。他们从未想到，一个大人物可能渴望避开名声，不把它放在眼里，知道那是件愚蠢的东西。他们不明白，一个渴望帮助同伴的人，可能仍然避开人群，因为人群阻碍他的目标。「没有尊荣的先知算什么先知？」他们实际上这样问，也不懂得那回答：「一个更有可能证明是先知的人。」这些人要用吹喇叭来偿还他们的医治者，而不是用顺服（obedience）。他们要叫他得着他的权利——却要照他们判定合适的方式！他以谦卑推辞，他们却要负责叫他不至没有报酬！他们要叫他借他们收割人的称赞！「不告诉！」他们喊道，「我们偏要告诉！」他们太感谢他了，不能不去传扬他；又感谢得不够，不肯顺服他。

我们对他们的自满，当然不会惊奇。

===Original===

How many are there not who seem capable of anything for the sake of the church or Christianity, except the one thing its Lord cares about﻿—that they should do what he tells them! He would deliver them from themselves into the liberty of the sons of God, make them his brothers; they leave him to vaunt their church. His commandments are not grievous; they invent commandments for him, and lay them, burdens grievous to be borne, upon the necks of their brethren. God would have us sharers in his bliss﻿—in the very truth of existence; they worship from afar, and will not draw nigh. It was not, I think, the obstruction to his work, not the personal inconvenience it would cause him, that made the Lord angry, but that they would not be his friends, would not do what he told them, would not be the children of his father, and help him to save their brethren. When Peter in his way next﻿—much the same way as theirs﻿—opposed the will of the Father, saying, “That be far from thee, Lord!” he called him Satan, and ordered him behind him.
Does it affect anyone to the lowering of his idea of the Master that he should ever be angry? If so, I would ask him whether his whole conscious experience of anger be such, that he knows but one kind of anger. There is a good anger and a bad anger. There is a wrath of God, and there is a wrath of man that worketh not the righteousness of God. Anger may be as varied as the colour of the rainbow. God’s anger can be nothing but Godlike, therefore divinely beautiful, at one with his love, helpful, healing, restoring; yet is it verily and truly what we call anger. How different is the anger of one who loves, from that of one who hates! yet is anger anger. There is the degraded human anger, and the grand, noble, eternal anger. Our anger is in general degrading, because it is in general impure.
It is to me an especially glad thought that the Lord came so near us as to be angry with us. The more we think of Jesus being angry with us, the more we feel that we must get nearer and nearer to him﻿—get within the circle of his wrath, out of the sin that makes him angry, and near to him where sin cannot come. There is no quenching of his love in the anger of Jesus. The anger of Jesus is his recognition that we are to blame; if we were not to blame, Jesus could never be angry with us; we should not be of his kind, therefore not subject to his blame.

===Chinese===

有多少人不是这样：为了教会或基督教，似乎什么都肯作，唯独不著作它的主所在乎的那一件事——行他所吩咐他们的！他要救他们脱离自己、进入神众子的自由，使他们作他的弟兄；他们撇下他，去夸耀他们的教会。他的诫命不是难担的；他们倒替他发明诫命，把它们当作难担的重担，搁在他们弟兄的颈项上。神（God）要我们与他同享福气——同享存在的真实本身；他们却远远地敬拜，不肯亲近。我想，使主动怒的，不是对他工作的拦阻，不是那要带给他的个人不便，而是他们不肯作他的朋友，不肯行他所吩咐的，不肯作他父的儿女、帮他拯救他们的弟兄。当彼得（Peter）随后以他的方式——与他们的方式大同小异——敌挡父（the Father）的旨意，说「主啊，万不可如此！」时，他称他撒但，吩咐他退到他后边去。

耶稣竟然会动怒，这会不会叫谁降低他对主的想法？若会，我要问他：他全部有意识的动怒经验，是不是只有一种怒？怒有好的怒，有坏的怒。有神的忿怒，也有那不成就神之义（righteousness）的人的忿怒。怒可以像彩虹的颜色那样多样。神的怒只能是神样的，因此是神圣地美的，与他的爱为一，有帮助、医治、复原；然而它确确实实是我们所称的怒。爱者的怒与恨者的怒何等不同！然而怒就是怒。有堕落的人怒，也有宏大、高贵、永恒的怒。我们的怒通常是堕落的，因为它通常是不洁的。

对我来说，这是一个特别可喜的想法：主来到这么近的地方，近到会向我们动怒。我们越多想到耶稣向我们动怒，就越觉得我们必须越来越靠近他——进入他怒气的圈子里，脱离那使他动怒的罪，靠近那罪不能到的地方。耶稣的怒里没有他的爱熄灭。耶稣的怒，是他承认我们当受责备；我们若不当受责备，耶稣就永不能向我们动怒；我们就不是他的同类，因此不属他责备的范围。

===Original===

To recognize that we are to blame, is to say that we ought to be better, that we are able to do right if we will. We are able to turn our faces to the light, and come out of the darkness; the Lord will see to our growth.
It is a serious thought that the disobedience of the men he had set free from blindness and leprosy should be able to hamper him in his work for his father. But his best friends, his lovers did the same. That he should be crucified was a horror to them; they would have made him a king, and ruined his father’s work. He preferred the cruelty of his enemies to the kindness of his friends. The former with evil intent wrought his father’s will; the latter with good intent would have frustrated it. His disciples troubled him with their unbelieving expostulations. Let us know that the poverty of our idea of Jesus﻿—how much more our disobedience to him!﻿—thwarts his progress to victory, delays the coming of the kingdom of heaven. Many a man valiant for Christ, but not understanding him, and laying on himself and his fellows burdens against nature, has therein done will-worship and would-be service for which Christ will give him little thanks, which indeed may now be moving his holy anger. Where we do that we ought not, and could have helped it, be moved to anger against us, O Christ! do not treat us as if we were not worth being displeased with; let not our faults pass as if they were of no weight. Be angry with us, holy brother, wherein we are to blame; where we do not understand, have patience with us, and open our eyes, and give us strength to obey, until at length we are the children of the Father even as thou. For though thou art lord and master and saviour of them that are growing, thou art perfect lord only of the true and the safe and the free, who live in thy light and are divinely glad: we keep thee back from thy perfect lordship. Make us able to be angry and not sin; to be angry nor seek revenge the smallest; to be angry and full of forgiveness. We will not be content till our very anger is love.
The Lord did not call the leprosy to return and seize again upon the man who disobeyed him. He may have deserved it, but the Lord did not do it. He did not wrap the self-confident seeing men in the cloud of their old darkness because they wrapped themselves in the cloud of disobedience. He let them go.

===Chinese===

承认我们当受责备，就是说我们本该更好，就是说我们若愿意就能行对。我们能够把脸转向光，从黑暗里出来；成长的事，主自会看顾。

一个严肃的思想是：那些他已使其脱离瞎眼与麻风的人，他们的悖逆竟能阻碍他为父所作的工。但他最好的朋友、爱他的人也作了同样的事。他被钉十字架，在他们是大恐怖；他们却要立他作王，毁掉他父的工作。他宁取仇敌的残忍，不要朋友的善意。前者怀着恶意成全了他父的旨意；后者怀着善意倒要挫折它。他的门徒以他们不信的劝责搅扰他。让我们知道：我们对耶稣观念的贫乏——何况我们对他的悖逆！——阻碍他迈向胜利的进程，耽延天国（the kingdom）的来临。多少人为基督奋勇，却不认识他，把违背本性的重担加在自己和同伴身上，就在其中行了基督不会怎么感谢的意愿敬拜与自拟事奉——那事奉如今反倒可能正牵动他圣洁的怒气。基督啊，在我们行了不该行、又本可以不行的事上，求你向我们动怒！不要待我们，仿佛我们不配你不悦；不要让我们的过错白白过去，仿佛毫无分量。圣洁的兄长啊，在我们当受责备的事上向我们动怒；在我们不明白的事上，容忍我们，开我们的眼睛，赐我们顺服的力量，直到末了我们像你那样作父的儿女。因为你的确是成长之人的主、夫子与救主，但你只对那些真实、安稳而自由、住在你的光中、神圣地喜乐的人，才是完全的主：是我们拦阻了你完全的主权。使我们能够动怒而不犯罪；动怒而不寻求最小的报复；动怒而满有赦免。直到我们的怒本身就是爱，我们总不满足。

主没有叫麻风回头再抓住那个悖逆他的人。他也许配得那样，但主没有那样作。他没有因那两个自信的得见者裹在不顺服的云里，就把他们重新裹进他们旧日的黑暗之云里。他由他们去了。

===Original===

Of course they failed of their well-being by it; for to say a man might disobey and be none the worse, would be to say that “no” may be “yes,” and light sometimes darkness; it would be to say that the will of God is not man’s bliss. But the Lord did not directly punish them, any more than he does tens of thousands of wrongs in the world. Many wrongs punish themselves against the bosses of armed law; many wrongdoers cut themselves, like the priests of Baal, with the knives of their own injustice; and it is his will it should be so; but, whether he punish directly or indirectly, he is always working to deliver. I think sometimes his anger is followed, yea, accompanied by an astounding gift, fresh from his heart of grace. He knows what to do, for he is love. He is love when he gives, and love when he withholds; love when he heals, and love when he slays. Lord, if thus thou lookest upon men in thine anger, what must a full gaze be from thine eyes of love!
Let us now look at the last case in which this word *ἐμβριμάομαι* is used in the story of our Lord﻿—that form of it, at least, which we have down here, for sure they have a fuller gospel in the Father’s house, and without spot of blunder in it: let us so use that we have that we be allowed at length to look within the leaves of the other!
In the authorized version of the gospel of John, the eleventh chapter, the thirty-third verse, we have the words: “When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit and was troubled”;﻿—according to the margin of the revised version, “he was moved with indignation in the spirit, and troubled himself.” Also in the thirty-eighth verse we read, according to the margin of the revised version, “Jesus therefore again being moved with indignation in himself cometh to the tomb.”
Indignation﻿—anger at the very tomb! in the presence of hearts torn by the loss of a brother four days dead, whom also he loved! Yes, verily, friends! such indignation, such anger as, at such a time, in such a place, it was eternally right the heart of Jesus should be moved withal. I can hardly doubt that he is in like manner moved by what he sees now at the deathbeds and graves of not a few who are not his enemies, and yet in the presence of death seem no better than pagans. What have such gained by being the Christians they say they are?

===Chinese===

当然，他们因此失去了他们的福祉；因为说一个人可以悖逆而无损失，就等于说「不」可以是「是」，光有时可以是暗；就等于说神的旨意（the will of God）不是人的福气。但主没有直接刑罚他们，正如他没有直接刑罚世上成千上万的恶行。许多恶行顶在武装律法的凸出处，自己刑罚了自己；许多作恶的人，像巴力的祭司那样，用自己不义的刀割伤自己；他愿意事情如此；但无论他是直接还是间接刑罚，他总是在作拯救的工。我想，有时他的怒气之后——不，是与他的怒气同来——有一件惊人的恩赐，新鲜地出自他的恩典之心。他知道该怎样行，因为他是爱。他给的时候是爱，他留的时候也是爱；他医治的时候是爱，他击杀的时候也是爱。主啊，你若在怒中这样看人，你爱的眼睛一次全然的凝视，又该是怎样！

现在让我们看 *ἐμβριμάομαι* 这个词用在主的故事里的最后一处——至少是我们在此间所有的那个形式；因为在父的家里，他们必有更完全的福音，其中毫无错谬的斑点：让我们这样使用我们所拥有的，好叫我们至终获准翻开另一本的册页！在钦定本约翰福音第十一章33节，我们有这些话：「耶稣看见她哭，并看见与她同来的犹太人也哭，就心里悲叹，又甚忧愁」——照修订本的页边注，是「他在心里动了义怒，自己烦乱」。同样，在第38节，照修订本页边注，我们读到：「耶稣又心里动怒，来到坟墓前。」

义怒——在坟墓前动怒！在那些因失去死了四天的兄弟——那也是他所爱的——而心碎的人面前！是的，真是这样，朋友们！这样的义怒、这样的怒，在那样的时刻、那样的地方，耶稣的心被它激动，是永远正当的。我几乎不能怀疑，如今在许多并非他仇敌之人的病榻与坟墓前，他也被他所见的同样激动——这些人在死亡面前，显得不比异教徒更好。这样的人，作他们自称的基督徒，得了什么呢？

===Original===

They fix their eyes on a grisly phantasm they call Death, and never lift them to the radiant Christ standing by bed or grave! For them Christ has not conquered Death:

> Thou art our king, O Death! to thee we groan!

===Chinese===

他们的眼睛钉在一个他们称为死亡的狰狞幽灵上，从不举起来，望一望那站在病榻或坟墓旁、发光的基督！对他们来说，基督并没有征服死亡：

> 死亡啊，你是我们的王！我们向你呻吟！

===Original===

They would shudder at the thought of saying so in words; they say it in the bitterness of their tears, in their eyes of despair, in their black garments, in their instant retreat from the light of day to burrow in the bosom of darkness? “What, would you have us not weep?” Weep freely, friends; but let your tears be those of expectant Christians, not hopeless pagans. Let us look at the story.
The Lord had all this time been trying to teach his friends about his father﻿—what a blessed and perfect father he was, who had sent him that men might look on his very likeness, and know him greater than any likeness could show him; and all they had gained by it seemed not to amount to an atom of consolation when the touch of death came. He had said hundreds of things to Martha and Mary that are not down in the few pages of our earthly gospel; but the fact that God loves them, and that God has Lazarus, seems nothing to them because they have not Lazarus! The Lord himself, for all he has been to them, cannot console them, even with his bodily presence, for the bodily absence of their brother. I do not mean that God would have even his closest presence make us forget or cease to desire that of our friend. God forbid! The love of God is the perfecting of every love. He is not the God of oblivion, but of eternal remembrance. There is no past with him. So far is he from such jealousy as we have all heard imputed to him, his determination is that his sons and daughters shall love each other perfectly. He gave us to each other to belong to each other forever. He does not give to take away; with him is no variableness or shadow of turning. But if my son or daughter be gone from me for a season, should not the coming of their mother comfort me? Is it nothing that he who is the life should be present, assuring the well-being of the life that has vanished, and the well-being of the love that misses it? Why should the Lord have come to the world at all, if these his friends were to take no more good of him than this? Having the elder brother, could they not do for a little while without the younger? Must they be absolutely miserable without him? All their cry was, “Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died!” You may say they did not know Christ well enough yet. That is plain﻿—but Christ had expected more of them, and was disappointed.

===Chinese===

用言语这样说，他们会战栗；他们却用眼泪的苦味这样说，用绝望的眼睛这样说，用他们的黑衣这样说，用他们即时从日光中退去、钻进黑暗胸怀里的举动这样说。「怎么，难道你要我们不哭吗？」尽管哭吧，朋友们；但要让你们的眼泪是那期盼之基督徒的眼泪，不是无望之异教徒的眼泪。让我们看这故事。

主这段时间一直在设法教导他的朋友关于他父的事——他是何等有福、何等完全的父，差他来，叫人得瞻仰他自己的本像，并认识他大于任何形像所能显示的；而死亡一触，这一切在他们身上所得的，竟似乎抵不上一点安慰。他曾对马大和马利亚说过成百件事，没有记在我们地上福音书那几页里；但神爱他们、神有拉撒路这个事实，在他们看竟算不得什么，因为他们没有拉撒路！主自己，尽管他曾是他的一切，也无法安慰她们——甚至用他身体的同在，也补不上她们兄弟身体的不在。我并不是说，神要他最亲近的同在使我们忘记或不再渴望我们朋友的同在。断乎不可！神的爱是每一样爱的成全。他不是遗忘的神，乃是永远记念的神。在他没有过去。他远不是我们人人都听见人归给他的那种嫉妒，他的定意乃是要他的儿女彼此完全地相爱。他使我们彼此相属，永远相属。他给不是为夺去；在他没有改变，也没有转动的影儿。但我的儿子或女儿若离开我一时，他们母亲的来临岂不该安慰我？那位就是生命者若同在，保证那已消逝之生命的福祉、保证那想念它之爱的福祉，这岂是小事？主的这些朋友若从他身上只能得到这么多好处，他又何必到世上来呢？有了长兄（the elder brother），他们难道不能有一阵子不需要这位弟弟吗？没有他，他们就必须绝对悲惨吗？她们满口的喊声是：「主啊，你若早在这里，我兄弟必不死！」你可以说，她们对基督的认识还不够。这是显然的——但基督对他们原有更多的期望，而失望了。

===Original===

You may say, “How could that be, seeing he knew what was in man?” I doubt if you think rightly how much the Lord gave up in coming to us. Perhaps you have a poor idea of how much the Son was able to part with, or rather could let the Father take from him, without his sonship, the eternal to the eternal, being touched by it, save to show it deeper and deeper, closer and closer. That he did not in this world know everything, is plain from his own words, and from signs as well: I should scorn to imagine that ignorance touching his Godhead, that his Godhead could be hurt by what enhances his devotion. It enhances in my eyes the idea of his Godhead. Here, I repeat, I cannot but think that he was disappointed with his friends Martha and Mary. Had he done no more for them than this? Was his father and their father no comfort to them? Was this the way his best friends treated his father, who was doing everything for them possible for a father to do for his children! He cared so dearly for their hearts that he could not endure to see them weeping so that they shut out his father. His love was vexed with them that they would sit in ashes when they ought to be out in his father’s sun and wind. And all for a lie!﻿—since the feeling in their hearts that made them so weep, was a false one. Remember, it was not their love, but a false notion of loss. Were they no nearer the light of life than that? To think they should believe in death and the grave, not in him, the Life! Why should death trouble them? Why grudge the friendly elements their grasp on the body, restoring it whence it came, because Lazarus was gone home to God, and needed it no more? I suspect that, looking into their hearts, he saw them feeling and acting just as if Lazarus had ceased to exist.
“Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. But I know, that even now, whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.”
“Thy brother shall rise again.”
“I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
“I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live. And whosoever liveth, and believeth in me, shall never die.”
I will not now endeavour to disclose anything of the depth of this word of the Lord.
