但如今，生命之主却要旁观他众受造者被任意的摧残。绊倒人的事是免不了的，但那绊倒人的有祸了！主似乎不理会，但他看见，他知道。

那么我说，我们每一个人都是别人所不是的一样什么，因此知道一样——也许并不知道他知道——别人所不知道的东西；而作为光之国（the kingdom）里的一员、国里一切的承受者，把他的份给其余的人，是每个人的本分；因为我们是一个家，神是这个家的头与心，耶稣基督——我们的长兄——把唯有他认识的父（the Father）讲给我们听。

那么我们可以说：凡是喜乐与爱的源头、凡是纯洁刚强、凡是唤醒憧憬、凡是把我们从自私里提出来、凡是美而可羡的——总而言之，凡是属于光的——无论它在比例上显得多小，必构成圣徒在光明中基业的一部分；因为如雅各书所说，「各样美善的恩赐和各样全备的赏赐都是从上头来的，从众光之父那里降下来的；在他并没有改变，也没有转动的影儿。」

孩子们怕天，因为那些没有孩子心的人给他们关于天的凄凉观念——那些人没有想象力，就无疑问地接受另一些同样没有想象力的人关于它的讲述。我看不出谁该在乎给它画一幅讨人喜欢的图画；因为，就算我能说服一个人，天是环绕他的一切他所愿之物的完全，那人或真理又能从中得着什么？他若认识主，就不会为天挂心；他若不认识主，也不会因此被吸引归向*他*。我不愿费力说服那软弱的基督徒，说天是一个值得去的地方；我更愿说服他：只要他还是如今这样，空间里没有一个点、永恒里没有一个钟头，于他有一文价值。但愿没有人胆敢把连自己也不知道的事教给小孩子！孩子们因努力强求去爱那些他们爱不起来的东西，受了多少苦！我清楚记得那前景之痛——不，是那因不能喜欢那前景而生的烦恼——就是被作成神殿中的柱子、永远不再出去！这些话原不是对小孩子说的。

===Original===

Yet are they, literally taken, a blessed promise compared with the notion of a continuous churchgoing! Perhaps no one teaches such a thing; but somehow the children get the dreary fancy: there are ways of involuntary teaching more potent than words. What boy, however fain to be a disciple of Christ and a child of God, would prefer a sermon to his glorious kite, that divinest of toys, with God himself for his playmate, in the blue wind that tossed it hither and thither in the golden void! He might be ready to part with kite and wind and sun, and go down to the grave for his brothers﻿—but surely not that they might be admitted to an everlasting prayer-meeting! For my own part, I *rejoice* to think that there will be neither church nor chapel in the high countries; yea, that there will be nothing there called religion, and no law but the perfect law of liberty. For how should there be law or religion where every throb of the heart says *God*! where every song-throat is eager with thanksgiving! where such a tumult of glad waters is forever bursting from beneath the throne of God, the tears of the gladness of the universe! Religion? Where will be the room for it, when the essence of every thought must be God? Law? What room will there be for law, when everything upon which law could lay a “shalt not” will be too loathsome to think of? What room for honesty, where love fills full the law to overflowing﻿—where a man would rather drop sheer into the abyss, than wrong his neighbour one hair’s-breadth?
Heaven will be continuous touch with God. The very sense of being will in itself be bliss. For the sense of true life, there must be actual, conscious contact with the source of the life; therefore mere life﻿—in itself, in its very essence good﻿—good as the life of God which is our life﻿—must be such bliss as, I think, will need the mitigation of the loftiest joys of communion with our blessed fellows; the mitigation of art in every shape, and of all combinations of arts; the mitigation of countless services to the incomplete, and hard toil for those who do not yet know their neighbour or their Father. The bliss of pure being will, I say, need these mitigations to render the intensity of it endurable by heart and brain.

===Chinese===

然而按字面取，比起连续不断上教会的观念，它们仍是一个有福的应许！也许没有人教这样的事；但不知怎的，孩子们得了这凄凉的幻想：有些不由自主的教导，比言语更有力。哪个男孩——无论多愿作基督的门徒、作神的孩子——肯拿一篇讲道换他荣耀的风筝，那玩具中的至圣，有神自己作他的玩伴，在蓝色的风里、在金色的空中把它抛来抛去？他也许甘愿舍下风筝与风与太阳，为他的弟兄下到坟墓里——但断不是为了叫他们得以进入一场永世的祷告会！至于我自己，我*欢喜*想：在高处的诸国里，将既没有教会也没有礼拜堂；不但如此，那里将没有一样东西叫作宗教，除了那完全的自由之律，再没有律法。因为当心的一跳一说*神*！当每一副歌喉都热切满溢感恩！当那样一阵喜乐之水的喧腾，正从神宝座之下永远迸发——宇宙喜乐的泪水，哪里还有宗教的地盘！宗教？当每个思想的本质都必是神，哪里还有它的余地？律法？当律法所能加一「不可」的每样东西都恶心得想也不可想，律法还有什么余地？诚实还有什么余地，当爱把律法充满直到外溢——当一个人宁可直直坠入深渊，也不肯亏欠邻舍一根头发丝？

天将是与神连续不断的接触。存在本身的感觉就将是福气。因为真生命的感觉，必须与生命之源有真实的、有意识的接触；所以单是生命——它本身、其本质是善的——善如神那作我们生命的生命——必是那样一种福气，我想，将需要与我们蒙福同伴相交之至高喜乐来缓和；需要各种形式的艺术、艺术的一切组合来缓和；需要给不完全者的无数服事、给还不认识邻舍与父之人的劳苦来缓和。我说，纯然存在的福气，将需要这些缓和，好叫它的强度为心与脑所能承受。

===Original===

To those who care only for things, and not for the souls of them, for the truth, the reality of them, the prospect of inheriting light can have nothing attractive, and for their comfort﻿—how false a comfort!﻿—they may rest assured there is no danger of their being required to take up their inheritance at present. Perhaps they will be left to go on sucking *things* dry, constantly missing the loveliness of them, until they come at last to loathe the lovely husks, turned to ugliness in their false imaginations. Loving but the body of Truth, even here they come to call it a lie, and break out in maudlin moaning over the illusions of life. The soul of Truth they have lost, because they never loved her. What may they not have to pass through, what purifying fires, before they can even behold her!
The notions of Christians, so called, concerning the state into which they suppose their friends to have entered, and which they speak of as a place of blessedness, are yet such as to justify the bitterness of their lamentation over them, and the heathenish doubt whether they shall know them again. Verily it were a wonder if they did! After a year or two of such a fate, they might well be unrecognizable! One is almost ashamed of writing about such follies. The nirvana is grandeur contrasted with their heaven. The early Christians might now and then plague Paul with a foolish question, the answer to which plagues us to this day; but was there ever one of them doubted he was going to find his friends again? It is a mere form of Protean unbelief. They believe, they say, that God is love; but they cannot quite believe that he does not make the love in which we are most like him, either a mockery or a torture. Little would any promise of heaven be to me if I might not hope to say, “I am sorry; forgive me; let what I did in anger or in coldness be nothing, in the name of God and Jesus!” Many such words will pass, many a self-humiliation have place. The man or woman who is not ready to confess, who is not ready to pour out a heartful of regrets﻿—can such a one be an inheritor of the light? It is the joy of a true heart of an heir of light, of a child of that God who loves an open soul﻿—the joy of any man who hates the wrong the more because he has done it, to say, “I was wrong; I am sorry.”

对那些只在乎东西、不在乎东西的魂——不在乎它们的真理与真实——的人，承受光的指望毫无吸引力；而为了安慰他们——何等虚假的安慰！——他们尽管放心，眼下没有要他们承受基业的危险。他们多半要被任凭继续把*东西*吸干，不断错过它们的可爱，直到末了厌恶那些可爱的壳——在他们的虚假想象里变成丑陋的壳。只爱真理之身体的，连在此世也终于称它为谎，为人生的幻影发出醉汉似的哀号。真理的魂他们失落了，因为他们从没爱过她。在他们能得见她之前，他们还得经过什么、经过怎样的炼净之火！

那些所谓基督徒对他们设想朋友已进入之状态的观念——他们称之为有福之地的——竟仍足以证明他们哀哭的苦涩有理，证明那「能否再认出他们」的异教式疑心有理。他们若真能认出，那才真是奇事！经过一两年那样的命运，他们很可能认不出来了！写这些愚妄，几乎叫人羞愧。与他们的天相比，涅槃倒是宏大。早期基督徒或许偶尔拿一个愚问搅扰保罗，那问题的答案至今搅扰我们；但他们中间可曾有一个怀疑自己要再见他的朋友？那不过是变形虫式不信的一种形式罢了。他们口里说信神是爱；却不能十分相信，他不至于使那我们最像他的爱，变成一场嘲弄或一场酷刑。若不许我盼望说「对不起，赦免我；奉神与耶稣的名，叫我在怒中在冷淡里所作的算为无有」，天上任何应许于我又值几何！这样的话必要有许多，许多自卑必要发生。那不预备认错、不预备倾倒出一心懊悔的男人或女人——这样的人能作光的承受者吗？一个光之继承者、那位爱敞开之魂的神的孩子、任何一个因自己作过而更恨那错之人的真心的喜乐，就是去说：「我错了；对不起。」

Oh, the sweet winds of repentance and reconciliation and atonement, that will blow from garden to garden of God, in the tender twilights of his kingdom! Whatever the place be like, one thing is certain, that there will be endless, infinite atonement, ever-growing love. Certain too it is that whatever the divinely human heart desires, it shall not desire in vain. The light which is God, and which is our inheritance because we are the children of God, insures these things. For the heart which desires is made thus to desire. God is; let the earth be glad, and the heaven, and the heaven of heavens! Whatever a father can do to make his children blessed, that will God do for his children. Let us, then, live in continual expectation, looking for the good things that God will give to men, being their father and their everlasting saviour. If the things I have here come from him, and are so plainly but a beginning, shall I not take them as an earnest of the better to follow? How else can I regard them? For never, in the midst of the good things of this lovely world, have I felt quite at home in it. Never has it shown me things lovely or grand enough to satisfy me. It is not all I should like for a place to live in. It may be that my unsatisfaction comes from not having eyes open enough, or keen enough, to see and understand what he has given; but it matters little whether the cause lie in the world or in myself, both being incomplete: God is, and all is well. All that is needed to set the world right enough for me﻿—and no empyrean heaven could be right for me without it﻿—is, that I care for God as he cares for me; that my will and desires keep time and harmony with his music; that I have no thought that springs from myself apart from him; that my individuality have the freedom that belongs to it as born of his individuality, and be in no slavery to my body, or my ancestry, or my prejudices, or any impulse whatever from region unknown; that I be free by obedience to the law of my being, the live and live-making will by which life is life, and my life is myself. What springs from myself and not from God, is evil; it is a perversion of something of God’s. Whatever is not of faith is sin; it is a stream cut off﻿—a stream that cuts itself off from its source, and thinks to run on without it.

===Chinese===

哦，悔改与复和与赎罪（atonement）的甜风，将在神国柔和的暮色里，从神的这园吹到那园！无论那地方像什么，有一件事是确定的：那里必有不止息、无穷尽的赎罪，必有永远增长的爱。还有一件也是确定的：凡那神人二性之心所愿望的，必不至落空。那作为神、又作为我们基业的光——因为我们是神的儿女——保证了这些事。因为那愿望的心，正是为此而被造来愿望的。神存在；愿大地欢喜，愿天欢喜，愿诸天的天欢喜！一位父所能作来叫他的儿女有福的一切，神都必为他的儿女作。所以，让我们活在不断的期待中，等候神——既是他们的父、又是他们永远的救主——要赐给人的美物。我在此间的东西既出于他、又明明只是一个起头，我岂不该把它们当作更美之事的定金？不这样看，又能怎样看？因为在这可爱世界的美物之中，我从没有过全然在家的感觉。它从没有给我看过足以满足我的、够可爱或够宏伟的东西。它不是我要住的地方的全部。也许我的不满足，来自眼睛开得不够、不够锐利，看不懂他所给的；但缘由在世界还是在我身上，都无关紧要，两者都不完全：神存在，一切都好。要把世界为我整治得够好——任何最高天没有它也不能于我为好——所需要的只是：我照他眷顾我那样眷顾神；我的意志与愿望与他的音乐合拍和谐；我没有一个离开他而从我自发的心思；我的个体性享有它作为他个体性所生者当有的自由，不作我身体、我祖先、我偏见、任何来自未知区域之冲动的奴隶；我因顺服（obedience）我存在的律——那活而赋活、使生命成为生命、使我的生命成为我自己的意志——而自由。出于我自己而不出于神的，就是恶；那是神某样东西的歪曲。凡不出于信心（faith）的都是罪；它是一条被切断的溪流——一条把自己与源头切断、还想离源而流的溪流。

===Original===

But light is my inheritance through him whose life is the light of men, to wake in them the life of their father in heaven. Loved be the Lord who in himself generated that life which is the light of men!

===Chinese===

但光是我的基业，是借着他——他的生命就是人的光，要在他们里面唤醒他们天上之父的生命——而有的。愿那位在自己里面生出那生命——就是人之光——的主受爱戴！

## Endnotes / 尾注
===Original===

1. There was no such change in the feeding of the multitudes. The fish and the bread were fish and bread before. I think this is significant as regards the true nature of a miracle, and its relation to the ordinary ways of God. There was in these miracles, and I think in all, only a hastening of appearances; the doing of that in a day, which may ordinarily take a thousand years, for with God time is not what it is with us. He makes it. And the hastening of a process does not interfere in the least with cause and effect in the process, nor does it render the process one whit more miraculous. In deed, the wonder of the growing corn is to me greater than the wonder of feeding the thousands. It is easier to understand the creative power going forth at once﻿—immediately﻿—than through the countless, the lovely, the seemingly forsaken wonders of the cornfield. To the merely scientific man all this is pure nonsense, or at best belongs to the region of the fancy. The time will come, I think, when he will see that there is more in it, namely, a higher reason, a loftier science, how incorrectly soever herein indicated. ↩︎
2. No doubt the humble spirit will receive the testimony of everyone whom he reveres, and look in the direction indicated for a word from the Father; but till he thus receives it in his heart, he cannot know what the word spoken of is. ↩︎
3. In the latter case a man may be mistaken, and his work will be burned, but by that very fire he will be saved. Nothing saves a man more than the burning of his work, except the doing of work that can stand the fire. ↩︎
4. It might be expressed after a deeper and truer fashion by saying that, God making human affairs after his own thoughts, they are therefore such as to be the best teachers of love to him and love to our neighbour. This is an immeasurably nobler and truer manner of regarding them than as a scheme or plan invented by the divine intellect. ↩︎
5. As it stands, it is difficult to read the passage without putting emphasis on the “me,” which spoils the sense. I think it would better be, “Why dost thou ask me concerning etc.?” ↩︎
6. That is, “which is still going to ruin through the love of the lie.” ↩︎

===Chinese===

1. 在喂饱众人的事上，并没有这样的变化。鱼还是鱼，饼还是饼，和先前一样。我认为这一点对于神迹的真正本质、以及它与神寻常作为的关系，颇具意味。在这些神迹里——我想在一切神迹里也是如此——只有显现的加速：把平常或许需要千年才成就的事，在一天之内作成；因为在神，时间不同于在我们。时间是他造的。而一个过程的加速，丝毫不干扰过程中的因果关系，也不使这过程多出一分神奇。的确，在我看来，生长中的麦子之奇，大于喂饱数千人之奇。创造的大能一下子——直接地——发出，倒比借着麦田那无数、可爱、看似被遗忘的奇观发出，更容易理解。在纯科学的人看来，这一切纯属无稽，至多属于想象的领域。但我想，时候将到，他必看见其中有更多的东西——一个更高的理性、一门更崇高的科学，尽管在这里指示得何等不正确。 ↩︎
2. 无疑，谦卑的灵会接受每一位他所敬重之人的见证，朝那人所指的方向仰望，等候父（the Father）的一句话；但直到他在心里这样领受，他不能知道那话是什么。 ↩︎
3. 在后一种情形里，人可能错了，他的工程将被烧毁；但正是借着那火，他要得救。除了作那经得起火的工程，最能救人的，莫过于自己工程的被烧。 ↩︎
4. 若照更深更真的说法，或许可以这样说：神（God）照他自己的思想安排人间诸事，因此这些事正是教导人爱他、爱邻舍的最好老师。这样看待它们，比把它们看作神圣理智所发明的一套方案或计划，无限更高贵、也更真实。 ↩︎
5. 照现在的样子，读这段话很难不把重音落在「我」字上，而那样就坏了意思。我想最好是：「你为什么问我关于……等呢？」 ↩︎
6. 就是说：「它因爱谎言，仍在走向败坏。」 ↩︎
